locationDesc: very year many thousands of respectful citizens and tourists visit the final resting place of the country’s most notable historic figure.

reviews.author: Igor Alexeev
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: For more than half a century, the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum (Lăng Chủ tịch Hồ Chí Minh) has been located in the Ba Dinh Square, where Ho Chi Minh, the first president of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam and founder of the National Liberation Front of South Vietnam, proclaimed the independence of Vietnam on September 2, 1945. The Mausoleum is a well-known attraction in Vietnam, including to numerous tourists. Visitor access to the mausoleum is open from 9:00, but I haven't managed to visit the mausoleum in my two visits to Hanoi. Evidently, I will have to come again. Ah, maybe not even once...

reviews.author: Russ Lacuata
reviews.title: Historic and Cultural site
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a powerful historical and cultural site that offers visitors a deeper understanding of Vietnam's heritage. I would highly recommend it to anyone interested in history, politics, or Vietnamese culture.  Features a well-maintained grounds, cultural importance, organized visitor experience. Consider long queues and strict visitor regulations.

reviews.author: Patty B
reviews.title: Worth Seeing
reviews.content: We chose this as part of our private tour.  Our driver picked us up early and advised we should do this first as it gets extremely busy.  He mentioned waiting in a queue for hours at times to get in.  We took his advice and were early enough to not have a wait.  The walk up to the mausoleum was far.  I just couldn’t imagine a long wait to do this when I saw how far it actually was.  We saw quite a few military members outside as well as in the mausoleum, they were quite intimidating looking.  Our guide told us to just walk quietly and respectfully past the glass enclosed sarcophagus to view his body.  As we were doing that I reached up to fix the Bobbie pin in my hair and it fell out.  I just kept walking, it was my only Bobbie pin, but I couldn’t risk even reaching down for it on the floor.  When we got outside a man from the group walking in front of us was being detained by one of the members of the military.  They took him away somewhere leaving the other members of his group standing there.  It was a little scary to witness that!   I knew then that I made the right decision to leave my only Bobbie pin behind.  We continued on with our tour to the other sights.

reviews.author: Andrea L
reviews.title: Interesting but not unmissable.
reviews.content: We visited the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex without going in to see the body. If you want to do it, organize your morning well because the mausoleum opens very early, at 7:30, but it also closes just as early, at 11:30.Access to the complex is free, but pay attention to your clothing: pants or skirts above the knee and tank tops should be avoided. Outside you will still find vendors selling sarongs: we bought one for 150,000 VND. For men, it seemed to us that there was a little less strictness, but it is still better to show up in appropriate attire.Inside the large complex, in addition to the mausoleum, you can visit the museum and the residences associated with Ho Chi Minh, including the famous stilt house. Be careful, however, because the various attractions have rather strict and not always continuous hours: it is best to check them beforehand to avoid finding something closed.Naturally, the classic photo in front of the imposing Mausoleum, with the large square that surrounds it, is a must.One last piece of advice, essential if you go in the summer: bring plenty of water. The heat and humidity can be really intense and the complex is very large. There are also some air-conditioned spaces where you can stop for a few minutes and recover from the heat!An interesting visit, especially to understand the historical and symbolic importance that Ho Chi Minh continues to have for Vietnam, but organize your schedule and clothing well before you go.

reviews.author: Guide38148870372
reviews.title: Bad.
reviews.content: The first time I went to Láng Bát and the experience was not very pleasant.Because the first time I knew that basket to send goods or luggage in the line I saw the employee Nam, the guiding guests in the line with a very unpleasant attitude.To the checking of goods I did not guide anything but straighten up the bag of goods and then call the guests with a broken voice.Because the first time I knew that basket to send goods or luggage in the line I also should see that people sorted goods in the line so that you did not behave correctly.If you are younger, then you also have to know how to wear long clothes is a good attitude and encourage me to get things to check out, not to let me get the stuff done, she also gave me the key to my residence but remembered my number of prisons, as I got crowded when I came out, you should not see the thing as well, and I had no difficulty to deal with it again.I want to visit you with a pleasant experience with gratitude, but I am not happy with the way ACHD works here.

reviews.author: Jean-Emmanuel R
reviews.title: Monument to the glory of Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: Closed during our visit. Nevertheless, the monument is well highlighted on a huge square and surrounded by pretty flowers.Several other must-see attractions in Hanoi (including the One Pillar Pagoda and the Ho Chi Minh Museum) are located on the site.

reviews.author: Ezra L
reviews.title: Interesting stop, but not a must-see
reviews.content: I visited the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum on a hot morning and it was an okay experience overall. The security line was pretty organized, and I liked walking through the grounds a bit before going in. The marble building is impressive in its own way, and the area feels very formal and quiet compared with the rest of Hanoi. That said, the visit itself was very short, and once you’re inside there’s not much to take in. It felt more like something you do because you’re in Hanoi, not because it’s especially memorable. Worth seeing once, but I wouldn’t go out of my way for it.

reviews.author: Tai L
reviews.title: Worth the visit, just go early
reviews.content: I visited the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum on a hot morning and it was one of those Hanoi stops that feels very different from the rest of the city. The grounds were calm and a bit formal, with guards everywhere and a long line of people moving pretty quietly through. Inside, it was very controlled and over quickly, but it did feel meaningful. I also liked walking around the surrounding complex and seeing the uniforms, the tidy gardens, and the big open square. My only real gripe was the strict rules and the wait, so wear something respectful and come early. Still, I’d recommend it if you want a bit of history while in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Travel Girl GR
reviews.title: It takes patience
reviews.content: Great trouble until you get into the mausoleum.The tail is huge so go very early when it opens.Remember that Monday is closed as well as three months from September until November that goes for maintenance in Russia.Be careful not to wear short pants and amane t-shirts, carry a scarf with you.You go through control and the water is banned.Backpacks are not allowed so lock them in closets after check.The tail is long but walking fast, it will take an hour to get in.Inside the mausoleum photos are prohibited and you just make a quick passage.

reviews.author: Kandis Post
reviews.title: A moving visit, but plan ahead
reviews.content: I’m glad I went, but it’s definitely a place to plan for. The area around the mausoleum is very orderly and the whole experience feels solemn, not touristy. I went early and still had to deal with a bit of a line, plus the security rules are strict, so wear proper clothes and leave bags light. Inside, it was quiet and a little surreal seeing Ho Chi Minh preserved like that. The square outside is worth a walk too, especially in the morning when it’s cooler. My only gripe is that it can feel a bit rushed, and if you’re not into historical sites, it may not blow you away. Still, I’d recommend it.

reviews.author: Roy Norvell
reviews.title: Worth visiting, but go early and expect rules
reviews.content: I’m glad I went, even though the experience was a bit more formal than I expected. The whole area felt very quiet and disciplined, with the guards, the big open square, and the line moving pretty slowly. Inside, it was actually more moving than I thought it would be, but you don’t get much time and there are a lot of rules, so it can feel a little rushed. I’d recommend going early because the heat and crowds build up fast. Also, dress modestly or you may have a problem at the entrance. Not my favorite stop in Hanoi, but definitely worth seeing once if you’re in the city.

reviews.author: Bandya Mama
reviews.title: Bandya Mama - The surrounding area forms a harmonious ensemble.
reviews.content: Visiting Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum again in February 2026, I was struck by how powerful the place remains no matter how many times one has seen it before. The architecture is simple yet majestic, built with clean lines and solid stone that express strength, dignity, and permanence. Standing in the vast space of Ba Dinh Square, I felt the same emotion generations of Vietnamese have felt—a quiet pride mixed with gratitude for the history that unfolded here.

reviews.author: dang d
reviews.title: Worth the visit, but plan for the queues
reviews.content: I’m glad I went, even though it was a bit more of a process than I expected. The whole area feels very formal and peaceful, and seeing the mausoleum up close gave me a real sense of the place’s importance in Vietnamese history. I liked walking through the grounds in the early morning before it got too hot, and the security checks were quick enough. That said, the lines can get long and the rules are strict, so be ready for that. It’s not really a leisurely stop, but it’s definitely worth seeing once if you’re in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Awilda R
reviews.title: Interesting visit, but a bit underwhelming
reviews.content: I went to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum expecting something really moving, but it ended up being kind of mixed for me. The building is impressive from the outside, and the whole area feels very controlled and orderly. I did like seeing the guards and the strict atmosphere, and the nearby grounds were peaceful in the morning. But the visit itself felt rushed, and the no-photos, no-standing-around rules made it hard to really take it in. It was also pretty crowded, so I spent more time waiting than actually looking. Glad I went, but honestly it wasn’t the most memorable stop in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Emmie R
reviews.title: Respectful site, but the visit felt rushed
reviews.content: I was glad I went once, but honestly the experience was a bit disappointing. The mausoleum itself is impressive from the outside and the grounds feel very calm and respectful, which I appreciated. But the whole visit was more hassle than it needed to be. The line moved slowly, there wasn’t much clear explanation in English, and the security rules felt confusing if it was your first time there. It was hot, there wasn’t much shade, and the visit inside felt very quick and impersonal. A few more signs, better crowd control, and some basic context would make a big difference. Still, seeing the place in person was memorable.

reviews.author: Ha Thanh T
reviews.title: Long wait, barely saw anything
reviews.content: I left pretty disappointed. We came early in the morning, stood in a long line in the heat, and then found out the mausoleum was closed that day. Nobody really explained it until we were already there, so it felt like a wasted trip across town. Even around the grounds, everything was super strict and rushed by guards, and you only get a quick look from far away. I was expecting a meaningful visit, but instead it was mostly waiting, shuffling, and being told where not to go. Maybe worth it if your timing is perfect, but for us it was a frustrating experience.

reviews.author: Necole B
reviews.title: Long wait for a closed mausoleum
reviews.content: I was really disappointed with this stop. I got there early, stood in a long line in the heat, and then found out the mausoleum wasn’t open to visitors that day. The security check also took forever, so by the time we realized it was closed, we’d already wasted nearly an hour. The square itself is impressive, but that didn’t make up for the fact that we couldn’t actually see the mausoleum. I wish the opening schedule had been clearer online or posted more prominently at the entrance. It felt like a lot of effort for very little payoff.

reviews.author: Sacha B
reviews.title: Worth a look, but not a highlight
reviews.content: I’m glad I went, but this was more of a quick cultural stop than a wow experience. The security was tight and the line moved slowly, which was fine, but the whole visit felt a bit rushed once inside. The mausoleum itself is very solemn and the grounds are well kept, with neat lawns and guards everywhere. It was hot and humid when I went, and the silence made it feel heavier. I liked seeing the area around it, but honestly there isn’t much to do beyond look and move along. Interesting enough, just not especially memorable for me.

reviews.author: sandydee_7
reviews.title: Go early to beat the queue
reviews.content: We were lucky as arrived early and no queue.  The Mausoleum itself was very imposing but the gardens and grounds of the complex were lovely and interesting

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: Bigger than the tomb of Lenin
reviews.content: This is an enormous building in a huge park. There is security to enter the square and water bottles are not permitted. The building is ceremonially guarded. There are also police stopping tourists getting too close. Periodically the guard changes. The marching is precise. You cannot visit Uncle Ho on Mondays or Fridays. As I went on Monday I cannot comment further.

reviews.author: Ceciledelanewyorkie
reviews.title: To do
reviews.content: Nice to do to clear the visit of the garden behind Be careful for the visits; women must have their legs and shoulders covered, and men cannot wear tank tops. Note that if you do not have the proper attire, it is difficult to find small vendors on the street to help you out. There is also no rental of attire at the entrance to assist you like in Thailand.

reviews.author: paolosbg
reviews.title: It's not worth it.
reviews.content: It's not worth it. Very cold building. Something can be glimpsed in a ballot box.

reviews.author: Adam G
reviews.title: Highly recommend
reviews.content: We visited Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum during my short stay in Hanoi, it is closer to center of Hanoi. It is always recommend to go early to avoid long ques due to many locals and other visitors. You should not wear fancy dresses if you are intended to go inside and pay your respect to the embalmed body of late president Ho 'hi Minh. You will not be allowed to take cameras inside and need to be quiet. It is always placed with Security forces every where. At the same premise you also can visit the Museum as well but need to buy a different ticket. To cover everything you will need a half day. One pillar pagoda also can visit around same area.

reviews.author: Marc B
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Being there early in the day is the message otherwise you have long waits. Ho Chi Minh has been laid out here in a glass coffin since his death in 1969.

reviews.author: David L
reviews.title: Huge mausoleum
reviews.content: This mausoleum is a huge monument in central Hanoi, built in honor of the revolutionary leader, considered the father of Vietnam.  The mausoleum is one of the must-see places in Vietnam.  Recommended.

reviews.author: 845daljinders
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mosoleum
reviews.content: Worth a visit. Go early as long queues can slow you down. No shorts or sleeveless shirts.

reviews.author: roberto p
reviews.title: To see
reviews.content: In order not to make the usual tour to the mausoleum that takes at least 2 hours, we decided to attend the morning flag that takes place every night in front of the mausoleum of Ho Chi minh, it happens at 21.00 is always quite crowded but the large park surrounding the mausoleum, welcomes several people allowing everyone to see the ceremony of the morning flag operated by soldiers in high uniform with a band in tow. It lasts about 20 minutes and is a nice ceremonial that compensates if you did not choose to visit the mausoleum that is open from 0900 to 1100.The ceremony is outdoors and is free

reviews.author: Gate88
reviews.title: Very moving experience!
reviews.content: Very moving experience & a definite must see if youre visiting Hanoi. Its very strict, no camera’s allowed & you mustn’t take photos on with phones etc. I used a “skip the line” service on the Get your Guide app (£12 inc) which saved literally hours of queuing and also included fast track security, an English speaking guide as well as entry to the grounds & museum.  Please remember - no shorts, no skirts, no sleeveless shirts, they absolutely will not let you in unless you are suitably dressed. Of course there are many locals outside willing to sell you sarongs or trousers for a few quid!

reviews.author: Go19460144302
reviews.title: Great place to visit !!!
reviews.content: Amazing place with respectful atmosphere. You should go early if you dont want to wait in a long line. Great history value

reviews.author: Cruiser14548402596
reviews.title: President Ho Chi Minh – A place where elite and dignity converge
reviews.content: President Ho Chi Minh Avenue, in Hanoi is a sacred architectural work, which holds the monument of Bác Ho, the highest respected symbol of the Vietnamese nation. Opened in 1973 and completed in 1975, it is located in the historic Ba Ling Square, distinguished by its solid architecture, sanctuary and green spaces. The Lan Bác is not only a distinct architectural work but also a sacred symbol, where the people of the whole country and international visitors show their affection for the great leader. This is the place where an important historical mark was recorded, where I once read the Declaration of Independence.

reviews.author: PavalikaV
reviews.title: Majestic Homage to Father of Nation of Vietnam
reviews.content: This place is where the final remains of Father of Vietnam is laid to rest and maintained in embalmed mode.Truly a splendid homage to their Father of Nation with utmost reverence by locals.Complex is large. Lots of walking is required. Security is very strict to the T.Got to deposit the bags, cameras, mobiles and even the waterbottles. But the best part is waterbottles(unused) were marked and are returned to you after the visit.Better signage would have helped the tourists. Similarly on certain days and timings, it is just shut. Security would not offer any reason or explanation. Nor is there any signage of such no entry days.Better to go in early mornings.

reviews.author: Mr Buster Bluth
reviews.title: Get there early. It's well worth it.
reviews.content: A vast, sprawling estate so make sure you get dropped off at the entrance or you'll have to follow my example and walk quite a way to get in.Watch out for the times. If you go in the morning you need to be there before ten. The do start shutting down from eleven.I was amazed how long I spent there. Must have been a couple of hours. The museum (an extra 40k) was well worth it but start on the first floor and work up. I thought that the second floor was brilliant. Loads of really interesting artistic displays.

reviews.author: Maria Rosaria D
reviews.title: Uncle Ho
reviews.content: Together, tourists and Vietnamese citizens, all pervaded by the emotion of being in the presence of “an uncle of the Fatherland” Uncle Ho. Great man, great country!

reviews.author: Jeremy C
reviews.title: Tribute to the Father of the Nation
reviews.content: Unable to enter the actual Mausoleum when we visited but still worth it and see the regard that the Vietnamese still hold for Ho. It is straight out of the communist copybook for gargantuan monuments to dead leaders and therefore good exercise to get around if nothing else, but I can't help but think that Ho himself would have been perfectly happy with something a lot more modest.

reviews.author: MrBoggen
reviews.title: Large building
reviews.content: It was quick to get in, a bit messy once you were inside. Many guards guarding the tomb. Nice to have been here

reviews.author: DRBAUKE
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Here, the ubiquitous worship for the former head of state becomes very tangible. The terrain is overall very impressive and a must-see when visiting Hanoi. Unfortunately, the grave vehicles let you out far from the main entrance.

reviews.author: Richard T
reviews.title: Worth waiting for the change of guard
reviews.content: Very popular with Vietnamese obviously, so arrive early to avoid queues. Everyone must dress modestly and even men cannot wear shorts…unless they are knee length at least. Not a big problem as there are enterprising locals on hand selling wraps and light trousers to solve the problem for 100000 Dong!Worth waiting for the change of guard. Only about a 5 minute ceremony.Also worth soaking up the atmosphere in the parade square.The mausoleum itself is very large and impressive and is a huge symbol for the Vietnamese.It is free to enter, but you have to go through security to get into the immediate square which causes delays at busy times.

reviews.author: Ross Owen
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh, Vietnam
reviews.content: a must visit site when visiting Hanoi. Now i can understand why Vietnamese people respect to his Uncle Ho, the great leader of the nation.This is also a beautiful complex includes big garden, house on stilt and fish pond

reviews.author: Murton68
reviews.title: Very good experience
reviews.content: We were lucky to go early and miss all the queues.  It was a very different experience to anything I’ve had before but certainly something I would recommend.

reviews.author: HamitGunesli
reviews.title: Uncle Ho
reviews.content: The founder father of Vietnam, a memorial tomb in memory of Ho Chi Minh, is located in a massive park.Inside, Ho Chi Minh is visited mummified.

reviews.author: Alexis P
reviews.title: An essential but highly structured visit
reviews.content: There is no doubt that Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum is a major national monument in Vietnam. That said, I would like to highlight a few practical points about the procedure and share some helpful warnings.If you are dropped off at the main square in front of the building, be aware that the entrance is actually located at the back. We had to walk all the way around the mausoleum, which took about ten minutes.Security is strict. You are not allowed to bring water inside and will be required to dispose of it at the entrance. Visitors are also expected to dress respectfully, with shoulders and knees covered. Interestingly, some men wearing shorts were permitted to enter, while women with uncovered shoulders were not.Cameras must be placed in provided bags and left at a counter before entering. They are returned after you exit the main chamber, though there may be a short wait.Inside, you are given only a brief moment — around 15 to 20 seconds — to view Ho Chi Minh’s preserved body before being guided onward.Overall, this is an essential visit when in Hanoi, as it represents a central pillar of modern Vietnamese history. However, I found certain aspects of the procedure somewhat lacking in clarity and consistency.

reviews.author: Talant2007
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh City Mausoleum
reviews.content: The mausoleum building was built in 1975 for Vietnamese statesman and founder of the Communist Party of Vietnam Ho Chi Minh (1890 - 1969). Security on the approach to the mausoleum is very serious :)

reviews.author: Flyingred
reviews.title: An insight into Vietnamese history and culture
reviews.content: For the local population, Ho Chi Minh is a much-revered hero, who is held in high regard. We decided that as we were in Hanoi, we should go to experience the visit.. We arrived around 8am and the queue was quite short. It's an interesting experience, following the route through the square to the entrance of the mausoleum, passing the military personnel who are on guard duty. Entering the inner chamber and seeing his embalmed body was a unique moment that was powerful.The pedestrian route takes visitors past the Ho Chi Minh museum and the presidential palace, which has a collection of the former president's possessions. Entry is chargeable and as we didn't have any Vietnamese currency, we missed out on these.As we left the complex, many coaches with school parties were arriving (around 9 am) so my suggestion is to plan a visit before the buses of children arrive. The route to the mausoleum is covered so there is adequate shelter from the sun or rain.We used Google maps for the walking route. It shows a direct route that doesn't take into account the military checkpoints and guards, so we had to walk around the block to reach the visitor entrance.

reviews.author: Vietnam immersion
reviews.title: A memorable visit
reviews.content: A nice walk to do at the complex of the mosollea Ho Chi Minh, if you want to enter to see his body in balm, you have to queue very early in the morning, after you cross the central square Ba Đình then cross to see the presidential palace, once also was the governor of Indochina., the temporary house and that of on stilts that Ho Chi Minh lived there until the end of his life,then you stop to see the single pagoda before leaving the site.

reviews.author: Steve_Grant1
reviews.title: A must see whilst in the city
reviews.content: This is a must see whilst you are in the city. Its not just about the Mausoleum but all the other historical sites around it. Be dressed correctly for the mausoleum and prepared to stand in a straight line to show your respect.

reviews.author: GlobetrotterMSK
reviews.title: Worth seeing
reviews.content: The tomb itself did not impress me very much, as I have seen Lenin's mausoleum and its creepy contents in Moscow before. I found the area of the memorial quite interesting. The official residence of Ho Chi Minh (originally built for the French governor of the colony of French Indochina) and its purpose-built buildings and other facilities are clearly worth a visit. Especially if you hire an expert guide who can provide additional information about the history of the museum.

reviews.author: Tripad86
reviews.title: Surprisingly emotional
reviews.content: I felt surprisingly emotional when visiting the mausoleum, though I have no connection at all with Vietnam. The man is so revered. We arrived at 8 am,  with only a short queue to get through security.  We didn’t have any bags with us, which simplified things. The Google maps walking directions from our hotel were very inaccurate - you cannot enter where it said. The entrance is on the west side of the site and you cannot walk across the huge area to the east of the building. A long way round! We wanted to visit the palace and the museum too but these are cash only places and we had none. The huge parties of school children getting off coaches  were entertaining as they all wanted to practise their English and say hello. Definitely a worthwhile visit. When we left the site at just after nine the queues were enormous.

reviews.author: FyingKiwi
reviews.title: Enlightening
reviews.content: A solemn and reverential experience which was enhanced through the tour guides descriptions of Ho Chi Minhs own philosophies. Much of what is portrayed of Ho Chi Minh in the western culture is contrary to what appears to be the more accurate portrayal of his life, reinforced by the displays of his work and wishes. Ho Chi Minh is described much more as a humble person with a passion for serving the people, rather than as one intent on radicalising the population against capitalism.What was learned by a visit here was that there was so much more to the social history of Vietnam than a vying for control, as is portrayed in the West.

reviews.author: beatrice g
reviews.title: not interesting
reviews.content: frankly it's not very interesting, to enter the mausoleum a route without stopping monitored by the military, entering think about taking off sunglasses and caps, not talking, no photo, we stop...

reviews.author: iPodsolnuh
reviews.title: Monument to the Chief
reviews.content: Like many mausoleums it leaves a rather difficult impression. However, it is definitely worth going here to get a better grasp of the history and modernity of the country. The line moves pretty fast, everything is organized wisely. Prohibited items may be deposited in the storage room.

reviews.author: Bernard W
reviews.title: When your wishes are ignored
reviews.content: Serious, long security lines.  Impressive monument, but one cannot always enter.  Sad that Ho Chi Minh’s wishes to be cremated were ignored.  He didn’t want such an imposing edifice.

reviews.author: JuanMarco31
reviews.title: It's worth looking at - Changing the guard every hour.
reviews.content: In the wake of the visit to the temple of literature we went to the park where is the imposing mausoleum of Ho Chi Minh. The gardens are perfectly maintained by a myriad of women and one can see pretty buildings behind the esplanade facing the mausoleum , If you have some time , the two guards who are stationary under the entrance structure will be replaced , interesting sight to watch .

reviews.author: Silke105
reviews.title: Rare place of interest
reviews.content: The entrance with security check and backpack drop-off is located in the SW corner of the widely cordoned off area. Those who step out of the grave incorrectly are allowed to circle the outside of the complex. We were there on Saturday and there were many school classes and other groups of locals on site.After passing the security checkpoint (as at the airport :)) we went to the Mausoleum in a clearly regulated manner. Due to the organizationally short stay in the Mausoleum, the visit was completed after 45 minutes. Admission was free for everyone. Admission to the presidential palace grounds is 40,000 dong for foreigners. We weren't there, though.Overall, an interesting experience.

reviews.author: Chanda Pit
reviews.title: Peaceful Plaza at Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum
reviews.content: Standing at the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum felt truly special—the enormous plaza in front was a breath of fresh air! After days of navigating Vietnam’s bustling streets, it was such a joy to finally walk peacefully, carefree and surrounded by open space, with no cars in sight. Pure serenity in the heart of Hanoi!

reviews.author: Travel@1964
reviews.title: This visit provides the opportunity for us all to explore our own personal experiences and perspectives on our lives
reviews.content: This is a rare opportunity to visit idealistic vision of influences of an era of Vietnamese Struggles …  it’s very glimpse into history.

reviews.author: jw6969
reviews.title: Catch the change of guard
reviews.content: We managed to get there just before 12 noon. Purelly by fluke, at that time there is a very theatrical changing of the guard. Goose stepping and so on. It was really fascinating. The mausoleum itself was distinctly Soviet in appearance - bland and sombre, but it was all well worth seeing.

reviews.author: possagol
reviews.title: Vietnamese history
reviews.content: The mausoleum contains the embalmed body of ho chi Minh. It is an important place for Vietnamese. In the mausoleum it is not possible to take pictures and you visit it in line without being able to stop. We saw it early in the morning because then it is full of people.  Check the timetable carefully because it is not always open. Monday and Friday closed on Tuesday from 8 to 16.30 the other days only from 8 to 11.30 women covered and men with pants at least below the knees at the back of the mausoleum the buildings and accommodations used by ho chi Minh with its cars

reviews.author: KaG
reviews.title: A long wait in line....but worth the visit
reviews.content: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum provides a sense of the Vietnamese admiration for this former leader, who is much admired by many Vietnamese.  It also provides an enhanced understanding of the culture and country's history.

reviews.author: nicodenheijer
reviews.title: Nice but unfriendly security
reviews.content: Entire property beautiful to see. But the security on the ground is not exactly friendly. Jr bag also goes through the xray again.  Road bandage stuff. Bit of a charade.

reviews.author: Alex J
reviews.title: Great if you are a history buff !
reviews.content: Unless you are a history buff like me, you might find this a bit underwhelming.  I grew up during the Vietnam War, and he was the great hero of my childhood, so for me it was an emotional experience, BUT....for the average person who doesn't care much for history, this may not be all that good.  The queues are long, and it could be quite tiring if it is a hot day.  The buildings are impressive, especially the main building.  Also, Ho's embalmed body looks very very lifelike.  There are other buildings on the premises (Ho's residence during the war, etc....)  We went because it was part of our itinerary, we were on a conducted group tour. But if you are on your own, you might give this a miss if you are pressed for time, and if you are NOT a history buff.

reviews.author: Glyn R
reviews.title: Informative and interesting
reviews.content: The site is impressive and the museum very interesting. The mausoleum was closed, but probably would not have qued anyway. Ho Chi Minhs stilt house worth a visit.

reviews.author: Michel10000
reviews.title: Must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: Must see in Hanoi, because Ho Chi Minh has been so important for the origin and independence of Vietnam. Impressive that he's laid out there and looks like it. Beautiful Presential Palace and nice to see where he really lived and worked in the large adjoining garden.

reviews.author: Myca E
reviews.title: A moment of quiet respect in the heart of Hanoi
reviews.content: We visited the mausoleum early morning—solemn, orderly, and deeply moving. Walking past Uncle Ho in silence with our friends made us reflect on Vietnam’s history in a way no textbook ever could. A must-see, done with reverence.

reviews.author: Beppe Marini
reviews.title: Very interesting: to see
reviews.content: Monument of historical significance especially for the Vietnamese people, I would say not to be missed for a visit to Hanoi. An impressive marble building, it houses the remains of Ho Chi Minh City that can be visited in silence and in continuous procession. You can't take pictures. It is also worth admiring the imposing spaces around the mausoleum

reviews.author: WHWhite
reviews.title: A must-see if interested in Vietnam's history
reviews.content: Free to enter. There is quite a long wait to get in. Staff impose a lengthy 'pause' so that a long queue builds up before letting people in, but at least you wait out of the sun. Cameras need to be handed in and reclaimed afterwards. You are kept moving as you go past the body, so you are through in a minute or two. The corpse is rather shiny / waxen in appearance, rather like Lenin as I recall seeing him in Moscow when I went there in my youth – similar techniques at work I suppose.

reviews.author: Frederique W
reviews.title: A peaceful and meaningful family visit
reviews.content: The grand architecture and serene gardens left a deep impression, especially on our children. Though solemn, it felt important to witness this piece of history. Well-organized and peaceful—a meaningful stop in Hanoi.

reviews.author: bhattesd
reviews.title: Must visit place
reviews.content: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex was a very moving experience. The place is beautifully maintained, and the atmosphere is solemn and respectful. It gave me a deep insight into Vietnam’s history and its beloved leader.

reviews.author: Xem Số Mệnh
reviews.title: Why No Trip to Vietnam is Complete Without Visiting Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum
reviews.content: A trip to Vietnam would be incomplete without visiting President Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum. This is where the body of a national hero, admired worldwide, is preserved. It is also the place where nearly every visiting head of state pays their respects.

reviews.author: TheLush101
reviews.title: Visiting Uncle Ho
reviews.content: Our tour of Vietnam included a visit to see Uncle Ho. We'd already been told that you needed to dress appropriately - in a similar way to visiting any religious site really - and to have covered shoulders and trousers on (not shorts). At the ticket entrance, there was security like at an airport. You then queue under walkways with a roof that keep the sun off. You then enter the main square and have a view of the outside of the Mausoleum. Again, we had to queue, but it does move as they keep people flowing through the complex. It's fairly small, you walk in and go up the steps - there are guards and cameras on the stairs. You then shuffle past Ho Chi Minh and work your way back out the other side - you're only in there 1-2 minutes max. I tried to slow down my walk a little bit and the guard politely said "please keep walking" so just bear in mind that they're always watching you! I'd already visit Lenin's Mausoleum in Red Square so had experienced something very similar. Our guide explained that it had been the same lab that had prepared Uncle Ho. This mausoleum and experience isn't on the same scale as the Russian one, but I think it's still important to see, and even if you don't enjoy it / think much of it, when you look around at what it means to the Vietnamese who will be visiting when you are, that says something.

reviews.author: Eli
reviews.title: A historical mausoleum in Hanoi.
reviews.content: A historical mausoleum in Hanoi. Quite solemn and has that classic monumental vibe. Learning more about its backstory was really interesting and surprising. If you’re traveling solo or on your own, you can use the Travellens AI app to explore it deeper.

reviews.author: salvatore1964
reviews.title: Typical mausoleum of totalitarian regimes
reviews.content: When you enter the (vast) area of the Mausoleum, you must abide by a set of rules that would be indigestible in most of our maximum security prisons.For heaven's sake, maximum compared to Ho Chi Ming: but if I enter the mausoleum where the body is exposed! If instead I visit the gardens, the pond, the wooden house where it turned off, etc. (with humidity at 90% and a perceived temperature of 45 degrees centigrade), someone wants to explain why I have to wear long pants?!?Moreover, you can not approach the sidewalk leading to the stairs of the mausoleum (you are first reprimanded and then rejected by the unfriendly military of Giardia), just as you can not smoke in the gardens: in short, the classic place where you observe the most rigorous "personality cult" typical of totalitarian regimes.Personally, visiting Hanoi again, I would not return.

reviews.author: AlexandraFlo
reviews.title: Worth it
reviews.content: Arrived at around 8am on a Tuesday, very busy. We were ushered into holding rooms which is unsure if that usually happens. After around an hours wait it was explained that there was a diplomat visiting and we couldn’t enter, thankfully that didn’t take too long and we were allowed through. Very happy we waited for the experience. After going inside there is an entry to pay around £1 to walk around the garden and visit his house see artefacts, this was great. Also thoroughly enjoyed the art we bought at the end as shown in photos.

reviews.author: lilybt
reviews.title: View appearance only
reviews.content: This mausoleum houses the remains of Ho Chi Minh, the Founding Father, who was given a permanent preservation measure. The inside of the mausoleum is cumbersome to secure and the entrance time is quite short, which limits the sightseeing of the surrounding facilities, so we only saw the exterior.

reviews.author: Ileniasu
reviews.title: If you like history, a must.
reviews.content: It is not permitted to enter the esplanade with lighters (they must be picked up at the entrance without returning them) and you cannot enter with bare shoulders. No straps or you have to cover them with a scarf.If you forget them at the entrance, there are vendors who sell them.

reviews.author: aurelieBou
reviews.title: Beautiful from the outside
reviews.content: We couldn't get in because we were in shorts. So let me say for the ladies consider taking a paraao so you can enter this place.

reviews.author: Fenzholt
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Memorial – Insightful visit
reviews.content: We did a guided tour of the Ho Chi Minh Memorial and really enjoyed it. The guide gave a clear and interesting explanation of Ho Chi Minh’s life, beliefs, and his huge role in Vietnam’s independence. He’s still deeply respected by the people, seen as a symbol of unity and national pride.We also got to see his old stilt house, which was simple but full of meaning—it really reflected his modest lifestyle. The garden around it is beautiful, with a peaceful lake full of fish and shady trees. There were also two of his old Russian cars on display, which was a cool touch of history.Overall, a great learning experience. I recommend to book a guided tour, or rent a “guide headset” to get most out of your visit.There is a security check at the entrance, they mostly look for lighters and stuff like that.We were allowed to bring our own water bottles.Definitely worth visiting if you’re in Hanoi, and if it’s not too hot :-)

reviews.author: Sayers Houston
reviews.title: A somber and poignant visit
reviews.content: The solemnity and respect shown here are palpable. It was an important history lesson for our children and gave us a deeper understanding of Vietnam's reverence for its leader. A truly profound and memorable visit.

reviews.author: Andrew S
reviews.title: Impressive and Solemn
reviews.content: It is worth the long line.  It is a source of rightful pride to the Vietnamese.  And, a stirring experience for non-locals.  I was thoroughly move.

reviews.author: Claire C
reviews.title: Mausoleum unexpectedly shut
reviews.content: Turned up two days in a row but uncle ho wasn’t taking visitors and the mausoleum was shut. You could view the building from the outside. It was on days advertised as open on the website and in the morning. Disappointing.

reviews.author: Katrin K
reviews.title: Imposing
reviews.content: The premises can only be entered through a security check. But that was relatively quick. We could only look at the mausoleum from the outside, as it was closed. It is very imposing with guards in front of it and you get an impression of how much Ho Chi Minh is worshipped. Opposite is the presidential palace, both built in a socialist style.

reviews.author: Adam K
reviews.title: Unexpected and spectacular.
reviews.content: We were very lucky as there were no queues when we arrived. We were ushered in by tall handsome white uniformed soldiers as though we were VIP dignitaries straight into the mausoleum. This was def one of the highlights of our Vietnamese trip.

reviews.author: Laura B
reviews.title: Pay your respects
reviews.content: How many places in the world can you see a world leader in such a state of rest?  Come here wearing respectable clothing (smart casual, I'm looking at you), take off your hat, walk the hallways to his resting place, then gaze respectfully.  Then go out and go to the museum right next door for the right history in context.  Worth a visit.

reviews.author: BorntocruiseUK
reviews.title: Don’t forget to cover your shoulders and legs!!!
reviews.content: I have visited before and managed to get into the museum but because of the limited opening times it closed on this occasion.I wore a t shirt and shorts and was made to purchase a shawl to cover my shoulders before I was allowed into the open air area in front of the building. This area reminds me of a car park. I could totally understand if I was entering the building but to just walk in the area seemed very strict. Lots of people were turned away as they didn’t have the correct clothes on. So be warned. There was a guy selling them by the entrance.Would I recommend going mmmm yes to tick the box.

reviews.author: Mark H
reviews.title: Goood places
reviews.content: Gooood places. We would like to visit one more time. This is a place where we can see the Ho chi minh’s body and explore a lot of things about him

reviews.author: John C
reviews.title: A must when visiting Hanoi
reviews.content: A must if you are visiting Hanoi. Large queues (both local and foreigners), but well organised - the line is always moving! It is worth the wait.When there, visit the museum as well.Check times before going to ensure it is open when you plan to visit.

reviews.author: oldmtravel
reviews.title: Impressive monument
reviews.content: The mausoleum is only open til 10 in the morning so get there early as it is a really busy place. Men and women need to be covered to the knee and shoulders covered to and they are strict  on this and that includes access to the house on stilts and the museum as they are all in the same complex there is an admission fee to the house it is only small so will need some money, it is a beautiful complex and the mausoleum is very impressive and over stated and a great tribute to the man that is held in such hi regard by the people of Vietnam

reviews.author: Alban F
reviews.title: Walking to ho chi min mausoleum. Don’t forget to cover your arms !
reviews.content: We arrived on n a Friday afternoon to find point the mausoleum was closed, which was a shame as we would have liked to have seen inside.

reviews.author: John P
reviews.title: An Essential Experience to Understand Vietnamese History
reviews.content: To begin understand the 2,000-year struggle for Vietnam to be independent from invaders and colonial powers, visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.  Get there early but only during the late fall, winter, and early spring when the body laid to rest in a glass coffin is not in Moscow for continued restoration.  The vast and sterile setting, long lines of silent citizens, and eventual passing by his preserved body from head to foot to head and out is somber and respectful.  I have passed the body of Lenin in his Red Square Mausoleum and Mao in his Tian'anmen Square Mausoleum are memorials to be understood in order to understand each of their national histories.

reviews.author: corinne_prevost
reviews.title: TO SEE
reviews.content: It's a mausoleum with reinforced guard. As with airports, you have to go under security gates. The thing to see is the changing of the guard. For the opening of the mausoleum it is not possible to take pictures and all electronic equipment is confiscated at the entrance. Behind it there is a small pagoda and a small temple. A short walk but especially not in full sun because there is no shade around the mausoleum. Hot stroke assured

reviews.author: Amy B
reviews.title: A Solemn and Memorable Experience
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum in Hanoi is the final resting place of an iconic leader and a very important part of Vietnam's history. When I visited, I found it to be a large, solemn space in Ba Dinh Square, and it was clear that respectful attire and silence are crucial here. There might be queues, but it's worth the wait. Inside, the atmosphere is quite dark and quiet, and seeing President Ho Chi Minh's body preserved in a glass case definitely creates a solemn and emotional feeling. The grounds are lovely, with gardens and monuments, and nearby you can find attractions like the Presidential Palace and One Pillar Pagoda. Overall, visiting the mausoleum provides a unique and meaningful experience.

reviews.author: GreGFlores
reviews.title: Skip this site.
reviews.content: Nothing to see except the closed mausoleum and a large flag pole when we went there. Maybe if there is a nice ceremony or event then it will be worth going to. Visit the nearby temples instead.

reviews.author: Eiffel
reviews.title: Vibrant tribute to Uncle Ho
reviews.content: We took the time to visit the mausoleum that houses Ho Chi Minh’s remains. It was an opportunity to share a moment with the Vietnamese people. Young and old come to pay tribute to their national hero, waiting in endless queues, until the body, kept in a glass tomb, is sneaked past. This is a solemn moment, a page in the rich and terrible history of Vietnam is before us, and this moment is unique.A little advice for those who do not want to queue for an hour and a half, you can arrive a quarter of an hour before the closing of the site (11:00 on Sundays for us) and you can access the tomb without queuing or at least much shorter.

reviews.author: Harirajan Varatharajan
reviews.title: Visiting ‘Uncle Ho’
reviews.content: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum was a profound and humbling experience. The atmosphere was solemn and respectful as we joined the queue of visitors paying their respects to Vietnam’s beloved leader. The mausoleum’s imposing structure, set against Ba Đình Square, reflected the significance of Ho Chi Minh’s legacy. Inside, the silence and precision of the guards added to the sense of reverence. Walking through the surrounding gardens and nearby landmarks like the Presidential Palace made the visit even more meaningful. It’s a must-visit to understand Vietnam’s history and the deep respect its people have for “Uncle Ho.”

reviews.author: rossbrownNottingham
reviews.title: Don't let the queue put you off.
reviews.content: We arrived at the Mausoleum at 9.06 am on a Wednesday. There was already a big queue there, but it was moving pretty quickly, we got through security, we had our water bottle confiscated which was fine, however, they did seem to be letting people through with mobile phones and smallish handbags. Long trousers, skirts and covered shoulders were acceptable but no headwear, we saw a woman get into trouble for having sunglasses perched on her head, the guard made her remove them.There were lines of Vietnamese primary school children also queuing to get into the mausoleum, their behaviour was impeccable, they had clearly been told how important this visit was by their teachers and parent helpers.Its very interesting to see the number of the military personnel around the mausoleum, a reminder that Vietnam is a communist country and that Ho Chi Minh is regarded as a great leader.We saw Ho Chi Minh lying in state and were out by 9.36 am, so a very slick operation, no one is allowed to stop. Well worth it to get a glimpse of another facet to life in Vietnam.

reviews.author: mion369
reviews.title: De Grote Leider
reviews.content: Thousands of people are lining up, but actually it's making reasonable progress. We sat down for 55 minutes, including a visit to the grave. Everything is done with military precision, anyone who steps out of line is immediately reprimanded. Beautiful terrain, interesting information about life and work of Ho Chi Minh.

reviews.author: Alison Townsend
reviews.title: Respectful
reviews.content: Very slick respectful experience, quite overwhelming.  So glad we did this tour/visit and into the gardens and the Stilted house.  Years on and Ho Chi Min is still so well regarded...

reviews.author: GIZMOKI
reviews.title: Unfortunately, it was Monday and I couldn't get in.
reviews.content: Unfortunately, it was Monday and we couldn't get inside, but we couldn't see the changing of the guard. There is a bit of distance from the old town, so I took a grab car.

reviews.author: Ian R
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Free to enter (museum is a paid for visit), most of the site seemed to be closed.That said the mausoleum was impressive and the gardens nice.

reviews.author: MrDream688
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: The scenery is truly impressive and solemn. The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a must-visit when in Hanoi. The surrounding area is well-maintained, creating a peaceful and sacred atmosphere. Visitors are very orderly, showing deep respect for the great leader. The flag-raising ceremony in the morning and the flag-lowering ceremony in the evening are particularly moving experiences. If you love history and want to learn more about Vietnam, this is definitely a place worth visiting!"

reviews.author: vidijo
reviews.title: Not wanted by the deceased person himself.
reviews.content: For the northern Vietnamese a place of pilgrimage and a very spacious site where these people come to honor their idol. In order to fully understand this, you should read through the history of Vietnam. The building is 21.6 meters high and has a length of over 41 meters. Ho's dying wish was to be cremated has not been fulfilled. Hồ wanted his ashes to be spread throughout Vietnam. Very strict rules are set here. No photography or filming is allowed. There are also rules on clothing and behavior. For example, the legs should be covered, in both men and women. There is also a change of guard, less spectacular than in Greece, for example.

reviews.author: alessandro s
reviews.title: Even not.
reviews.content: Undoubtedly very important for the Vietnamese for the fundamental role of Ho Chi Minh in the history of the country.That said, to visit the interior you have to queue for over an hour (if there is unpleasant sun), airport style checks, absolute prohibition of photographs with a camera deposited at the entrance.The visit is a line up to Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body inside an imposing building but of zero artistic value.In my opinion, apart from being able to say you have been there, in the economy of travel it is better to spend a couple of hours more in Hanoi's old quarter, what is worth seeing of the Mausoleum can be seen from the street outside in front of the Parliament

reviews.author: Sue M
reviews.title: Crowded and Tight Security
reviews.content: We came in the afternoon so no chance of going into the mausoleum, the complex is vast and security is tight.  A tourist tried to come into the complex with a knife through security, the military guards stopped everyone from coming in for a period of time until they were satisfied that no one else was involved.  We did go visit the Ho Chi Minh Memorial Complex to see Uncle Ho's stilt house and how simply he lived.

reviews.author: Jey
reviews.title: Worthwhile but very strict
reviews.content: It was very special to see the body of Ho Chi Minh and I am glad to have gone to the mausoleum however the staff were extremely rude. Everyone seemed to dislike tourists and had no interest in helping. This could be because perhaps they are unable to speak English but I don’t think that should stop them being kind. We were told you walk in two single filed lines and told not to walk too fast and not to step out of line but not really given more direction on where to go and then were yelled at for stepping the wrong way. You walk into the mausoleum and then around the body of Ho Chi Minh. You cannot stop you must keep walking and then back out again and there are guards everywhere. No photos and no talking. It was quite nice to be able to see something like this without people crowding around.You can walk around the grounds and see other information on Ho Chi Minh. I would recommend this but be aware, it is extremely strict and at the security screening many items may be taken off you and they are strict on dress code.

reviews.author: Edward B
reviews.title: You need to allow alot of time
reviews.content: We had stayed overnight in Hanoi from Celebrity Solstice. We went to the Mausoleum but it was clear we were not going to have time to go through security and then the queue to see inside the Mausoleum and then get our transfer backWe walked around the outside and could see the Mausoleum and the Palace, which looked spectacular If you have more time than us then like us we will visit in future but allow the time to visit Next time we return then will be the first thing to do but you will need to queue early which we would not mind as we would have the time

reviews.author: alessandra_biondi3
reviews.title: The great President Ho Chi Minh always lives in our lives
reviews.content: The Mausoleum is surrounded by 79 (in honor of his years) very long-lived Japanese palm trees that bloom every 15-20 years, stand the inscriptions praising the life of Ho Chi Minh forever in us and long life to the socialist republic of Vietnam.. the Mausoleum was built 4 years after his death in 1973 and finished in 1975, it is on the square overlooking the Ministry of Foreign Affairs office, Parliament, the Presidential Palace of the Party, all around there are bamboo plants. Ho Chi Minh was born 9.5.1890 to a Confucian and patriotic family, at 21 he left the country to move to France because he had to find his own path to save his country. He was a great leader revered by the people.

reviews.author: gfsc5
reviews.title: Imposing
reviews.content: We didn't enter the mausoleum as it was closed on the day we visited (Friday) which was ok as we mainly went to see the area and grab some photos.  It's an imposing building built up high and with lots of open area in front of including grassed and paved.

reviews.author: OnAir38937315268
reviews.title: Good, Eclectic View of Uncle Ho
reviews.content: A Must See, the actual mausoleum, with the embalmed 'Uncle Ho' in it, has limited opening hours. It's located in a large complex of government buildings (Parliament, President's House, Ho Chi Minh's old house and more) so be prepared to walk around. Well kept, it provides a good view of Vietnamese history. Lots of security.

reviews.author: Thomas S
reviews.title: Focused Communism
reviews.content: Terrible. In the afterlife I think it was a total waste of time to see a dead dictator. This is communism at its worst. The soldiers there and the security guards are treating you like a criminal. The place is full of propaganda, and it was all just awful. How we had to stand in line and get crash orders. Have little sense for the whole experience. Steer away, read the bad comments.

reviews.author: Teresa
reviews.title: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum was a unique and solemn experience
reviews.content: The atmosphere is highly respectful, with strict rules on dress code and behavior. The line was long but moved quickly, and seeing Ho Chi Minh’s preserved body felt surreal. While the experience was interesting, it’s quite formal and not for everyone. Worth visiting if you appreciate history and cultural insights.

reviews.author: El Diavoloroso
reviews.title: Ok
reviews.content: Access to the complex is highly restricted. We had to leave our backpacks, handbags, and personal belongings in the entrance lockers. Guided along covered walkways, we proceeded toward the mausoleum. Security guards constantly reminded us not to take photos and to keep moving.

reviews.author: Minadua85
reviews.title: Must Visit
reviews.content: A solemn and respectful site honoring Vietnam’s great leader. The architecture is imposing, and the surrounding gardens are well-maintained. Arrive early to avoid long lines!

reviews.author: Safari31281666077
reviews.title: One of the feature hotspot
reviews.content: Lăng Chủ tịch Hồ Chí Minh in Hanoi is a solemn and powerful tribute to Vietnam's revolutionary leader. Visiting the mausoleum felt deeply moving, as it's not just a place to pay respects but a reflection of his lasting influence on the country. The atmosphere is respectful and quiet, with guards standing watch over his preserved body. The surrounding Ba Đình Square adds to the sense of importance, making it a meaningful experience for anyone interested in Vietnam's history and culture.

reviews.author: Simon
reviews.title: Interesting and educational.
reviews.content: Very easy to get in. Great building and more soldiers present. You really get an insight into how much Vietnamese value the former leader.

reviews.author: Mork001
reviews.title: Single file
reviews.content: Got a taste of being corralled in single file to go to the mausoleum.Don’t step out of line after being screened….😀 or bring any water…Will have to be stored.File passed in two single files and up and out you go.Only open for a small window of opportunity so it will be crowded.Has to be done while in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Liliane M
reviews.title: Nothing exceptional.
reviews.content: I personally was not impressed.You can't take pictures, you can't talk. Throughout the tour you are escorted with young armed soldiers.Although I understand that you have to have respect and recognition for what you did for your country I did not like the way we had to do the tour.

reviews.author: Hugary1
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: This is one of those place that if your in the country is worth seeing. Do it on a tour for quicker entry or you may have a 3 to 5 hour wait.No images inside as that is very much taboo.

reviews.author: eve3
reviews.title: I'm free in the early hours of the morning.
reviews.content: It is basically closed on Mondays and Fridays except during the long closure period. Early morning hours are recommended to avoid crowds. Visit with minimal luggage to avoid being caught up in the same checks as you would on a plane. Anything over the size of a handbag is not allowed.

reviews.author: Nostran Gerry
reviews.title: A place that needed to be visited
reviews.content: During our Vietnam Tour we could not miss this place. We start queuing early in the morning because of the large influx of people, we leave our backpacks and cameras, and agents accompany us to the grand entrance walking in two rows. Immediately at the entrance several guards dressed in white accompany you inside in total silence.

reviews.author: Shafinah J.
reviews.title: A Quiet Reflection of Vietnam’s History
reviews.content: Ever wanted to see a body that has passed on for more than 45 years? In Hanoi, you actually can. Believe it or not, the embalmed body of the much-revered Ho Chi Minh lies in a glass casket within his monumental tomb in the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, despite his wishes to be cremated and his ashes to be scattered in the North, Centre, and South of the country. Rules are strict in the Mausoleum though: no cameras, no bags, no talking, and no laughing. Oh, and take off your hat if you’re wearing one. Etiquette reads that it is rude (not to mention disrespectful) to wear hats indoors. A quick word of advice: do a check before visiting the Mausoleum. Apparently, Uncle Ho’s body gets packed off to Russia three months out of every year for major embalming maintenance. And wake up early too, because the last entry into this sacred Mausoleum is at 10.15am sharp daily.

reviews.author: Louise
reviews.title: Must See Be Patient!
reviews.content: If the experience didn’t feel like I was in North Korea this would be a 5 star attraction! If you’re in Hanoi this is a must but BE PREPARED! We have been to many religious sites and know about dressing modestly etc, my male partner was caught out for wearing shorts, we went across the road and got a pair of pants for about $5 AUD, no worries. We then got into the line with every other person local and tourists, to be screened by security more than the airports! Don’t bring any bottles of water or any big cameras, they will all be taken, cameras will be stored - to top it all off we get inside after the escapade of security and pants and see other people inside IN SHORTS!! As we go through the area we are marched in 2 straight lines for 40minutes! And might I mention no phones, photos or cameras - that’s fine totally respect it but honestly it was over the top and a double standard, tourists were being targeted and further only tourists have to pay. A small fee I know, but the negative attitude toward tourists put a slight damper on the whole thing! Nevertheless seeing the preserved body was amazing and such a feat, the communist influence throughout was very interesting to see and it was awesome to stand where many great political leaders have stood before! Would totally recommend but be prepared!

reviews.author: Maison Nhã
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum in Hanoi was a deeply moving experience. Located in Ba Dinh Square, the site holds the embalmed body of President Ho Chi Minh, the leader who played a pivotal role in Vietnam's history. The atmosphere is solemn and respectful, with guards ensuring decorum.The mausoleum itself is an impressive structure, blending traditional Vietnamese elements with a modernist design. Inside, the atmosphere is quiet and reflective as visitors file through in silence to pay their respects. It’s remarkable how much care and effort goes into maintaining the site, reflecting the reverence Vietnamese people have for "Uncle Ho."I recommend going early in the morning to avoid long queues, especially during peak tourist seasons. Nearby attractions, like the Presidential Palace and Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, add depth to the visit, offering insights into his simple and impactful life. Overall, it’s a must-visit landmark that encapsulates Vietnam’s modern history and enduring respect for its leader.

reviews.author: Passport38984184928
reviews.title: HA NOI: 8 Hours Tour Plan Recommendation
reviews.content: Here is a recommendation tour plan for 8 hours when you visit Ha Noi:13:00-13:30: Arriving to President Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum13:30-14:30: Visiting Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, Museum, and One Pillar Pagoda (note to dress politely and properly)14:30-15:30: Visiting the Temple of Literature15:30-17:00: Visiting Hoa Lo Prison17:00-18:00: Choosing to enjoy dinner with the dishes suggested by the tour18:00 - 19:15: Moving to watch the  Quintessence of Tonkin show19:15- 19:30: Buying tickets and check-in 19:30-20:45: Enjoying the Quintessence of Tonkin show20:45: End of schedule.I/ A few descriptions of the above locations:1. Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum, located in Ba Dinh Square, Hanoi, is one of Vietnam's most important historical landmarks. It serves as the resting place of President Ho Chi Minh, the beloved leader who led the country to independence and unification. Constructed from 1973 to 1975, the mausoleum's architecture reflects the simplicity and solemnity of his spirit. Inside, President Ho Chi Minh's body is preserved in a special glass chamber, attracting millions of visitors annually. This site is not only a symbol of historical significance but also an educational space for future generations.2.The Ho Chi Minh Museum, located in Hanoi, is a grand tribute to the life and legacy of President Ho Chi Minh. Opened in 1990, the museum is designed to resemble a lotus, symbolizing purity and the revered leader's modesty. It houses a vast collection of artifacts, photographs, and documents that chronicle Ho Chi Minh's journey from his early life, revolutionary activities, to his leadership in Vietnam's struggle for independence. Through its exhibits, the museum offers visitors profound insights into the history of Vietnam and the enduring influence of Uncle Ho's ideals and vision for the nation.3. One Pillar Pagoda, located in Hanoi, is one of Vietnam's most iconic Buddhist temples. Built in 1049 during the Ly Dynasty, it stands on a single stone pillar, resembling a lotus blossom rising from a pond. The unique architecture symbolizes purity, akin to a lotus blooming in muddy water. Originally constructed to honor the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the pagoda has become a symbol of Vietnam's rich cultural heritage. Despite being destroyed and rebuilt over the centuries, it remains a beloved landmark and a testament to the country's enduring spiritual traditions.4.The Temple of Literature - Quoc Tu Giam, in central Hanoi, is one of Vietnam's most significant historical and cultural sites. Built in 1070 during the Ly dynasty to honor Confucius, it became Vietnam's first university in 1076, training many talented individuals. This site symbolizes Vietnam's dedication to education and meritocracy. Its five distinct areas include Van Mieu Mon, Dai Trung Mon, Khue Van Cac, Bai Duong, and Hau Palace. A highlight is the 82 stone steles of doctors from the 15th to 18th centuries, recognized by UNESCO. Today, it's a venue for cultural and educational events and a place where students pray for exam success, showcasing Vietnam's long-standing respect for education.5.Hoa Lo Prison, centrally located in Hanoi, stands as a poignant symbol of Vietnam's history. Built by the French in 1896, this "Maison Centrale" initially held revolutionaries opposing colonial rule. Known as the "Hanoi Hilton" during the Vietnam War, it detained captured American pilots, including Senator John McCain. Despite its grim past, today it houses a historical museum displaying documents and artifacts from different eras. Attracting numerous visitors, the site highlights Vietnam's struggle and resilience, educating future generations about patriotism and the indomitable spirit of its people.6."The Quintessence of Tonkin" is a unique art program that authentically recreates the culture, history, and life of the Northern Delta region of Vietnam. Performed on an outdoor stage near Thay Pagoda, it attracts a wide audience. The program features a large water stage blending with nature, enhanced by modern lighting, creating a vibrant artistic space. It comprises six chapters depicting various aspects of Northern culture and history through dance, folk music, and modern theater techniques. Combining tradition and modernity, it utilizes lighting and projection technology alongside traditional elements like ao dai costumes and ethnic musical instruments. This program not only honors traditional values but also serves as a profound cultural lesson, promoting Vietnamese heritage and pride.II/ Transporting Recommendation:Travel by private rental car or book a taxi on the Xanh SM app (when visitors experience the quality of Xanh SM services, they will also learn more about innovation in using public transportation in Vietnam when traveling with a car company manufactured by Vietnamese people, it also helps save travel costs)III/ Recommended Cuisine:1. Cha Ca Thang Long Restaurant (21 Duong Thanh, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi) is renowned for its unique grilled fish, a symbol of Hanoi's culinary culture. Fresh fish, usually lentil or fruit fish, is marinated with turmeric and traditional spices, then grilled and stir-fried with dill and spring onion. Served with vermicelli, grilled rice paper, roasted peanuts, herbs, and shrimp paste with lemon and chili, this dish attracts both local and international diners eager to experience Vietnamese cuisine.2. Bun Dau Hang Khay (31 Hang Khay, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi) is a traditional dish and a must-visit for vermicelli with tofu and shrimp paste lovers. Located near Hoan Kiem Lake, it attracts locals and tourists with its fresh ingredients: crispy fried tofu, soft vermicelli, fragrant boiled meat, and signature spring rolls. The shrimp paste dipping sauce, seasoned with lemon, chili, and hot fat, creates an unforgettable flavor. Served on bamboo trays, the small, bustling eateries offer an authentic Hanoi atmosphere. For a true taste of old town cuisine, Hang Khay vermicelli and tofu is a top choice.3. Bat Dan beef pho (49 Bat Dan, Hoan Kiem district, Hanoi) is a traditional Vietnamese dish beloved worldwide. Originating from Hanoi, it features soft rice noodles, thinly sliced beef (often rare or thin), and a clear, sweet broth simmered from beef bones with spices like anise, cinnamon, herbs, ginger, and onions. This dish symbolizes the sophistication of Vietnamese cuisine, blending ingredients meticulously. Starting your morning with a hot bowl of beef pho promises a delightful experience.4. Co Vietnamese Restaurant & Vegan (21 Hang Can, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi) specializes in serving international guests with fresh, typical Vietnamese dishes. The menu features traditional flavors, including both classic dishes and unique vegetarian options. Whether you're exploring Hanoi's bustling streets or seeking a cozy dining spot, Co Vietnamese Restaurant offers a warm, inviting atmosphere for a memorable meal.IV/ Favorable weather and travel time:- Time: Because Hanoi's weather changes with the seasons, the best time to visit is in the fall and spring (from September to November and March to May).- The weather is comfortable, moderately sunny, not too hot or cold, and suitable for outdoor activities. V/ Estimated cost.1. Entrance ticket price:- Ticket price to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum:+ Ticket price to visit Uncle Ho's Mausoleum: free+ Museum admission price: 40,000 VND (1.58 USD) + Ticket price to see One Pillar Pagoda: free2. Ticket price to visit the Temple of Literature: 70,000 VND (2.76 USD)3.  Ticket price to visit Hoa Lo Prison: 30,000 VND (1.18 USD)4. Meal prices:- Cha Ca Thang Long Restaurant: ranges around 300,000 VND (11.79USD)- Bun Dau Hang Khay: 30,000VND to 50,000VND (1.18USD-1.96USD)- Bat Dan beef pho: 50,000VND to 100,000VND (1.96USD-3.93USD)- Co Vietnamese Restaurant & Vegan: about 300,000VND/person (11.79USD)5. Ticket price the Quintessence of Tonkin show: - Silver seats (located on both sides of the stands): 320,000 VND (12.57 USD)- Gold class seats (located in the center area, in front of the stage): 400,000 VND (15.72 USD)- Platinum class seats (located in a private seating area with a central view of the stage, snacks served, and limited quantity): 640,000VND (25.15USD)6. Taxi rental cost: Vinfast VF 9 Eco 7-seat taxi rental: 2,300,000 VND/day (90.37USD)These are some suggestions for the 8-hour tour plan, hope it will be useful for you, and wish you a wonderful trip!

reviews.author: Almacsixtyeight
reviews.title: Extraordinary place, highly recommended
reviews.content: If you love history, I strongly recommend a guided tour here. The whole complex is filled with architectural gems, incredible stories and beautiful gardens. Lying in state for over 50 years I feel that his spirit remains strong. It is obvious why Uncle Ho is still revered today and that successive government remain open armed to the rest of the world. In the same way that dispersed Vietnamese people across the world continue to charm us all, made us curious enough to find out more. I learnt more on this day, then from any book, film or documentary. The highlight was to see quite a few war veterans in full uniform with their comrades still paying homage.

reviews.author: Brian Jude
reviews.title: It’s a tomb and it’s grey
reviews.content: It’s a tomb and you can but stand outside it and look at it. Nothing special. You can walk past it and view but that’s the sum of it

reviews.author: Ilaria S
reviews.title: A place of worship
reviews.content: More than a site of interest, it is a real place of worship where the population goes to give a heartfelt tribute to the remains of Ho Chi Min, enduring long in perfect order. Children are also brought from schools to learn a sense of respect and local worship.In addition to Ho Chi Min's body you can visit his first house (where leaders are now hosted during political events), his second humblest house, built of wood on stilts to "live like the people", the communal kitchens where he ate with his servants. Inside the complex there is a museum open only to students.All immersed in a huge well-kept park, rich in greenery and colorful floral beds, around a lake populated by carp.

reviews.author: LSQRD1
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: It was impressive to see this representation of the resting place of the father of modern Vietnam.  We opted for a walk past the mausoleum as opposed to lining up int the morning for a viewing.  The scope of the monument and its setting, to me, demonstrated the importance of Ho Chi Minh to Vietnam and this helped me gain understanding of the country and its culture.

reviews.author: christine s
reviews.title: This is protected by military ,ceremonial guards,which change,so get your cameras ready for changing of the gaurd.
reviews.content: Here we came,sited in HO CHI MINH quarter,is this huge mausoleum,dedicated to the father of modern VIETNAM,there are lots of gardens and building worthy of a visit,each with is own historical record of past  events,allow 2-3 hours here

reviews.author: Matilde Michael
reviews.title: A profound tribute
reviews.content: Standing before the grand structure in Hanoi, we felt a profound connection to Vietnam's history. The solemn atmosphere inside compelled us to reflect on the nation's journey. It's a humbling experience we'd recommend to anyone seeking cultural insight.

reviews.author: Alberto G
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Mausoleum of Ho Chi Min - the Vietnamese leader who defeated the US. Venerated and with his body embalsamed for visitation. Beautiful on the outside and beautiful on the inside. Well organized and with controlled entrance. Interesting.

reviews.author: Julianne L
reviews.title: A solemn but rushed experience
reviews.content: We arrived early to beat the crowds but still waited 30 minutes. The guards were quite strict about dress code and photos. The actual viewing felt rushed - they keep the line moving quickly. Impressive architecture though! Be prepared for security checks and remember to dress respectfully.

reviews.author: Huntlee P
reviews.title: A solemn tribute to Uncle Ho
reviews.content: A landmark and historic visit to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. The atmosphere is full of respect and reflection. We were impressed by the fervour of the Vietnamese coming to mourn the remains of their national hero. An experience to live to understand the importance of "Uncle Ho" in Vietnamese culture.

reviews.author: BTS1972
