reviews.content: While there is tight security and therefore a long queue, what you get in return for the visit is marginal. You see a Soviet-style building from the outside and several buildings, where Ho-Chi-Minh is supposed to have sat, eaten, slept etc. Nothing important worth seeing - unless you are a real Uncle Ho fan. Otherwise, save the time.

reviews.author: thebestjourneyyet
reviews.title: Worth a visit if in Hanoi
reviews.content: If you are visiting Hanoi it’s definitely worth visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the Presidential Palace as well as the house on stilts where Uncle Ho spent his latter years.

reviews.author: Concettina Z
reviews.title: Dawn Visit to Uncle Ho
reviews.content: We arrived early to witness the changing of the guards - what an impressive ceremony! The atmosphere is incredibly reverent, and although the visit was brief, it gave us profound insights into Vietnam's deep respect for their revolutionary leader.

reviews.author: Andrew
reviews.title: Journey to the source with President Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a place that every Vietnamese should visit at least once in their life. The solemnity and respect from the time of lining up until entering the mausoleum made me feel grateful and respectful towards Uncle Ho. The surrounding scenery with the large Ba Dinh Square and historical buildings made for a meaningful trip

reviews.author: yang
reviews.title: Memorial to the father of the nation
reviews.content: The solemn atmosphere and the respect of thousands of people visiting Uncle Ho's Mausoleum made me feel proud and moved. The line of people was long but moved very orderly. This is a destination that every Vietnamese person should visit at least once in their life.

reviews.author: Alex
reviews.title: An emotional visit
reviews.content: As an American, I am always looking for new experiences and challenges. I love to be active, explore, and enjoy exciting activities, from sports to adventure travel.

reviews.author: Hoi An Free Walking tour & Cycling tour

reviews.content: Such a Good place to learn about the life of President Ho Chi Minh and Vietnamese history. You should avoid to visit this place at the weekend  because a lot Vietnamese  people come here to show their respect and love to President Ho Chi Minh. HCM mausoleum is the place where VIP of the other countries must visit when they have meetings in HaNoi.  Next to the mausoleum,  you can buy a ticket to visit the place where President Ho Chi Minh use to live and work.

reviews.author: BellBoy53
reviews.title: Solemn Experience
reviews.content: Our morning visit to see inside the Mausoleum and view Ho Chi Minh in state was all done in well under an hour (out before 10am). Despite the long line consisting of locals and visiting local military personnel, it kept moving smoothly, it never felt crowded, and so we moved through quickly. There is a respectful dress code and no photography. Visiting the nearby gardens and Ho Chi Minh Museum add to the experience and knowledge.

reviews.author: Anna
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Musolem,HaNoi
reviews.content: It is a sacred place for the Vietnamese people and world tourists in general. The surrounding landscape is solemn but also poetic and full of love

reviews.author: arthur S
reviews.title: H Chi Minh
reviews.content: Very interesting and educational having an Australian back ground . It is part of our both country's history..........

reviews.author: Fred M
reviews.title: A Solemn Tribute to Vietnamese History
reviews.content: This symbol of Vietnamese independence really touched us. The solemn atmosphere and respect of the local visitors were palpable. We were fascinated by the imposing architecture and the guard of honor. Don’t miss to understand the soul of modern Vietnam.

reviews.author: Scenic26291367848
reviews.title: A true patriotic symbol of Vietnam
reviews.content: We were struck by the solemn atmosphere and the reverence shown by locals and tourists alike. The imposing structure houses the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh, Vietnam's revolutionary leader. We learned about his significant role in the country's history and independence. The mausoleum's strict rules and meticulous maintenance reflect its status as a national treasure. It's an educational experience that offers insight into Vietnam's cultural and political landscape.

reviews.author: Jean Dupont
reviews.title: A Solemn Tribute to the Heart of Hanoi
reviews.content: This impressive monument, dedicated to Uncle Ho, offers a peaceful atmosphere despite its historical importance. The imposing architecture and the guard of honour ceremony create an atmosphere of profound respect. We enjoyed the order and tranquility that prevails in the complex. The surrounding garden adds a touch of serenity to the whole. For couples interested in Vietnamese history, this site is unmissable.

reviews.author: Alessandro
reviews.title: Striking building
reviews.content: Striking building externally and internally. The room with the body is clearly very cold and with low lighting. It's very reminiscent of Lenin's. Before you can get there there is a long walk to do. Luckily we didn't find a big line

reviews.author: Dr Kulkarni Mohina S
reviews.title: Monument of honor
reviews.content: This mausoleum reminds us of personal sacrifice..goal and human struggle for independence. Open square for parade helps to do reflective thinking. A must visit

reviews.author: lucycan
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: This was really cool.  Stand in line for (if you are lucky) about 30 min and go in and see Ho Chi Minh in his final resting place.  He looks great for being dead for 70 years!

reviews.author: dawn3103
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Might be classed as a little morbid, but the Vietnamese have so much respect for him and so he could be with his people and they can still see him, his body is preserved in a glass case and once a year the people embark on paying their respect to him. We had to queue but the guards have it all under control and everyone is more than happy to wait their turn. We queued for about 45 mins in total.

reviews.author: Stephanie M
reviews.title: Unique way to experience Vietnamese history
reviews.content: Interesting way to learn more about Vietnamese history and the story of Ho Chi Minh. We really liked the museum at the mausoleum and would highly recommend getting a free tour guide, they are very knowledgeable and great to learn from.

reviews.author: Kirikouette
reviews.title: A site to do when you are in Hanoi
reviews.content: Tour scheduled by our agency from outside the mausoleum with our Guide. What to do when you are in Hanoi to understand Vietnamese history. Impressive site for its size and architecture. Around there are temples to visit. Attention extremely guarded site, security device at the entrance.

reviews.author: Govi
reviews.title: Hot sultry and full of people
reviews.content: Stopover more than useless, horrible Soviet-style building not very different from our fascist monuments, you can not do anything, you can not take pictures, monstrous queue, guards staring at you and whistling at all those who handle the cellphone, in front of a useless square all fenced.

reviews.author: ellen m
reviews.title: Mausoleum close in connection with renovation Museum was nice to visit
reviews.content: Too bad the mausoleum is closed due to a renovation but the museum was very nice to admire. We also saw the changing of the guard

reviews.author: OHKSO
reviews.title: Open-top bus circuit
reviews.content: At first, I was going to try to get into the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, but to be honest, I gave up because I didn't have that much passion. But when I got on the open-top bus, I passed by on the circuit course and was able to see the huge buildings, only from the car. It gave me a mixed impression that the bodies were actually laid to rest so that I could see them.

reviews.author: woodfamily2013
reviews.title: Uncle Ho
reviews.content: We went very early as it was extremely hot . Did have to queue for a long time . However the line kept moving . As we entered the resting place of Ho Chi Minh it was darker and cooler . I was told off for talking loud to my wife by a guard . However upon reflection realised it was in fact disrespectful . As we walked (shuffled) past his body both of us found it very intense and moving . Would definitely recommend this to anyone as a ""do not miss""

reviews.author: Yvonne S
reviews.title: A clone environment as compared to the Mausoleum of Mau in China
reviews.content: The Mausoleum grounds is where in September 1945 that Ho Chi Minh read Vietnam’s Declaration of Independence, and it’s here today that the national leader’s body rests within a massive granite mausoleum.  In his speech back in 1954 Ho used quotes out of the preamble of the US constitution to set the pace of getting rid of the French, who had moved back into Vietnam following the Japanese occupation during WW II, and where the country was split in two at the 19 th parallel (communist influence from Russia in the North and wester influence in the South). This area of the Mausoleum is somewhat like what we observed a few years back in Tiananmen Square in Beijing China with Charman Mau’s mausoleum, with a big national flag, and a single military guard under the flag.  Here in Vietnam, there was no solders standing under the national flag, but there were sure a lot of Soldiers at the Mausoleum entrance and posted around his body.We had to check our cameras (as no pictures are allowed inside the mausoleum).  You must remove your hat, and have your knees and shoulders covered, plus no sunglasses (all as a position of respect to the country’s former leader).The line to view the body of Ho Chi Minh, was very / VERY long (well over 1000), but we received a VIP pass and jumped right into the middle of the line.  The Mausoleum is closed on Mondays, and we were originally scheduled to stop here yesterday, but our great guide Henry just swapped the schedule.The setting of the body is very elegant of a well-preserved person.    Originally, Uncle Hoe had requested to be cremated and his ashes scattered over the waters, but following his passing in 1969, the government decided to display his body, as a symbol of the inspiration of a simplistic, modest educated gentleman that had inspired his nation to throw off the yoke of colonialism.The government wanted the body to be preserved like Lenin in Moscow and Mao Zedong in China, and thus approached the Russians for help.  The Chinees did not want the Russians to help as the Chinese and Vietnamese were at odds AGAINST one another, so the body was moved rom cave to cave until the Russians finally preformed the cosmetic preservation.After viewing the guards, flowers, the body of Uncle Ho (no pictures allowed), we continued to the Prudential Palace next door to the Mausoleum; viewing the massive building, and the plush grounds around it.  As part of the grounds, we viewed where Uncle Ho lived on the grounds in a masonry building during the war with a bomb shelter and underground tunnel over to the Citadel where communications to the arms was sent out.  After the war he moved into a stilt house on the grounds until his passing.

reviews.author: FredoG11
reviews.title: Impressive filling
reviews.content: The mausoleum is currently closed, but the whole area is impressively beautiful and revealing . It provides a deep insight into the history of this proud people and their Uncle Ho.

reviews.author: Callmeducnguyen
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: It's better to have a guide to understand who Ho Chi Minh was and what he had done to Vietnam and how did he get so respected here rather than the fact he was a communist leader.Ho Chi Minh was humble but seeing the way guards there doing just disturbing me so much.The toilet is disgusting in this important area???

reviews.author: Axbridgemum
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh died September 2 1969
reviews.content: Honestly worth the very long queue. Very respectful shuffle past Uncle Ho's  body was unexpectedly moving, perhaps because he still commands such reverence from the very old to the youngest citizens of this unique country. The mausoleum is now closed until August 12 for his body to be 'maintained'

reviews.author: Onas
reviews.title: Imposing from the outside
reviews.content: Very imposing building from the outside. makes beautiful photos. Inside it is a little disappointing. We are guided to where Ho Chi Minh's body is. You can't take photos.

reviews.author: Ludo V
reviews.title: impressive but not very elegant
reviews.content: A mastodon-like gray structure is Ho Chi Minh's final resting place. Although he had expressed the wish to be cremated to save costs, the government decided to build this mausoleum for him. His body lies in state there, mumified by Russian specialists. It is flown to Russia twice a year for maintenance.The architects saw a lotus flower in their design. In my opinion, this requires a lot of imagination. We were lucky to experience the changing of the guard. A visit to the refrigerated room was not an option for us.

reviews.author: iayzit2
reviews.title: Must visit the Mousoleum
reviews.content: Must visit site! It is in Old Quarter and walking distance from any hotels you stay in this area. When we were there in early May 2024, the entrance was free. Usually, entrance fee is very minimal.

reviews.author: Dimitris L
reviews.title: Amazing experience.
reviews.content: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is an amazing place. We went there early morning, as it is meant to be open only for a few hours early in the day. The day of our visit was a special one as it fell on a public holiday and thousands of visitors had already lined up by the time we arrived (around 9.00am)! The whole operation was conducted with military precision! Visitors had to line up, single file, and be exactly behind one another! Officials with loudspeakers were in charge. No bags or water could be taken and had to be left in storage for free and collected at exiting. Water fountains could be seen at various spots throughout and cups were provided, however we did not take up this opportunity! It was a very long walk around the whole area before we eventually reached the room with Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body, which was placed in what seemed to be a horse carriage, with his upper body slightly elevated so he could be seen easily by visitors. No photos were allowed to be taken inside. It was only a few seconds of viewing as we had to keep walking. It was very special and a moving moment. The Mausoleum is a beautiful building and photos of the building can be taken from a distance outside. The place is steeped in history and we could sense locals had a deep regard for "Uncle Ho" as they call him.

reviews.author: Marc B
reviews.title: Super Super Busy
reviews.content: The mausoleum itself is impressive to look at but you have to wait about 3 hours to get inside. The other stuff in the park isn't particularly impressive and just not worth the investment of time. When I went it was super super busy, disgustingly so, which may have negatively impacted my view. I would advise people to skip this attraction if you are short on time in Hanoi. If you have the time or really want to go just have a look at mausoleum from the outside, do a quick lap around the park, and get out of there. Don't bother entering any of the paid attractions like the house or museum.

reviews.author: Graham S
reviews.title: If you are in Hanoi this is a must
reviews.content: Wildly busy at weekends and closed Monday and Friday so we went for the opening time of 0730 on Tuesday morning (it’s only open 0730-1100 in summer). The queue was about 200 yards long. Predictably, everything ran like clockwork and we were moved forward to the door just before 0730. We were divided into two adjacent lines (tip: left-hand line is closer to the body). Total silence, guards everywhere, in you walk, keep moving, no photos and out by 0738. Amazing. And it’s free.Then into the stilt house (40000VND) and out by 0800. We didn’t bother with the HCM museum.Shock! When we left there was no queue at all so we could have had another 30 minutes in bed.Make sure you are dressed appropriately; no uncovered shoulders and no knees showing.Another freebie that we enjoyed was the lowering of the flag at 2100. Get there at 2045. You can also see the raising of the flag at 0600.

reviews.author: Felix F
reviews.title: History before your eyes
reviews.content: A piece of history! Went on a sunday when nearly all Vietnamese coming to see the founder of their current nation. Very interesting.

reviews.author: WanderingWilbur
reviews.title: Ignore the queues: its the best managed attraction I have been to!
reviews.content: I would just say that this is well worth a visit for a sense of history and the legend that is interwoven in the culture of this country. Plus, being communist, its free....If the queue looks ENORMOUS when you get there, take heart! It is so well managed by a plethora of police and military, that it takes so much less time than you may initially think. It took us 45 minutes, from halfway down the road outside of the start of the queue to being in the mausoleum itself. And when you emerge, staff are on hand to offer free water and snacks! Who would have thought?

reviews.author: George Severin
reviews.title: A monumental facility
reviews.content: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a large memorial dedicated to the former Vietnamese leader Ho Chi Minh. The monumental building was built in the style of the Lenin Mausoleum in Moscow. There is a large area around the mausoleum that is monitored by the military. You enter the area after strict controls and regulations (such as dress code). When we got there, entry was no longer permitted. Therefore, we looked at this monument outside the area. If you are already in Hanoi, you should visit this mausoleum.

reviews.author: Peter B
reviews.title: Interestingly sureal.
reviews.content: Had always wanted to visit Ho Chi Minhs Mausoleum. First time we tried it was a Sunday, don't try on a Sunday totally packed ques massive. Finally got there on a Tuseday as they close on Monday's. Super sureal. Its free to enter and the ques though longish move well. Once you are in the Mausoleum its a 30 second walk past to view Ho Chi Minh, but surprisingly satisfying, in a strange way.  Be respectful in what you wear, plenty of info on do's and don'ts.

reviews.author: pieter
reviews.title: Confusing opening hours.
reviews.content: The opening hours of the Mausoleum are a bit confusing. We thought it was until 11 o'clock in the morning, but already at 10.20 o'clock we could no longer visit the mausoleum. After a 40 minute wait we were able to view the square in front of the Mausoleum and the house where he lived. You will be strictly checked (backpack had to go through the scanner).

reviews.author: Mie R
reviews.title: Sooooooooo impresive
reviews.content: I visited this destination at night and i was a great place to refresh some cool breeze, i do love the massive and green square grass. Next time I will visit it on daylight to have a chance to come in to the mausolem....

reviews.author: dianedinky
reviews.title: A bit strange
reviews.content: First off, the tomb is within a large complex so there is more to see than just the body of Uncle Ho.  And the surrounding area with the Palace, Gardens, Ho House, Pagoda etc is great for a visit.I titled this visit strange as it is a weird experience for a tourist.  Ho Chi Minh is revered by all of Vietnam so a serious and solemn event to be in this place.  As a Western tourist his reputation is not so golden so he didn't have that aura for me.  I also am not convinced it is his body preserved that you see.  He looks remarkably young considering when he died and even with the body being removed for a few months to Russia for 'maintenance'.  It could actually be a Lenin looky-likey in there...Glad I can say I was there but the security guards are very strict and too much for me.Note that the complex had many gift shops but they basically all just sell Vietnamese flag t-shirts or plates with Ho's face painted on.  Which was a bit of a let down.

reviews.author: Julian S
reviews.title: A moment of reflection
reviews.content: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum was a somber but powerful experience. It offered a chance to learn about Vietnam's history and pay respect to a revered leader.

reviews.author: F M
reviews.title: Great Vietnam History
reviews.content: The grounds are large and well maintained and entry through security was pretty quick despite the number of people (went around 11am). Because of the size of the grounds, you never feel crowded. Read up  on the history of the mausoleum and Ho Chi Minh beforehand if you aren't going with a tour guide who can give you the info.

reviews.author: Niko
reviews.title: A long wait for a disappointing glimpse
reviews.content: The line to see Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum was ridiculously long, and the viewing itself was a quick, underwhelming experience. We felt rushed and couldn't appreciate the historical significance. There are better ways to learn about Vietnam's past.

reviews.author: Otto
reviews.title: A respectful visit
reviews.content: We paid our respects at the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. The somber atmosphere reminded us of Vietnam's historic struggles. A place to learn and appreciate the sacrifices made for Vietnamese independence.

reviews.author: Ellen M
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: If you want to visit inside the mausoleum and see Ho Chi Minh, you have to go in the morning. Problem is, that's when thousands and thousands of school children also go. We estimated we'd have to stand in line in the hot sun for about 3 hours to get in. Instead, we returned and visited the external grounds in the afternoon and it was peaceful and lovely. Worth a visit for the architecture, culture, and history.

reviews.author: LolaGo1
reviews.title: Feeling grateful that I was able to enter it before leaving Hanoi
reviews.content: Through Booking.com , I was able to book a walking tour with a  Vietnamese college student. Cost for this service was only for $5.00. Entrance to the Complex is quite restrict. We had to leave our backpack, handbags and personal stuffs at the Entrance Lockers. We were ushered in walkways that have roofs before entering the Mausoleum. Security Guards kept reminding us NOT to  take photos and keep moving. The body is an enclosed glass compartment,  with 4 guards standing around it. There are more security guards along the way. In the wide, open space infront of the mausoleum were several groups of school children who also visited the Mausoeleum. Other attractions in the Complex include the HCM Museum, Pagoda Shrine, Gardens,  Palace (closed during my visit). Recommended to visit them as well.Note: Visiting days and hours to the Mausoleum are limited. Entrance is FREE, consult with the locals regarding their opening and closing hours.Picture- taking at the other attractions in the Complex is allowed, NOT just inside the Mausoleum!

reviews.author: Elsa D
reviews.title: must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: One of the tourist attraction in Hanoi. The place is magnificent. I did not visit inside because it was already noon (closed by 11 am). The next morning we saw the lines of people wanting to get there, my tour guide said it takes 2 hours in line to get inside. We took nice pictures just outside

reviews.author: arpitam
reviews.title: Salute to the great leader
reviews.content: If in Hanoi this is a place to pay a visit. The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is located in the Ho Chi Minh complex, a luxuriantly large and beautiful esplanade. I was unfortunate to have landed up on a Monday (Mon & Fri closed) but had the opportunity to watch the daily morning parade.

reviews.author: The-Mong-Melbourne-Australia
reviews.title: A couple of tips for you
reviews.content: 10 April 2023, the mausoleum itself is still closed, so you can’t get to see, nor file past Uncle Ho’s body…. Do you have to queue to get through security, and at 1 pm on a Thursday we wait about 20 minutes so no major drama. You do NOT need to have identification so you don’t need to carry a passport like we did. Importantly, females (women not kids as far as I’m aware) have to have their shoulders covered so at minimum a T-shirt and also the knees covered or you certainly can’t wear tight shorts. If you do, they will not let you in. That said some random dudes offer to sell you scarves to cover your shoulders if you don’t have something appropriate. Whilst you can’t go into the mausoleum itself it is worthwhile having a look at Ho Chi Minh’s Stills house and other buildings on the site, you do not need to prepay you can purchase a ticket after entering security at the internal gate to get into the building area …40,000VND to get in and will take you approximately one hour or so to have a good look around, and you certainly are beautiful place so it is well worth while doing.

reviews.author: RoverP
reviews.title: A good insight into a powerful but humble leader
reviews.content: This is an experience not to be missed.  It is certainly very interesting but it would be a push to call it excellent.  You can only go so close to the Mausoleum itself.  The scale of the building and the security certainly reflect the esteem in which Ho-Chi-Minh is held by the Vietnamese people.  The mausoleum dominates an absolutely massive square which is devoid of any other structure.  It looks across the square to the National Assembly building as if the great leader is checking that current day leaders are not betraying the revolution.Also on the site and in much more attractive surrounds are the yellow walled official presidential residence (which Ho only used for official business) and two much more humble dwellings which Ho actually lived and worked in.  You can't go in, but you can get a good look in through glass frontages.  A good insight into a leader of the people for the people.

reviews.author: Chris318i
reviews.title: Arbitrarily selection of visitors
reviews.content: We were not allowed to enter the mausoleum, because our youngest son was too young (ten month old). The "official rule" is that kids under three are not allowed to enter the mausoleum. I'm ok with that rule, but it should be applied to all families then. Several families waiting with us brought kids below the age of three. When I asked the staff why some are allowed to go in and some not, they made up new rules. First additional rule, it's too cold for our kid. Second additional rule, the kid needs to be able to walk on its own. We were not the only ones that had to stay out. I'm really ok if there are clear rules, but from my point of view, the staff arbitrarily selects who is allowed to go in and who needs to stay out. In the end we visited the mausoleum only from the outside.

reviews.author: Людмила Пластинина
reviews.title: tribute and history
reviews.content: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum in Hanoi is a memorable and poignant experience. The mausoleum, which is an iconic monument, has deep spiritual significance for the Vietnamese people. Inside, a solemn atmosphere and an aura of respect surround the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh.A strict dress code must be followed and respect for the location must be maintained. Be prepared to queue as the mausoleum is a popular attraction. A visit to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is not just a tourist activity. This is an opportunity to bear witness to a historical figure and pay tribute to a leader who left an indelible mark on Vietnam's history.

reviews.author: Asden D
reviews.title: Excellent But Time Consuming
reviews.content: The mausoleum is of great historic and social importance to the people of Vietnam, which in our opinion makes it well worth a visit.   However, it is worth being aware that the lines can be extremely long and it may take up to several hours to get to the inside of the mausoleum. We weren’t aware of this and visited around 8.30 am on a Sunday without having had any breakfast and it was 11 am by the time we finished seeing the mausoleum - we didn’t end up seeing the presidential place, museum, or the stilt house because we were too tired at the end of it/didn’t have the time. The time spent in the mausoleum is about 5 minutes. Our advise is don’t skip your breakfast/cuppa, come prepared to stand in the sun for few hours, and make sure you have sufficient time if you want to see everything in the complex.

reviews.author: Barrie W
reviews.title: A Must Visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: A respectful memorial to the leader who unified the nation. Amazing legacy: overcoming foreign control. Highly revered now and an important place for understanding today’s Viet Nam.

reviews.author: Daniel K
reviews.title: Just stay away and leave the dead alone.
reviews.content: We were not impressed, it was a lot of employees who were angry and did not bother to help us. They gave us more, wrong information and wasted our time. I would recommend doing something else. Or get out of town as soon as possible. Definitely the city we least liked being in.

reviews.author: SEALS
reviews.title: I wanted to see the changing of the guard.
reviews.content: I visited on a tour of Hanoi city. I was told that there would be a long queue, but I entered through the gate and walked along the long corridor without stopping, and entered the huge building where Ho Chi Minh's body was kept in a refrigerated container, guarded by many guards. I was told that stopping, taking pictures, and talking were prohibited inside the building. Most of the people in line looked like they were Vietnamese. I wanted to see the changing of the guard.

reviews.author: Angelo M
reviews.title: Ok
reviews.content: This was ok.  Nothing exciting but if you’re a history buff you might enjoy this. Keep in mind you can’t go in here wearing shorts. We tried to and were turned away and then had to buy some dead sexy pants from a street vendor so we could get in.

reviews.author: m2347m
reviews.title: Preservation is amazing!
reviews.content: Visited in March. The weather was perfect. Was warm but not hot.  Lot's of people and school children but the lines go fast so dont let that intimate you. The lines stop at 11AM as it closes by 11:30AM. Closed Monday and Friday.Amazing how well preserved this guy is.  Is it plastination? Is it a wax figure? Who knows but word is he is taken to Russia for touch ups every year.  Has Russia found the fountain of youth for the dead?

reviews.author: Alessandro S
reviews.title: Too many people
reviews.content: The mausoleum of Ho Chi Min who was president from 1945 until his death in 1969 is definitely a destination worth visiting. There is a long queue to do some kind of check at the metal detector. They put my camera in a red bag.We pay the ticket 40,000 Dong each. The guards have a particular all-white uniform because on Saturdays and Tuesdays there is a kind of special ceremony. the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a complex that includes the monumental tomb, the house, the Presidential Palace and the Museum dedicated to Ho Chi Minh. It is now considered a sacred place for all Vietnamese.The complex was built in the period from 1973 to 1975

reviews.author: LondonFamily88
reviews.title: The queues move quickly
reviews.content: We are glad we had a  guide when we visited in order to navigate the security and adhere to the strict deferential protocols. The queues appear long, however, move swiftly, particularly in the mausoleum. This is on the list of things to do in Hanoi, and certainly, there was lots of respect and reverence by the Vietnamese visitors.

reviews.author: Henry E
reviews.title: A beacon of history and inspiration
reviews.content: The detailed sculptures were an inspiring sight, each one meticulously maintained. The mausoleum stands as a testament to the resilience and spirit of the Vietnamese people. A visit to this iconic landmark is a must for any solo traveler seeking to delve deeper into the rich tapestry of Vietnam’s past.

reviews.author: Angeles Echevarria
reviews.title: YOU ONLY ENTER ESCORTED IN A GROUP. WITH SOLDIERS
reviews.content: The entire complex is escorted with very young soldiers dressed in white uniforms. We visit the place where the embalmed corpse of Ho Chi Min called Tio Ho is. Some Russians embalmed it and they check it from time to time.There is a guard inside the mausoleum for 24 hours, they never leave the body alone.It is located where Ho Chi Min had his modest house on stilts that can be visited on one side.

reviews.author: nasser
reviews.title: great leader
reviews.content: It was a fun day, the atmosphere was beautiful, and there was a very wonderful organization on the website to visit this remarkable person and the great leader who led the country to freedom. He deserves all the appreciation, reverence and respect.

reviews.author: DotsGirl2
reviews.title: There is a lot to see here beside the Mausoleum
reviews.content: Be prepared for long lines. They do move pretty quickly. The mausoleum is based on one in Russia. Basically you go into a cooled building and file past Ho Chi Minh’s body. The interesting part is seeing how much he is loved and revered by his people. When you come out you can see the Presidential Palace he refused to live in. Then go to house no 54 where he did live  for 4 years, which is basically the servants quarters for the presidential palace. Then you can go through the stilt house that he lived in for the remainder of his life.

reviews.author: BrakiWorldTraveler
reviews.title: Inform yourself if you want to see Mr. HCM body
reviews.content: This was my second visit to Hanoi, however both times I didn't manage to see Mr. Ho Chi Minh's body in his Mausoleum, but was around in front and on other sites around the complex.So basically, you're reading tips from a traveler who didn't make it inside, but for sure will next time :-) HCM Mausoleum is within a huge space with several another sites.When entering the area you pass an airport style security check. After that you can roam freely exploring the area. You need around 2 hours min for that, excluding the Mausoleum, which visit length depends on the queueing line.Besides the Mausoleum within the complex is the Presidential Palace, One Pillar Pagoda, HCM stilt house and a Museum (small entry fees for the latter two).People here review and post pics of all these together, but I'll focus on the Mausoleum, while others you can read in respective reviews.My previous visit in 2017 was during some Vietnam holidays, so the waiting line in front was very long, some 2+ hours as I was told by police, so I gave up.This year, in Jan 2024 I put it high on my to do list saving our last day only for that.Unfortunately, I did not know the Mausoleum is NOT open every day. It's open only 4 days a week and some of these days only 8-11 AM. So, inform yourself beforehand if you want to enter it and see Mr. HCM body.All other attractions on the premises are open every day, so you still have plenty to visit.

reviews.author: JanAarup
reviews.title: A tourist attraction in an authentic city
reviews.content: The rush of history alone makes the mausoleum and the surrounding area worth a visit.However, you probably don't go to Hanoi just to visit this.There are many other things that draw in a tourist experience that is much more authentic than the norm

reviews.author: Lori M
reviews.title: don't miss - very respectful and tastefully executed
reviews.content: this was special to visit... HCM is preserved with so much dignity and reverence. the line is long but it moves very fast.

reviews.author: Trevor N
reviews.title: Recommend going with a guide
reviews.content: Definitely need a guide to explain the significance of Ho Chi Minh to the Vietnamese people as there’s no information boards or other materials. We were lucky to visit when the guard was changing, otherwise not really a lot to see. One lady in our party was wearing shorts and had to ‘hire’ a skirt from a vendor near the security gate otherwise she wasn’t going to be allowed in.

reviews.author: Shannon
reviews.title: Strange
reviews.content: Large square with a security entrance into it. Keep in mind the restricted area markings, it's easy to miss as it's marked along the ground on footpaths. Recommend coming when they raise the flag but other than that this site is pretty odd.

reviews.author: sydneysider48
reviews.title: Monument to an important world figure
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh’s embalmed body lies in state in this monumental building, set in the middle of a large, manicured square. While the lines to enter are long, the organisation is excellent and they move very quickly, directed by smartly uniformed guards who ensure that visitors behave with dignity (no hands in pockets, sunglasses or talking etc) in the presence of the remains of this important figure in world history. Many Vietnamese were clearly moved in the presence of their country’s revered founder.

reviews.author: Dave Smith
reviews.title: Millions of Vietnamese can’t be wrong?
reviews.content: There was a huge queue, lots of school children, but it moved quickly. Millions of Vietnamese make the journey to see Ho Chi Minh lying in state, so thought why not. Security is airport style, and there is a strict dress code, don’t wear shorts! If you have a camera, you will be given a canvas bag and told to hand it in before you enter the mausoleum (weird they don’t take your phone off you as they have cameras?) You are guided to the entrance by immaculately dressed guards who will also advise you to take your hat / sunglasses off / hands out your pockets etc. as you enter the only sound is feet on the ground, as you enter the viewing room the carpet sucks up the sound, silence reigns, and there lies the main man. You file past and exit to pick up your camera on the other side of the building. You’re then free to visit the museum (Vietnamese go free, but everyone else has to pay (around £1), lots to see and a couple of gift shops as well. If you’re visiting Hanoi, you should go.

reviews.author: kohechin
reviews.title: Appearance only
reviews.content: I visited on a tour, so I only got to see the exterior. The guard was changing at that time, so I was able to take photos. Unfortunately, it was cloudy, so I think I could have taken better photos if it had been sunny. If I have the opportunity to visit again, I would definitely like to visit at a time when you can see the inside.

reviews.author: Merlin Alejo
reviews.title: Majestic
reviews.content: It looks great but the air around it was so polluted from the traffics. The building itself looks stunning and really shows the landmark of Vietnam

reviews.author: Steve B
reviews.title: Uncle Ho.
reviews.content: Incredible experience. Strangely moving.Our tour of the mausoleum was made all the better thanks to Huyen out tour guide. Her knowledge of Uncle Ho and his life was second to none. Thank you Huyen for spending the time with us and educating us. Every days a school day!!!

reviews.author: mandy l
reviews.title: Unusual experience
reviews.content: A very interesting experience unlike any can have in the uk. Must do it if u have time, we were fortunate and went in January so no crowds. Not sure we believe it is his real body but the respect given to uncle Ho is unbelievable given the time lapse from his death.

reviews.author: Dan Sullivan
reviews.title: Good stop on the Hanoi tourist route
reviews.content: We visited on a Saturday and managed to see the body of Ho Chi Minh which is preserved here. Very strange experience but worth it. Get there early to avoid queues as it’s only open certain hours and these are limited.

reviews.author: Shruti Pramod Reddy
reviews.title: Historical
reviews.content: Visited here on the morning of Dec-22,2023 & saw the change of guard ceremony too (apparently height requirement for men is 175cm)Also saw his living quarters such as the house on stilts, his rooms like dining, living rooms and the cars he used etc. Nice pond and bridge in the central area.Didn't get to see his preserved actual dead body though.

reviews.author: JJ Montinola
reviews.title: Viva Uncle Ho
reviews.content: When in Hanoi Vietnam, never fail to pay homage to the Uncle of the Country by visiting Ho Chi Mihn's Moseleum. The truest tribute to such a distinguished individual and continuing inspiration to his people

reviews.author: Filiz Baltacı
reviews.title: Mausoleum of a national hero who spent his life for the freedom of the Vietnamese
reviews.content: The mausoleum of Ho Chi Ming, the national hero of the Vietnamese, a palace built by the French during the colonial period, and the outbuilding where Ho Chi Ming, who refused to live in this palace after independence, stayed in the same garden and grew different plants in the huge garden around it, are among the places to visit.

reviews.author: Leatherlion
reviews.title: You are in a dictatorship and here you realize it
reviews.content: Visiting this monument you realize something that you don't notice in the rest of the city and the nation: that you are in a dictatorship! You queue and they shout at you if you go a millimeter out of the queue, they shout at you if you turn your head behind you and don't look forward, if you stop for a second longer than necessary, they take your hat off your head and take their hands away badly from your pockets when you enter the room where Ho Chi Minh's mummy is. All the soldiers are mean and frowning. I don't know if the hero of the Vietnam War would have wanted all this, but you really understand the weight of dictatorship in the life and society of men. Bad experience from this point of view.

reviews.author: Nilmini D
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh, The Great Leader of Vietnam is sleeping here
reviews.content: We visited Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum in the evening of the same day we arrived in Hanoi. It is open from 5.00 pm to 10 pm.  It was the winter in Hanoi I suppose since we felt quite cold. There were thousand of tourists hanging around this place. It is nicely maintained. I think the Vietnamese people give due respect and show their gratitude to the leader who lead them to win the war.

reviews.author: Seaside25841925893
reviews.title: A sacred place worth visiting
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum, located in the center of Hanoi, is an extremely impressive and sacred historical site. With unique architecture, the mausoleum provides a solemn and respectful space, expressing the Vietnamese people's deep respect for President Ho Chi Minh.Visiting the mausoleum is a solennel experience, from moving in the long walkway lined with lush green trees, to entering the mausoleum space with ceremony and gratitude. The President Ho Chi Minh Museum next to the mausoleum helps visitors gain a deeper understanding of the President's life and career.In addition to its historical aspect, the mausoleum is also a place of cultural exchange, attracting international and foreign tourists to visit. Here, people often feel the solemnity and gratitude of an entire nation.Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum is not only a destination for Vietnamese people but also a symbol with global significance, expressing respect and gratitude to an outstanding leader.

reviews.author: Hằng
reviews.title: The trip back to Uncle Ho's Mausoleum - sacred and proud.
reviews.content: The atmosphere is very solemn and ancient. All tourists seriously follow the regulations of this sacred place.I was able to participate and witness two wonderful moments: Flag raising and Flag loweringI feel very happy and sacred.

reviews.author: SF Guy
reviews.title: Must Visit
reviews.content: When I visited I only wanted to remain on the outside but when you arrive and go through security screening you are placed in a group and guided through the mausoleum that holds the well preserved body of the great Ho Chi Minh. It was a good experience and I recommend.

reviews.author: swings
reviews.title: Great Site
reviews.content: Amazing place, not to be missed.  Luckily not too busy when we went but guide said normally long queues.

reviews.author: HMKaren
reviews.title: Worth a quick visit
reviews.content: We figured a trip to Hanoi would not be complete without seeing Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum, so we had a look. The streets around it are closed off, so our Grab driver dropped us off a couple blocks away and we walked over. It was nothing very exciting, but it didn't take much time either. We didn't go inside---we didn't want to be bothered with the dress code or the line. I wouldn't make this one a high priority, but I'm glad we saw it.

reviews.author: Michelle B
reviews.title: No go
reviews.content: Came heren, it was stil closed.Came back after one hour and suddenly i wasnt dressed properly. My shoulders had to be covered.I bought a scarf around the corner nobody could see my arms and shoulders anymore. But the unfriendly men said it was stil not good enough while i saw people entering with the same scarf wrapt around their body.Went back to the sales man, bought a T-shirt and went back AGAIN. And now the rude men starts complaining about the short jeans of my husband, hè didnt say a word about this before!!! This all happend within 5 minutes so he knew what he said before. Very rude very unfriendly never come back would not recommend going here. They treath you like a criminal

reviews.author: Marina M
reviews.title: Mausoleum of Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: I didn’t get into the mausoleum, unfortunately ;( you need to find out the schedule. You are allowed into the territory in clothes with long sleeves, or take a scarf to cover your shoulders and arms, short shorts are also not allowed. I liked the museum, the entrance costs 40,000. There is also small temple. Lots of souvenir shops, cafes.

reviews.author: 137liz
reviews.title: Visit to Mausoleum ruined by taxi scam at exit.
reviews.content: Interesting to walk around the tomb and explore the gardens / surrounding buildings.  Got a bit confused about the one way system.Extremely bad experience when leaving.  Beware taxi scammers waiting outside the exit for the unwary.  The authorities need to deal better with taxi scams as they seem commonplace.

reviews.author: Garfieldluvr
reviews.title: Must See in Hanoi
reviews.content: A must see while you are in Hanoi. We did not go inside, just stopped by the see the outside. A very impressive mausoleum.

reviews.author: James N
reviews.title: Get there before 10.30am
reviews.content: Worth it. Be aware it says it closes at 11.30am but that really means 10.50am. And it's closed two days each week. Go early.

reviews.author: Christine
reviews.title: First place to visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: This was the first place I visited in Hanoi. It took about 2 hours of walking. You will first visit the main mausoleum, followed by the stilt house, fish pond, one pillar pagoda, and finally Ho Chi Minh Museum.

reviews.author: André K
reviews.title: Not interesting
reviews.content: Look very impressive with the big open grounds in front of it and the ceremonial guards standing guard. If history is your thing then this maybe of interest. For me it was not very interesting.

reviews.author: r2thebizel
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum: Special
reviews.content: When you take in the magnitude of what this 1 man means to these people, this is a very special place. Go between 07:00 and 10:30 as otherwise you cannot enter. Free but very strict, organised, no photos, you follow a path, there is no waiting inside but you will see his preserved body, almost glowing. The path takes you out to the stilt house and the pagoda is not far from the exit.

reviews.author: lnswest
reviews.title: A must see as Ho Chi Minh body is there
reviews.content: The Vietnam government did this as if they never did anything wrong during the war. How ever there is a lot of interesting pictures , information and Ho  Ho Minh’s body laying in state

reviews.author: Coopper29
reviews.title: Don’t miss this
reviews.content: This is a magnificent monument to the old leader of the country, everything is immaculate and a vast open area with fine gardens, well worth a visit.

reviews.author: maughams
reviews.title: A must-have
reviews.content: A dive into the contemporary history of Vietnam. A tribute to the father of the nation. We learn little there. Attention ladies, bring "a decent outfit", women's knees must not be visible, a police officer checks and refuses the recalcitrant who are reduced to buying pants either from street vendors or in shops a little further away, cheaper. As you leave, the street vendor offers you to buy the pants at half price.

reviews.author: Waterend
reviews.title: Interesting but not a ‘must visit’
reviews.content: Not much more than an interesting memorial to Ho Chi Minh. It’s one to ‘tick off’ when visiting Hanoi provided the queues to get in aren’t ridiculous. Fascinating to see the cross section of people - Vietnamese nationals and foreign tourists who visit and their differing reactions.

reviews.author: Loud1Canberra
reviews.title: A must do
reviews.content: Really a must see, not just for the sight of Ho Chi Minh but the setting with the grand parade ground, the guards, the wreath laying and the general sight of  the variety of visitors. We were lucky as it only took about 10 minutes to get into the Mausoleum.Definitely take the time to go to the parade ground and watch the crowds.

reviews.author: orrdin
reviews.title: Interesting but not a must see
reviews.content: Long lines and a long walk to see the actual body of Ho Chi Min - interesting experience but not a must see. Expect to spend over an hour here.

reviews.author: Ryan C
reviews.title: If you're tall prepare to duck your head when waiting in line outside
reviews.content: Early in the morning at 5 am it was illuminated with red light. In the evening on the first day I arrived and there was a pathway that people liked to walk around on. There is a yellow painted line that visitors are not allowed to cross. Avoid using your selfie stick here outside the masoleum. Although there is no sign indicating this, but the guards will tell you no and indicate you are not allowed to use one. Of course inside you're not allowed to take pictures. You'll walk through the masoleum and be able to view Ho Chi Minh. Leave your hands to your sides. Don't wear glasses or sunglasses on top of your head.

reviews.author: Κλωνη
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: Very impressive, to enter I had a lot of difficulty because I was wearing Bermuda shorts and it was not allowed, I bought a skirt from a street vendor and entered not the Mausoleum, but outside the Mausoleum, where Ho Chi Minh was kept.

reviews.author: EndlessTravels
reviews.title: Closed when we visited but worth a walk past
reviews.content: The mausoleum was closed to the public at time of our visit but was still worth a look while in hanoi. Be aware that it’s heavily guarded and they don’t appreciate you walking over the boundary line

reviews.author: MizuhoK
reviews.title: Heart of Hanoi
reviews.content: We visited here in late afternoon. So we didn’t see the dead body of Ho Chi Minh or natural flag raising at 6AM or flag lowering at 9pm but still we enjoyed the atmosphere. The building of mausoleum of grand, both slogan at left and right deliver strong intentions of the establishment of the country. The square is so vast that we imagine the people who have been enthusiastic for listening the speech of independence. Even you don’t enter the mausoleum, you’re asked to be dressed properly. The modern building at the opposite side of mausoleum is the diet. We wish we could come back to see inside of  mausoleum and see the guards exchange.

reviews.author: Laura
reviews.title: No need
reviews.content: At the time we were there, we could only look at the mausoleum from the outside. The dress code had to be correct and you had to go through a baggage check before you were even allowed to go near it.

reviews.author: Akshay Sharma
reviews.title: A tribute to the nation builder
reviews.content: This place holds a unique position in the history as well as geography of Vietnam. Built impressively in an expanding area, it is a must visit place while in Hanoi. It is lit up during the night time which adds beauty to the whole complex.

reviews.author: cramac
reviews.title: Not good experience
reviews.content: I'm writing the review even though I wasn't able to visit the interior. The reason is that at the entrance, during the check, not only did they want to confiscate my lighter but also the pack of cigarettes without returning anything at the exit. I understand that you can't smoke, but this seems excessive to me. Furthermore, it was impossible to visit even the one-column pagoda without going through the same security checkpoint. The visit probably could have been interesting but I decided not to do it for the reason stated above.

reviews.author: Stephanie R
reviews.title: Definitely with a guide
reviews.content: Not very exciting for non-communists or non-Vietnamese, as we don't celebrate the cult of Ho Chi Minh to the same extent; lots of people and quite crowded; if you go, then definitely with a guide to understand the background.

reviews.author: Paulo N
reviews.title: History of Vietnam
reviews.content: Entry to the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum is not permitted and the time I spent standing and observing the place was only worth it because I was accompanied by a Vietnamese guide who knew a lot about the country's history and was able to explain many things to me.

reviews.author: mojeed o
reviews.title: A Reverential Aura with a Hint of Humor: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum in Hanoi
reviews.content: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum in Hanoi was an educational and spiritual experience. The reverential aura and respectful atmosphere created by the place was palpable. Despite the solemnity of the occasion, I couldn't help but be amused by the fact that I was standing in the presence of the embalmed body of a former leader! It was an eye-opening experience that gave me insight into the spiritual significance of the mausoleum and the reverence it holds in Vietnamese culture.

reviews.author: Dipen Nath🎭
reviews.title: Great Leader Mausoleum
reviews.content: The president Ho Chi Minh was burred in this place called Mausoleum, this is main attraction of Hanoi in our tour, there many other important official building nearby the Mausoleum, the beautiful building is surrounded by parade march pass ground.

reviews.author: Frodo_10
reviews.title: Awesome and inspiring
reviews.content: We visited as part of our motorbike tour , dropped off and walked through . Huge monumental business , awe inspiring and to be respected .Great gardens behind to have a cool drink with well kept gardens .

reviews.author: gregsf11
reviews.title: Make sure you go when it's open, and entry point matters.
reviews.content: The line is long, but it moves fast. Very, very solemn and reverent scene inside the mausoleum itself. For the Vietnamese, it's more than about Communism. Ho Chi Minh was their leader in liberation and independence, and he is widely revered. There were people literally crying when we went by. Obviously no photos allowed inside. Outside, however it's entirely different. Hordes of schoolchildren and ordinary folks taking pictures. The kids are eager to meet foreigners, take selfies and practice their English. It's a really festive scene. The best way to do this is to go very early. Both Tripadvisor and Google are wrong about opening times. When I was there it was open 3 days a week, 7:30-10:30 AM only. And it's best to use the museum entrance on the West side and leave your bags there. If you got through the South entrance, they can hold your bags, but you have to rush back before they close that checkpoint at 11AM to get them. That is extremely far out of the way, because generally there is a whole circuit that begins at the museum entrance, goes to the mausoleum, then through the old presidential palace, Ho Chi Minh's stilt house, one pillar pagoda, and back to the museum. The museum is open till 12 and then closes for lunch. You generally can't go backwards on the circuit.

reviews.author: ctm7944
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: HCM Mausoleum (Open 730AM-1030AM) Rode GRAB Motorbike @ 730AM. 20KVND/85 cents charged to my CC. There were 2 different places to leave possessions. One was for cameras (not phone). They gave me a plastic tag. And said the camera will delivered to a pickup point after viewing HCM.At a 2nd place I dropped off my backpack with phone inside. And they gave me another numbered plastic tag. After the viewing; the camera was awaiting me at a nearby pickup point. But, I had to go back to the original dropoff point to retrieve my backpack. Then, went to the HCM Museum.(Open 8AM-Noon).While inline waiting to enter Mausoleum; watched soldiers perform changing of the guard and laying of wreaths, which was interesting.

reviews.author: Mariana Magalhães
reviews.title: Could not visit
reviews.content: Was denied the entry because I was using shorts just above the knee. At the same time there were male tourist inside with shorts the same length.

reviews.author: Shelley M
reviews.title: Dont wear shorts
reviews.content: We had wanted to walk in the square, not so keen to actually go in to be honest.  Seemed a lot of guards around the day we were there, they were all armed which was a bit creepy.  I wasnt allowed to walk in the square because I had shorts on, thought that was a bit strange, but respected the guard and walked around.  It was 36 degrees!

reviews.author: devina1991
reviews.title: Not to miss while in Hanoi
reviews.content: one should  not miss visiting this mausoleum while in hanoi. Went there at 9:00AM and there was not much waiting time to enter the mausoleum.  One is not allowed to carry camera and bags into the mausoleum and need to deposit our belongings in the security office before entering the mausoleum.The entrance is free and the mausoleum is open in the morning and after a break, it is also open in the afternoon, the surrounding gardens are beautiful  and  well  maintained

reviews.author: Keith F
reviews.title: An interesting morning
reviews.content: The museum is only open in the morning and we timed our arrival to beat the queue but it was still a very long wait to enter the mausoleum. The building is quite stark and no bags are allowed. We entered in single file and moved past the body of Uncle Ho (as the locals call him). It was in interesting experience and there were many groups of school children in the queue, all keen to practice their English.

reviews.author: Phi Somchai
reviews.title: Grand architecture
reviews.content: The mausoleum houses the body of Ho Chi Minh, who was a national hero of Vietnam.   When we came here, the mausoleum was closed.  The structure was grand and reminded me of the Acropolis in Greece.We took very nice photos in the open square in front of the structure.

reviews.author: Monica S
reviews.title: Not much to see except a big grey building
reviews.content: Interesting to watch if you arrive there when they change the guard. The place itself does not offer much to look at except a big grey building, and the guards defending it.

reviews.author: Craig R
reviews.title: Vietnam Holiday 2023
reviews.content: It is only open in the morning, and you are not allowed to take anything in with you, no camera or bags. It was closed when we went. It is a very impressive building, and we watched the changing of the Guard at the entrance door while we were there. It is a lovely area to walk around however the attitude of some of the guards, if you ask them for directions needs a bit of adjusting, as it is a tourist area.

reviews.author: Leannie
reviews.title: Beautiful grounds, but not too fussed on seeing Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: We came as a group of 4 on a Thursday morning arriving about 9.30am, there wasn't a queue outside which was good, we probably queued inside for about 30mins total and most of it was under shade at least.They seem very hit and miss on their must leave bags policy as loads of people were wearing backpacks, but they were strict on not taking pics on way round or inside.It was fairly straight forward going through a small x-ray area and then to the queue.For me seeing HCM was on the little creepy side but at least I can say that I have been.We wandered around the beautiful grounds afterwards and saw the one pillar pagada amongst around 1000 other people - it was certainly a lot busier. I preferred in the past not going to the mausoleum and wandering the grounds on the days that the mausoleum was closed - far more peaceful

reviews.author: irina j
reviews.title: Important site for Vietnamese people
reviews.content: This is a well respected place for Vietnamese people and many come to visit mausoleum. We came in the afternoon when crowds disappeared and we could explore everything. The complex contains presidential palace and also few last places where Ho Chi Minh lived last years of his life. He was well respected and it’s amazing to see his truly humbling accommodation

reviews.author: Patric D
reviews.title: Peaceful ...
reviews.content: As soon as you enter the grounds, you leave the hustle and bustle of hanoi behind,  It is peaceful.  You need to follw the rules and make sure you walk the prescribed route around the Mauslleum.  There are lots of guards and iot is clear that 'Uncle Ho' has a very special place in the heatrs of the Vietnamese people.  if visiting Hanoi, this is amust-do attraction as it is central to the history of modern Vietnam

reviews.author: Yann Renaud
reviews.title: Strange place worth visiting once
reviews.content: This is a very strange place, worth visiting once to get an idea of it. Be ready to queue. We had to wait in line for 45 minutes to get in the mausoleum. Check the dress code to visit the place beforehand. Avoid taking a back pack, you will have to leave it at the entrance, and a big camera that you will have to hand over.

reviews.author: Ali07London
reviews.title: Interesting and pretty gardens
reviews.content: Very strict entry rules to go in the Mausoleum. No water allowed and bags are scanned. You need to follow instructions or you will be told. You do see his actual body and no photos. The other parts of the complex are also allowed to be viewed but it shuts at 11.30 am so go early. It’s very pretty. We were too late for the museum

reviews.author: Angela G
reviews.title: Time your visit
reviews.content: We didn't go inside the tomb as we thought there was some official event going on, thousands of people in white and red queuing in the square in front. We later found out this is an everyday occurrence as only open on a morning until 1130. We went to the grounds and presidential palace. Very strict dress code ( no bare shoulders, no shorts) and security, through scanners ,armed soldiers everywhere. We walked around the grounds and saw the house "Uncle Ho" used instead of the old colonial palace. All in all very interesting.

reviews.author: scholken
reviews.title: Mausoleum
reviews.content: It is really big to explore . Beautiful place with the rich history. I spent a lot time walking around this place. You will have a nice tour

reviews.author: S Sewpersad
reviews.title: Revered Leader Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: Visited the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, the final resting place of a revered and hard working leader who liberated and unified Vietnam. We visited on a Saturday and were fortunate that we did not have a long queue. Very orderly and disciplined visit with very strict dress code. The main section where the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh is   guarded. The entry and exit time in the Mausoleum is about 2 minutes as you keep moving. A must visit when you are in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Asia Mystika Travel
reviews.title: Must Visit when you travel to Hanoi
reviews.content: The mausoleum itself is an impressive structure made of grey granite, with a large central hall that houses the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh. Visitors can pay their respects to the leader by walking past the glass sarcophagus containing his body.Visitors are required to dress modestly and respectfully, and photography is not allowed inside the mausoleum. The mausoleum is usually open to the public on weekday mornings, but it may be closed on certain days or during official events.Overall, the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is an important historical and cultural site in Vietnam, and a visit can provide insight into the country's revolutionary past and the legacy of its revered leader.

reviews.author: Nashes_5
reviews.title: The highlight of our visit
reviews.content: We got up early to beat the queues which was a really good idea as they were already there in large numbers at 7am. We were the only westerners there as the Vietnamese queued in large family groups to pay respects to the country's former leader and revolutionary. It was fascinating just to see that on such a scale. We paid our £2 and shuffled along in a queue and soon enough filed past the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh, lying in a glass case, clearly revered by the visitors. It's all over very quickly but compared to the chaos of the city in general, this was well organised, clean, respectful and interesting. The soldiers on duty are immaculate and there's some marching and laying of wreaths. As one of just 5 remaining communist countries in the world it was fascinating to see the real respect the people showed.

reviews.author: KTP310
reviews.title: Incredibly busy so we enjoyed the grounds
reviews.content: We arrived at 9am on a Saturday to find the queue was over 2km long! This was estimated to take several hours so we chose instead to walk in the grounds, where you can see the one stilt house and the amazing bonsai trees, and view the mausoleum from the outside.

reviews.author: OneTrip with local
reviews.title: Nice place to visit for the first time
reviews.content: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a must-visit destination for anyone interested in Vietnamese history and culture. Located in Hanoi, it is the final resting place of Ho Chi Minh, the revolutionary leader who helped to liberate Vietnam from French colonial rule. The mausoleum is open to the public for a limited time each day, and visitors are required to follow strict dress codes and conduct themselves with respect and decorum. It is recommended to check the opening hours and guidelines before visiting the mausoleum. You need to check the schedule before visiting this place as it might be closed,

reviews.author: TravelsDaGlobe
reviews.title: A terrific thing to do in Hanoi
reviews.content: A terrific half day experience. Don’t get there too early as you get caught up with the masses of school kids that visit each morning. I recommend an 11am arrival.Plenty to see and do but your time with Uncle Ho is very short.

reviews.author: Steve Buckley
reviews.title: Must Do!
reviews.content: My wife and myself are currently visiting Hanoi (staying at the excellent Lasiesta Hotel - Review to follow) and earlier today we visited Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum.To my mind, this is a must do but needs a little planning as not only is the Mausalium closed on Mondays & Fridays but only open in the mornings on the other days. It is also very popular and attracts large crowds. Decorum (closely marshalled by the Presidential Guards) and a dress code (no shorts or certainly none below the knee) also applies.My advice go later rather than easier when the queue can be very long but the choice is very much down to the individual but - above all - go as this is a must do!!

reviews.author: Mandy M
reviews.title: worth a visit
reviews.content: bit of a queue to get through the main entrance and then flowed right through to walking through and seeing ho chi minh lying in state.  a bit surreal but worth doing.   then we saw the buildings where he worked, his lovely stilt house on a lake that you can walk through, some old cars, a very cute one story pagoda and a gloriously gold and fruity temple.   dont miss the guide to buddhism on the walls!  all very enjoyable

reviews.author: Jonathan C.
reviews.title: ho chi minh mausoleum
reviews.content: The burial place of Ho Chi Minh and where he frequently gave speeches. No pictures/dress code required.

reviews.author: Alex H
reviews.title: Perhaps controversial but interesting nevertheless
reviews.content: We had read online that Ho Chi Minh suggested he wanted to be cremated and his ashes scattered in different places. Clearly it’s a bit controversial, but nevertheless we thought the experience was very interesting. You only get around 20 seconds or so in the room with the embalmed body, and the guards are extremely strict on clothing and the way you act when you are there. I suggest long trousers and something to cover your sleeves (men included) as I was told to put my jumper on. Also cover your ankles, feet and shoulders. Entry is free and queues can be long, and be wary of opening times as my understanding is you can only see him in the morning.

reviews.author: Celtic3401
reviews.title: A must if you are a history buff
reviews.content: do not be scared off by the line.  It was unbelievably long when we were there (holiday for locals) but it moved very quickly  We had an English speaking guide so got a lot more out of it than if we went on our own

reviews.author: fal3
reviews.title: A must do that can honestly be skipped…
reviews.content: The staff were rude and hostile, which unfortunately is a common theme in most places in Hanoi.The mausoleum itself is quite quick and I’m not sure what the interest is with seeing a dead body.The surrounding areas were a bit more interesting with displays of how Ho Chi Minh lived “as it was” in the past, but I find it hard to believe it’s not highly staged.This places feels like one big piece of propaganda for north Vietnamese people.Definitely worth skipping if you don’t have lots of time.

reviews.author: Leonhkny
reviews.title: Communist imprint
reviews.content: This encompassing commemoration is a reminder of Vietnam's communist identity. The mausoleum is a Lenin-sque monument to the founding father of red Vietnam. Patriotic Vietnamese goes inside to see the remains.

reviews.author: Deb B
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: Your website said it was open, after a 2.2 km walk l arrive at 12.30 and it’s closed, took a couple of pictures and left, very disappointing.

reviews.author: Olivia H
reviews.title: Crowded by worth it
reviews.content: We went here on a Saturday (morning - NB: it closes at 11am) and followed the long queues of school children. Despite it taking around an hour and a half to enter, it was worth the wait…and the kids were really sweet. Something you will probably never experience anywhere else in the world.

reviews.author: palawanismyhome
reviews.title: We cannot forget Uncle Ho
reviews.content: I saw the mausoleum for the first time in 1993 and each time i visit Hanoi i always take a walk in that area and admire the huge building. You can see the changing of the guards or the flag raising at certain times of the day. In the old days you could cycle to the area but now all the streets are cordoned off and there is a security search and xray machine 150 m before you approach the mausoleum.

reviews.author: Monica G
reviews.title: HCM Mausoleum
reviews.content: A bit crowded but interesting to take a visit to experience a glimpse of history. The area is nice with many places to visit nearby.

reviews.author: Traveling Ammonite
reviews.title: Wonderful glimpse into Vietnamese history. Sad glimpse into human (tourist) behavior
reviews.content: This will probably be a stop on most city tours, and rightfully so. It gives you deeper insight into the history of the country as well as the respect the Vietnamese people have for their country. As such, there are a lot of basic rules for respect, such as no shorts, dress modestly, and don't take photos in certain areas. For some reason, people did not understand this and showed up in beachwear. For bizarre and inexplicable reasons, their toddlers had bare midriffs (but were denied access). And people of course kept taking photo, photo, photo. Interesting glimpse into Vietnamese history. Sad and depressing glimpse into human behavior.

reviews.author: Ali921
reviews.title: Everyone visits - time it right
reviews.content: Everyone visits this site. Check opening times because they vary by day/week/month/holidays. Do not visit on holidays because the lines are huge. Go early as well. A lot of rules to follow - dress code, hats, how to walk (!), no talking (inside). After seeing HCM himself you can then walk around the grounds and visit his house etc. Easy to spend a long time here.

reviews.author: J S
reviews.title: Grand.
reviews.content: The mausoleum was closed. I was fine with that. Interesting displays on the grounds. Nice park like setting. Governor's mansion is nearby. No surprise that the government is attempting to(or has) establish a 'cult of personality' around their leader. Certainly, the reality of the life of HCM, and what is presented here probably do not align. Still worth a visit if you are in Hanoi.

reviews.author: BertSG
reviews.title: Educational
reviews.content: We went on a weekend morning around 10am. There a bag drop at the entrance which is convenient. We were fortunate as there was only a very short wait to visit, about 10 minutes. Similar to visit Chairman Mao, we queued and made our way to see the well preserved body. We then made our way to his old house and in total spent a good 1 hour visiting. Entry was free. Most were dressed in smart casual which is the appropriate wear as a courtesy and respect to the host.

reviews.author: sugees
reviews.title: “Great place to know about the Vietnam’s first president”
reviews.content: Well maintained and huge campus. At least you need  minimum of 2 hours to walk around the full museum and the surroundings.Lot of information about Ho Chi Minh the great man of Vietnam. The presidential palace, his house, cars all are in display. Entrance ticket is 40,000 VND per person.To know the Vietnamese history and to walk around and see the palace, mango path, buddha tree root pathways are worth walking around. Luckily rain god stopped and we could enjoy the walk.

reviews.author: Wonder A
reviews.title: Relishing the days of Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: We had a life history lesson when we visited the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and were amazed at the way Ho Chi Minh's body was so well preserved.

reviews.author: wombatdavid
reviews.title: We enjoyed meeting uncle
reviews.content: We walked up from the Old Quarter which only took about 30 minutes. You drop off your bag and then we did not queue for long at all before we were in the mausoleum. Uncle was resting in a glass case. We loved the experience and it is free. Note you must wear long trousers and shirt with sleeves (short sleeves ok). A must see!

reviews.author: Lovetotravel240689
reviews.title: A must do in Hanoi
reviews.content: I got a motorbike taxi from old town for 22,000 VND. Arrived at 8am on a Saturday morning. Queued at the main entrance & quite quickly got through. Took around 30mins waiting in total before I got to enter the main Mausoleum building. Water and food you have in your bag is held in a secure free of charge area at the reception which you walk back to on the way out & collect. Was able to take backpack with phone inside, strictly not phones or photos allowed once you reach the main mausoleum compound. Make sure you wear long trousers and T-shirt. Well worth doing, amazing to see the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh at rest. Lovely walk back through the gardens afterwards. You can take photos of the mausoleum building once you are outside. Picked up a motorbike taxi back to old town from the main entrance area.

reviews.author: Face_The_Elements
reviews.title: Lots to see here!
reviews.content: This area has lots to see here. The mausoleum, presidential palace, uncle Ho’s house on stilts, one pillar pagoda, temple of literature and lots of history. Wear good shoes, and bring some water as you’ll be getting your steps in.

reviews.author: MikeH98
reviews.title: Interesting place to visit
reviews.content: Really enjoyed our visit here. The outside of the mausoleum is impressive and the gardens and lake are lovely. Lots of interesting history to learn about..

reviews.author: CRISTINA Z
reviews.title: Must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: It is an impressive monument and everyone who visit Hanoi should see it. Many people recommend to go early at 7.30 am, but I can tell you from my experience that I enter the gate at 8.50 am and at 9.10 I've already seen the Mausoleum.It is a check at entrance and then a queue, but It is all very organized and you walk very quickly from the gate  to  the Mausoleum.

reviews.author: ash44_in
reviews.title: Be aware of the rules before visiting
reviews.content: This is a must see if you are interested in history and the life of Ho Chi Minh. However you need to keep the following in mind before you visit :1. Check the official website for opening hours as it varies during the year. In October, when we visited the mausoleum was open from 7.30 am to 10.30 am on all days except Fridays and Mondays. 2. Reach early at around 7.30 am to avoid the crowd and the blazing sun. It becomes extremely crowded from 9am onwards and you will have to stand in a long queue, although they move fast.3. Dress modestly and ensure that your arms and legs are covered. Shorts are not allowed and you will have to buy a skirt from the store on the premises/ from hawkers just outside the gate to cover your legs.4. Camera, bags have to be deposited while entering the mausoleum and photography is not allowed inside. 5. Please make sure that after visiting the mausoleum, you visit house no 54 and the stilt house (separate tickets to be purchased which is not included in the mausoleum tickets) before you see the museum. Otherwise you will again have to queue up for a second round of mausoleum visit if you see the museum first and then plan to visit the stilt house. We were not aware of this and we spent 20 mins doing an extra round of the mausoleum before we could go towards the stilt house.

reviews.author: Ms Lena
reviews.title: The beloved President Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: A beautiful sunrise, great weather too. Dress respectively and don't bring any bags as these will not be allowed in. On days when visitation is allowed.

reviews.author: WhyDontWe
reviews.title: Massive compound
reviews.content: The entrance is at Ngoc Ha street and not via Huong Vuong which is the listed map address. There is security and you are required to check your bags at the counter. Even just a single bottle had to be checked in. Either bring absolutely nothing or be prepared to check in your bag. No photography is allowed within the masoluem but we were lucky we didn’t have to check in our mobile phones. Just don’t take it out where photography is not allowed. There are paid photo taking services after you exit the masoleum where HCM’s body rests. There’s no queue to see HCM as the traffic moves swiftly and you aren’t allowed to stand still for too long. It will take about a minute or two to enter, walk a round past where his body lies, pay your respects and leave. The room is heavily guarded.
