They shouted at us because they assume we were Vietnamese because to them we do not look like foreigners and my brother in law who is English and also at the same counter was not scolded bcoz he obviously looks like a foreigner!At the Mausoleum grounds, one of the guards was posing with a local Vietnamese kid and family for photos...and we witness a foreigner asking them politely if they could also take photo with him, he curtly refused and looked so fierce and unfriendly.Hmm...maybe they feel that we are intruders in the sacred HCM Masouleum ...that is why they were so  unfriendly & surly.

reviews.author: Henry Ooi O
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: Thank you Chuong of Seven Tours for touring us and explaining the history of this place. I rate your service 5 star.

reviews.author: Oisin K
reviews.title: A taste of Viet cong
reviews.content: We visited on a Sunday. Long queues that moved quickly, and to my delight were authoritarianly marshalled by the local police. We (the queue) were told to move more quickly, to get in single file, and get closer to the kerb. The Mausoleum was also great, and there is clearly deep and genuine affection for their saviour and father of a nation.

reviews.author: Tony O
reviews.title: Not worth the time
reviews.content: Whilst I'm sure this is a meaningful visit for Vietnamese people, to stand in the heat for over an hour to walk past the glass tomb for 1 minute was not worth the time. We got the diostinct impression that this was  a requirement of our tour company since, unlike other excursions, we were not given the option of skipping it for something else. If this is important for you to do, plan to stand in line for 1 - 2 hours in hte heat. The tomb itself is air conditioned.

reviews.author: Saf Traveler
reviews.title: Little weird but glad I went
reviews.content: It is what it is and it was an experience.. but keep in mind that this might be your only chance in your life to see an embalmed leader's body and likely this will be the last leader in human history to have their body prepared like this. Don't miss out if you have a little interest.The long line you see to get in moves pretty quickly, so don't be scared off. You literally get quickly hurried along. However, go in the morning as early as possible to beat the crowd.Here is a tip:Your taxi driver will likely drop you off at the big intersection next to the Mausoleum. Where you will see the huge field and building. However, You can only enter from the main gate. Your driver will be trying to avoid the traffic jam at the main gate and will screw you and your ignorance over. Set your address correctly and if you can still actually see the Mausoleum when you get out of the car.. then you're in the wrong place and will need to walk about 1km or more to get around the complex to the actual gate.

reviews.author: autobiztravel
reviews.title: A humble leader who believed in Socialism, so why did if falter?
reviews.content: I've visited the tomb of Lenin in Moscow as well. These men had powerful feelings, society would have more harmony without disparity. The reality is, it doesn't work. Basic human nature dictates we want more, we what what other's have...in all these socialist societies, it ends this way. They become market societies again.

reviews.author: Mohan K
reviews.title: The mausoleum of a humble leader of the country fought aganist the invaders.
reviews.content: I have much respect for Ho Chi Minh who had a humble living even as the President of Vietnam. So it was one of the reasons to visit and pay respect to the leader who fought against the world's mightiest country. Ho Chi Minh mausoleum and the surrounding gardens are well-maintained and it takes at least an hour to complete the tour. We had to wait in the queue for about 20 minutes to pass through the entrance. The only thing bothered me heavy military presence as if we were in a garrison.

reviews.author: A P
reviews.title: If i had choice i would skip it
reviews.content: Booked by agency with full all day program we visited HCM mausoleum. We weren't very interested in seeing his tomb to tell the truth, we went early so people was not quite a lot. Lines went quick so didnt have to wait long time. So many guards and deadly silence inside. We really liked the beautiful gardens and the guards shifting! It was just just good compared to  the museum that was amazing! No photos are allowed inside!

reviews.author: Vida Foo
reviews.title: Visited with 2 students from Student Free tour
reviews.content: Very well organised & am impress with the help given by the seeing I'm struggling  with my walking stick.

reviews.author: traverseinfinity
reviews.title: Great
reviews.content: Amazing insight into the culture and wel worth a visit tonthe complex even if uncle ho has gone for his Russian touch up

reviews.author: sarsdow
reviews.title: Great history lesson
reviews.content: Great visit, great history lesson. Didn’t go inside but walked around the outside and saw the changing of the guard.  If you happen to be there at the right time, the changing of the guard is an exercise in precision and well worth watching.

reviews.author: Johnmagfam
reviews.title: Stoic and plain
reviews.content: Picture paints a thousand words, all could only be experience from the outside. There was a museum but it was closed on a Saturday, 30 Nov while I was there.

reviews.author: Jessie Hoh
reviews.title: Good walking tour
reviews.content: Better walk in the morning for Ho Chi Minh Complex before getting hot sun and to visit body Ho Chi Minh are early if mistake around 11am

reviews.author: Furterbrown
reviews.title: Lovely spot
reviews.content: We tried to visit last time we were here but it was Ho’s birthday and every man, woman and child had come to visit! Thankfully the line was significantly shorter this time. Yes, you don’t get to stop and see Ho for very long but the grounds are lovely to walk around, check out his cars and lake. A very calm spot.

reviews.author: atontao
reviews.title: Political monument
reviews.content: A sort of copy of the Lenin maussoleum for the local communist heroIn terms of architecture there is nothing special in this monument

reviews.author: Hartdmuth
reviews.title: Must for history lovers.
reviews.content: There is not more to say that my predecessor said. If you are passionate about culture and history, a must do in Hanoi. Despite the huge lines, you will see Uncle Ho in no time.  Be sure you dress appropriate as the guards are pretty strict about it. No photos, no talking loud or anything that could disrespect this Mausoleum. Open from 08:00 to 11:00.

reviews.author: BMO
reviews.title: Visit to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: There was a long queue before going to the mausoleum itself but the pacing is quite fast. There are several rules that are strictly followed while in queue (the guards are very attentive) - no using of face masks and sunglasses/shades, and no taking of photos.

reviews.author: MilneBayPatriot
reviews.title: Short trip
reviews.content: We were ushered through queues of hundreds of people. Our belongings were scanned and we had to walk through a body scanner also. All water bottles and food were removed and thrown out of our bags.  We had to walk from station to station with cameras in coloured bags or tags to collect our cameras at certain stops. A tab but annoying. The thing that did not impress us on this tour is that NO-ONE was allowed to use the toilets unless the tour was over. A bit over the top if you ask me. We had a  teenager and older people on our tour who came away with with a disappointing impression of this only this particular part of our tour. Otherwise okay as this tour is free and the Moselium is open 3 days a week to see "Uncle Ho" as per the brochure and website.

reviews.author: Annette D
reviews.title: Very long lines
reviews.content: We managed to get there but the lines were long. So we walked around the block and had a perfect photo op of the outside. To be honest the only attraction inside is tomb

reviews.author: uncledave1980
reviews.title: Visit to Ho Chi Mins Mausoleum
reviews.content: This was a fascinating experience. There was a 35 minute queue so take water and maybe an umbrella if it is hot.It is worthwhile to observe the Vietnamese adults and children whilst queuing. No short shorts or vests. Respectable dress is required. It is a 30 second shuffle around his mummified body and strictly no cameras. Expect confiscation and arrest if you take a camera shot. The guards are very attentive. There is silence throughout the mausoleum and if you are not prepared to behave in a respective manner don't go.If you don't have respect don't go

reviews.author: EddieTdot
reviews.title: Worth visiting - night time recommended
reviews.content: I went to the Mausoleum in the evening just prior to sunset. I have to say the place looks better after dark when the lights are on. A lot of locals come here for jogging and other exercises, if you can stand breathing in the polluted air in Hanoi, come here for a good jog. To go inside to view Ho Chi Minh's body, you'll have to go early in the morning to line up. Another note is that although short pants are allowed, women need to cover their shoulders to get inside. My gf was wearing a tan-top and was denied entry and she had to buy a scarf nearby to cover her top.

reviews.author: MrsLunchy
reviews.title: My Uncle Ho
reviews.content: I have always wanted to see the Mausoleum of Uncle Ho and this provided me the perfect opportunity to do so.  I could not help but feel a sense of pride on how his people revere him.  Our guide was quite strict and in no uncertain terms told us not to sneakily take photos inside and even castigated another who was going to!

reviews.author: Steve Q
reviews.title: Great people watching
reviews.content: I was pretty nonplussed by the viewing of the chalky looking corpse of Uncle Ho as he is known. Most interesting to me was the experience of watching the Vietnamese citizenry as they came to pay homage to their dead leader.

reviews.author: Raymondale
reviews.title: Pay the respect to Ho
reviews.content: the mausoleum was modeled on Lenin's mausoleum in Russia and was first open to the public in 1975.many locals come here to pay respect to their beloved leader,so will be long queue.must come here very earlier.Security is tight and visitors should dress with respect.bags and camera are not allowed,must deposit them before entering. Visitors are not allowed to stop while paying respect to mr.Ho.an amazing trip and worth a visit.

reviews.author: Robdog2909
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh museleum
reviews.content: Long queues to get through. Although the queue can keep moving. When you finally see Ho Chi Minh, there is no stopping to pay respects, you keep moving. Then you’re out the door. Interesting place though, looking at his houses and the surrounding gardens.

reviews.author: Judy D
reviews.title: Uncle Ho’s resting place
reviews.content: Awesome building, guarded by goose-stepping guards in immaculate white uniforms. Our guide was full of interesting facts and stories. The gardens are well kept, as is the fleet of cars Ho Chi Minh owned.Interesting view of the history of the Vietnamese, Uncle Ho and where he REALLY worked.

reviews.author: Hanzen
reviews.title: Interesting Visit
reviews.content: In visiting the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum, tourists and local visitors have to pass through inspection.  There is an x-ray scanner right at the entrance to the complex.  Water bottles are not allowed inside.  At the second gate, visitors are advised to put their cameras inside a red bag since taking of pictures is strictly prohibited inside the mausoleum.   They will be able to get their bags after they exit the mausoleum.  Tourists will then be able to take pictures around the Ho Chi Minh Complex which includes the following:  the Ho Chi Minh Museum, the One Pillar Pagoda, the Residence of the former president which is the House on Stilts and have an amazing view of the lake inside the complex.  It was an amazing trip.

reviews.author: MLG
reviews.title: As Good As the Guide Is
reviews.content: It is big for sure but a view face on is all one gets for the price of admission.  The narrative from our guide was good and that was the value for me.  I would put this towards the bottom of the list of things to do, especially on a busy tourist day.

reviews.author: Esteeohenee
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: Honorable and memorable tribute to Ho Chi Minh provided an opportunity for many to take time to reflect on a man who contributed much to the people of Vietnam.

reviews.author: Hannah W
reviews.title: Definitely worth the wait
reviews.content: As the mausoleum is only opened for limited time everyday, one can expect the queue to be long, regardless of the time. However, it does move very fast as you can only spend at most 30 seconds in the mausoleum as they do not allow visitors to linger. Remember to dress appropriately and be respectful.

reviews.author: Pavije
reviews.title: Intimidating
reviews.content: Visited the Mausoleum and it reminded me of institutional behaviour. The grounds are amazing but the staff are serious and strict. Do not attempt to visit without complying to the regulations. It’s an interesting place but in hindsight I would not have bothered had I known the regime.

reviews.author: SANDEEP Varma
reviews.title: Resting place of a great leader
reviews.content: Must visit place if you want to know more about the founder and great leader Ho Chi Minh. There is the One pillar pagoda nearby and the museum too. I couldn't go inside the mausoleum because i visited the place on a weekend.

reviews.author: Madancer
reviews.title: Interesting experience
reviews.content: Its a surreal experience viewing Uncle Ho's extremely well preserved body! Honestly felt like he was going to get up any moment and start speaking. The viewing itself is a highly regulation and organised exercise. Everything else is far more relaxed once you exit the mausoleum.The one pillar pagoda is really underwhelming and can be missed. While the mausoleum is free entry, the entrance to the museum is ticketed.

reviews.author: ricardofmbr
reviews.title: Probably the most important leader in the modern history of Vietnam
reviews.content: You can get inside the mausoleum and see Ho Chi Min's body - in this sense, very similar to Lenin's mausoleum. You can also visit a former home of the leader and learn a bit of the recent history of the country. The mausoleum is an imponent building reflecting the leader cult.

reviews.author: Mr Noor
reviews.title: Historical visit
reviews.content: We had a group visit to the museum, it’s was a good experience seeing the great leader. The residence of the leader were her humble he spent most of time away from the Yellow palace. Great experience.

reviews.author: Sheetal K
reviews.title: Grand !
reviews.content: It is a must visit if you are in Hanoi. It should not be missed. If you can walk, it is walk-able from the old quarters but some walking is required. Less tourist in the early hours.

reviews.author: chiangmaicharlies
reviews.title: Many more interesting places
reviews.content: A very popular destination for tourists, but once you're queued up, walked past the body and left, you may feel underwhelmed. I was when I did this on a previous visit.On this visit, it was during the two months each year that the mausoleum is closed to the public.As you walk by, there are some interesting trees and gardens to be seen, plus the many white-clad guards stopping tourists from getting too close.The building itself is minimalist.Visit it if you wish, but if you do want to go inside, make sure it's open when you're there.

reviews.author: monacdal
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: Good to walk by and take pictures. The place is highly secured and you would be required to go through security prior to entry. If you smoke, leave your lighters and cigarettes at your hotel. Also no chewing gum inside its premises.

reviews.author: amber d
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Very organised (bordering strict) but that made it all the more interesting. Make sure you go in the morning, as I think it shuts at 11am daily, and the queue for me was less than 20min

reviews.author: sportcar
reviews.title: Very interesting visit. Lines are long but move very quickly. Worth the wait.
reviews.content: Very impressive, so glad I took the time to visit this site.  Soldiers and changing of the guard every hour very impressive too.  Throngs of people but not intolerable.

reviews.author: KEColorado
reviews.title: A must-See in Hanoi
reviews.content: The line to the mausoleum can be very long, so I recommend going first thing in the morning.  It’s worth seeing this immaculate mausoleum and the preserved body.

reviews.author: alicewong4
reviews.title: recommend to drop by
reviews.content: Unfortunately, didn't get to go into the mausoleum as went during afternoon closing time. Still recommend to go as you can see local activities and laid-back lifestyle. Wide land space and windy.

reviews.author: Harin Fernando
reviews.title: Facinating and Interesting for the curious
reviews.content: Go early to avoid long ques. But the lines do move really fast. No matter within 20 minutes you can easily finish the main viewing. There is a ticket fee and x-ray scanning also for entry. Dress modest (silent) and leave electronics behind. Small bags and purses and mobile phones are ok to carry but not to use. After if want the is HCM dedicated museum and his royal palace exhibition (tickets).

reviews.author: Customer909
reviews.title: Be there as early as you can to avoid the long queues
reviews.content: On Weekends entrance is free and doors open rather early. If you can be there for 07:00 am, you can avoid the very long queues in the hot burning sun. If you can, do not take valuables such as very expensive cameras, as you have to leave them in secure places. They will not allow you to take them with you. Although it is secure  for peace of mind I would leave them back at the hotel.Atmosphere inside is electric and they have done a great job of controlling the crowd and the speed at which people walk through.

reviews.author: Tatjana T
reviews.title: Well preserved historical spot
reviews.content: Reasonably priced  ( 40k D) and well preserved site with memories of the great historical leader of Vietnam. Average time spending about 2 hours. Opens only in the morning from 7:30am.Remember about a modest dress code.

reviews.author: jeffchia88
reviews.title: Interesting place and beautifully landscaped
reviews.content: I had missed this place on my first visit because of the opening times so I made sure I was on time this time around. Getting there was no issue but getting back was a slight issue as in Hanoi, I found that when you to get a Grab back to the hotel  you need to communicate with the  driver by taking a photo of where you are waiting as there is no taxi pick up point. The place is beautifully landscaped with interesting information about Ho Chi Minh.  Make sure you carry an umbrella or rain coat  or hat.  You will need if it rains and protect yourself from the scorching sun on sunny days as the passage in is not well shaded.It was really unfortunate that I did not see any schedule for the changing of the guards and was caught by surprise as I would have love to take photos of the smart military drills. My only unpleasant experience there were a group of lady tourists that were pushing and dashing there way to the toilets really being oblivious of one's presence. Souvenirs are available the exit with may shops offering various goods for sale.There is a charge for entry.An interesting sign board that said -No Chewing Gum, for a moment I had thought that I was in Singapore.

reviews.author: Lennyg
reviews.title: Unusual experience, museum and stilt house worth seeing
reviews.content: Do not be intimidated by the long lines, they move quickly and are part of the experience.  We went solo, and heard two different English-speaking guides giving very different information, better to learn on your own.  The viewing process goes quickly and in an orderly manner, stopped only for a delegation of visiting dignitaries.  The stilt house is very simple, the museum very well-displayed with many things to read, lots of documents as well for history buffs like me. The exhibition 50 years after Ho's death had interesting commentary, particularly a strong statement about the mistakes and problems in the immediate recovery period 75-86, and then lauded the opening of Vietnam to the world post 86.  It seems that the only venerated leader is Ho--the  pictures of leaders were not Vietnamese but foreign leaders, including Pres. Clinton and John McCain on the recognition and reconciliation of the US and Vietnam.  It was also notable for what it didn't say--some reference to the Soviets but none to the Chinese, although Vietnam development is closer to the Chinese model.  If you know the history (I had read an extensive biography of Ho as well as extensively about the French and American wars), this is a worthwhile experience.

reviews.author: Sue Anne O
reviews.title: Insight to Ho Chi Minh’s life
reviews.content: Personally felt the wait, the security checks, the Q, and the walk well worth the time. Everything is presented in a respectful way, and while some people insisted in talking when silence was requested or snuck out a camera in an attempt take a photo where we were clearly asked not to, the guards were very gentle in how they approached people reminding them to observe the requests which I felt was very fair of them. The love people clearly have for Ho Chi Minh was so obvious at this site

reviews.author: jazzymama1
reviews.title: Go early and enjoy the theatrical experience
reviews.content: We arrived at 7:30am and basically walked straight through. We took no bags so didn’t have to leave anything at any counter.It’s a theatrical experience and Ho (if it is indeed the real Ho) looks wondrous after so long. The space is imposing and the brutalist architecture is fantastic.The other garden bit is not incredible but a nice walk around.

reviews.author: Slo01
reviews.title: Part of the history
reviews.content: You need to go early as the number allowed in is limited.  Expect along queue to see ‘The man’ entombed in a glass case but don’t step out of line, take of sunglasses and wear appropriate clothing.  All chatter to stop as you approach the mausoleum.  Get this over with and the lovely grounds are then free to explore.

reviews.author: Anne N
reviews.title: Viewed from afar.
reviews.content: Beautiful area with interesting architecture, the queues though can be two or more hours long unless you have pre booked for fast access.

reviews.author: Greenclifflady
reviews.title: Definitely Worth a Visit
reviews.content: The Father of Vietnam’s final resting place is well worth visiting. It’s set in gorgeous grounds. Ho Chi Minh’s remains are currently being “renovated” and therefore not available to view but it’s still interesting to visit. Lots of little stalls selling memorabilia and snacks. You need to be “respectfully” dressed (Women’s shoulders have to be covered, but they seem fine with men’s shorts). There is a stall at the entrance selling scarves, for forgetful folk like me! Barter with him - he starts at 200k and came down fairly quickly to 100k:) And it was a very nice scarf!!

reviews.author: 1MariaTeresaMauri1
reviews.title: Beautiful Surrounds
reviews.content: Visiting the Mausoleum can be disappointing for those who just want to see Ho Chi Minh lying in his glass coffin, nothing much to see and you have to keep moving so there's not time to just stand for a moment to look at the body or reflect. But the surrounding gardens is worth the visit.

reviews.author: by anilsah.us
reviews.title: Nice formal Square
reviews.content: The queue was long when we arrived but moving quite fast. The policemen/guards are really strict. It was an amazing experience to see 'sleeping' Ho Chih Minh.

reviews.author: Ed P
reviews.title: Worth a visit!
reviews.content: Had to walk quite a distance to find the entrance, lots of people in the line but it kept going at walking pace so no real queuing. There is no charge, you can take mobiles and bags but no cameras, they supply you with a bag in which you put the camera and collect it later. Lots of soldiers in uniform line the route and  as you enter you have to be in pairs, no sun glasses or talking! It is well worth seeing and probably took no longer than 15mins. You can then collect your camera and tour the rest of the grounds.

reviews.author: katielittlered87
reviews.title: Imposing building
reviews.content: A huge grey building that holds ho chi minh's body. You can view his body but in Oct /November he goes to Russia for keeping him looking good so not avaliable to view when I was there. Security at gates to check bags and appropriate dress only, no bare arms etc. You will here whistles blow when people step on the grass.

reviews.author: Cat_the_rine_1
reviews.title: Be there early and do your research
reviews.content: Was there but didn’t manage to enter. The building itself is guarded by 2 guard at the door and the whole premise is huge, lots of empty space  prob 2- 4 Football field? Please be there early. It only open to visitor in the morning and certain day is closed to public too. If you dont mind just admire the structure of the grey building and the surrounding, it is open till evening.

reviews.author: Tamara A
reviews.title: Too busy, missed it 2x in 2 yrs
reviews.content: Went to go in 2018...closed.  Went again, at opening time in the am, line ups over 2 blocks, then more line ups inside!

reviews.author: Abdur Rahman
reviews.title: It was a great pleasure to pay my tribute to this great leader.
reviews.content: This place is highly sensitive to every Vietnamese people. Short skirt, short pant, half sleeve shirt can't be worn for visiting this place. This maouselum is normally closed at 1030 though officially written that it will be closed at 1100. You will see the body of this great leader of the Vietnam.

reviews.author: Shu P
reviews.title: Boring
reviews.content: Go there to take a look at what Communism values.... Himt: Not freedom.An exact copy from"mother" Russia Lenin's mausoleum

reviews.author: Jennifer Tan
reviews.title: Visit
reviews.content: It is necessary to have a tour guide to explain to you the history to understand. I enjoyed it, though we need to queue for 40 to 45mins to just view President Ho Chi Minh's body.

reviews.author: Jeannie M
reviews.title: Worth taking the time to see
reviews.content: Very informative. It really help to tell the story of Ho Chi Minh. Staff were very helpful / my husband has issues with doing stairs and they came to assist him. Note to ladies - if your are going don’t wear shorts or sleeveless tops. If you forget there is a shop next door you can buy wraps for minimal cost.

reviews.author: Yo Giacomo
reviews.title: Long lines
reviews.content: It was incredibly organized and even though the lines are long, they do move consistently well because you can’t do anything but do a walk by. Without a guide to help with the background information, It wouldn’t have been that interesting.

reviews.author: Mark
reviews.title: Stunning--Significant--Mandatory!
reviews.content: Long lines, but they moved quickly. I was the only tourist out of hundreds upon hundreds of Vietnamese students. It's a serious place and taken seriously as you would expect out of the National Emancipator. People are quiet and respectful and the route inside is closely guarded by ever-so serious Vietnamese soldiers. It's a place of pilgrimage and if you're interested in Vietnamese history, and America's involvement in the Second Indochinese War, it's a station of the cross you cannot miss. Inside Uncle Ho looks like he just relaxed for a nap and might sit up at any moment. You move quickly through the mausoleum itself and have less than a minute to see arguably the world's greatest revolutionary. Dress appropriately, don't chew gum, leave your camera in your pocket and show some respect. Many of the students left weeping, they were so moved by seeing the man who liberated and unified their country. An important visit for any student of history.

reviews.author: Clare S
reviews.title: Interesting but different
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit - like nothing I'd ever done before. Had to queue for about 20 minutes but it was moving at a pace all the time. Guards were very officious but this added to overall experience. Not something you do every day!!

reviews.author: Tony Kok
reviews.title: Family Trip
reviews.content: Generally the HCM Mausoleum is amazing and you can see the embalmed body of the great vietnamese leader, Ho Chi Ming in close view. The mausoleum is very informative and documented the life of the great leader and history of the long fought Vietnam War. Plenty of photo collection of HCM and also many interesting art works and cultural display too.

reviews.author: isabella_deruiter
reviews.title: Mausoleum
reviews.content: Worth seeing and experiencing something unknown to our Western culture: cult of personality. The Vietnamese take this very seriously when it comes to Ho Chi Minh, he is obviously still very admired, if truly or habitually - who knows. You will be lead in a queue across the huge premises, all the time accompanied by soldiers in white uniforms, until you get to the room where he actually lies. You can't stop, you have to walk on, around the coffin and then you're out again and that's it. Entrance is free. I still recommend to do it when in Hanoi, check out the other sights related to HCM as well.

reviews.author: Tet M
reviews.title: Good visit!
reviews.content: We learned so much about Ho Chi Minh, how humble he was, & saw how he lived. Inspection before entering but it's ok. Be early. Closed monday to Friday. Saturday only until 10:30 the guide said.

reviews.author: Sawilliams01
reviews.title: Different
reviews.content: Found it odd to see a preserved dead body laying in a bed in a huge mausoleum built in his honour. The line up to get in is massive every day of the week which goes to show the respect the Viets have for the man. Worth a look.

reviews.author: Pushpal P
reviews.title: Respect to the President!
reviews.content: We visited the Ho Chi Minh  Mausoleum and the complex around with the museum. The history and the artifacts are quite fascinating. You get to see the various items used by the President when he was alive. How he coordinated his movement etc. Must visit!

reviews.author: Jud1thmason
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: This is not a lighthearted visit.  You are paying your respects to his corpse.  Guards are everywhere and the rules are strict.  Having said that, it was an interesting place to go.

reviews.author: AnnieLouDean
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: We knew very little about Ho Chi Minh but the visit was very informative. Lovely place to visit whilst in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Rinaap
reviews.title: President memorial
reviews.content: Having not search information about the place, actually the place is last rest place for Uncle ho, thats why the line is very huge because we go there on sunday, theres no ticket fee, but if you want to go around the palace the ticket fee is VND 40.000, not much to see, since many place that we can only see from distance, and crowded that we hard to get a photo

reviews.author: Helen
reviews.title: Definitely worth going
reviews.content: Unfortunately we visited in the afternoon. Viewing is only on the mornings. Allow plenty of time to view. The grounds, museum and one pillar pagoda.

reviews.author: Leffy
reviews.title: So so
reviews.content: It's located in the embassy section of town. So things are a little bit quieter than the old quarter. Where to visit if you have time but if you didn't go I don't think you're missing much. If you do go for fun step a little bit over the yellow line the guards a whistle at you.

reviews.author: Deepak DB
reviews.title: Meet The Leader
reviews.content: When planning to visit the place do check with locals about the days and time. It is shut twice a week and the days when you could visit the timings are limited. Please dress appropriately avoid shorts, sleeveless, on safer side. Big bags, etc are not allowed and mobiles HAVE to switched off, no photography inside.The mausoleum is located on large expanse of land with multiple attraction points around like the One Pillar Pagoda.We got goosebumps as we neared the mausoleum and were totally disappointed as that they they were not allowing any visitors due to some reason. Worst thing, it was our last day at Hanoi, so we missed on meeting the President, but glad that we could at least reach till the door step. A good knowledgeable guide who speaks English could help speed up the tour around this huge expanse.Must Visit!!

reviews.author: Robert and Sandra
reviews.title: Visiting the President
reviews.content: What an amazing experience cannot believe that the Vietnamese people allowed us to visit their President Ho Chi Minh. Thank you

reviews.author: Me1
reviews.title: Interesting experience
reviews.content: the place is huge and crowded, worth the visit if only to grasp how much the people love and worship their former leader. Don't forget suitible clothing, and don't bring a large bag.

reviews.author: Jocelyn D
reviews.title: Very interesting insight
reviews.content: Although it appeared to be busy, the queues moved quite quickly, they are mostly covered from the hot sun. Obviously when you go to the mausoleum you have to be respectful and quiet. You can see Ho Chi Min’s embalmed body. Everyone is quiet and there are soldiers guarding. From there you go around the living and working area of Ho  Chi Min. The big palace built by the French and painted bright yellow, now offices, there are his two Russian cars and a French car. The stilt house where he chose to live is simple airy and made of wood. It is possible to go up to see where he slept. The grounds are pretty. There are shops and places to eat.

reviews.author: Dave T
reviews.title: Worth A Visit
reviews.content: Lines move fairly quickly when you visit here so don’t be put off if you see a massive line. There are people (scammers) around trying to tell you to come back later and they can take you somewhere else for a couple of hours. Don’t fall for it. Make sure you have appropriate clothing Tshirt and shorts acceptable for a man and equivalent for a woman. Enjoy!

reviews.author: christine n
reviews.title: Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh home and Stilt House
reviews.content: Make time to walk though this enormous square, see the mausoleum, palace, home and stilt house.  It is an interesting view into Ho Chi Minh.

reviews.author: Artita J
reviews.title: Great landscape and building
reviews.content: Ho chi minh mausoleum is one of the must visit place when you travel in Hanoi. Great scenery, green yard and grey building, great historical museum inside.

reviews.author: Valery Belyanin
reviews.title: I was lost and got no help
reviews.content: The guide said that we should meet in 15 minutes inside the Ho Cho Min eztate, but I decided to go to the bus stop. When I realised that the group stayed inside I decided to go back. There was no way I could explain the guards that I needed help. The did not speak English and were extremely useless. The group lost 20 minutes and I lost a lot of nerves.Awful experience.Socialism sucks.

reviews.author: wesley t
reviews.title: A place of importance in Vietnam
reviews.content: I was accompanied by a local tour guide to visit this iconic place. There were beautiful garden and guards stationed around the corners to ensure security and respect to Mr Ho Chi Min, highly regarded and respected by the locals. The guide shared the history of Vietnamese and the important role played by Mr Ho.

reviews.author: Dave P
reviews.title: City tour
reviews.content: Saw this on our city tour. Was great to learn the history of Ho Chi Min. The gardens and his houses were lovely

reviews.author: Tiktok
reviews.title: Fascinating and sad
reviews.content: This is a special place of honor for one of the truly great individuals who attempted—and ultimately succeeded—in achieving independence for Vietnam after a lifelong struggle against colonial powers. Americans should take time to enter the long, but well organized lines to view Ho Chi Minh’s remains but should also learn this man’s indomitable spirit. There is an especially tragic cast to Ho’s attempts, after WWI in Paris, to obtain the aid of the US in escaping his country’s subjugation by France. President Wilson’s aides brushed this effort aside, and thus foiled what could have meant the avoidance of what Vietnamese call the American War.

reviews.author: Virginia T
reviews.title: Love of a Leader
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh is a beloved father figure.  The respect his people give him is noteworthy.  Expect long lines.

reviews.author: Marilyn S
reviews.title: Solemn Site
reviews.content: We visited the Mausoleum as a starter to our trip.  The lines were manageable and the walk by was enough.  To get your bags out of the “free” storage you had to pay to go through the museum or walk a mile around the area to get back to the front.Taxis are available at the entrance but be careful because they will rip you off.  There are plenty of scammers in Hanoi taxi ranks.  It was very hot and rainy which added to the unpleasantness.

reviews.author: Woon29
reviews.title: Interesting and should visit
reviews.content: We were shocked that there was such a long queue outside. But the queue moved very fast and security is very tight. My brother had sweets inside his pocket, the security guard took and threw into the dustbin. Our guide has warned us not to bring any bag in. Dress code is also strict, top must not be sleeveless, bottom should be below knee. No usage of handphone is allowed. The stairs up is also very dark.It was a good trip, all should visit.

reviews.author: suitcase1958
reviews.title: Respecting Uncle Ho
reviews.content: The debt Vietnam owes to Ho Chi Minh is incalculable his legacy is all around to be seen no more so then in his mausoleum were he still lies in state and is watched over by  immaculately turned out Vietnamese army guards An eerie and Solemn atmosphere but a must for anyone who visits Hanoi

reviews.author: Nikola S
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: Thus place is really impresive. You have to go through the hole complex and see everything related to Ho Chi Minh.Must go

reviews.author: Jas
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: Even though I did spend a couple of hours here and some of it was quite interesting the experience as a whole was quiet disappointing i couldn't see the body which was probably the only reason I went there I kept asking the guards and ticket counter as to which way to the body either they didn't know themselves or they provided me with wrong infoNot a great visit and yeah the tickets were 80,000 VND (3.5$)

reviews.author: BabsSC
reviews.title: A Must See
reviews.content: This was a stop on our day tour of Hanoi. Unfortunately the day we visited the mausoleum was closed.Very impressive location and the architecture stunning. Make sure you dress appropriately or you will not be allowed to enter the grounds. No shade so walk slowly👍

reviews.author: Susannah P
reviews.title: Solemn
reviews.content: This site shreaks out communism, the colours, architecture, signs and uniforms.  Very atmospheric.The main man wasn't in residency, he was back in Russia to have his embarlming refreshed.Worth a visit, particularly if you also stop by the Tran Quoc Pagoda in the same vicinity.

reviews.author: Bermondsey_7
reviews.title: Great experience.
reviews.content: Was not expecting to get inside to witness the body of Ho Chi Minh as it had been away for it's annual restoration in Russia.However turned up and indeed it was open.Join the queue. Not that easy to find but there are plenty of signs pointing the way. The guards aren't as scary as they look, they're helpful and keep everything flowing.The queue is long but moves along steadily. Dress modestly. Shorts must be knee length and definitely no vests. It's all very respectful.Everything is highly organised and orderly. Cameras not allowed, hand them in and get them back at the end.Once inside there's no stopping as you file past the body, solemnly guarded by four soldiers.All in all the visit was around an hour. Amazing experience that I felt honoured to have been allowed to participate in.

reviews.author: Dana
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: I was so humbled by the way the young army officers marched out of the mausoleum and carried me up the stairs in my wheelchair to view Ho Chi Minh....   It was a surprise and not expected....   Absolutely humbling experience.....

reviews.author: Ann W
reviews.title: Interesting cultural experience
reviews.content: I discovered the odd as visits go! I've never ever been to many mausoleum and also found a body lying in state. The cue generally shows up long, but do not be switched off by this, it moves at an cozy speed. Furthermore, see to it that you are heading rather initially as to stay away from the fantastic majority of people! so no time actually being around! Very interesting insight into this particular period of the story of Vietnam. A dramatic and historic encounter but check times while you have to go to AM and also it's not open every day

reviews.author: 714trish
reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh has been dead now 50 years but you are able to view his body for only a couple of hours a day, I think it was about 8am to 10am & only certain days. We were able to view whilst we were there & you queue in a single line & pass the guards. It is very cold (obviously for the body) &  he looks very 'pristine' laid out. It was amazing to do this & feel the reverence of the Vietnamese people for their past leader. My husband had his arms folded across his body has he was cold & the guard indicated he needed to have them by his side as a sign of humbling & respect which I can understand.

reviews.author: nisimbarda
reviews.title: a must site, not only mausoleum
reviews.content: we haven't entered the grave site, yet the whole complex, the way he lived, the way the Vietnamese people adore HCM is amazing and important for understanding major part of the new history a must site

reviews.author: Wayne H
reviews.title: History lesson
reviews.content: Impressed by the simple living quarters of the past Vietnamese leader. Lovely gardens and interesting trees and plants.

reviews.author: Catherine
reviews.title: Incredible sight to behold
reviews.content: Seeing the embalmed body of the revered Ho Chi Minh himself really was a very surreal experience. As others have said, the visit itself only lasts about 15 seconds as you walk around his body and if you get hurried along if you’re not walking fast enough. You have to drop your bags off at one counter and then drop your camera up at another - you can pick up your camera immediately after seeing the body, but as your main bag will have been dropped off near the entrance of the complex, it’s quite a way a way to retrieve that (and note that the bag counter is in fact closed between noon and 2pm, meaning if you went to see the presidential palace after seeing the body, as the two are very closed together, you might have to wait till after 2pm to pick your bags up again...).

reviews.author: edenxo1212
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: Get yourself a chance to look deep into for a historical insights of Vietnamese ancient history and culture. Even in the early morning, the queue is pretty long. You only can see Ho Chi Minh's body while you were walking your way through it. The architecture as well as the scenery from the inside out is quite pleasant. Definitely worth your visit

reviews.author: Sofie J
reviews.title: No small children allowed
reviews.content: My husband and older child enjoyed the mausoleum although it was very turisty and they felt like cattle being driven.. My 8 months old daugther was denied entry, without any explanation. So we had to sit outside and wait.

reviews.author: fionamcgrath23
reviews.title: Incredibly interesting
reviews.content: We spent the morning visiting this very interesting mausoleum and museum. It was intriguing reading about Ho Chi Minh’s life and achievements. Would recommend to any visitor to Hanoi to learn more about one of most interesting modern figures.

reviews.author: Jane J
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh mausoleum
reviews.content: Well today we only had one mission to visit the tomb of Ho Chi Minh.  We arrived at 9,30 and with stress Free admission and security checks we walked towards tomb. Upon entering the mausoleum you were embraced by the revered atmosphere and then you approached the glass tomb.  You could not help being affected by the sight of him lying there. It was light he had just fallen asleep.  Is it worth the visit.  Absolutely.  But ensure you know the opening times for mausoleum as he is not always available to see.  Tuesday before 10.30 am totally recommended in Oct.

reviews.author: Maurice Llanes TL
reviews.title: Better from the outside than going in....
reviews.content: Very interesting in the point of view of history and culture. However you are going to see somebody's dead body. The queu is very long from very early in the morning. It is very strict, even if you opt not to see Ho Chi Minh's body, in the middle of your way there, you can not. The mausoleum from the outside and gardens next to it is a most in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Ian H
reviews.title: Huge place!
reviews.content: A Huge place to visit, we missed going inside account they close the mausoleum on Mondays, but amazing place and grounds including the House of parliament behind it...

reviews.author: Iris T
reviews.title: Not much to see
reviews.content: It is a nice space and a building, but this spot look like you are in china,they keep it nicely, but Nothing much to see.It is a busy area and not much information of what to do and how to get in and etc.

reviews.author: Gez Beck
reviews.title: Tourist attraction
reviews.content: You need to take a hat as there is no shade  whilst there a short walk to see the single pillar pagoda which is beautiful. Lots of small stalls around it with trinkets to buy. Beautiful place to take pictures

reviews.author: Hoang Do
reviews.title: Big Green Space
reviews.content: The last I was inside the mausoleum was more than ten years ago, so I don't know what it's like now. However, I frequently pass by the field in front of mausoleum, and the people seem to be doing a nice job. As a citizen of Hanoi, I really need to commend the upkeep of the place.

reviews.author: peter g
reviews.title: Propaganda entral
reviews.content: Not worth the time in line. No sense of the person. More like visiting a wax museum with armed guards. Spend time at the citadel and ethnographic museum.

reviews.author: Tracey G
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Wasn’t quite what I was expecting. Not too busy and the queues kept moving. No pictures allowed inside but then you get your cameras backA must do when in Hanoi

reviews.author: Sushant Khera
reviews.title: Huge, beautiful and with historic importance!!!
reviews.content: It is a glimpse into the great leader ho chi minhs life during the Vietnam war. It is a stark contrast to the huge independence palace used by south Vietnam's leaders. The palace is beautiful. Do not carry lighters as security check will not let it pass. Food, drinks available inside. Few souvenir shops. Clean bathrooms. No need of a guide.

reviews.author: Jason S
reviews.title: Quite place of reflection
reviews.content: What a beautiful place Very clean Very wide and open away from the Hanoi traffic You won’t get run over by a moped here

reviews.author: Mary LC
reviews.title: Ho chi minh mousoleum
reviews.content: Visiting this place is showing us how locals and other countries their love and appreciation to this great leader.  I for one is not aware that he is well preserved to let other people know ow grateful they are to him. The first part of the visits,  people are not allowed to take pictures...  So i only have this coz this is the are where you can take pictures.When you have this trip dont bring big bags..

reviews.author: Melanie M
reviews.title: Make sure your shoulders are covered
reviews.content: There are a ton a people selling stuff in side the gates which surprised me. Other than that everything was nice, just make sure you have you shoulders covered or you won’t be aloud in

reviews.author: Malcolm C
reviews.title: Important history.
reviews.content: This site has excellent information about Ho Chi Minh and his role in the Vietnam War. He was much more civilised than the propaganda we were fed in New Zealand at the time, as evidenced by the decent treatment of US pilots such as John McCain. This was way more civilised than the French treatment of Cambodian rebels earlier in Vietnam's complex history. Seeing the simple "hut" he worked from and reading about his desire to make Vietnam independent made it clear why so many of us were against the awful intrusion by the US and allies with napalm, bombs and other offences.

reviews.author: Jay K
reviews.title: A must do in Hanoi
reviews.content: We visited as part of an organised tour so got a great history lesson thrown in. An absolute must when visiting Hanoi as it puts Vietnam completely into context.

reviews.author: Victor M
reviews.title: Not to be Missed
reviews.content: More than just a mausoleum as there are large grounds gardens and buildings of Vietnamese history. Immaculately laid grounds enclosing historical places and artifacts. We spent several hours here with our well informed guide.

reviews.author: Dafna Messing
reviews.title: Wow
reviews.content: Definitely one of the top cultural experiences i was engaged in.Do not bring water- you cannot enter with it

reviews.author: Anupam_Chakrabarti
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: Absolutely must see. A lot of walking is required to reach the mausoleum but it's worth it. No cameras or photos allowed. Seems Ho Chi Minh is sleeping in a bed just as we have seen him in photos.

reviews.author: mrswills1
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: A symbol of the esteem in which this leader is held. Tight dress restrictions - no bare shoulders. Tight control of where you can walk.Definitely worth visiting.

reviews.author: Debs362014
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: Huge queue to get in but it moved quickly. Dont take water or food as it will be confiscated. Women must have covered shoulders. An interesting experience. The gardens an Museum  are worth a visit afterwards.

reviews.author: Carol O
reviews.title: Worth the wait
reviews.content: Waited in line for 2 hours, piece of advice watch out for the Chinese they try to push past to the front of the queue which moves fairly quickly once the mausoleum actually opens its doors at 9. Everybody stays strictly in line all the way and we filed past took a whole 30 seconds but can say been there done that.

reviews.author: SamT
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: May after visiting Halong bay and Ninh Binh, we were looking for something special and We felt there was not much here. We would not regret if we didn't have a photo in front of it. If would are desperate for a photo,  you can have it from roadside and it would be the same.

reviews.author: Cee Jay
reviews.title: Interesting experience
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body is on display in a timber/glass casket in this building. The amount of security we had to go through was amazing. No drink, food, camera, mobile phone, chewing gum and you put your bag away to be locked. Hundreds of people in a line up to get into here, but the line was constantly moving over the 15 min walk. Guards everywhere and 4 at all times around his body. They file you in pairs of two and you are not allowed to stop. Such a surreal experience looking at this man under a soft light looking peaceful.Get here early, from 8am, or if you leave it too late you will be denied entry.  Entrance to see his body is free and I was glad we did this on our last day.After seeing Ho Chi Minh's body you have the choice to buy additional entrance tickets.1. Vestige in the Presidential Palace area VND40,000 per person, can't go into the Palace though and limited entrance into buildings but a nice walk.2. Ho Chi Minh Museum which is on the same grounds cost VND40,000 per person, is just another museum and we had seen many before so knew a lot about the history, take it or leave it but the Museum building itself is very impressive inside.Allow at least 3 hours to do all.

reviews.author: michael p
reviews.title: Not much to see
reviews.content: The mausoleum was not open so we saw the outside and Ho's house. Worth a look, nothing very interesting there and was free.  It is not far from the Old Quarter.

reviews.author: Patti C
reviews.title: A must see
reviews.content: This was a great sightseeing activity. Photo opportunity but that’s about it We walked there from around the lake area. Was interesting seeing the sights along the wayGet a cab to or from there and expect to be ripped offWalking for public transport best

reviews.author: Dhennver Ng
reviews.title: Just putting my mark
reviews.content: You can't miss this place if you are in Hanoi. It's a landmark but i didn't quite need to go in to see.... The locals here idolises HCM. You have to walk through security at the parameters. No singlets allowed.

reviews.author: Ash Mehta
reviews.title: Amazing place with tribute to Ho
reviews.content: Magnificent place to visit this very strictly controlled mausoleum.We stared very early and still found large que.Lots of security to clear, but once you enter the ground you feel history and peaceful place.After eating in line for 25 minutes you enter the place and spend maximum five minutes.The grounds are worth walking around.Take as little as possible ,no cameras allowed and have to deposit it locker rooms.At the end you have to walk quite a distance to collect them.So leave behind or be prepared to waste time.

reviews.author: Sebastian Q
reviews.title: #Vietnam2019 weeklong vacation
reviews.content: Of Course a must visit place in Hanoi!Uncle Ho’s body is still there and one can quickly see it under very strict supervision. You can clearly feel the reverence given to this great leader by a grateful nation. No photos allowed...

reviews.author: Indonesian-Jetset
reviews.title: Memorial Place
reviews.content: Must visit this Landmark. It is very nice Landmark to visit. Where they put the body in this Mausoleum.The garden around the Mausoleum also very pretty.

reviews.author: Ryo
reviews.title: Wheelchair Users Beware of Incompetent Whims
reviews.content: Technically, we didn’t get past the security checkpoint, so I can’t say much about the mausoleum itself.But the security gate was nice: modern, clean, and inconsistent.I heard that some wheelchair users on TripAdivsor were able to get in with the mausoleum’s wheelchair, but we weren’t given that option. If Vietnam want to modernize, she needs to work on communication and get rid of the inconsistency — build a protocol and follow it! As a suggestion, the staff at HCM Mausoleum should put more effort into accommodating for people with mobility issues rather than outright barring people interested in the revolutionary leader who created the country we know. In any case, powered wheelchair users should just avoid this place, don’t play by others’ whims and do something more worthy of your time.

reviews.author: Stephanie J
reviews.title: Lots of history, beautiful campus.
reviews.content: This was a neat experience. We were able to view Ho Chi Minh, the One Pillar Pagoda and the Stilt House. There were more guards and military around,but we didn't have any problems. Be respectful, wear modest clothing and realize many people are on a pilgramich and not a tourist attraction. I recommend getting advice from a local on the best time to visit because the hours can seem confusing, but we didn't have any problems.

reviews.author: Wayne
reviews.title: Beware closed on Mondays Fridays and afternoons
reviews.content: Only got to see it from the outside as we were ushered away by officials and the opening times are very rigid. Hard to walk to from the old quarter and fences make it hard to get closer to see anything. Nicely maintained from what we could see.

reviews.author: Wulandarie W
reviews.title: Nice place that I can visit when I'm at Vietnam
reviews.content: The place was nice and extraordinary good. The mausoleum also representative for the tourist. We can see the former President of Vietnam too. Nice explanation from the rour guide too.

reviews.author: Milceyboy
reviews.title: Beautiful monument to a Vietnam Leader
reviews.content: Visited the mausoleum recently, can't go directly inside though as it's blocked by military staff. You have to pay to enter Ho Chi Minhs actually house and gardens though.And there aren't many signs outside to actually find a way into the area. Nice area to spend an hour or two

reviews.author: Julie F
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: The entrance is a journey in itself. No lighters allowed inside. No food or drink past the entrance although they are available just before the exit  (lol)  Allow a minimum of 30 minutes in the sun get to any of the buildings and /or information. Once inside information and buildings are nothing to write about.

reviews.author: Momo_yeu_sunny
reviews.title: Monument to a beloved figure
reviews.content: A great conversation starter with young minds, I had a fantastic chat with my 9 year old daughter about communism, political systems, progress and more all starting from the question "What is a mausoleum?" and it's a powerful tribute to Vietnam's most beloved leader. Also worth a look is some of the other government buildings in the area if you have some time for a wander.

reviews.author: Paul Lawrence
reviews.title: Long walk
reviews.content: A long walk from the old quarter but worth the health outcomes.....once at the Mausoleum it’s huge and striking and the history was engaging and interesting. The WC for females was poor and not clean.

reviews.author: Johan Zarn
reviews.title: Very beautiful and memorable!!!
reviews.content: You had better get up early in the morning to join the queue to get in. Very beautiful and memorable place that you should visit. Ho Chi Minh is their Great Leader of all time. Respect him!!!

reviews.author: GermanShepherdDog
reviews.title: Everything was closed with no information
reviews.content: Visited late morning. We were allowed in to the complex only to find that the Mausoleum, Museum and Presidential home were randomly closed with no information on opening times. We got waved away by guards when we tried to read information panels, and sent out of the pagoda by monks who were busy on their smart phones inside the temple. The complex is clean and interesting but we were disappointed and a little perplexed as to why everything was closed. A little information would go a long way!

reviews.author: ExplorerGabor
reviews.title: Peaceful
reviews.content: There was no queue to enter the mausoleum today though based on the queueing lanes it must get really busy.  HCM looks peaceful in his mausoleum.  We also walked around the traditional houses and past the Presidents palace.  Nice and cool walking under the huge trees.

reviews.author: Rainsford61
reviews.title: Mr Jordan Rainsford
reviews.content: It was fantastic to see the preservation site of one of the most historic political figures in the country's history. The tour guide showed immense passion and pride in showing us a major part of his home nations history.

reviews.author: Adam Pham
reviews.title: the Ba Dinh Square, and Ho Chi Minh complex
reviews.content: it takes 20 minutes by taxi from the old quarter there, and it is worthy!you will see why Ho Chi Minh is important to Vietnamese people

reviews.author: Marc Holt
reviews.title: A MUST if you visit Hanoi
reviews.content: This structure is amazing!The access is free of charges, but you have to wake up early in the morning if you want to see something. Is part of a building complex of many other historical and official buildings, that are nice to visit.

reviews.author: KGB777
reviews.title: Restricted opening times
reviews.content: I came in the middle of the day and by that time the mausoleum was already closed. Because it was meant to be a family trip, I didn't get the chance to visit on the other days in Hanoi. So I just have to be content that I already visited this about 10 years back on my last visit to Hanoi. The opening times are quite restricted so make sure you check in advance if you actually want to go inside the mausoleum.

reviews.author: Anthony R
reviews.title: Peaceful and Respectful
reviews.content: With all the uniformed personnel around the complex it felt a little intimidating, but it was very well organised. It was a shame we couldn’t spend more time with the man, but I think this is why this site stood out from other similar landmarks around the world.

reviews.author: Latif T
reviews.title: Interesting to see uncle ho
reviews.content: The housing area / museum wasn’t really worth to see but the mausoleum was a really good experience. 40.000 entry for the area housing etc Another 40 for the museum locals can enter free

reviews.author: D.j. B
reviews.title: If you are in to this kind of thing...
reviews.content: To me, this was a great experience. Never viewed a dead communist leader until now. When you first get there, it is a little confusing because they tell you to put your electronics and cameras in a bag (that they supply you) that you have to check in to their window. I ask them if that includes iPhones and they tell me now so I had no issues carrying my iPhone into the building. My wife had a Sony camera that we had to leave with the front window clerk but they let us keep our phones on us which I thought made no sense. We walk through a line up into the building where Ho Chi Minh is laid to rest with guards everywhere. When you enter the room where he is laid, you CAN NOT take pictures or you WILL get called out. We walk in the room where Ho Chi Minhs body is displayed and its dark and cold. His body and skin tone is white but he still has his signature FuManChu. You walk in a single file line around him while guards are at every corner. The room is dark while his glass casket is lit up like he is an angel. When I walked in front of the casket I could see up his nose. Great experience but maybe not for young kids that don't understand.DRESS CODE: Wear something presentable or they will not let you in. Guys, you can wear shorts but the ends need to be at your knees or longer and also wear shoes. No sandles. Make sure that what you are wearing is conservative.

reviews.author: Lara
reviews.title: Interesting experience
reviews.content: Interesting experience despite being rushed through the main room in less than a minute. Worth visiting but come early to avoid the crowds.

reviews.author: Ushandra
reviews.title: His corpse looked unreal
reviews.content: Very interesting history and any Vietnamese has the highest respect for HoChi Minh. He seems a visionary but mostly humble. Great place to visit but go early, ques for the mosleum part can get long.  Worth the trip.

reviews.author: Alejandra LAG
reviews.title: Interesting but politically sensitive
reviews.content: This one is an experience with many possible sides. If in Vietnam and want to see the corpse and house of one of its most relevant characters, head hear. If you, on the other hand, don’t care about the politics or have strong feelings against personality cults, then definitely skip this place.

reviews.author: Madame_Trey
reviews.title: A lesson in living well
reviews.content: To understand how much Uncle Ho is well loved by the Vietnamese, a trip to the mausoleum is a must.The expansive and well kept grounds are a testament to his philosophy. Live simply but live well.It's incredible to imagine him strolling his grounds.The mausoleum is a must visit tourist and local destination. I recommend visiting in the afternoon, when the throngs of visitors die down and you can enjoy the grounds in peace.

reviews.author: walkasone
reviews.title: Interesting and moving at the same time
reviews.content: On a good day it only takes 20 or so minutes to see Ho Chi Minh lying in the crypt. If you see a line of people just join it. It was actually a moving experience and unexpected emotion so can imagine what the Vietnamese feel. There is no entry fee to go into the Mausoleum. There is a fee to visit the botanic gardens next door where you see Ho Chi Minh’s living quarters/house.

reviews.author: 188petere
reviews.title: Very organised & easy process
reviews.content: A large modern air conditioned building is home to the body. A very impressive marble building built by the Russians in a Russian style. Lots of guards in their formal whites add to the spectacle. Quite a process & walk to access it but all flat & under cover. Very hot in sun.One pillar Pagoda within the same complex. seemed to be quite a bit of transport in the area - we were on a bus trip.Security is tight - no big bags or big cameras or food/fluids. No photos inside.

reviews.author: AWCostless
reviews.title: Very impressive
reviews.content: Lots of rules,no hats, no sunglasses, knees and shoulders covered, no cameras, no food or drinks, but going passed the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh was quite an experience. Next to the Mausoleum is the park and different houses he lived in, well worth the visit.

reviews.author: Euan
reviews.title: Worth a visit but not a whole lot to see
reviews.content: It was quite cool to see this but there isn’t much to do there. There is a museum there too but it wasn’t open when we were there.

reviews.author: mark19620727
reviews.title: This is a must visit if you appreciate the political history of Vietnam
reviews.content: It was a very surreal experience being so close to the body of such an iconic person in the history of Vietnam.  But a visit to the Mausaleum is more than seeing Ho Chi Minh in his resting place.  The chance to view his homes & the beautiful gardens around the Presidential Palace were well seeing.

reviews.author: Andrew R
reviews.title: Worth the Experience
reviews.content: The queue was short and the wait was worth it. The short journey around Ho Chi Minh was an experience for the whole family and raised a lot of questions from my daughter. Unfortunately you are unable to take pictures inside. And make sure the ladies cover their knees.

reviews.author: Cindy Marie Azur
reviews.title: Good place to visit
reviews.content: It’s a must I Guess to visit this place as it’s open place and great to understand the history behind it 👍

reviews.author: Kalyani G
reviews.title: Quick trip
reviews.content: It was a quick trip because:-temperature was mid 30 celcius-not sheltered walkway-ho chi minh's tomb was closed (Mondays and Fridays) -attraction closes by middayPositives- nice gardens- good display of cars and buildings used by ho chi minh- costs on 40k dong per person

reviews.author: Dean M
reviews.title: Great morning out
reviews.content: This is a fascinating place. Well recommended. The Pagoda outside is lovely and the museum articles are great. Only open in the morning though

reviews.author: doctorfoxtrot
reviews.title: Just for photo ops
reviews.content: Quite frustrating to miss the chance going inside this deeply historical place in a political sense. Lines are long that we forego the wait since we need to visit some sights.  Next time we visit Hanoi I’ll be ready.

reviews.author: ritchieorlando
reviews.title: Historical purpose
reviews.content: I think if u interested in history you should visit this mausoleum. Pay for 40.000 each person to visit this complex

reviews.author: Liyhc5
reviews.title: Eye opener...
reviews.content: We came here on our first day and whilst it was relatively interesting to read more about Vietnamese history, it was more interesting to see how biased everything was! Essentially every museum in Hanoi is an appreciation society of the former leader, Ho Chi Minh. Slightly propaganda-like from our view. I still would actually recommend visiting the museums as it is an insight into the culture but probably would take it with a pinch of salt!

reviews.author: Brent
reviews.title: Worth a look
reviews.content: The HCM mausoleum and museum are located all within the same property. The mausoleum is definitely the highlight for sure. First thing to note is that women must have shoulders covered and their skirts or shorts must cover the knees. If you’re wearing shorts you’ll have to go across the street and buy a skirt/ wrap for 90k dong. Guys can’t wear sleeveless shirts either. The mausoleum is free but once you exit you are guided towards the presidential palace and other buildings and coy ponds. This cost 40k dong per person. If you want you can go into the museum for a additional 40k dong per person. We personally found the mausoleum interesting and the palace really nice. The museum in our opinion was kinda boring and nothing really exciting in it.

reviews.author: JimOtto
reviews.title: Great Historical Site
reviews.content: Enjoyed the tour of the site!  Loved the cars used by Ho Chi Minh, and the sparse residence he lived in.  Great history lesson.

reviews.author: Mrs Evans
reviews.title: Mrs Karen Evans
reviews.content: Too hot in the sun and too many rules and the entrance is not sign posted so a long walk was necessary. You even have to buy your toilet paper. Avoid.

reviews.author: Liz G
reviews.title: Visit to the Mausoleum
reviews.content: We were lucky it seems as the embalmed body of Ho Chi Min was elsewhere when we visited hence we avoided an hour long queue. The gardens were very beautiful and his 1950s house on stilts, his cars and the other properties were interesting to see. I would recommend a tour guide/ audio tour to understand it within the context of Vietnamese culture. The tranquility was great within the grounds to escape the chaos of the City.

reviews.author: Kiwi_Bliss
reviews.title: A must in Hanoi
reviews.content: Fascinating. I learnt so much. Very formal. Make sure you wear conservative covered clothing. Be prepared to hand in day bags. Hand bags were ok. This does close by midday and I’m not sure when the last entry is so check this out or go early. Quite expansive so also includes Ho Chi Minh museum and stilt house so a real bonus to easily get round all these sites in one location. really special. One of my highlights of Hanoi

reviews.author: 1traveladdictcom
reviews.title: Beautiful gardens and historical site
reviews.content: Visiting the mausoleum and watching the guards ..the amszing respect of the people for this leader.  Stoping at temple on the property as well as visiting museum was informative

reviews.author: KiranJ1303
reviews.title: Average
reviews.content: While its a highly respected place, there is not much to see. And my guide was no help at all as he was in a rush to get us out of there

reviews.author: Justine P
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: Moving is the best world that I can use to describe this mausoleum. The Vietnamese people loved their leader and it shows! No trip to Hanoi is complete without visiting Ho Chi Minh’s mausoleum!

reviews.author: Jean-Pierre K
reviews.title: A Must for every visitor to Ha Noi
reviews.content: To pay respects to the founder of this now great emerging nation, it is almost incumbent on visitors to visit the mausoleum of the revered "Uncle" Ho Chi Minh. Queues can be long so try to avoid weekends when many Vietnamese visitors visit the capital. The entrance is often quite crowded but once inside beyond the ticket office, on a normal working day, the fairly long trek though corridors, across yards and parade grounds the queue moves fairly swiftly, although there are pauses to allow pre-booked groups go go ahead. The body lying in state is up a medium sized staircase with guards posted at intervals. You may have to leave elements of your personal belongings behind - cameras and mobile phones, for example; and once inside the state room where the body lies, you will have to walk fairly briskly around the mausoleum before exiting into the courtyard - from there one can visit the Museum and the one-legged Pagoda but there is an entrance fee - which allows you to visit the former home of the leader and get glimpses of his life-style, even seeing the cars he drove or was driven in at that time! it is well worth making the trip. Afterwards getting a taxi back to the old quarter is pretty easy except when it is raining and all the taxis are full.

reviews.author: Harvey S
reviews.title: A Sight
reviews.content: This was something to see and visit.  Would not want to miss it.  You need time to walk around inside and then to walk around outside but you do not want to miss seeing it.  Make sure you have plenty of time as there are long lines but you move quickly.

reviews.author: Praful G
reviews.title: Ok Place
reviews.content: This place is very significant for the vietnamese people and has a big square in front of it. Nothing much to see in it but still has a nice surrounding. The guards stand there for hours without moving an inch.

reviews.author: michaelkS1933CR
reviews.title: Interesting monument
reviews.content: Unfortunately, closed during summer, but still worth seeing. The are is very pretty, lots of walking, but well worth the visit.

reviews.author: Stephanie H
reviews.title: Definitely Worth A Visit!
reviews.content: If you are planning to visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum,do go early. The place is closed on Mondays & Fridays. Opening time is from 8am to 11am. You will need to be decently attired and have to go through body & bag screening. If you have backpacks there is a storing facility available. If you hv a small handbag, they just let you go in while bigger handbags are given a blue recycle bag to put that in to certify that you had gone through screening and to return that bag after your visit. We are told by the guards to line up in two rows. There are few stops in between which are done in an orderly fashion under shaded walkway. When we approach closer to the main doors, there are signs to stop using your mobile devices. After that, we were guided to go into the building. When you go in, it is in a dimmed light and we are told to walk to the left then up a flight of stairs, so pls be careful not to fall. Then we come to a guarded room when we see Ho Chi Minh's body lying serenely and in peace & nicely embalmed! We are told to continue walking and not stop while our eyes are glued to him! Maybe around 15 seconds opportunity to do that then it is all over as we take the flight of stairs down and guided out of the building.

reviews.author: TheNemo
reviews.title: What a nice place to visit!
reviews.content: I love Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh mausoleum  is one of must go place when you visit Hanoi. You can get the ticket with just 2 USD and I'm so comfortable to pay for it. Love

reviews.author: Shira B
reviews.title: Flag ceremony
reviews.content: There is a flag ceremony at 6 am in the morning.  The only reason we were there at this time was we arrived on the night train from Sa Pa early in the morning.  So it was interesting looking at the many many people doing their morning sport activity.  We were surprised at the number of people doing that.... They all stopped what the do when the flags where up and the national song was playing.  These people are very proud of their country and their culture

reviews.author: Kim L
reviews.title: Beautiful gardens
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit even if the tomb is not open . Beautiful gardens  with lots of history about Ho Chi Minh.

reviews.author: Zuzka123
reviews.title: Not that interesting - mausoleum and presidential palace
reviews.content: Mausoleum is apparently shut in July and August due to preservation work on uncle Ho, so you can just walk around the building and the presidential palace gardens. Loads of local tourist. Women should wear “respectable clothes “ - this means no naked shoulders, short skirts or shorts. You tick the box and move onto another sight...

reviews.author: Jasmine
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: Very interesting place and a lot of  history - however the main section was closed upon visit (5pm Monday)  Females make sure you have something to cover up bare shoulders!

reviews.author: FlipViet
reviews.title: Long line for a 15 seconds look
reviews.content: Go early in the morning. Prepared to be screened like going through airport security. Then there maybe a long line to wait and shuffle  towards the mausoleum. Seems like there are guards at almost every turn. You are being watched through the entire time from entrance to exit. The ground are beautifully kept. But you are not allowed to walk around the ground.Once reached the inner chamber, everyone must keep moving with the line. You are not allowed to pause to view. You probably have 15-25 seconds to look as you must keep moving along with the line.

reviews.author: Sharif Razi Al Mahmud
reviews.title: Historical Place to Visit
reviews.content: Should visit a bright sunny day. Best place for photography and surrounding area also nice. 3/4 Visiting spot in close of this place so nice place to visit.

reviews.author: Troy M
reviews.title: Get the timings right!!
reviews.content: Most Important. GET YOUR TIMINGS RIGHT. This place works on a timing of its own. No site on the web can give you an accurate schedule and no local tour operator will give you accurate details as they want your business and rather you take a tour with them. Get there nice and early. Before 8am and you will be lucky enough to go inside. We go there late. At 945am and they didn’t let us in. So we had to settle for the photos on the outside and could not go inside to see the body. Dress well as they are strict about the attire if you go inside to view the embalmed body. We missed out, hope you get to see it.

reviews.author: sophie d
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Again, with a free half day tour with a local student, I could learn about Ho Chi Minh, and it was very interesting. The tour is a must while getting in Hanoi to see and have a better idea of the history

reviews.author: Chandrashekar Naik
reviews.title: Nice one..
reviews.content: We had been to this place along with friends and family. Architecture of building is very beautiful and it’s opposite you can see The Vietnam assembly.View is very nice, better to visit in the evening time bcoz it’s summer in Hanoi now, you can click beautiful views and take good pics.Carry umbrella and sun lotion.Be careful with local taxi guys , don’t just get into local taxi before asking the price. we were got cheated by local taxi guy,while travelling from PK restaurant from old quarters to HO Chi Minh Mausoleum , taxi guy charged VND 400000 that was too huge charge.It’s better to carry small hand fans to enjoy the climate due to its humidity.

reviews.author: Sue
