reviews.title: Plan to visit this place during early morning
reviews.content: It is a historically important place to visit in Ha Noi.  However, I would say that it was not easy to find the entrance.  Also, keep in mind that it is closed during a long lunch break from 10:30 or 11:00 (not sure, pls check) until 2pm.  Also, afternoon visit does not last long either.If you plan well, I believe it worth visiting.

reviews.author: Peter
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: While the site is not hugely impressive in terms of things to see, the history behind does make it worth a visit. Definitely read up a little before going.

reviews.author: Bandeppa Biradar
reviews.title: Nice Architecture and Structure
reviews.content: Nice architecture and historic place. It was closed when we went so couldn’t mange to go in but spent some time outside . Worth to visit this place .

reviews.author: Chita & Nigel
reviews.title: Imposing
reviews.content: A fine example of Soviet era architecture. Worth the short journey from the city centre and don't miss the street with many embassies closeby for some contrasting buildings.

reviews.author: Jennifer R
reviews.title: Walk Through Like Lemmings
reviews.content: Yes- probably a place to visit- but I felt over saturated by the militia watching every step. We were marched through with not a minute to stop and appreciate the history and integrity of the place. Don’t bother going - and if you do- take a water bottle, a hat, an umbrella and sunscreen- you’ll need it.

reviews.author: RieksLok
reviews.title: Respect for Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: Mausoleum for a great leader.  Impressive and massive.  When visiting you get to understand the greatness of Ho Chi Minh.  Although it was not his wish, the majority respects Ho Chi Minh.

reviews.author: John Q
reviews.title: A sense of history
reviews.content: This imposing structure, located in Ba Dinh Square, is the final resting place of Ho Chi Minh (1880-1969). It is a ‘must see’ when in Hanoi. It’s a heavy grey granite structure and is likely modeled on Lenin’s mausoleum in Moscow. We were satisfied to admire it from a distance

reviews.author: Graeme R
reviews.title: Interesting place
reviews.content: Kind of quirky and not what you would expect. I strange mixture of old doctrinated (is that even a word) writings and scripture mixed with popular culture and modern art. It is worth a visit if only to pay homage to a great man and founding father of a unity Vietnam.

reviews.author: giji365
reviews.title: Another must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: You can't say you visited Hanoi, if you haven't visited the Mausoleum. The embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh is kept here. He looks like just gone to sleep. More than that, it's the building that attracts you along with its history.

reviews.author: Volodymyr
reviews.title: Interesting cultural experience
reviews.content: I found this strange as appointments go! I have never been to several mausoleum as well as discovered a body lying in state. The cue typically shows up long, but don't be switched off by this, it moves at a more comfortable speed. Additionally, make sure you're going quite in the beginning as to avoid the great bulk of people! so no time being around! Really intriguing insight into this specific time of the story of Vietnam. A historic and dramatic experience but check times while you've to visit AM plus it is not open every day

reviews.author: historiker_13
reviews.title: This is a must on every Trip to Vietnam! Uncle Ho worth it.
reviews.content: The place is well kept and you get a sight into Uncle Ho's daily life while in Hanoi. Don't expect too much but a serene place and a well kept palace ans mausoleum sight. This man is loved by nearly all Vietnamese People and not only. #forpeaceandfriendship

reviews.author: Sainesy
reviews.title: Worth a stop if you have a guide
reviews.content: It's a big space with Ho Chiinh's mausalium. It wasn't open when we went. Not much to see but our guide gave us a great history which made it all the more interesting

reviews.author: B New
reviews.title: Impressive sense of reverence
reviews.content: Security check quick and easy.Very beautiful gardens and temple behind the mausoleum itself -- worth a visit for these alone. Refreshments available.We didn't explore the whole site, so perhaps even more further in. Perhaps more on the life of the Bringer of Light?

reviews.author: fozjon
reviews.title: Closed in the afternoon
reviews.content: I'm glad that I got to see the mausoleum and the Ho Chi Minh area of Hanoi. I knew before I left that the mausoleum would be closed, so, not a problem

reviews.author: Steve W
reviews.title: Fine Communist Edifice.
reviews.content: There is no doubt this is a mausoleum for a national hero.Hard looking and symbolic of the communist era that it represents.

reviews.author: Govindan N
reviews.title: An Interesting Place
reviews.content: The place where the revered Father Of The nation - Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body is kept for worship by a grateful nation. Though there was a long queue we could see the embalmed body. The crowd was quiet and respectful. No Photography is allowed inside the Mausoleum. We did take some photos outside the Mausoleum. An interesting place to visit in Hanoi

reviews.author: steadfast90
reviews.title: Simplistic
reviews.content: Beautiful gardens and surroundings which are well maintained. A highly respected president and figure He led a very simplistic lifestyle. An important historical sight in Hanoi. Fortunate we caught the changing of the guards as well, this was very interesting. A worthwhile experience.

reviews.author: Tran Ngoc Qui
reviews.title: A historical site where uncle rest his life!
reviews.content: This is one of the most impressive attraction which is a must when visiting Ha Noi. This is where the great president of Vietnam rest and his body was reserved very well.

reviews.author: Feragne V
reviews.title: We were told to visit but nothing is in English
reviews.content: Wish they had had more English so we could have understood.  Thank goodness we read up on it prior to our visit.   Warning!!!   Closes early in the day.

reviews.author: Ellen
reviews.title: Only the Outside View
reviews.content: This historic sight in Hanoi is very well maintained.  It was only to be viewed from the outside when I visited.  Watching the changing of the guards was interesting.  It is probably the most important historical sight in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Carol W
reviews.title: Cultural Visit
reviews.content: This was a great insight into the history of Hanoi and Vietnam. Especially the character of Ho Chi Minh .It was not clear from the online information that women had to be have their shoulders and legs covered..When we arrived I had thin strapped t short and my daughter had shorts. They wanted us to buy 2 scarfs each to cover up.Luckily we had sarongs and didn’t have to buy.You can spend at least a few hours as it’s a 6 hectare sight.There are many restaurants and cafes outside , and if you walk through from Doi Can you exit at West Lake.

reviews.author: nidkirm
reviews.title: Was closed so just saw it from outside
reviews.content: The mausoluem is apparently closed every summer for three months for maintenance, so I just saw it from outside. Visited the museum in the same complex, which was very interesting though.

reviews.author: William
reviews.title: great place
reviews.content: This is the most famous place in Hanoi. It is very sacred to Vietnamese people. Any Vietnamese must come here once when going to Hanoi

reviews.author: michelle b
reviews.title: vietnam
reviews.content: this was very interesting and is next to the presidents residence when he is in.well worth a look but keep to the paths unless the guards will be all over you

reviews.author: Romulus
reviews.title: Interesting, but not a must
reviews.content: The mausoleum is the appreciation and respect prof of the Vietnamese people for Uncle Ho, the founder of independent Viet Nam. It was build in cooperation with Russia, being inspired by the Lenin Mausoleum.It is in the political and administrative quarter of Ha Noi. There is also a large square where the parades take place on National Day.It is closed in June and July for maintenance.

reviews.author: Colin G
reviews.title: Nice experience
reviews.content: It was a nice experience. A lot of things were in Vietnamese, not so much in English. You could get a guide though who can explain things better. It was nice to get some information about Ho Chi Minh.

reviews.author: BCSinig
reviews.title: View the changing of the guard
reviews.content: The only real interesting part of this stop on our Hanoi Tour was the changing of the guard. The Mausoleum was large but lacked the style of the other monuments in Hanoi.

reviews.author: ToonTowner
reviews.title: Don't bother
reviews.content: A very long wait for a 20 second peak at Ho Chi Minh. To me it wasn't worth the wait. For others it might.

reviews.author: Stuart W
reviews.title: Lovely gardens and buildings
reviews.content: Beautifully laid out and spacious area. Interesting to note the Buddhist style life of Ho Chi Minh and to view his various homes and motor vehicles during his time in office.Definitely a must visit attraction.

reviews.author: Jacki H
reviews.title: Interesting to learn more about Ho Chi Minh but the mausoleum is closed until 14 August 2019 for renovations
reviews.content: Interesting to see and hear more about Vietnam’s highly revered leader. I really enjoyed seeing the different houses within the complex built for him by the government over the years. The gardens are also an oasis away form the organised chaos of Hanoi streets. Interesting trees (check out how their roots grow!), lotus and lily ponds and bonsai trees which provide some great photo opportunities. Recommended to learn more about how the Vietnamese people regard their leader.

reviews.author: Aped308
reviews.title: Closed for maintenance
reviews.content: The 2 stars rating is only because there is no information about the closure for maintenance. We were aware of the place being closed on Mondays and Fridays, but there was no information about it being closed for longer. Disappointed that we couldn't go into the mausoleum, but his museum and the Pagoda were open. Entry for the museum is only free for locals.

reviews.author: sunnivastene
reviews.title: Not there
reviews.content: We didn’t Get to go inside. We were told that Mr Ho sometimes needs to go to Russia for a touch up. Check out if he’s there or not before you go.

reviews.author: Northern Correspondent
reviews.title: Worth the Visit
reviews.content: Part of Vietnam’s history and definitely a place to visit. we were lucky on the day as it wa snot too busy and were able to see the changing of the guard as well.

reviews.author: NN C
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.content: Uncle Ho was under restoration at the time of our visit so we couldn't get into the mausoleum.  We visited the museum next door but to be fair, it lacked in substance and there was little in the way of text for the foreign visitor to read and understand.  It would have been nice to have entered the mausoleum but circumstance prevented it.  Check before you head out to visit.  The museum ism't worth the journey from the city centre alone.

reviews.author: S2417
reviews.title: A historical place not to be missed.
reviews.content: This museum will be the place to know how Vietnam began and how it evolved over the years. A place not to be missed if you are a history buff and good for instagram moments haha

reviews.author: Paul S
reviews.title: Hanoi Highlights
reviews.content: Visited this complex as part of a organized tour of Hanoi. Large crowd and rain on the day.  No cameras in the mausoleum. Strict protocol entering and leaving the mausoleum.

reviews.author: Mai
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh residences
reviews.content: Great place to visit to see Ho Chi Minh’s old residences.   We were unable to enter the Mausoleum during our visit due maintenance.

reviews.author: JJx82
reviews.title: Uncle Ho not home during the summer
reviews.content: I did not know before I went here that the mausoleum undergoes maintenance every summer between June and August, so only the outside could be viewed. The museum was still interesting, although a bit abstract.

reviews.author: nichollsid
reviews.title: Parade Ground and Museum
reviews.content: Mausoleum closed but good to see from outside. Cloudy morning so not hot. Would be terrible if sunny. Museum not that informative as very little English or French signage. Historical photos interesting. Headphones available but we didn’t purchase. May have helped. Displays very “ modernistic” and “symbolic” style. Not enough actual historical artefacts.

reviews.author: Tracey S
reviews.title: Interesting!
reviews.content: Fascinating to walk through the square and see the mausoleum - not sure if you can, but we couldn’t actually go up the steps and inside. There are signs saying no gatherings or photos, but we saw both!I went in above the knee shorts and a vest top and was told to cover up - l’d got a t-shirt and sarong with me, so slipped those on. Did see others wearing shorts, so took off my sarong after a while.

reviews.author: global_teacher
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: Busy and full of information. Unfortunately the mausoleum was closed on the day we visited but still a great visit.

reviews.author: John b
reviews.title: Interesting history & nice architecture
reviews.content: This is one of the most interesting tourist spot in Hanoi for our family. Through tour guide who introduced very details about Ho Chi Minh also french war. Love to see French architecture building surround this are.

reviews.author: Ann O
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: Thoroughly enjoyed our visit to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum we were lucky enough to be there to witness the changing of the guard in the morning

reviews.author: canito1963
reviews.title: Nice!
reviews.content: Very impressive to see how many people waned to see the mausoleum....I waited about an hour and a half to get into the mausoleum and I got inside only took 1 and half minute to see ho chi ming..it was all worth it!

reviews.author: Teresa C
reviews.title: relaxing and majestic
reviews.content: needs to be visited because of ho chi Minh  and interesting feel to it. interesting to see and hear about his modest life

reviews.author: asw71
reviews.title: Closed for maintenance - worth a visit
reviews.content: Recommended a guided tour for the history of ho chi minh. Even though it was closed for maintenance there is lots to see in the surrounding grounds. Must cover knees and shoulders to get through security. Interesting to watch the guards change every 30 minutes.

reviews.author: Jasmine
reviews.title: Closed for maintenance
reviews.content: The mausoleum is closed during the summer months for maintenance, therefore you could not get into the building to look at HCM dead body now. You can spend time wandering around the compound and One Pillar Pagoda, it is free of charge. You will need to go through a security check to get into the compound. You can also pay to get into the museum which is just beside the mausoleum.

reviews.author: Epic-Traveller
reviews.title: Closed 😫
reviews.content: The mausoleum was closed when we arrived! Arghhh our final days in Vietnam and I really wanted to go inside! Oh well.We were allowed around the outside of the building and a little bit around the back by the guards, enough to snap some quick pics as a reminder of what to do when I’m back!

reviews.author: denimw
reviews.title: Would have been interesting if he was there!
reviews.content: Has anyone actually seen Ho Chi Minh? I’ve been twice in 10 years and he wasn’t there. The guide said he gets more embalming done each year from June 15-August 15 so I guess that’s why. The mausoleum itself is huge but that’s all that is there.

reviews.author: Donna A
reviews.title: Amazing building. So beautiful.
reviews.content: Hi Chi Minh is kept inside this building. We were really looking forward to going inside to view his body. Unfortunately the inside was not open to the public when we visited. His body goes overseas in October each year for maintenance, but not sure why it was not open during our visit. There are very strict rules to enter when it is open so make sure you are aware of them if you plan to visit. We still enjoyed seeing this building from the outside, it is quite stunning. The guards protecting him all have to be single men. We still had to cover our shoulders and knees to view this building from the outside. And remember not to cross the line on the footpath, the guards will go crazy at you.

reviews.author: Reyna
reviews.title: AWESOME
reviews.content: Very beautiful place with flowers and green ground. We engage a tour guide (LamHue) for this trip. Well lead, explaination history of  each place to place and able spoke very fluent Mandarin. Few architeral design building surrounding. Can check with your agency if wanted to visit in indeed.

reviews.author: Mlynch
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Interesting visit. Sadly not able to go into mausoleum but the grounds were impressive and interesting.  Very imposing and revealing as to the importance of this leader.

reviews.author: 1000Yossi
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Interesting place in memory of hcm. Can not visit all places i July August but it’s a must see place in Hanoi

reviews.author: engineer2207
reviews.title: Bad bad really bad
reviews.content: I have read about uncle ho and ho chi minh mausoleum alot before travel to Hanoi but i had very bad experience when i was around there. The guards around there treated the guests / foreigners very bad. Thats something to be condemn badly. I do not wish to comment more on it and i would like to forget these bad memory in my trip in Hanoi eventhough i have great respect on Uncle Ho

reviews.author: Mohammed Alam
reviews.title: Really awesome
reviews.content: This place is really very calm n quite. Historical value of this place is also not countable. If anyone visits Hanoi then he/she should visit this mausoleum.

reviews.author: Smashcbe
reviews.title: Visited museum only
reviews.content: Mausoleum was closed in the month of June so we visited the museum which is in the same complex. We had a free guided tour. Our guide Ms Chang was well informed and patriotic. We met her inside the museum. There are lots of artifacts on display. Gives a deep insight into the phenomenal life of Uncle Ho. We took around 1.5-2 hours. Taxi taken from Old Quarter through Passapp charged 27000 VND and on return, the best bargain charged 50,000 VND. Entrance fee to the museum 40 USD.

reviews.author: diannepieterse1
reviews.title: Interesting visit
reviews.content: It was good to view the Mausoleum and the nearby palace.  The changing of the guard takes place every 2 hours, and shouldn't be missed.

reviews.author: emirati_nomad
reviews.title: Beautiful
reviews.content: Beautiful place to visit and pay respect to the man who made Vietnam for what it is today. Thought you can't get that close to it but you can still get close enough.

reviews.author: Francis Martino
reviews.title: Take a tour
reviews.content: Amazing to be able to see Ho Chi Minh Museum.Take a tour at the lovely sights. Great place to feel apart of history as you walk around the building .Very nice landscaping and cool architecture. Wasn't open Mondays.Opening Hours is Tuesday - Thursday 07:30 - 10:30, Saturday & Sunday 07:30 - 11:00We don’t have chance to visit inside if building,time is over.So we just walked outside only.Be sure to dress appropriately especially for ladies and respect the entry rules. Otherwise take scarfs or not wear short skirts .

reviews.author: Mona H
reviews.title: Saw the figure lying in a peaceful sleep!
reviews.content: Ther were ques and ques of local and international visitors waiting patiently to pay their respects to the amazing leader of Vietnam. When we semi-circled around his preserved figure/mummy, we (college group of Tourism course)  were told that his body is kept fresh with continuous and expensive treatment. I remember the child of a couple before me was just "being a noisy kid" you know and he was strictly silenced by parents because it was a solemn procedure. The guards would also remind the visitors to be silent and respectful in addition to being fully dressed like you would when you would visit a Masjid. I went with my college class and teachers of Travel & Tourism in April  2014

reviews.author: Mick M
reviews.title: Resting place for Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: Visited the very impressive Mausoleum in Hanoi. Was disappointed we could not see inside. Too much time required to queue around the block from early morning put the damper on seeing the inside. Immaculately clean and managed befitting the man and nation who stood up to USA

reviews.author: BPWATL
reviews.title: Know for sure if it's open...
reviews.content: Went there with the understanding that it was open but when we arrived we learned otherwise.  Despite this we see that the grounds are beautiful and it was interesting, albeit quite the propaganda lesson, to learn about Uncle Ho and to see where he lived. The party is on overload here with pushing how great he was.  If you take it in good fun it will be worthwhile. Reminds me of trips to Soviet satellite back in the day...

reviews.author: Slk T
reviews.title: Sightseeing
reviews.content: We wanted to see Ho Chi Minh’s stilt residence and the One Pillar Pagoda and didn’t realize that one has to walk through security check point and pass by the Mausoleum to get to the inside of this entire area. It was a very hot day and to go around a huge square just to see the 2 places was quite challenging for the kids. On a good note, the Presidential Palace is right next to the security checkpoint.

reviews.author: DHook
reviews.title: good history; don't miss his stilt-house
reviews.content: Very interesting experience - I don't know what it is about Communist figures being embalmed (Stalin, Lenin, Mao, etc). You're not allowed to take photos in the mausoleum itself; the guards seem pretty intent and this is a no-nonsense Communist government, so definitely comply.We heard that the embalmed body used to be taken to Russia for yearly "maintenance" ; apparently, that is done here now.The grounds are interesting. The mid-1900's stilt-house that Ho Chi Minh lived in is essential to visit. It's fun, historic, and very nicely decorated. Loved it.

reviews.author: Loh
reviews.title: Entrance to the main hall
reviews.content: To visit you must find out whether it's off peak otherwise you have to wait for hours to get in. The purpose is to view the body of their Great Leader Ho Chin Minh.

reviews.author: Arabiak1996
reviews.title: Closed for the month of June-July
reviews.content: I came to visit HCM Mausoleum, but unfortunately they are currently closed for renovations during the months of June and July. I was able to tour the beuatiful surrounding grounds and take pictures, but was unable to visit inside.

reviews.author: Asamie2013
reviews.title: City Tours
reviews.content: Danny our tourguide was very well informed and fluently in english. He was very friendly and was very sympathetic when we complained about the weather

reviews.author: Muzza-X
reviews.title: The worst experience in Vietnam
reviews.content: This is a nasty place to visit. There is little to see and it is mostly closed - it closes for three hours in the middle of the day, ffs. This was an unpleasant experience and a waste of half a day. We are trying not to let it spoil our impression of Vietnam, however. Here is a list of issues, in no particular order:- The entrance is unfathomable difficult to find. - It is closed for half the day and no one seemed to know the opening times. - The guards are unfriendly. - The mausoleum is ugly. - There are no signposts and the site is huge so you end up walking in circles a lot- The museum is worse than useless: just a load of communist propaganda trying to justify the regime. - The one pillar pagoda is deeply unimpressive. - The botanical garden entrance is not at all close and is hard to find, despite being next door. And it is the worst botanical garden I've been to. There is an unnecessary dress code (long trousers). A waste of time - half a day of my life that I won't get back.

reviews.author: Tripped_Ted
reviews.title: Closed !
reviews.content: Really impressive museum and surrounding area. The actual mausoleum is actually closed during the summer months so whilst understandable it was slightly disappointing. Nonetheless it was very impressive and learning about Ho Chi Minh was really interesting.

reviews.author: N_i_b_a_r
reviews.title: A very big park
reviews.content: 1st we have to walk through the parade square. Then we will reach the mausoleum but the time we came, it was closed due to annual restoration so we couldnt see Sir Ho Chi Minh body. We went to this huge park with many houses where he used to stay and his lifestyle. There is a big pond. Good place to take pictures but very warm during the day.

reviews.author: NickT
reviews.title: Well worth a visit.
reviews.content: A very interesting place to visit. Walk around the house and gardens where HCM lived. See him laying in state and visit the museum. A good history lesson.Warning. Check the opening days and times. They do close for various reasons and at lunch time. Plus you must be dressed appropriately and they do restrict the taking of photos in some areas. Always show respect, he is highly revered.

reviews.author: Stephen B
reviews.title: Sobering
reviews.content: Well worth the visit this is a we’ll organise visit and even though time was short it was enough to pay ones respects to a great leader of his people

reviews.author: Irving K
reviews.title: History Vietnam Style
reviews.content: Our visit to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum was the first stop as part of our Buffalo Tours Hanoi City tour. Our guide (Ti) did a great job explaining the history of Vietnam and the rise of Ho Chi Minh. I must admit that I was listening with a skeptical ear as having had an uncle killed in the ‘American’ War as Ti called it with good-natured humor. I was pleased that the history lessons came across as fair and factual. I got past my personal issues and took in the tour as a whole with good intentions. He was very knowledgable and clearly a more modern thinking gentleman than what I had expected. The tour of the mausoleum and surrounding buildings was interesting - but I recommend a guide to really grasp the history and present of Hanoi and Vietnam.

reviews.author: Danglish.adventures
reviews.title: Closed :(
reviews.content: Unfortunately it was closed during our visit and the dress code to enter the park was stricked. We decided to just stroll around the perimeter and appreciate masoulem from a polite distance.

reviews.author: Bis Nicole
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: Very nice because you can meet the first President of Vietnam and the atmosphere there was very special.

reviews.author: Hanners-Trips
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: The entrance is not from the park in front of the Mausoleum and is not very well signposted. It is located at the rear and requires a little walking to find it. The queue may be quite long depending on the time you visit. It is a high security venue and liquids containers and cameras must be left for pickup at allocated collection points after you visit.You can actually see his body and there is a sense of reverence in the mausoleum.

reviews.author: tlynn63
reviews.title: Very impressive
reviews.content: This place is huge and very impressive.  Very somber area.  To get into the area you will need to go through a scanner for purses and backpacks.  We only saw it from the outside and waited for the changing of the guard.  Our guide told us that the hours are restricted and if we wanted to go in on our free day that many schools go there to visit and we should be prepared that the wait can be very long.  The One Pillar Pagoda is a very pleasant stroll nearby and would be worth taking in on the same trip.

reviews.author: Declan H
reviews.title: Peaceful visit
reviews.content: Certainly worth a visit on your trip to Hanoi. A nice peaceful area away from the busy bustling streets. Worth visiting the palace next door once completed.

reviews.author: Mike H
reviews.title: Masoleum closed until Aug 19
reviews.content: You can still go in and visit ‘uncle Ho’s’ house, car collection and stilt house. Of the three his house is the most interesting - the exhibit currently showcases a huge number of photographs of dignitaries he entertained and of his assembled government plotting various movements in the very rooms you can view inside.Don’t plan for a peaceful visit, absolutely packed with other tourists so that you move between and around the 3 sights in the same way as you might queue to get into a music festival. Beautiful grounds but unfortunately not much to learn here

reviews.author: Phillipajc
reviews.title: Apparently there's Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: Do not go by any of the times listed anywhere, ask a local when it's open. We went on a Sunday.... mausoleum not open, museum not open, no signs up giving any information. We went back at 7.45 a.m. on a Wednesday with intentions of queuing up to see Ho...... buses parked up, lots of people around..... this is better than Sunday.... 8 a.m. when you're meant to get access to the viewing of Ho, no doors opening, no queues, ask a helpful guard only to be told it's under maintenance for another 15 days. 'Totally read that - no where!'Wandered to the museum to be abruptly pointed at to buy tickets but no one else was, went through the security check, headed upstairs to check out Ho's life. I had high hopes of learning more of the famous leader. Minimal English, only a single sentence explaining an entire document or important time factor. Everything seemed quite interesting but we got bored with guessing so we turned back to leave and got yelled at. It seems there's only one way around, felt like IKEA in a way but less fun, found the exit - down four flights of stairs out a dingy back door. The gardens are lovely, the pagoda didn't seem like a special place with a coffee shop playing music next door, the drink vending machine doesn't work but again, the gardens are lovely. Up to you if you want to visit, hope you have better luck than we did.

reviews.author: Guest048
reviews.title: Vietnamese culture
reviews.content: It is remarkable to see the emotions and reactions of Vietnamese, as they visit this mausoleum. Arrive early, the queue moves swiftly, and the heat isn't too oppressive!  It's a bizarre experience to see such an important figure of the 20th century, almost 50 years after his death.  We highly recommend visiting the adjacent complex to see and learn more about Uncle Ho, after the mausoleum.

reviews.author: Travelingjohn123
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: It was closed when we went so we only saw it from the outside. We saw enough to realise we need to return to give this justice. It certainly looks impressive from the outside with its beautifully manicured gardens in the complex and marching soldiers. It’s certainly very peaceful after the hustle and bustle of the city.

reviews.author: mosthecat
reviews.title: Spooky
reviews.content: Drastically serious.  That's the mood of the silent, perfectly lit chamber where the supposedly preserved body of the former leader resides, flanked by guards.  No talking, no hands in pockets, no pictures, etc.  The lines can be very long, but after security, our wait was about ten minutes.

reviews.author: WorldTravelManTerry
reviews.title: ONE of the Best things to see in Hanoi
reviews.content: Go early get there by 7 AM. Line ups are long but move at a very steady pace. I thought I would be there the whole day but got through a four block line up in a matter of only a few hours. They are very well organized. Wear appropriate attire otherwsie you will be turned away. Not usually opened on Friday's Or Monday so check first. Also closed for October for maintenance but please check first before you visit Hanoi.. Located in Binh Din Square which in of itself, is a great plaza to see the marching soldiers prior to the opening of the mausoleum and other things. Great spectacle. While you are at it visit the Presidential Palace, Ho Chi Minh's tree house home and car museum, all are in the same plaza. Also the Ho Chi Minh Museum is a must see, also in the same plaza. can be done in the same day. I did it in two.

reviews.author: Paddleboardbb
reviews.title: Queued for ages , so worth the wait
reviews.content: A must do in Hanoi ! An experience , you don’t get this opportunity often . A great man . Take a fan and a hat .

reviews.author: jim b
reviews.title: A learning opportunity
reviews.content: A very interesting and informative visit. Respect is crucial and I found the visit solemn. Very well organised and lots of new information.  A true liberator

reviews.author: HendryD
reviews.title: Quite far from the old town quarter.
reviews.content: If you stay at the old quarter, it is really far to explore by foot and during summer is just hell. The entrance is free to the area. Quite strict with your belonging i.e lighter can't bring inside. In this complex you will find the mausoleum, the one pillar Pagoda and another big museum. The big museum you have to pay to get inside it. It's a really big complex.

reviews.author: Tania T
reviews.title: Sombre mood of visitors
reviews.content: The tour brought us here and we queued for more than one hour just to view the embalmed body of their leader Mr Ho Chi Minh. Well worth the long wait and upon entering no cameras, handphone or wearing of hats are allowed. No noise or talking either, the mood was very solemn and respectful. Guards are strict and they made sure you line up two by two. Upon exit you can visit the grounds which is huge and beautiful, well kept and simply amazing.

reviews.author: Tony L
reviews.title: Viewing Visit
reviews.content: Worth a look. Don’t be put off by the large crowds. The lines move very quickly. And whilst you don’t spend a lot of time seeing Ho Chi Minh, it is worth a visit. The museum is also good that is part of the grounds.

reviews.author: Đức Phong N
reviews.title: Worth to visit once to understand more Vietnam's modern history
reviews.content: I would say if you want to understand more Vietnam's modern history, you should visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleu once.

reviews.author: EWPD
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: Don't be put off by the length of the queue when you first arrive.  It moves quickly and there are covered walkways which provide shade the whole way.  It took around 45 minutes to get in - and that was at a very busy time on a Saturday morning.  The vast majority of the visitors are Vietnamese - paying their respects to a much revered leader.  You should be respectful too - no shorts/short skirts/vest tops....and no photograhpy.  There are signs clearly stating all this - but it was embarrassing to witness a small group of idiot Western tourists trying to get away with taking photos, and then getting annoyed when the guards told them to stop!  Once inside the mausoleum you will be urged to keep walking slowly - past Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body.  He appears quite peaceful, but is very dimly lit.  There are four soldiers guarding his glass-walled coffin, and others standing around the walkway.  All are armed - so don't even think about flaunting the no photography rule!  You exit into the gardens, where you can choose to visit a stilt house that Ho lived and worked in, or a larger museum, or just sit and have an ice cream and enjoy the tranquility.

reviews.author: adelaidesurflifesaver
reviews.title: Amazing place to reflect on history
reviews.content: Amazing place to reflect on history and take many happy snaps. There are also some other touristattractions nearby byt better signage would help to discover them.

reviews.author: kkwalia
reviews.title: Waste of time as inside remain closed most of time
reviews.content: Huge complex, went there twice to look at HO Chi Minh's mummy but they hardly open that area, it get closed early may be they want to avoid tourist's heat. Outer are well planned and maintained. If you want to visit go early by 8 AM.

reviews.author: Valerie R
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Visited here frim one of the stops on the Open Top bus tour. Quite a lot to see although some of the indoor exibitions close in the middle of the day. Still plenty to see if they are closed, plus places to get drinks and snacks and market stalls. Enjoyed our visit

reviews.author: Joanna Gulliver
reviews.title: Recommend a visit
reviews.content: This is a great place to learn a lot of history about Vietnam in one visit. It is a busy place and would pay to arrive early in the morning as they close at lunch for two hours

reviews.author: Clue7
reviews.title: Overrated and too long lines
reviews.content: Went to see the outside but from other tourists who went inside, you can’t take photos, you can’t stop and there are horrendous lines. Even our tour guide said the same thing. Some people told me it would be only good if you see a Vietnamese citizen and were really in love with hi chi Minh; otherwise, as a tourist, probably would just skip this.

reviews.author: scowy68
reviews.title: Essential
reviews.content: A very surreal experience. Obviously still held in high esteem by the people of Vietnam Ho Chi Minh and his life are celebrated here in this beautiful setting.A must do if you visit Hanoi.

reviews.author: Cast@72
reviews.title: Day in Hanoi
reviews.content: Nice visit , I really enjoyed the city tour guide and the site we visited along with the food and cyclo ride.

reviews.author: Praxmeyer
reviews.title: Impressive building
reviews.content: We walked around it. We were going to go in but there were literally thousands of people and we didn’t want to queue in 34 degree heat and 100% humidity. We had arrived a 7.30am thinking we might beat the rush but no such luck.

reviews.author: FisherLiu
reviews.title: Three in One Mausoleum, Presidential Palace, Musuem
reviews.content: Visit the Mausoleum at noon and see the change of guards. Stroll around and wait for 1;30pm for the Presidential Palace to open and  see the residential compound where  the Great Leader of Vietnamese people used to live and work. After that visit the musuem and see the events it has to showcase and learn the history and culture of this interesting nation. Take it nice and easy and enjoy it.

reviews.author: Yoel S
reviews.title: The heart of Vietnamese government
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh mausoleum is one of the government places around Ba Dinh Square, together with the parliament and the presidential palace and more. The mausoleum itself is open only for 2 hours each day with long line before opening hour and strict security measures. But walking in the Square and the garden in the rear side of the mausoleum is nice, especially if you have a tour guide that explains the history of this place.

reviews.author: 391yy
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Very well organised, there were staffs outside the entrance making sure you are in the right dress code, if not you gotta buy a long covered up next door. Dress appropriately and be prepared to queue.

reviews.author: Shauna H
reviews.title: Not worth it
reviews.content: We visited this museum with high expectations considering how loved Ho Chi Mihn is in Vietnam. This museum was very disappointing. It is so hard to follow. The staff are no help and there are many things that I wonder how they had any relevance to the man himself. Not worth the walk or money. Read everything you want to know about this amazing man online or in books.

reviews.author: timboglos
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: I suppose if you are in Hanoi I guess you should visit but it is just a big building in a big square and if you are not into political history it means very little

reviews.author: CollRr
reviews.title: Flag lowering ceremony at night is spectacular.
reviews.content: The flag lowering ceremony at the mausoleum takes place at 9.30pm and is a spectacular event to watch. 34 military men  all the same height and weight march around the square in front of the mausoleum to the sounds of a brass band. The flag is then lowered. Few tourists seem to know about this event, which occurs daily. We also visited the mausoleum during the day and field past Ho Chi Minh in his tomb. The mausoleum during the day can be photographed from directly in front of it. The mausoleum has great symbolism in every way. It is worth having an English speaking guide to point out the various symbols. Lots of school groups visit here and are keen for a high five! Once you have been through the mausoleum , you can then visit the museum in a park like setting and see where Ho Chi Minh lived, studied, the car he used and the hospital.

reviews.author: wendelena50
reviews.title: Superb Historical Visit
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and grounds I found the most interesting in all the visits I did over 30 days in Vietnam. It is very well organised and though it is a very big tourist attraction it is History and it is real and we have all Heard about Ho Chi Minh and it was an Honour to actually see him lying in state.

reviews.author: Kaleena Vanni
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: It's the must visited place in Ha Noi.It's so special.It bring many many to emotion to my mind.I will come back here again.

reviews.author: hem0116
reviews.title: Austere, calm
reviews.content: A welcome calm and quiet oasis in central Hanoi respected by the Vietnamese.The gardens behind the mausoleum have interesting buildings where Ho Chi Minh lived in his final years.  The house on stilts is very elegant

reviews.author: Gerrard
reviews.title: A lovely place to look at the history
reviews.content: Worth a visit, but be careful the lines to get into the mausoleum,can take an hour or so depending on the time you get there and be careful to obey all the signs and don't step over the yellow lines or the officials will blow there whistles and remind you get back over the lines otherwise an memorable experience.

reviews.author: Rajasingam B
reviews.title: Ho Chih Min Mausoleum
reviews.content: THIS IS A MUST DO IN HANOI. For me this was the highlight of my stay. Don’t worry of the long lines, you will get to see him. Don’t fall for short cuts proposed by touts. Dress appropriately. See attached pic on the their house rules. Try to be there early . At least by 9 am.

reviews.author: Deborah P
reviews.title: Mausoleum
reviews.content: I am glad I did this, (ticked off the list) but after querying in the heat for 2 hours, I won't be going again.

reviews.author: Luisa A
reviews.title: Missed out
reviews.content: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex is comprised of the mausoleum, stilt house, Presidential Palace, Museum, and One Pillar Pagoda.What we didn’t know even after looking up the website was that you can only go into the mausoleum in the morning, so we missed the boat on that one.The complex is open, but you only walk past the mausoleum and some of the other attractions there were also closed.Disappointed but not crushed.

reviews.author: Alicia P
reviews.title: Humbling
reviews.content: It is amazing how the love for this great leader is reinforced daily by community. What a somber and reverent place.

reviews.author: David D
reviews.title: Interesting Mausoleum.
reviews.content: The Mausoleum displays the body of Ho Chih Minh which is displayed in a glass case.  Free to the public, the mausoleum is closed on Fridays and Mondays.  On the other days, it is open only in the mornings for about 4 hours starting at 7:30 AM. People start lining up well before 7:30 AM.  When we arrived at 7:30 AM on a Sunday morning, the line, stretching at least 1/2 mile had just started moving.  Bring plenty of water, sun screen, a hat and plenty of patience due to the long lines and people trying to cut in line in front of you.  Short sleeves are ok but wear long pants or you may be denied entry.  Will have to go through airport type security and backpacks must be checked just past the security gates.  It took us about an hour to get to the gate once we got in line.  From there, it was about another 40 minutes and at least 1/4 mile walk to enter the mausoleum.  You're in the mausoleum for only about 2 minutes as the line moves fast and the guards keep you moving.  Pictures are not allowed nor is cell phone use when in line.  Once finished with the mausoleum, you can access the nearby park with vendor stalls, the museum if you have a paid ticket, or simply exit.  Overall, good experience but once is enough.

reviews.author: Shadow
reviews.title: Spacious but no that Interesting
reviews.content: There are tons of places to visit in Hanoi.  Limit on carrying belongings and dress appropriately. Not worth the time to spend 1/2 day there.

reviews.author: A_C_2024
reviews.title: Worth seeing but get there early!
reviews.content: This is a must do in Hanoi, but be prepared for some logistical difficulties. We visited at 8am on a Saturday morning and unfortunately wasted some time waiting in the wrong line - we needed to be in the line for people without appointments - it's not exactly that well signposted or clear. The lines can be quite long (even at that time) with big tour groups and groups of school children, but they do move reasonably quickly. We had to check in our water bottles at security on a very hot day in Hanoi and then found getting them back before touring the rest of the complex (Ho Chi Minh's stilted house and museum) was quite difficult. You have to be dressed modestly - no shoulders or knees exposed or you will be turned away. There is no chance of photos inside the mausoleum or even at close proximity outside.With all of that said, you can't go to Hanoi and not visit this. But you do need to get there early and if possible avoid weekends.

reviews.author: Pam-travelfan
reviews.title: a must-see
reviews.content: I feel like a trip to Hanoi would not be complete without a visit here.  It is clear it is a communist country once you visit here.  Helpful to have a guide for the whole complex.

reviews.author: 13dilly
reviews.title: Emotional and Breathtaking Experience
reviews.content: Definitely worth visiting Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.  This is a beautiful place.  They are very secure with bringing in belongings and limit when you can have your camera.  Getting through the mausoleum takes time.  After seeing the mausoleum, you can explore on your own.

reviews.author: richardaluke
reviews.title: Well worth the queue
reviews.content: Important place to visit and to get a sense of the reverence accorded to HCMLong queue to get in but worth the wait

reviews.author: Amanda H
reviews.title: Tips for visit
reviews.content: The actual site is worth visiting but I’m sticking to tips we discovered from our visit (which was a Saturday so probably peak times) Firstly it is free and well organized. Things to note You need to dress respectfully when going into the mausoleum so make sure shoulders and knees are covered. You can buys scarves at stalls and they will cover you up but save money and plan ahead. You walk through security scanners and they will take food and water from you (but you can pick it up at end) Get there early as it’s a long wait. However people are polite and don’t push in the queues. Also if u take a camera or electronic devices they will take them away but you can pick them up after going through mausoleum. If u need transport after try to arrange a Grab (Asia’s Uber) somewhere away from the entrance as that is hectic and full of buses and cabs and cyclos. Beware the cabs there as they probably will have a ‘tourist metre’ And rip you off badly. The museum is separate and you pay for that. Everything is clean and well organized

reviews.author: Sebastián M
reviews.title: Crowded
reviews.content: We’ve been here at 9 am and there were too many people waiting just to get inside and que at least half an hour to see Ho Chi Minh. Native people have entrance for free, tourists have to pay for every entrance (garden, museum). You have to wear long pants, otherwise you won’t get inside. There’s a lot to see. I think visiting Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex is a must.

reviews.author: melbviccath
reviews.title: HO CHI MINH MAUSOLEUM
reviews.content: He was so central to Vietnam prospering and is still revered by the people. Lots of school groups visit so go early and miss the queues.

reviews.author: Sotontraveller
reviews.title: Need to see but without entrance interest is minimised
reviews.content: Typical Communist mausoleum that was shut when we visited.  Yes, large, grey, imposing, sombre, dull.  No doubt impressive if you get entry to see HCM.  I've seen the Kims' so had no special regret at missing his.

reviews.author: Sumedh V
reviews.title: Well Managed centre
reviews.content: The things as require are placed as per order. Hope the Govt. of Vietnam as well as residents will take care for all those modern and Ancient Culture.

reviews.author: Kim G
reviews.title: Impressive & Imposing Monument; Just Behave!
reviews.content: Impressive structure in a vast public pedestrian square, we were fortunate to witness the structured changing of the guard.  Lovely potted flowers, lawn and trees soften the harsh lines of this imposing monument.  We did not venture inside; however, should you wish to view the well-preserved body of Ho Chi Minh, ABSOLUTELY DO NOT take a photo.  You will be jailed!Also, stay outside of the confined areas. The One Pillar Pagoda is situated around the corner, and the Presidential Palace sits at the opposite end of the Mausoleum. Much to see and absorb here.  Notice the detail on the light posts.

reviews.author: Andrew N
reviews.title: Be careful of taxi over charging
reviews.content: The mausoleum was very impressive.  A taxi driver attempted to charge us six times the usual fare to return back to our hotel.  We would have tipped if usual fare.  Agree the fare before taking the ride.  Beware

reviews.author: 1709_Vanessa
reviews.title: Very Interesting
reviews.content: Great learning experience. Learned all about the life in time of Ho Chi Minh. We had an excellent guide, so that made it more interesting.  Its a must visit place in Hanoi

reviews.author: Heads5
reviews.title: Good for history buffs
reviews.content: Once you understand the history of the Vietnam war, Uncle Ho is well worth a visit. Don't be put off by the long line, it moves very quickly!

reviews.author: Hi-there-all
reviews.title: Sadly it was closed when we toured
reviews.content: We were on a private tour and unfortunately it was closed. When it is open our guide said the lines takes hours to get in, but they do have movable walkways that cover the queues.

reviews.author: C F
reviews.title: Time your visit
reviews.content: Don't be surprised by the long lines. This is all very serious business and the changing of the guard is rather impressive.

reviews.author: Henrique Rozenfeld
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh was a great leader and unified the country and his memorial is very impressive. Full of people and children visiting.

reviews.author: Shounak
reviews.country: Glacier National Park of Canada, Canada
reviews.title: Great to visit
reviews.content: We was there in April and walk through around Mausoleum, and also we look inside the Mausoleum where is show the influence of the Man HoChiMinh with all respected. Great to visit here.

reviews.author: Syd3333
reviews.title: Interesting to get the history
reviews.content: Interesting  to see how Ho Chi Minh lived. you see his house, car etc. Nice lake where he fed the fish and conducted business.

reviews.author: Matt N
reviews.title: Do your homework, never open in the afternoon
reviews.content: I have seen multiple sources of misinformation about the hours you can enter the mausoleum.  It is only open Tues, Wed, Thurs, Sat and Sunday.Never later than 1030 or 11, depending on the day.The line is long and moves quick. Soldiers are pretty serious, so you don't want to make jokes or giggle/etc in the line close to the mausoleum.  Inside, you get to see him from 3 sides, for maybe 30 seconds total. Of course no pics inside.

reviews.author: Susan C
reviews.title: Worth the walk
reviews.content: Walking through the whole park area with the buildings, lake and mausoleum is well worth it. It shows the influence of one man on the country, and the honour shown him.

reviews.author: Ernest W
reviews.title: Not great!
reviews.content: I have been here twice, at different times on different days, but still, the mausoleum was closed. I have no idea why. Did I come at the wrong time on both days? Because I know people are able to see him. Anyhow, the second time I went, I was yelled at by one of the guards. Apparently, I was standing somewhere on the pavement I wasn't supposed to be. There were no signs, though, saying you were not allowed to stand there. He motioned for me to move, so I moved a few steps in the direction he was motioning . But he kept yelling at me and motioning me to move. So I moved a few more steps in the direction he was motioning. When he yelled at me again, I lost it and yelled back, "What do you want me to do?" Probably not the smartest thing to do, as a) he had a gun and b) it's not like he would have understood English. But that just serves to show what you might encounter if you come. Not much to see. Mausoleum closed. Angry, rude guards that speak no English. I think you might have better luck going elsewhere.

reviews.author: 331jenna
reviews.title: Beautiful park, not a long wait
reviews.content: We went on a Wednesday morning. There were a lot of people and school groups, but they keep the line moving at all times so there wasn’t an actual “wait”. Shade is provided along the waiting areas, but helpful to bring a hat and umbrella too.Note, you are not allowed to bring in liquids. There are plenty of places to buy drinks inside.House and garden were beautiful. Overall, the park is pretty and well maintained but very commercialized.

reviews.author: GeorginaGal
reviews.title: Arrive in the morning
reviews.content: Arrived here in the afternoon and there was nothing much here to see other than the outside of the mausoleum. and there is a yellow line on the pavement that you are not allowed to step over. Apparently if you arrive in the morning then you can go inside, but for afternoon visitors there is just a yellow line on the pavement.  There are of course flowers by the entrance and honor guards.

reviews.author: Debra R
reviews.title: Queues a mile long
reviews.content: You had to queue for over an hour to go inside.  Our tour guide suggested we go back later when the mausoleum was closed, which we did.  Then it was only the outside of the building.

reviews.author: Dev
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: Go check it out, a very unique experience but go early to avoid lines - bring clothing suitable for a temple and be prepared to check your bags and phones. Overall GREAT experience.

reviews.author: ironfamilyNewZealand
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit. Finding the entrance is a little confusing from the street, it is free to visit the musoleum. The queues of people are constant and long but move relatively quickly and under shelter all of the time. There are many guards and strict rules of behaviour and clothing eg: no hats, singlets , shorts above knees- they even made men adhere to this. Also no large bags or electronic equipment beyond a phone . Seeing Ho Chi Minh is quick as you are filed through- I believe he is raised out of the underground tomb for a few hours at a time- 9am- 11am worked for us and it was difficult to find info on viewing times. After the musoleum there is the option of paying to see his home, cars etc.... this was not that worth doing due to large crowds and not really that greater things in view.

reviews.author: Tino Orlin
reviews.title: Not the most important on Hanoi, but you must have seen it.
reviews.content: Not the most important on Hanoi, but you must have seen it.Relatively interesting and during the week in the morning hours the waiting time ist acceptable! 3 Hours are enough!

reviews.author: Mary Sanesy
reviews.title: Mary Sanesy
reviews.content: Was well worth the walk. We were privileged to see the changing of the guard which was awesome and the parliament buildings.

reviews.author: Theo
reviews.title: Too much hustle just to see Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: Wasn't really worth it, as you spend so much time waiting in line to see embalmed Ho Chi Minh. Staff didn't speak English and wasn't helpful to wander around

reviews.author: TravelBird74
reviews.title: Must Visit for Hanoi
reviews.content: If you are visiting Hanoi then visiting this Mausoleum is a must. We reached there by 0740hrs and entered as soon as gate open by 0800hrs. Entry is from 0809 to 1000hrs. Entry is on Southwest corner road of Mausoleum compound. We took taxi from our hotel and asked him to drop at entry point. Most guide books including Lonely planet don't give location of entry point. There is no fee of Mausoleum.

reviews.author: manalaysaymd
reviews.title: Historical trip
reviews.content: The visit to the Mausoleum invoked respect for a great leader. One experiences how a person can make a great nation because of vision. The Mausoleum trip is so organized, and respectful, every step signals anticipation to take you closer to seeing a great leader. Kudos.

reviews.author: Travel AL 04
reviews.title: Amazing place to visit
reviews.content: The Mausoleum is a great place to visit if you are interested in history. To be able to see the great man's embalmed body is amazing. Be prepared for a long wait to get in. We were in line for about an hour before reaching the mausoleum. It is only open in the morning so try to get there early.

reviews.author: Bluecarrot2020
reviews.title: Nice, spacious greens; Rude guards
reviews.content: The mausoleum is quite imposing as a structure. Its design is a replica of Lenin’s in Russia. What is great about the landmark is it is spacious and is surrounded by a lot of greens (trees, grass, shrubs), thus, making it a nice place to spend a quiet day. What was a but traumatic is how the guards at the reception/entrance area conducted themselves. We saw them rudely “manhandle” a Vietnamese woman. While we couldn’t understand what the conversation was and if indeed she had broken a law/policy, it is still a big no-no to grab a female like that. One of the female guards was also shooing us away not knowing we were asked by our guide to wait in that place. She just kept shouting at us (and others). While we know we must respect the culture of every country,  we would not also definitely agree to be treated this way. We calmly told her that she does not need to shout because we can hear her. If this is supposed to be a “sacred” landmark and a tourist place, perhaps the reception guards (or military or whoever they are), should be the first to make it as such. People will respect the landmark if the reception-people assigned there are better educated, trained and are oriented in proper behavior.

reviews.author: mikemurray2009
reviews.title: Its a Tourist thing to do
reviews.content: Have to go if your anywhere close.  Easy and fast in and out.  Its more about where you are and seeing the locals veneration for the man than anything else.

reviews.author: Hemant01
reviews.title: A Large Mausoleum dedicated to The Great Leader Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: The construction of this Mausoleum was inspired by Lenin's Mausoleum in Moscow.The Mausoleum has a huge Parade ground in front,which even now is used on Special occasions & for Parades. The whole place is vast and is a befitting place for the great Leader's Mausoleum.

reviews.author: amanda w
reviews.title: In honour of Ho Chi Min
reviews.content: Try to visit when they do the parade everyday of the year twice daily whereby they raise and lower the flag in honour of Ho Chi Min, it had rained when visited so we had the entire square to ourselves it was fantastic

reviews.author: Fatboy
reviews.title: History
reviews.content: It is an interesting part of the history of Vietnam and worth a short visit to walk around the grounds and is in an interesting area

reviews.author: KRia1212
reviews.title: Nice structure
reviews.content: What I liked most about the mausoleum was the grand building. We had kids with us and they got really bore there. I know in mausoleum, kids are not interested. However, the interior and the glass box all we're creating an amazing aura. The only problem was the long queue.

reviews.author: Antonia Grier
reviews.title: Ms Grier
reviews.content: We didn’t get to go inside we did a red bus tour that covered this area. Would’ve like to busy inside. Will update with pictures as soon as I find them.

reviews.author: Sophie Turner
reviews.title: Meaningful visit
reviews.content: A moment to learn and remember how such country like Vietnam could win the war and claim their independence with such great leader. The queue was quite long though.

reviews.author: Jean-Marie G
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh's memorial
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum is situated in a vast landscaped property that also houses the Presidential Palace, the Ho Chi Minh Museum, Ho Chi Minh's small house on stilts and the One Pillar Pagoda (Chua Mot Cot).  The mausoleum is of an impressive size building  that houses the remains of Ho Chi Minh which can be visited from April to September but was closed when we visited in March.  It is well worth the view.  If you are lucky (we weren't) you can witness the changing of the guard in front of the massive doors leading inside.

reviews.author: Hoan
reviews.title: impressive
reviews.content: Great to see - long queue but it did move very quickly and you are provided with shade for most of it. A must see if you are in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Krishna
reviews.title: Very Impressed
reviews.content: I was very Impressed and the Guards who are taking care of Ho Chi Minh's Body, Wow very dedicated Soldiers.

reviews.author: Julian E
reviews.title: You have to do this
reviews.content: The queue looks massive but it moves so quickly. Not everyones cup of tea but the man is revered and you get a sense of what the people feel for him and his achievements. Gets you very interested in history.

reviews.author: Tambonz
reviews.title: Too too busy...
reviews.content: I'm sure it's great... But when we went on a Sunday morning there must have been 300000 people queuing...It went right round the outside and all the way inside.Heaps and heaps of children and groups of Vietnamese people.It was 32 degrees and far too long to stay in the queue.

reviews.author: Catherine P
reviews.title: Iconic site
reviews.content: A walk past the (supposed) Ho Chi Min mummified corpse. This is one of those sights of Hanoi to be checked off the list. The gardens are quite beautiful and it was interesting to observe the reverence of the masses.

reviews.author: Elkin C
reviews.title: Beautiful place, but crowded.
reviews.content: It is a nice place to visit during your stay in Hanoi,  but if you go in the morning, the lineup to visit the mausoleum are too much.  Better to go in the afternoon,  less heat and no lines...the only thing is: that you won't be able to visit and see his body.

reviews.author: Rschagrin
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: A fitting tribute to founder of the Democratic republic of Viet Nam. he wanted to be cremated but his wishes were ignored.There are long lines since it is only opened from 8 to 11 AM.

reviews.author: David D
reviews.title: Long lines but nice quiet respite from noisy Hanoi
reviews.content: The lines are always long so be prepared for at least an hours wait. And do not forget to wear long pants or skirts to cover your knees or you’ll have to leave the line and buy a covering cloth. The mausoleum was OK. It’s sad to learn that Ho Chi Minh wanted to be cremated but the wishes of the leaders that followed him superseded his own instructions. We all file quickly past his embalmed body then our to the more interesting tour of the beautiful gardens and his simple home.  Go only if you have a guide as we did to tell you the history or if you’ve studied on your own.

reviews.author: Tara Campbell
reviews.title: Great for history
reviews.content: This museum was really informative, I would highly recommend accepting the guide to take you through to explain the exhibits and ho ch Minh story in English. If you go and see his body, be sure to wear something that covers your knees. My husband got pulled up and had to buy a scarf, when his shorts just showed his knees. Wasn’t really a drama, just good to know before you go as I think the scarf selling ladies are making a small fortune there lol.

reviews.author: CC-Lisboa
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: impressive the respect to Ho Chi Minh for the reunification and independence of the country. Have a huge square, like Kremlin, but much bigger. This city have 8 millions of people, but in this place you can feel the sound of silence.

reviews.author: Carlos Vera
reviews.title: very informative

reviews.author: Anthony B
reviews.title: Looking Into The Face Of History
reviews.content: The route into the strangely angular Ho Chi Minh mausoleum is made up of a sober queue of people anxious to see the carefully conserved remains of Vietnam’s legendary leader. A line of curious tourists and locals nervously contemplating the idea that soon they are going to see the preserved body of the father of modern Vietnam. The shuffling throng is strictly policed by white-uniformed attendants discretely admonishing people for not showing appropriate decorum in their wait to enter the sanctum to look upon the face of real, world-changing history. Entering the mausoleum is a uniquely eerie experience. The Stygian darkness and the palpable feeling of awe lies heavy. Tourists know this is the one chance they’ll have to convene, however briefly, with a titan of twentieth-century Asian politico-history. And soon, as your eyes become accustomed to the sepulchral atmosphere, in a dimly lit glass sarcophagus, Uncle Ho’s carefully tended remains are there to be seen. Under pale yellow light, you can certainly see Ho's papery features and his carefully combed hair and beard. No doubt nourished and sustained by the carefully managed atmosphere in the dimly lit display case. Does this look like a nation’s leader in temporary repose or a carefully staged display that acts as both a point of pilgrimage and a totem of the ongoing consolidation of Vietnamese communism? Judging by the hordes of primary school kids in attendance, their education starts at an early age. This is tourism at its most profound. No statues, gravestones or picture archives will quite compare to seeing the mortal remains of a person of note. And there are only a few opportunities in the world to do this. So if you’re in Hanoi then put this sombre visit on your agenda. It will help you to understand the world Ho Chi Minh fought for and, indeed, give an insight into how revered he still is in today’s Vietnam.

reviews.author: Michael B.
reviews.title: Unforgettably Strange Experience
reviews.content: When I saw the line down the street to enter security for the mausoleum, I was very skeptical that this attraction would be worth the wait. I reluctantly joined the line of tourists and Vietnamese schoolchildren, and to my surprise, the line moved fairly quickly--we waited about an hour. Finally, we got to the heavily air-conditioned entrance, past the stoic white-clad soldiers bearing bayonets, and up the stairs. As we climbed the stairs and grew nearer to the body, it became darker and darker. We got to the room, walked a brisk semicircle around Uncle Ho's dramatic body, and exited.The whole experience felt surreal, like something out of a cold war fantasy novel. Truly unforgettable.

reviews.author: chhhh6

reviews.author: Patrick D
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: Hồ Chí Minh (literally, "the one who lights"), his real name Nguyễn Sinh Cung, was born on May 19, 1890 in the village of Huang Tru bordered by rice paddies 360 km from Hué and 1442 from Saigon, is the founder of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam. In 1975, his name was given to the first city of Vietnam, formerly Saigon, Ho Chi Minh City.Ho Chi Minh died on September 2, 1969, while the conflict is still raging in Vietnam. His death is officially announced as having taken place on September 3 to not tarnish the National Independence Day of September 2.The construction of the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum began on September 2, 1973, 4 years to the day after the death of the "Father of the Nation", and opened in 1975The monument was built on the site where Ho Chi Minh made his famous speech proclaiming the Independence of Vietnam in 1945.The architecture of the building, massive and angular, is reminiscent of Lenin's mausoleum in Moscow, on the Red Square. The body of Ho Chi Minh is preserved in the cold, under a glass sarcophagus lit by the blue dim lightsHis body was embalmed for over a year by a Soviet the chief embalmer Dr. Sergei Debrov. The latter was forced to work secretly for a year in a cave to avoid American bombing.The "father of the nation" had expressed the wish to be cremated, he wanted his ashes to be scattered to the summits of three hills of Vietnam (in the North, in the Center and in the South of the country); the embalming and the construction of the mausoleum are therefore against his last wishes.The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is secured by a guard of honor.To enter it:You must have your arms and legs covered and put your bags in the locker room.Cameras are not allowed, it is strictly forbidden to take pictures or videos inside the building.Visitors must stand in two rows and remain silent. Moreover, it is important not to cross your arm or put your hands in your pockets.It is also forbidden to stop in front of the body.The monument is normally open to the public daily from 9 am to noon. but for foreigners only Tuesday- Thursday 8 am-11.00am.Preferable to come early because there is often a long queue (about 1 hour) where you spend no more than 30 seconds in front of the sarcophagus.Ask before you go because it is closed occasionally for regular work of restoration and preservation of the remains  .. A must see in Hanoi

reviews.author: Agkarajit

reviews.author: whatevereverever
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh mausoleum - when and where to go...
reviews.content: When to go...I found lots of info about where and when to go for a visit of the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum in Hanoi, Vietnam. First of all, it's closed on Mondays and Fridays. For the other days, these seem to be the opening hours: Tuesday - Thursday 07:30 - 10:30, Saturday & Sunday 07:30 - 11:00. Having said that, Tuesday to Thursday is better, because the lines get really long on weekends. However, I went on a Saturday and the whole thing took about an hour from lining up to leaving the mausoleum. Some of the signboards around the mausoleum say "open till 22.00", but that is just for the square in front of it, not the mausoleum itself.I would recommend going not after 9.30 - you never know how long the line is and where and where they cut it off and send you home.Where to go...The entrance to the mausoleum is on the side of the square, obviously. But if you want to take a cap to line up and go in, you should go to this address: 17 Ngọc Hà, Đội Cấn, Ba Đình, Hà Nội, Vietnam. That's where the entrance is and where the line will be - depending on the number of people you might see the line stretch up the street (Ngọc Hà) a bit further or on weekends also almost up to the Botanical Garden (North of the entrance gate).When I was there in March 2019, phones were allowed and bags were searched, but small bags were definitely allowed in. Not sure what happens when you have a huge backpack with you, but the whole thing looked pretty straightforward and unproblematic, even on a weekend. Then the "procession" through the covered walkway starts and it will take you about half an hour or less from the entrance gate to the mausoleum itself. Soldiers maintain order and you can play with your phone until you get to the square where you have signs that it's not allowed anymore. You might want to try and stay towards the left before going in to the mausoleum. You will be closer to Ho Chi Minh that way since people are led through in two rows and the left row is on the "inside", i.e. closer with a better view.After leaving the mausoleum, you are free to roam around the area behind the mausoleum and can go to the Ho Chi Minh museum if you like, check out the One-pillar Pagoda or just do whatever else you please.Uploading a map of the area with this post. Enjoy your trip!

reviews.author: Joni W
reviews.title: Fascinating!
reviews.content: Our family, including teen grandsons, were fascinated by this experience.  His body is amazingly well preserved and most people have a morbid fascination looking at him and considering he is preserved in the same way as Lenin.  It's quite a somber experience with the guards making certain there is no talking and everyone being totally respectful, as is appropriate and would be expected.  I slowed down at one point walking around the body and a guard promptly pushed me forward.  There are so many people one must move much as a "people mover" would move hoards of people.  Considering the number of people moving through the facility it is amazing how well managed and quiet it is.  Well worth seeing!

The communist nature of the country is evident from the square, as the country's "legislature" is viewable from the square, and the statue of Lenin stands proudly on a little nook. The square itself is a required visit if you are in Hanoi, however, as it shows

reviews.content: What you see is obvious but what you feel is not. Seeing different generations of vietnamese pay tribute to such a great man is moving

reviews.author: dhura
reviews.title: Complex great, Mausoleum not worth the wait
reviews.content: Get there early as his Mausoleum closes at 11 AM and that line takes forever. I would forego the Mausoleum and just stroll through the complex, tour the Museum, and get out of there. You can take pictures all over but you can't even move your arms inside his tomb. Reminder, no bare shoulders allowed at all!

reviews.author: Zledna
reviews.title: To get to know more about history
reviews.content: The tour inside the Museum complex, while full of tourist, was organized.  If you are carrying a backpack or big bag, they should be deposited in with a number and instructions where to pick up later. Had to line up going into the museum -which is a one-way affair to the floor where Ho Chi Min is laid.. and out at the back of the building. Now you can go around the museum sorroundings and see other areas where he used to spend his days here, including the vintage cars.

reviews.author: JudgeJer
reviews.title: An Amazing Piece of World History
reviews.content: Men women and children, workers all over the world benefit today from the philosophy and work that was done decades ago by Ho Chi Minh. It does not appear that he took a great deal for himself but he did great things for others. This museum is amazing and to walk past his preserved remains in the glass case is even more amazing. Well worth the trip. The lines look long but they move fast. Very respectful.

reviews.author: binonatrip
reviews.title: Closed at the time I chose to make my visit
reviews.content: I made the walk here on a Tuesday morning. Contrary to other visitors reviews, there were not many people waiting for entry to the site, probably because there was little for me to see. I was not alone in experiencing some trouble in locating the main entrance but at least there was no entry charge. It was probably so quiet because the Mausoleum was closed for the day and the museum was not opening until later. I was continually pestered by an old man who wanted to tell me of his life as a Vietcong soldier but in reality wanted to be an unofficial tour guide. He kept waving his notebook at me containing written testimonials from previous ‘customers’. It was at least good to see the soldiers marching in front of the Mausoleum. In the event I had to admit I was not too bothered that it was not open.

reviews.author: Baxie
reviews.title: Interesting Enough
reviews.content: An interesting stroll around the large buildings.Monday is a great day to go if you don’t want to see the actual body of HCM - as Mausoleum is closed that day it means the crowds are way less

reviews.author: Andrew H
reviews.title: Another must do....
reviews.content: A visit to where Uncle Ho rests is another must do in Hanoi. Don’t wander over the yellow lines or the guards will offer some advice. Only one entrance and no short cuts across the grass in front. Once you have walked past, then keep going to enter the palace and the house on stilts. Cost was 40k. Another tick in the box and a touch of history.

reviews.author: goodguyjas
reviews.title: Moving tribute to Vietnam’s great leader
reviews.content: As most have pointed out the visit to Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum can take a very long time depending on the crowds and once inside you file round his embalmed body laying in state quite quickly. But in order to allow as many people as possible to visit this is the only way. To me it is done very well and is a very fine tribute to him. The massive site does have more to see from his cars to his house as well as the stylish stilt house where he worked. Although you don’t go in you get clear views of the preserved rooms in both. The views of the yellow French style presidential palace and nearby small lake also adds to the grandeur of the area. The large white museum dedicated to Ho Chi Minh comes into view as you exit the main area. The place has a lot of space to sit or wander around and is very well maintained. To finish you of course have the requisite places to snack and buy souvenirs.

reviews.author: Robertn0007
reviews.title: The wait not worth it.
reviews.content: Took nearly an hour to file past a mummified body that they allow you about 1 minute to see. The gaurds are a very unhappy looking lot! The just order the crowds to keep in line and keep moving.Must say the grounds & gardens were very nice..

reviews.author: Chris W
reviews.title: Worth doing but be mindful of the wait.
reviews.content: We were there early but there was still a queue and a bit of shuffle to get to Ho Chi Minh's resting place - his embalmed body being revered by what we understood was all Vietnamese. It is worth doing as you also have access to the grounds where there are a number of his former residences, the latter of which reflects his love of simplicity but contradicted to a degree to the cars he used.Worth doing but do it early as we understood the queues could lead to a 2 hour plus wait.

reviews.author: George O
reviews.title: Long Lines and lots of visitors
