reviews.content: Our tour guide took us to the entrance around 9:30 am. Upon seeing a crowd of visitors and a waiting line that would be about 1.5 hours, we opted to come back in the afternoon to visit just th outside areas which are very beautiful. Lots of walking, take a hat and wear sunscreen.

reviews.author: Seamus G
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: You will need an early start to join the queue which will most likely be massive when you get there...but it moves quickly. Once you’re in, you’re only there for about 2 mins (if even) as the guards quickly push you around if you even stop for 5 seconds! Whilst it’s not long, it’s quite fascinating to look at. Make sure you don’t go in shorts, follow the rules etc. as they are quite strict.

reviews.author: MrSwarm
reviews.title: Mausoleum visit
reviews.content: If you always wanted to experience a socialist style mausoleum this is your chance.Very interesting albeit somewhat eery.Try to be there by 7:00 am on a weekday to beat the crowds or be prepared for a longer waiting time in line.

reviews.author: ScotlandWeelass
reviews.title: Interesting visit
reviews.content: firstly, we were really put off by our tour guide, who made out that we were in for a scary, regimented time!   Once we got there, it wasn't.  understandably, we were asked at times to stand in two's or one's depending on the queues going through.  this is a really iconic heartland for the Vietnamese, and is treated with real respect especially in the Mausoleum.  (Do not that on entering, only small bags and cameras area allowed.  If you have a larger camera, then you are directed to a place where it can be safely left and collected after the mausoleum part of the tour)  You will also go through an airport scanner - think Buckingham palace. We were lucky enough to arrive in time to see a ceremony of young school children being awarded some prizes.  After the ceremony we were allowed into see Ho Chi Minh lying in state.  do please be respectful here.  it is cooler here as well.  Once outside again, it was off to see the houses and gardens were he lived and worked.  They are lovely.  Here there are toilets, some cafes and shops - well worth making the trip and far less formal.  Interesting to see the houses and rooms where he entertained Cuban leaders and others.  the gardens are in themselves very beautiful.  Oh, do please remember to wear respectful clothing in the mausoleum part, with covered shoulders etc for ladies, and no short shorts for men.  Also it seems Vietnamese and Cambodian cultures do not like hat wearing in these respected places.

reviews.author: Hock
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh maosoleum
reviews.content: Learnt about this great vietnamist leader who built and made the country stronger. He died in this place during American war in 1972

reviews.author: JRKSA
reviews.title: Stop By for Brief Visit
reviews.content: We stopped by the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum twice for brief visits during separate tours. Our first visit was watch the nightly flag lowering ceremony at approximately 9:00pm. We did that with the Paloma motorbike tour. It was worth doing, as it is neat ceremony and good for a few pictures. We had booked another tour of the mausoleum assuming there would be a museum about his life. Our guide described that there would be a long line to get in to view his body in a glass coffin. We were not interested in this, so we just visited the exterior. The grounds are beautiful, and again definitely worth a stop for pictures. We can offer no opinion on the interior as we were a bit put-off by the idea of viewing a dead body... even if it is a major historical figure.

reviews.author: Ignace B
reviews.title: Iconic place in Vietnam
reviews.content: Must see in Hanoi. You cannot take pictures inside and respectful clothing is obligated. Makes me think of the Che mausoleum in Cuba.

reviews.author: Iain P
reviews.title: An iconic experience !
reviews.content: Once arriving at the mausoleum site and finding the end of the queue,we thought it was going to be a long wait.Surprisingly,we moved quite rapidly along and in no time at all were approaching the very impressive mausoleum.Everything is very orderly under the watchful eye of immaculate soldiers in white uniforms and to see how seriously they take their responsibility has to be admired.Once inside the building,there is no stopping and passing by the final resting place of Ho Chi Minh is over so quickly although no visit to Vietnam would be complete without seeing this iconic place.Outside,the grounds are quite pleasant and the One Pillar Pagoda is worth seeing .An altogether interesting place to visit when in Hanoi.Iain and Carol Patterson.Newcastle upon Tyne.

reviews.author: RMJ59
reviews.title: It is set in a park with lovely gardens
reviews.content: The crowds on the day we were there meant we could not queue to see the Mausoleum itself, so we returned in the afternoon when we were able to visit the grounds and gardens and one pillar pagodaWorth the visit, but be ware of the crowds and queues in the morning when you can walk by the body of HO Chi Minh.

reviews.author: Zachary H
reviews.title: Left side of the line is best
reviews.content: Hands down the longest line I have ever waited in, but so worth it. Plus, don’t be intimidated by the long line, it moves quickly. Be aware that cameras are not allowed and have to be checked before entering the Mausoleum. Telephones seem to be in a permissible grey area, so long as you’re not using them to take photos around the Mausoleum.

reviews.author: chachie
reviews.title: Good
reviews.content: The queue is very long and they are very strict..no food and drinks allowed inside.. if you are planning to visit this, make sure girls are wearing something long enough to cover until knee area..but it is worth it and an experience to see:)

reviews.author: Bangoe
reviews.title: A Must to visit. Sometime.
reviews.content: Sooner  or later you have to visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. It's such a connection with the history of modern Vietnam.I was surprised by how quick and efficient the queue moved to get in and through the mausoleum. It's only open a few hours in the morning, and it's free.

reviews.author: Anna
reviews.title: Love it
reviews.content: I love this place and spend a lot of time around this area, we think it is a highlight of Hanoi. Highly recommended for other tourist

reviews.author: Gordo4037
reviews.title: Was OK
reviews.content: We found this an interesting place to visit. We arrived after 11am so too late to view Ho Chi Minh but enjoyed the grounds, museum and pagoda.

reviews.author: Shervin Ziabakhsh
reviews.title: Nice experiance
reviews.content: I had seen Mao Maoseleum previously in Beijing, hochi minh's also is the same ,it is only for comunistic countries  that keep the leaders in a maner like this.cell phone is allowed but camera not allowed the cur goes fast.

reviews.author: Wayne B
reviews.title: So much history
reviews.content: I took two teenage children to visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and the surrounding Presidential Palace.It is always busy as Ho Chi Minh is such a revered leader.You queue to visit the Mausoleum and walk pst Ho Chi Minh quite quickly.Also in the same complex are several places where Ho Ch Minh lived a very simple life.He wanted to live a similar life to the ordinary people and for this reason and his love of children he was given the respected title of a Uncle Ho.The One Pillar Pagoda is also in the same complex.

reviews.author: Maggie S
reviews.title: Interesting!!!
reviews.content: To see Ho Chi Minh’s preserved body under glass is something you won’t forget, nor the soldiers wearing their white uniforms guarding the place.

reviews.author: Trainman95630
reviews.title: Why did I stand in line 3 hours to see this dead commie's desiccated body ?
reviews.content: We got to our hotel and were talked into a Hanoi City tour for what I thought was a price of $54 (including lunch). It ended up being $54 per person so total of $108. When the guide got to our hotel , he asked what we wanted to see. I gave him a list of 3 or sights and he kind of pushed me into seeing the mausoleum first. On the way over he gave us some good insights into Vietnam and Hanoi although his English was a little hard to follow. Arriving in the area of the mausoleum I couldn't believe the line. It was a Sunday and lots of people from the countryside come into Hanoi on buses to see this site. We were probably in line 2 to 3 hours. It does move fast but I bet it was the longest line I've ever been in. During the time in line it was cool seeing people doing group exercise classes in the parks -  never saw anything like that - it was like a taste of local normal life.During the time in line I got the whole spiel on Uncle Ho and how great communism is. (Really , cause the only reason your country is doing so well is the market reforms you instituted in the 90s). So I listened politely and wondered how long this would take. Fortunately it was March and the weather was pleasant but mild.Even once you get to the entry gate and have your bags checked, it still takes 45 minutes to get to the mausoleum. As I said the line moves fast , you keep moving as you go past the body, you probably only actually view it for 60 seconds max. It is almost a religious experience for the native born people, not so much for me.Once we were done, we were taken to a great Vietnamese restaurant for a lunch which was excellent. After that our half day tour was over. We had the guide drop us at Ho Loa prison which we toured on our own. All in all, I wish I had insisted on seeing other sights in Hanoi instead of this one.

reviews.author: Andreaobrien1
reviews.title: Fascinating to see
reviews.content: Although large queues, they move very quickly. For westerners you need to be dressed appropriately, no knees showing or low cut tops. Strange to see but fascinating.

reviews.author: Voyage688975
reviews.title: Hanoi city tour
reviews.content: This was part of a city tour of Hanoi that included access to pottery and lacked ware production facilities.

reviews.author: Keith J
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: My wife and I recently visitedHo Chi Minh Mausoleum, very impressive and our guide was very informative,well worth a visit to see a part of history.

reviews.author: Víctor
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: It was impressed, but massive queue to get in. Be respectful and visit the garden and then museum, free entrance.

reviews.author: lyttlemarg
reviews.title: Group golf tour
reviews.content: Very busy, long wait to go inside, guide told us it was only open in the morning, but was open in afternoon as well.Interesting but not sure it was worth the wait in the heat, no water bottles allowed. Grounds very nice, but still hard to see due to crowds.

reviews.author: cyclisttorrens
reviews.title: Moving experience
reviews.content: In the queue leading up to the mausoleum you are not allowed to take any photos and obviously not in the mausoleum itself. However after the visit you can approach the entrance from the other side and take photos of the outside from a discreet distance.Only other experience was a visit to Lenin’s tomb in Moscow so a similar experience to that.

reviews.author: SeeMoreLiveMore
reviews.title: Impressive building ...
reviews.content: This place is highly revered because of its significance. The centre piece of the Ba Dinh Complex, many tourists do a visit here when in Hanoi. Do be properly attired and respectful because it is of especial importance to Vietnam. When I went, it was not open, so cannot comment on going into the mausoleum itself, though.

reviews.author: JeffCypress
reviews.title: Well worth the visit
reviews.content: We were advised to visit in the afternoon as there are big queues in the morning to go inside the mausoleum itself to view HCM’s body which is closed in the afternoon. You can see the outside in the afternoon.  There is a lot to see here - the one pillar pagoda, the mausoleum, botanical gardens, presidential palace and HCM’s quarters and offices. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: ZBH88
reviews.title: A good experience
reviews.content: This place is a must to experience the importance of the site. Free entry but extremely popular (you have to see the queues to believe it) avoid the weekends and only go first thing unless you like waiting.

reviews.author: Ssaravanan1
reviews.title: Must Visit if you believe
reviews.content: This place queue starts every early and close by 11.30 am. Try to go early but incase you go little late, it is fine. The queue moves very fast and you will be able to see the great leader.

reviews.author: Ken G
reviews.title: Ugly building - not a "must see" visit
reviews.content: I got the impression that all Vietnamese guides are required to bring you to Ho Chi Minh's memorial. We were on a tour, but had a local guide in Hanoi. Nobody asked us if we wanted to see this. We were lucky - the mausoleum is closed on Monday so we didn't have to wait in a long line to view Ho Chi Minh's body, which I thought would be pretty gruesome anyway. We were told that a few months out of the year he's sent to Russia for a little tune up and then they use a wax replica in his place, so who knows what we would have been treated to anyway..

reviews.author: Jay S
reviews.title: Expansive museum
reviews.content: This museum complex is very big and revals the museums we have here in Washington DC. We had vey nice weather for our visit, our guide was extremely  helpfull with explanations.

reviews.author: dmrbay
reviews.title: Worth to visit
reviews.content: The mausoleum of Ho Chi Minh the leader and founder of Vietnam is worth the time you spend. Wake up early and go early otherwise the queue will be long enough to make you think twice. Beware: it is closed on Fridays.

reviews.author: mugisele
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: Its quite impressive to see the magnitude of the Mausoleum as well as the complex where HCM resided. Worth visiting to understand the history of Vietnam.

reviews.author: williamkassel
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: While Ho Chi Minh is not actually here the Mausoleum is on a grand scale.  You may even catch the changing of the guard.  Just do a quick walk around.

reviews.author: Nonapama
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: Our guide timed our visit in nice time for the 1200 changing of the guard which was well worth while. Just to see the impressive monument and the guards standing it was all worthwhile. The gardens are worthwhile alone and there is lots of room on the wide paved area.

reviews.author: John S
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: I was surprised that this area of town doesn’t pop up on TA as a recommended thing to do.All in all, whilst we didn’t get to see the embalmed “Uncle Ho” himself, there was enough of interest to make it worth while.

reviews.author: Alan B
reviews.title: A weird experience!
reviews.content: It is really something that one must do when visiting Hanoi, so don't be put off by any reviews and do go. However, it is just such a weird thing, to be walking fairly fast past a waxlike mummy of what was once a real person.Uncle Ho is laying there, just as he would if he was a Madame Tussaud's waxwork, and the crowds are moved along with firm politeness, but is something that needs to be done by the visitor. This is in order to try to get a feel for the awe and respect with which many of the Vietnamese people hold for their former 'Chu Tich' (President). The whole complex is enormous and the gardens and his summer house are also well-worthwhile visiting, something not obvious when first checking in. There's much more to this visit than just the mausoleum.Be prepared to be correctly dressed and to have bags and large cameras, or laptops, removed and retained until you exit, but this is not something I felt you needed to be concerned about.

reviews.author: Anders H
reviews.title: Free visit to a glimpse of avcommunist symbol
reviews.content: A free and easy way to see and take some photos of some soldiers, the Mausoleum and mausoleum grounds. Just take 30 minutes to stroll the area. :-)

reviews.author: Maree H
reviews.title: Treasures of Vietnam intrepid Tour
reviews.content: The mausoleum was closed when we visited. There is strict security on bags and dress code.Best to have your shoulders covered and knees. It is a big place, with beautiful gardens although you are not allowed on the grass and there is a “no go zone” around the building. Spend some time looking at the other structures they are quite interesting.

reviews.author: Lee A D
reviews.title: Go early and make sure shoulders and knees are covered
reviews.content: Vietnamese flock here to honor their hero except in early fall when his body gets shipped to Russia for “restoration”.  Long lines filled with schoolchildren from throughout country.  Interesting scene.  Changing of the guard is fun to see.

reviews.author: Liz C
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
reviews.content: We arrived with our tour guide with no line at the entrance. You walk through a scanner before entering the premise. The area is huge and an interesting place to visit, walk around the grounds. We were not able to go inside the mausoleum as it is closed on Friday and Monday to visitors.

reviews.author: AnniK0210
reviews.title: Interesting place
reviews.content: We went there with a tour. It was an interesting place. We couldn't go inside the mausoleum at the time we went.

reviews.author: SixpackDC
reviews.title: Walking the grounds may be enough
reviews.content: My tour guide and I arrived here around 8:00 PM. Obviously the mausoleum was closed but there were a lot of local people enjoying the grounds. What surprised me was that there were absolutely no one stepping on the grass...I mean no one, including the kids. As a result, the grass is impeccably maintained. The guide also told me that all the flowers that were located in the periphery of the grounds were there because of the visit by Kim Jung Eun. It is a nice area just to stroll...

reviews.author: Jafe A
reviews.title: The long wait
reviews.content: We got up early as we were told to get there early as the queues could be very long. We arrived at 07:20 to find the queue stretched forever and there were no tourist signs to help the traveller understand the process.We finally got to the back of the queue to find that queuing isn’t a Vietnamese custom and found ourselves going backwards after 1:30 hours!!We gave up and went to the pool

reviews.author: Cassandra R
reviews.title: Bag check absolutely ridiculous
reviews.content: We have to check out bag and pram which is fine, however we were not able to walk back through the grounds the quick way as we were the last entry for the day, we had to exit the grounds walk 1.3km AROUND the outside back to the bag check location. Absolute disgrace we had to carry our daughter while navigating streets. No staff inside could understand that we wanted to get out bags and just ignored us or pointed us to the road!

reviews.author: lmo3
reviews.title: Intriguing
reviews.content: We queued for what seemed like ages, partly in the rain, but it was well worth a glimpse of this revered leader. I have never seen an embalmed person before so the experience was memorable. Well organised and efficiently directed. You must be properly dressed and behave respectfully when entering the mausoleum.

reviews.author: john
reviews.title: Prepare for long lines to enter!
reviews.content: This complex is located outside of the city center! There is always a lot of queue to enter the mausoleum, for my part I could not visit it since I had planned to go one Saturday and that day was visited by many schools and the queues were terrible. inside the mausoleum is forbidden to take pictures, you can not enter with cameras or backpacks, when you enter the guards you take care of them while you visit the mausoleum!

reviews.author: Ana
reviews.title: Impressive but be aware...
reviews.content: It’s very impressive place. Really enjoyed walking around presidential palace area. Things to be aware:- mausoleum is open only in the morning between 8-11am but not on Monday and Friday. So you should consider visiting it in the morning. When we arrived, we weren’t allowed to enter it due to visit of Kim Jong Un so we stood outside outside for hours. Eventually got to mausoleum and stood in a queue to do a security check for 30min but it wasn’t so bad. - if you have any cameras with you please be aware what you will have to give them to security which will be returned to you at the exit as you are not allowed to take any pictures inside.-LADIES - please have a scarf with you and don’t wear shorts or open shoulder tops, otherwise you won’t be able to get in and stopped at the entrance.- moreover, you will spend in mausoleum only 5min, you’ll be lined up like in school, walk inside and walk out without stopping. Only have a look at Ho Chi Minh while walking. - and most important, do not put your hands in a pocket, or talk, otherwise guards will start giving out to you or kick you out. No phones out either...However, once you leave mausoleum, to can walk around grounds for hours! Just don’t forget to buy a ticket - 40.000 p/p.Enjoy! It is impressive overall :-)

reviews.author: Michael k
reviews.title: Very impressive
reviews.content: The mausoleum is very impressive.The guards are wearing white uniforms over red colored trees and flowers dpend on season.

reviews.author: SusanF
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: On a day tour with Go-vacation ( excellent guide Ping) this was much more than I anticipated- changing of the shift, pagodas an Ho Chi Minh houses at the back of the Masoleum- great history, makes you think, tranquility in hustle and bustle of Hanoi

reviews.author: Lisa S
reviews.title: Very strict, quick visit
reviews.content: We are on a tour and had an early morning visit arranged by our local guide.  The line was really long and guards were placed outside and once you entered the complex.  They were very strict from making you stand close to the people in front of you to ensuring you were 2x2 in line.  Also no talking was allowed.  No big cameras or large bags are permitted on site either.  Although you are allowed to take pictures outside when in line the guards are upset if you do so and hold up the line!  Of course NO pictures are allowed at the entrance but you can get a good photo after you leave from behind.  It’s a very quick walk through to see the body which is in a huge glass sarcophagus.  Every year his body returns to Russia to be touched up for 2 months.  I believe 2019 our guide said the body will be gone in October & November.  Although there are operating hours they can and do close the mausoleum whenever they want.  I think it’s based on how many visitors show up.  When we departed late morning they had closed for the day!Also you must cover your shoulders and knees, so no shorts or tank tops allowed.

reviews.author: Helmut1954
reviews.title: A must ecperiance to express the admiration to this great leader
reviews.content: The site is very popular. It is perfectly organised to manage the thousands of people that are coming to visit. You are not allowed to take pictures. In walking distance is the On stilt Pagoda, HoChi Minh House and Ho Chi Minh Museum. Absolutely worth to visit

reviews.author: EmmelineBC
reviews.title: Staff are suspicious of wheelchairs!
reviews.content: I am in a wheelchair and was allowed entry into the mausoleum but had to use their manual wheelchair. Four men in military uniform carried me up the multitude of steps to see Ho Chi Minh. Like HannoH3 said, visitors are not allowed to take pictures, our backpacks and iPads had to be checked in.  We were also asked not to talk while in line and a senior staff member accompanied me and my family group of 4 plus a tour guide the entire time.  The entire viewing time took about 1 minute.After the visit to see HCM, we weren't allowed to use the Mausoleum's wheelchair to go to the Museum which was in the same complex only a few hundred feet away.  We were required to return it IMMEDIATELY to the entrance from where we left my personal wheelchair, accompanied by a staff member.My tour guide asked if we could use my own wheelchair to visit the other buildings in the complex, such as the Museum.  We were told we could but we had to come back to the complex after the Mausoleum was closed at 12 noon.  When we returned, we were not allowed to enter.  They kept pointing at my wheelchair.  It didn't matter even when my tour guide explained what their superior had said that morning because by the afternoon, another superior was in charge.  We left and tried another entrance with the same result.  My tour guide wasn't ready to give up so we tried a 3rd entrance. He spoke to a man in military uniform of senior rank if we could enter using my manual wheelchair.  The man assured us we could, so we line up again.  But when we got to the security checkpoint we were denied entry again.  The military officer who said we could pass through was informed by someone higher in rank, whom we never saw, that we couldn't enter because of my wheelchair.  The military officer took pictures of my wheelchair to show that it was a harmless, folding wheelchair but I was still denied entry.  The tour guide said, if you don't trust my wheelchair, provide me one of the museum's but there was none they could provide.  Apparently, all they had was the one by the Mausoleum.I was naturally disappointed because I was interested in knowing about Vietnam's history and seeing her historical places not just from what you can read online. I didn't want to just see the preserved body of HCM but wanted to see the other buildings that all visitors were allowed to see at the complex, especially of his life and works. But because I am disabled and in a wheelchair, I was discriminated against.  Sad but true.

reviews.author: Lars
reviews.title: Visit old Uncle Ho
reviews.content: Ho Chi Minh is such an important figure in newer Vietnam history which is why we prioritised to give him a visit. Be aware that if you want to get inside the mausoleum and see the guy, open hours are 8-11 and prepare to stay in line. Long sleeves and no hat. You are required to leave your daypack, but they have a system for that. Entrance is free and the kids thought it was exciting to see a dead guy.

reviews.author: Johannes R
reviews.title: Be early!
reviews.content: Try to be there waaay before opening time or be smarter: book a tour! Then you can entry on the side at the group entrance. Super crowded!!

reviews.author: Hanno H
reviews.title: Worst museum
reviews.content: Although standing in the longest queue of my whole life (Saturday 10 AM) it worked out to visit the mausoleum at 11 AM. All bags and cameras will be taken from you and stored to pick up after your visit. Small handbag and camera you can keep. The mausoleum itself takes approx. 1 minutes or less, no pictures and short trousers allowed.The museum afterwards is in my opinion really bad, confusing set-up, bad English description of what has happened, pseudo artistic elements. Compared to the museums in hcmc (very well made) this one is not worth the entrance fee. Only if taking a guide, maybe...beware it closes at 12 PM or similar, so you need to leave early to do both or come back in the afternoon.

reviews.author: faboio
reviews.title: Historical
reviews.content: Huge queues but move along at a reasonable walking pace, most of the time. We started at 10.10am, took an hour to get to mueselium. Very impressive and well worth the wait. Gardens are beautifully.

reviews.author: Coleenp3
reviews.title: Vacation
reviews.content: Very moving and quite remarkable. Interesting to go see and experience. The grounds are quite beautiful.

reviews.author: JaniJermans
reviews.title: Visit
reviews.content: Must visit, unfortunately it was closed on the day we visited but went around the big campus. It has most of the govt buildings are around

reviews.author: giacomofopp
reviews.title: HE'S ACTUALLY DEAD!
reviews.content: Went to see him, honestly amazing to see. Just a tip don't laugh/smile/talk or anything like that, they'll shoot you. I really needed a fart and had to let a sneaky one out while the guard wasn't paying attention so make sure to let them out before you enter.

reviews.author: Cindy Soka
reviews.title: Do some research
reviews.content: I visited the mausoleum on two occasions. The first time I went I wasn’t able to cross security because I was wearing a vest/string top/tank top (whatever you would like to call it). They said I couldn’t go in unless I was able to cover my shoulders.The second time I went I got through security fine, but the mausoleum itself was closed. I didn’t realise it was only open on specific days - so make sure you check before you go.I was able to walk through the grounds and took a picture outside the mausoleum. I am not sure what I would have been able to see if the mausoleum had been open. Possibly Ho Chi Minh himself (embalmed obviously)? Even if it had been open, I’m sure it would have been busy inside because there were a lot of tourists taking pictures outside.

reviews.author: Julia
reviews.title: what an experience!
reviews.content: I've visited several mausoleum in the past but none like this one!In line two-by-two almost at military pace you have to walk in silence to the mausoleum and keep walking to the exit ...but it is a place that need to be seen!

reviews.author: Edmund E
reviews.title: historical sight seeing
reviews.content: impressive layout of building and parade square.   dignified and wonderful to see many people going there to honour HCM

reviews.author: JellyB
reviews.title: It is an experience
reviews.content: Short daily visiting hours with thousands queuing for up to 90-120 min just to get in for a minute or so. For the Vietnamese, this trip is a must. I have never witness such a long line for a musoleum. That in itself is a sight to behold. TipCome early.

reviews.author: Shane Huth
reviews.title: Advice For Future Travelers
reviews.content: They stop selling tickets around 12pm during the week. On the weekend the line extends several city blocks. This is no exaggeration. Also if you go by cab make sure they drop you off at the entrance. Otherwise it'll take you 20ish minutes to walk around the entire complex to get in. This being said we were unable to get inside the mausoleum because of these circumstances.

reviews.author: glp012849
reviews.title: Long wait for short view
reviews.content: Waited in line over 2 hrs. to view the body of Ho Chi Minh.   Although he is loved and revered by the VN people, I was not that enamoured.   I probably would have passed on this venue, but did not wish to insult our VN guide.   HCM was a part of history, but it was a long wait for a 2 minute viewing.  I suggested returning later, as the kids were getting agitated, but our guide said it was always this busy!   The grounds are lovely and there are a lot of impressive structures to view.   Saw a group of Chinese children who were anxious to "high five" us and were just delightful !

reviews.author: druidwicklow
reviews.title: Comunist Pionires marching
reviews.content: Masses of comunist red scarf children uniformed laughing and moving towards mausoleum together with other school kids constantly moving in masses like no end od it, waiting is hours on.....I didnt go inside .If any want go please  come early  morning and observe  strict regulations.Long live working class and Cominterna.Ante G

reviews.author: TraceyMelb
reviews.title: You need to do it, but you probably won't write home to your Mum about it...
reviews.content: Its a long process to go through, but ultimately the revered Ho Chi Minh and how they have honoured him is worth seeing.  No photos allowed.

reviews.author: kcchin
reviews.title: Arrive EARLY!
reviews.content: Check the days the mausoleum is open before visiting. They open at 7AM. On the days it’s open the line snakes at least half a mile long at least. It is a solemn place, so dress appropriately. Any short dresses, tank tops will not be allowed to enter the grounds. Quiet is the rule. Any backpacks can be stored for free at the entrance. No crossing of arms or hands in your pocket. No gum chewing.... you all get the picture ! A 2-3 hour half day tour of the grounds includes the Ho Chi Minh museum. Your 45 seconds in Ho Chi Minh’s presence is something you won’t forget. A must for visit while you’re in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Chutatsu
reviews.title: Ok
reviews.content: I visited here with my friend and that was worth visiting but nothing interesting as well actually. But worth to see anyway

reviews.author: Mr. Mike
reviews.title: It was an honor to pay my respects.
reviews.content: There’s no way to give such a place any less than 5 stars. Ho Chi Minh’s life story and legacy has been hidden from the West because of the Cold War, and US involvement in a senseless and ideological war.The mausoleum itself is only open 3 hours, 5 days each week: 8AM to 11AM, closed M and F. 50 years later, the line is still hours long, every day. If you want to see him, come early and expect a long wait. Otherwise, it may be enough to just stroll along the massive plaza outside. You cannot take photos inside, and I am told the hours are short to help preserve his remains, which are on full view.

reviews.author: Nash
reviews.title: Average
reviews.content: We went on Monday and found that the gate is from behind and you need to walk for 5 mins. Once we went inside we saw museum was closed and there was a temple to see and take a picture. Nothingmore

reviews.author: exchips51
reviews.title: Long Queue
reviews.content: We went as part of an organised tour but still had to experience a long queue and a 50 minute wait to get a glimpse of Uncle Ho. The mausoleum is impressive directly opposite the “parliament “. It is fronted by the usual large communist square for grand parades. Worth ticking off your bucket list if you have the interest. Visiting Ho,s house etc is very worthwhile.

reviews.author: Sam S
reviews.title: A homage to President Ho Chi Minh
reviews.content: A centralised location for government buildings, the morsleum is fronted by a large square. Those from North Vietnam pay homage to their beloved saviour. Alongside, there are the living quarters of Ho Chi Minh. They have been preserved and are open for viewing. Ho Chi Minh was not one to live in the splendour of the adjacent Presidential Palace.A good place to visit.

reviews.author: jcn_uk
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: Say what you will about communism, but they know how to build huge squares and mausoleums. Mao, Lenin, and “uncle Ho” rest in some impressive buildings, surround by even more impressive squares. Ho Chi Min is the father of a proud nation and his memory is preserved in a vast square that dominates the north-west corner of the city central area.It is serene and impressive

reviews.author: Braeden B
reviews.title: Very Long Wait
reviews.content: Went here on a whim because we had some extra time in the city before our flight and didn't really know what to expect. We got in line and waited about 2 hours to get to the mausoleum with lots of pushing and shoving going on. The actual mausoleum building was cool and the experience inside was interesting but lasted about 30 seconds. It could have been visiting on a Sunday was a busy day but we did get there 10 minutes before it opened at 8 so we were just surprised by how long the whole thing took. It was free though so can't complain too much.

reviews.author: Luckylibrarian-The Last Hurrah
reviews.title: Home on Stilts is Interesting
reviews.content: Feel free to line up for hours to see a mummified Ho Chi Minh lying in state. Afterward visit his last home on the same property. The house is what looks like a Mid-Century Modern design. I can see why he preferred this house to the larger official home (not currently open to visitors). Sorry but Trip Advisor appears to be allowing only live shots, so no photos.

reviews.author: Darian R
reviews.title: Biggest entry line I have seen in my life
reviews.content: We only got to sss the Mausoleum from the outside as the line to visit inside was over 5km long. If you want to see the inside, I suggest arriving well before the gates open to secure a place in the line. You may also need to give a day to this activity based on the length and slow pace the line moved.

reviews.author: ozvpm_andy
reviews.title: Tick it off the Hà Nội list
reviews.content: While I have visited this site on a few occasions, I must confess to never viewing the body or visiting the on site museum (always check opening times as these seem to change daily)Regardless, it’s a great an interested area to visit for other reasons - the surrounding streets are filled with buildings like the Presidential Palace, the Foreign Affairs building, the citadel and a host of international embassies.So make sure you wander and don’t just visit the mausoleum site - there’s more to see in the area

reviews.author: RovingSoraSon
reviews.title: Worth to visit
reviews.content: You can find it tired after a long queue to get inside but it truly amazing how they made this place. The atmosphere is cold, of course as this is a mausoleum.

reviews.author: Lin W
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Worth a visit to see and take a pic of the resting place of Ho Chi Minh. Even when I was there, there are many locals visiting the place and taking pic. Furthermore it is within walking distance to the Ho chi minh museum.

reviews.author: William H
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: The mosaleum was very imposing, searches took place prior to entry no lighters. The Police/Army officers watch to ensure you don't stray off the no go zones. Look at past visit pictures to appreciate the magnitude of the build. Gardens are immaculate.

reviews.author: Dobanjare
reviews.title: Good place to visit
reviews.content: You will see a lot of things at this place. Other than Mausoleum beautiful garden , pond , temple and place where ho chin Minh used to live.

reviews.author: A A
reviews.title: Could be better
reviews.content: I had long anticipated visiting Uncle Ho but had put it off due to the fact that there is always a long queue.  Finally had the chance on a quiet day and after a short wait was able to enter the Mausoleum.  I would have liked to be able to stand for a minute or 2 but every just keeps moving along and dinh really have much time inside.  The outer grounds area as well as the museum itself could do with a makeover but still worth the visit

reviews.author: John E
reviews.title: A must see in Hanoi
reviews.content: This is one of those must see places when you visit Hanoi. Lots of impressive buildings. I thought the gardens were excellent. Very spacious location. You can probably spend one to two hours here walking around.

reviews.author: mary l
reviews.title: Worth waiting in the queue
reviews.content: We visited the Mausoleum while on a tour and we are glad we did as it was quite interesting.  There are very strict rules for viewing the Mausoleum and the queues were long but it did move very fast.  Dress code is strict so women should make sure shoulders and knees are covered.  I was dressed suitably but my sister’s shorts ( above the knees) were deemed too short so she used a sarong to cover up.

reviews.author: TGSA
reviews.title: Impressive building, fantastic gardens!
reviews.content: Unfortunately, only saw the building from the outside as the Mausoleum was closed the day I tried to visit. Spectacular building!

reviews.author: EgbertHerts
reviews.title: Important visit
reviews.content: Can be long queues to visit this site. It is a very important for an understanding of the reverence and affection in which HCM is held by the Vietnamese population. You must be appropriately dressed and respectful. When we visited there was a whole school visiting and they were well behaved.

reviews.author: Maria T
reviews.title: Weird
reviews.content: This was included as part of our tour, not really something I wanted to do but we had to as it was part of the tour route. Luckily we didn't really have much of a queue, then we shuffled through passing in a gloomily lit room what absolutely looked like a wax model.A bizarre experience!The military control where you can walk in the complex, so pay attention to signage etc, as its very easy to just wander off the designated area and get shouted at!

reviews.author: R V
reviews.title: memorial to visit
reviews.content: We wanted to visit this memorial inside, however we could not go inside the building as it was closed for visitors when we went around non time. We were not having prior information that it is open only for an hour or so in the morning, hence went around the place, without seeing the memorial, otherwise outside the building is maintained very well.

reviews.author: GWYN33
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh's resting place.
reviews.content: We were lucky, we didn't have to queue but be prepared to do so and be prepared for it to be very hot - , Being of a certain age, this man's cause was part of my youth. To actually be here was spine tingling - A really impressive place and quite moving. A small nation's fight against a super-power....That visit changed me and I must read more about the war. Peace.

reviews.author: xabiirure
reviews.title: Ho Chi Minh memorial
reviews.content: We had time to spare and after checking the Hanoi Old Quarter, we decided to walk there to take a look.Interesting scenario for pictures, not so much for anything else.

reviews.author: Jeff D
reviews.title: Cool Place to See
reviews.content: We needed to kill some tim and the monument was only about a 30 minute walk from Hoan Kiem Lake. The mosoleum is beautiful. We were able to observe the changing of the guards and just a really amazing experience to be there.

reviews.author: pngocduong1
reviews.title: Pho Thin - Delicious & Huge Portions
reviews.content: Pho Thin 13 Lò Đúc was another great pho experience in Hanoi! My daughter recommended it from her previous trip, so we had to give it a try. I thought the pho was delicious, and the portion was huge! They definitely don’t skimp on the beef! There was so much of it! They only have one size, and it was more than enough for me. I couldn’t even finish the bowl. Definitely come hungry!

reviews.author: Maps37681545689
reviews.title: SCAM
reviews.content: charged us 100k for a bowl each

reviews.author: deborah t
reviews.title: Great pho for lunch!
reviews.content: Colleagues ordered lunch for us - great Pho!  The soup was flavorful, vegetables plentiful, and portions were good.  Would visit again!

reviews.author: rara
reviews.title: Delicious local experience
reviews.content: It's cheap and delicious. It gives you a local mood and makes you happy to go. I was happy to see a local uncle who shared a table with me casually pass the seasoning around and teach me how to eat!

reviews.author: Edokko
reviews.title: Four shop opened in Ikebukuro
reviews.content:
Visit on December 7, 2025.
I went out for dinner by myself because it was a branch in Ikebukuro!
Pay at the entrance and enter. I was asked if there was any cilantro on the list when I ordered it, so I thought many people didn't want to put it in, but there was a pretty large amount of cilantro on it that I couldn't see the noodles! The noodles and soup were delicious and I finished them in no time!

reviews.author: Zung H
reviews.title: A bowl of powder to wake up Hanoi's early morning
reviews.content: Queue up with friends for Pho Thin early in the morning, now fried beef aromas, soup is rich and refreshing. The small storefront was packed with locals, and a bite down instantly understood what "authentic" was! It's not fancy, but it's memorable, and it's definitely a taste memory that Hanoi must punch in!

reviews.author: Damian C
reviews.title: Fabulous Pho
reviews.content: First impressions do not do the food justice. Having been up for 24 hours our first evening in Hanoi was concluded with a trip to Pho Thin. The standard bowl is ample pho for any meer mortal and did not disappoint! Cheap, tasty and filling! 60k Vkd so about £2:80 at time of visit fantastic on any budget and a great “hole in the wall”.

reviews.author: Selig Getz
reviews.title: Famous Vietnam noodle
reviews.content: The beef pho was rich, aromatic, and hit the spot after a long flight. No fancy seats, just plastic stools and big flavor. A messy, noisy, perfect taste of real Hanoi with the whole crew.

reviews.author: Adventure05703998509
reviews.title: Good pho but not the best
reviews.content: It's hard to understand the enthusiasm for this place. It's better than average and full of herbs, but it's not the best we've eaten.

reviews.author: Janis Yana
reviews.title: Best Pho noodle in Hanoi
reviews.content: The rich, savory broth and the unique stir-fried beef were unlike any pho we've ever had. Sharing this delicious bowl of noodles in such a bustling, authentic setting was the perfect Hanoi experience for us.

reviews.author: lilybt
reviews.title: Famous Four Shops (authentic)
reviews.content: Affiliated or unrelated stores of the same name? I arrived paying attention to this. The most famous restaurant in Hanoi, Pho Bo (beef pho) is the only item on the list, and you tell the old man at the entrance whether you want to attach quantity and oil gruel or not, and whether coriander can be added. I'm delighted to say that I've arrived soon after and added tabletop lime, chili peppers and chasing nyocum as appropriate. Beef bone and beef broth is a good soup, which fits in with crisp rice noodles and is quite delicious. The amount is not small portions like Taiwanese noodles, and it is equivalent to Japanese ramen, so you won't be unhappy.

reviews.author: Ines L
reviews.title: Super delicious and traditional
reviews.content: Super tasty pho, just like you traditionally do. It was sensationally delicious. The food was super fresh. From the outside it looks like the worst cashmere, but inside everything was clean and good.

reviews.author: 이준호
reviews.title: Special Lunch in Hanoi, Poetin
reviews.content: It was really attractive, with a soft, rare piece of beef in it, and the taste of cold in your mouth. The fragrant aroma stimulated the nose and was the perfect place to enjoy a quick lunch. However, it's better not to have too many expectations. The atmosphere was normal, and the service was just like that. Yet the landscapes here have a charm to make you remember! I'll think about hearing it again next time.

reviews.author: 劉 維杰
reviews.title: Delicious Tour in Hanoi - Pho Thin
reviews.content: The Vietnamese food here is authentic, the soup is delicious, the rice flour is smooth and tender. Sitting in a small shop filled with Hanoi's atmosphere, it's like time is still. It's a big crowd, but the atmosphere is warm, and enjoying this meal with your lover makes us feel so happy. It's definitely worth a try!

reviews.author: Willie Cilla
reviews.title: The best Pho in Hanoi
reviews.content: The richest, most flavorful pho we've ever tasted. The charred onions give it that unique smoky taste you won't find elsewhere. Yes, it's basic seating and quick service, but that's part of the authentic charm. Worth queuing for!

reviews.author: Hiroshi Tanaka
reviews.title: A traditional pho specialty shop loved by locals
reviews.content: The lively atmosphere with the locals was also great. The soup with condensed beef flavors and chewy noodles go well together. The simple but profound taste captivated us all. This is one of the must-stop places when you visit Hanoi!

reviews.author: 최선우
reviews.title: Hanoi Rice Cuisine, Portin
reviews.content: Portin is the northern part of Hanoi where you can feel the street food culture. A place loved by locals, always crowded with people. When you pass the front of the store, the smell of deep rice sauce that stimulates the sores will stop. Make sure to taste the rice sauce, which has a deep and nuty taste!

reviews.author: 시연차 X
reviews.title: Hanoi's local cuisine, genuine rice sauce at Poetin
reviews.content: We visited Poetin, a Recommendation of the locals during our Trips to Hanoi. This place is famous for its local cuisine, and I could experience it personally. After ordering a fast and efficient service, gold-heated rice sauce arrived at the table. A mixture of deep, abundant meat and soft beef was one. The atmosphere full of locals was also attractive. If you want to taste genuine Vietnamese rice in Hanoi, Poetin is a strong Recommendation. The price is reasonable and suitable for Travellers.

reviews.author: Alfons
reviews.title: Authentic Simplicity
reviews.content: Don't let the crowds put you off! Pho Thin is a must-see experience in Hanoi. The place is simple, always crowded, but the service is fast. We tasted their famous pho bo tai lan: a tasty broth with tender meat, just delicious! A culinary adventure for those looking for authentic Vietnamese flavors without frills.

reviews.author: Luis L
reviews.title: Best pho
reviews.content: I've never had better pho than this! It was absolutely delicious, and the soup was exceptional. Everything was perfect, and it's no wonder that both tourists and locals flock to this place.

reviews.author: Sohan
reviews.title: Good Pho, terrible service.
reviews.content: It was a delicious bowl of Pho not gonna lie! The broth is rich and flavourful with good taste, the meat is just superior compared to other bowls of Pho I’ve had in my Vietnam adventure. But their service is really poor. I wanted Chinese bread to have with the Pho, no one spoke English and they never understood / served me.

reviews.author: Chloe
reviews.content: Execellent beef pho, mainly local eating here which i view as a sign it's authentic and good value. This pho is more savoury than other i had in Hanoi, I found it rich and filling. Good value for money, I would come again

reviews.author: Howard L
reviews.title: The best beef phô in Hanoi is right here, and they've been at it for 50 years!
reviews.content: Our tour guide who grew up around Hanoi said this was the best beef phô eatery in Hanoi and who were we to dispute that??  It's record speaks for itself - they have been in continuous business for 50 years and serve only one dish.  The beef phô bowl currently goes for 70,000 VND or $2.80 USD.  It's a flavorful and delicious phô bowl, maybe a little more oily than South Vietnamese phô but that is the style and the source of the flavor.  It's a no frills operation and you pay cash at the restaurant entrance.  It was a delightful foodie stop for us.

reviews.author: Mark M
reviews.title: Just better than the same things elsewhere in VN!
reviews.content: We arrived at our Air BnB across the street, and hungry for lunch. We all had different things, everything tasted fresh and just better than we had had elsewhere in VN. Server was super-helpful in how to eat to get the best flavour mix.

reviews.author: Alex Phạm
reviews.title: Pho Hanoi
reviews.content: A must-try dish when you go to Hanoi is Pho. The beef pho here is still complete and with quality, the price is also very high. You should try both beef pho and chicken pho to see the difference. Chicken pho should be eaten at Pho Tien or Pho Nguyet

reviews.author: Lori M
reviews.title: not great but we couldn't find anything else suitable in that area
reviews.content:
not great food but location near HCM Mausoleum so convenient

937773261

went here due to its proximity to HCM Mausoleum. it was pretty meh. soup didn't have much flavor and the fried bread things were not appealing. price was ok, maybe a little high for the area bc it's in the convention center.

reviews.author: Diarmuid Lennan
reviews.title: Exactly what it says on the tin!
reviews.content:
No nonsense place. Read about it so went along as I was staying nearby. The guy asked us to pay up front, no menu, no choices. Pay, enter, share a table with other patrons, served within a couple of minutes. 

The beef Pho was excellent and that’s all I was looking for. Ridiculously cheap (approx. 5€ for two) is always a plus. 

If what you want is a good meal and go on your way to do anything else, this is the place.

reviews.author: sow s
reviews.title: Best Pho in Vietnam
reviews.content:
After traveling through Vietnam for a month I can confidently say that this is the best Pho. 
The broth is rich and filling. Personally, I like to get the beef raw and let it cook inside the broth, u can ask for extra noodles or if you feel like it, add an egg! Gives extra richness to the broth.
Few spots to sit, mostly locals eat here. 
It is not open all day, they have a lunch shift and a dinner shift.

reviews.author: 理一郎 中
reviews.title: Fast, cheap and delicious
reviews.content:
Fast, delicious, and cheap.
It's crowded, but the turnover is fast.
If you pay at the entrance and sit down,
they'll bring you your pho.
If you follow the crowd and eat it, it's delicious.

reviews.author: kenichiw2015
reviews.title: My expectations were exceeded in a good way.
reviews.content:
This bowl of pho changed my concept of pho, with its light soup and soft, flat rice noodles.
It was rather rich and chewy, and the noodles were very satisfying.
Next time, I'd like to try topping it with a raw egg like the locals do.

reviews.author: bochitabi
reviews.title: Only one menu option
reviews.content: The menu only has beef pho, with pineapple eye as a topping. I pay the bill to the man sitting boldly next to the entrance, who boldly accepts the bill with his right hand and puts it in the stack of bills he holds in his left hand without saying thank you. The interior of the store is not exactly clean, with counter seats on the right side and long tables and chairs lined up from the center to the left. The beef and chopped green onions are boiled in the kitchen at the back of the store, and the staff pours the pho and soup into bowls and tops them with the beef and green onions, and serves them one after another. The boiled beef, crispy chopped green onions, smooth pho and mild soup were very delicious. Incidentally, the flavor of the soup is slightly different from the Ho Chi Minh store, Shinjuku store, and Ikebukuro store. The pho is not slurped like ramen or soba, but is eaten by scooping it up with chopsticks and placing it on a spoon, so it took a little time to eat. There is no water, but you can bring in drinks purchased at the store next door.

reviews.author: angie
reviews.title: Hanoi: Vietnamese cuisine
reviews.content:
When I said I wanted to eat pho for breakfast, a friend who lives in Hanoi brought me here.
It seems to be a famous pho restaurant in Hanoi.

There is an older man working at the entrance, so you pay first and enter the restaurant.
If you also buy fried bread, you will be given fried bread at the entrance.
The restaurant is quite crowded...
However, there is only one type of pho on the menu, so it is served quickly.
Although the restaurant is crowded, the turnover is fast, so there is not much of a line in front of the restaurant.

The pho is served with plenty of green onions.
The soup is also very flavorful and delicious.
I ate pho at other restaurants during my stay in Vietnam, but I felt that this restaurant had the strongest soup flavor and the saltiest taste.
This restaurant changed my image of pho.

My friend paid the price, so I don't remember...
It seems to be around 300 yen.

reviews.author: Noah
reviews.title: Savoring Pho Thin's Authentic Delight
reviews.content: I was so eager to leave for Vietnam because this country is noted for its budget and delicious food. And it would not be a trip to Vietnam if I didn't eat Pho here. We just looked at the Google map and headed to Pho Thin, where we ordered two bowls of rare beef Pho. Pho here was so good and so Vietnam. The things in the USA stand no chance to compare to Vietnamese real Pho. I highly recommend this diner.

reviews.author: Chopper44
reviews.title: Believe the hype. This place. Is amazing.
reviews.content:
Delicious beef Pho. High quality. Sitting at shared table, lightning fast service and really delicious beef. Tender. Full of flavour. 
2 beef pho, 2 beers and 1 coke less than £6. 
Unreal.

reviews.author: CoolGuy
reviews.title: Only one option - Beef Pho!
reviews.content:
Been here before as I can remembered, long before covid, as brought here by my Vietnamese colleague. 

So this time i bring my Japanese colleague to come here for the pho. Yes! Beef Pho. Not chicken. You don't have a choice! Breadstick and drink needs to pay separately! Yes! two different sellers.

Nonetheless, I find that the taste is still good. But as far as i can remember, the spring onions seems to be lesser this time round as compared to last time before covid period we came.

Narrow place with only two long bench tables. Still worth a visit and try out this old shop!

reviews.author: Tj
reviews.title: Food so good!
reviews.content: Very home  feeling food is delicious went here after a long day and the pho hit the spot! This is exactly what I came to Vietnam to have!

reviews.author: Henry N
reviews.title: Great Pho
reviews.content: If you're a Pho lover, then you absolutely must check out this Pho restaurant! From the moment you walk in, you can smell the savory aroma of the delicious broth cooking on the stove. And once you taste it, you'll know why this is the best Pho restaurant around. The broth is rich and flavorful, with the perfect balance of spices and seasoning that creates a truly authentic taste. The beef is tender and cooked to perfection, and the noodles are perfectly cooked and add a great texture to the dish. Overall, this Pho restaurant is a must-visit for any food lover, and I can't recommend it enough!

reviews.author: Matteo Conti
reviews.title: Best Pho
reviews.content: Simply the best Pho in Hanoi. Authentic pho at very cheap price. You absolutely have to try it if you are in old town.

reviews.author: Peter M
reviews.title: Brilliant authentic Pho packed with people who clearly seek out a taste of home
reviews.content:
Found this place at the end of Hardware Lane. Packed. Great Pho and very reasonable prices. Lots of add on options. 
My new Pho home in CBD

reviews.author: Travelly HN
reviews.title: Pho Thin is absolutely MUST-TRY
reviews.content:
Pho has many ways to prepare and Pho Thin is a MUST-TRY as their chef possesses one of the most special recipes. Pho is pre-fried with garlic, so the noodle soup is very flavorful. It would be perfect if you get fried dough soaked in Pho broth!!

Price: a bit too high for a standard bowl (but it's worthy!! Trust me)

reviews.author: Stephen B
reviews.title: Best pho in Vietnam
reviews.content: Best pho I've had in my life. Amazing. So simple, yet it was perfect. Don't think I can order pho back home again, just doesn't compare at all. The pickled garlic was so good. Tried pho several times travelling through Vietnam and this was the best, hands down. Note to travellers, you need to pay before you sit down.

reviews.author: Andrew
reviews.title: Pho Thin
reviews.content: Actually the pho is “thin” too. Anyway, nice bowl of authentic pho bo. Price is high by Vietnamese standard. Highly recommended if you like beef rice noodles with soup. Don’t forget to pair it with the mini fried fritters.

reviews.author: waylandtony
reviews.title: Do one thing very well.
reviews.content:
Having traveled for the last month in Vietnam I have had a lot of their national dish Pho. I didn't realize it before I was here that it is widely a breakfast dish, but I had no trouble having a hot savory bowl for many a breakfast.
I was told by my daughter that Pho Thin was a must go to. They only serve Pho Bo the beef version, a large bowl of wonderfully flavorful broth with thinly sliced beef and green onions. They also serve a Vietnamese savory donut that by themselves are rather plain but when dipped or floated in the Pho was fantastic.
I would highly recommend Pho Thin for an authentic Northern Vietnamese Pho that is sure to rank with the best you have ever had.

reviews.author: Sasha
reviews.title: Delicious
reviews.content: The pho here is wonderful, so flavourful and very quick service. Full of locals who are all friendly. Would defo recommend!

reviews.author: Larry C
reviews.title: Best Pho Ever
reviews.content:
Our tour guide told us about Pho Tin and we had the best Pho ever here.

The place only serves one dish and you pay as you enter (65,000 VND per bowl)  you can also order some fried dough like things if you want.  Although they only serve one type of Pho it is by far the best we have ever had.  You sit at long tables or against the wall with other patrons.  the service is quick and the place is always busy.  We stayed in Hanoi 3 days and ate here twice.

Very much worth the price.

reviews.author: Austin T
reviews.title: Pho get about it....
reviews.content: We visited this place off of a YouTube video highlighting Pho Thin. It’s in the French Quarter and pretty easy to find. It’s simple as in you pay first, seat yourself and someone delivers a delicious bowl of Pho...pronounced like “Fuh”, not (Fo). The soup was fresh and very good. I believe it cost something like $4-$5.00. Very reasonable.

reviews.author: bas0921
reviews.title: Doesn't look like much from the outside, but go in and enjoy!!
reviews.content:
Recommended from a foodie tour, so we went for it. Community seating - great opportunity to meet new people! And the food was perfect Pho!! Buy the bread (extra) from the guy selling it separately.. Delicious soaked in the Pho broth! 
The place looks like some "hole in the wall" which it is but, a great value and even better food!!

reviews.author: Macdarien
reviews.title: Don’t judge a book by its Cover
reviews.content:
Excellent Pho, one type of Pho beef and beer and soft drink. 

A great local resturant with excellent Pho, grab a bowl and enjoy the flavors.

reviews.author: Xavier
reviews.title: Good but ...
reviews.content:
I gave a try to this restaurant, based on the shitload of positive reviews about it.
First, it’s quite small place, you will see many locals eating at this place, which is usually a good sign.
Then to my surprise, we had to pay before we could get a seat. A staff member kept saying “money first” without properly explaining the reason. As uncommon as it was for me, I paid, then took a seat to get immediately served without a smile or even an “enjoy your meal”. Quite rude from my opinion.
An other shocking view was how dirty the place was. Trash everywhere on the ground, even if bins were near each table. That was kind of disgusting, but then I focused on my dish.
The Pho was indeed excellent, it’s far from overrated. Broth was tasty and meat was tender too. 
To conclude, if you want to go for a good local Pho, this is a place I’d recommend. For attitude, it’s an other matter, but I could give them the benefit of a doubt, even if the place wasn’t even crowded when I came.
My ratings are:
Service/hygiene 3/5
Pho 5/5

reviews.author: Philip Lim
reviews.title: Hole in the wall Pho place
reviews.content: Pho Thin serves pho with abundant onion leaves.  Beef here is stir fried first, giving it a different flavor from the usual pho.  The place is a real hole in the wall.

reviews.author: cracyDP
reviews.title: Delicious soup
reviews.content: There is only one type of beef noodle together with green onions, you only decide how many bowls you want to order. Donut is a must try. Dip the donut into the soup before you eat. The soup is delicious and I will not feel thirsty even i drink almost all the soup. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Wagner Pereira
reviews.title: The best !
reviews.content: The best ! Have so much Pho in Hanoi but this is so good! Only one price , one dish ! The kitchen in the door ! Basic and efficient !

reviews.author: Mikaela Z
reviews.title: Worth the Money!
reviews.content: Delicious food at a low price point (60,000 dong=$3-4). They only speak Vietnamese here but if you order the speciality you will not be dissappointed

reviews.author: Adventure
reviews.title: Very special and delicious Phở
reviews.content: This place is near the center and easy to get there. They serve only one type of food which costs 60.000đ for one bowl. It is very delicious with full of meet, noodle and green onion. Their soup is fabulous and perfect tasty.

reviews.author: dhui
reviews.title: pho @ CBD
reviews.content:
one may visit if you want pho badly at CBD.

the broth was intense and good.  yet the rest was average.

the way they made the pho was different with what pho was served elsewhere, one did not get those spouts and mint leaves kind of thing.  So simply broth, rice noodles and beef in the bowl.

seating was not too comfortable, good for solo quick fix.

reviews.author: Travel for events
reviews.title: Service really slow, waited to be seated for a while
reviews.content: Service really slow, waited to be seated  for a while food arrived and it was vary nice, the staff did keep apologising but it never improved  the waite was ridiculous

reviews.author: LMX
reviews.title: Fabulous Beef Pho!!!
reviews.content: This unassuming bowl of pho will have you blown away by its clear delicious soup broth and soft rice noodles. It wont leave you feeling thirsty even after you drink the whole bowl of soup. The soup is not oily and very flavorful, combining sweetness from the beef stock, slight sour fr the add on lime and vinegared garlic, spicyness from the chilli. It was mind blowing goodness. Warm the stomach and make u yearning for more. Two types of beef was given. One was slightly on the tough side but the other was tender n sweet. No beefy taste for those who are particular. They are also not stingy with their spring onions. Loads on them floating on top. It was amazing slurping the tangy pho w the soup. Yummy goodness.

reviews.author: Shuke Skywalker
reviews.title: Best Pho Bo
reviews.content:
I lived in Japan for long time, and the country is known for the food quality for any kinds of cuisines. But for pho I have to say you have to come to Vietnam and try this real stuff.
Rich beef broth with refreshing spring onion. Onky for 60K Dong.

reviews.author: maverikbc
reviews.title: Just hype
reviews.content: The greasiest broth I've ever had.  Packed, but I didn't see any foreigners.   While I appreciate the plenty of boiled green onions, and I  don't mind the greasy broth, I find it to be average.  Deducted 1 star because 60k is overpriced for it, I frankly don't understand why the Vietnamese (I couldn't tell if they were locals or domestic tourists) love this place.

reviews.author: Samuel Piette
reviews.title: Pho Thin
reviews.content: Being a symbol in Hanoi is definitely not an easy things to achieve. It has meet my own expectation, it's not like any other pho i've have in Hanoi. It's actually good and i would love to eat it the whole freaking day if i could

reviews.author: Max R
reviews.title: Lives up to reputation
reviews.content: Having heard about this place we were keen to try it. We had eaten a delicious Pho during our walking food tour a few days before, so had a reference point, but were not disappointed. More of a hearty pho than the the more delicate, spiced broth of the other version, but very solid on flavour and ingredients - many locals also there tucking in, and certainly not for the decor!

reviews.author: Joseph T
reviews.title: Worst pho of my life
reviews.content: This place was recommended by my cousin, but when I got there the pho didn’t even taste like pho. It was watered down and they added tons of onions to mask the non existent flavor. Asked for a donut after we saw a lot of them right out front, but the server said they were out, probably because we ordered one to share. My hotels pho was a thousand times better. This place sucks pho real!

reviews.author: SomeKent
reviews.title: Great Pho in a raw local environment
reviews.content:
If you want good Pho in a real local setting come here.
One item on the menu, Beef Pho, but its good. Try and get the donut thingies “phonuts”

reviews.author: Han K
reviews.title: Local Recommendation
reviews.content: It seemed like they were serving just one dish, beef pho.  Pay before you sit.  60,000 dong.  My advice: use all the condiments on the table.  My preference was with two limes, some fish sauce,  & some sort of hot sauce.  Glad that I brought my own water.

reviews.author: Che R
reviews.title: Really good pho but ambiance may not be for everyone
reviews.content: It is in a small alley which a lot of people may not view as clean. I didn't mind it as much and I really enjoyed my meal there. The broth was tasty and the meat was cooked well. I thought it was really good pho and would eat there again. I did hear from a local that they weren't too fond of this place because they feel that there is fat in the broth and that this wasn't authentic pho. I really liked it anyway and would eat here again.

reviews.author: Dan B
reviews.title: Great little place!
reviews.content: Small, very personable. Great pho, place made me happy, highly recommend. Word of mouth recommendation from a local: spot on.

reviews.author: PAPA
reviews.title: Nice PHO!
reviews.content:
The most popular pho restaurant in Hanoi.
So usually the line is so long, but we went late night and we didn’t line up.
If you don’t like waiting in line, you’ll go there late night.
Pho was so tasty.
It was the best I had ever eaten.

reviews.author: Miranda
reviews.title: The best pho in Hanoi
reviews.content: This place makes only one type of pho and that is beef pho but it is incredible - the best i've ever had. You walk in and pay at the front, then next grab a seat and they will bring it to you. It is very busy and packed with locals so don't hesitate. Just pay and find a seat. I highly recommend if you're visiting Hanoi.

reviews.author: Samm
reviews.title: Awesome Pho!
reviews.content: You pay 60 vnd a bowl as you walk in. That's the only menu they have, so they will bring in. Great local experience. The beef is charcoal cooked. and has so much spring onion and a bit of cilantro. The soup is rich in flavor and aroma but not too much. This was different kind of Pho than I was used to, but is now my favorite. I saw some guys ordering 2 bowls per a person and I totally get that. It was that good.

reviews.author: MightyMike_France
reviews.title: Good Pho in Hanoi
reviews.content:
I was suggested by a friend to try Pho Thin.
I have tried it and I can say that this is a good Pho Bo.
This is the only dish they serve.
Walk in, order, pay and go sit...soon your Pho is served.
Nice portion. Good tasty broth.
I recommend !

reviews.author: Anas A
reviews.title: Authentic food
reviews.content: One of the best places in Hanoi to serve the infamous pho. The place is hard to find even with navigation maps. We got help from locals to show us the location. The restaurant is narrow and packed with hungry locals. They serve only one dish and the payment is made before seating. We enjoyed the food. It was quite an experience.

reviews.author: manki m
reviews.title: Best Pho!!
reviews.content: Hanoi was the starting point of our 3 week Vietnam tour (north to south) and we tried Pho Thin on our very first day. I've waited for 3 weeks and countless more pho bowls all over Vietnam to write this: the Best pho in Vietnam by far!!!! It is a must if you are in Hanoi :))

reviews.author: Hi-there-all
reviews.title: Great dinner
reviews.content: Very tasty spicy dinner which we enjoyed on a hot night,  didn't stop sweating.  Local street food at it's best

reviews.author: SelenaTran
reviews.title: Amazing Pho
reviews.content:
Dinner was fantastic. Meals were terrific and reasonably priced. The service was exceptional and a credit to the restaurant. Very welcoming, thankyou John for your hospitality .
Well done. I will be recommending to others.

reviews.author: grace cahyadi
reviews.title: Amazing Pho On My First Day In Hanoi
reviews.content:
price was 60k VND. came with friend for a quick brunch and it was amazing. the thin noodles with great beef & coriander topping will sure warm up ur body. and the beef had that smoky flavour that enhance everything 👍

u hv to eat fast cause a lot of ppl are waiting outside to get in.

reviews.author: Spkster
reviews.title: One if the better pho bo in town
reviews.content:
This is one of the most popular pho bo in Hanoi with tourists. Price has increased to VND60K  per bowl from VND50K in 2018.

To order, walk in through the narrow aisle and inform the person cooking how many bowls of pho bo you want and if you wish to have the "quay" or fried dough. Pay the amount asked and take the bowl of fried dough to any empty seat available inside. The noodle will be sent to you. Not much customisation available except for a bowl with no vegetable or added egg. Squeeze some lime (from the bowl on the table) and enjoy. Soak the fried dough in the broth for a satisfying meal.

reviews.author: John_Allwright
reviews.title: Holiday
reviews.content: Wow, we had our evening meal there the food and service is outstanding a great find highly recommended if you are in the area.

reviews.author: Eddie Gaze
reviews.title: Best pho in hanoi!
reviews.content:
Been searching for this place for a while. The pho is amazing! The broth is clear but full of flavour, its smokey with a hint of bbq. The greens are as fresh as they come too. 

The service is speedy and friendly it was 60,000VND so its the upper end of pho prices (it has a right to be!).

reviews.author: Carlos S
reviews.title: Insanely good
reviews.content:
My gf and I spent 6 nights in Hanoi. We had researched the best Pho spots beforehand but after going to Pho Thin, we just couldn’t stop going there. 

The Pho is incredible. There is only one type of Pho they serve and that’s a good thing. They have perfected their craft. 

The place is constantly busy with many locals and tourists alike.

reviews.author: Noelle Marques
reviews.title: Very tasty
reviews.content: Very tasty, easy to order and fast service. Really busy but you can find a place fast. The price per pho was 60,000.

reviews.author: Josie G
reviews.title: Amazing! Use the spicy sauce
reviews.content: Hard to know which local spots are good, clean, and worth the stop or not. This place passes all 3. Communication is made easy since they only serve one dish - beef pho. It’s delicious!! And cheap, about 40000 VND or a little less than 2 USD. Comes with all the green herbs on top too. I recommend mixing in the spicy red sauce on the table with it - adds an extra kick if you’re adventurous enough!

reviews.author: Leigh-C
reviews.title: Best pho in Hanoi!
reviews.content: Hearty bowl of beef pho, buried under a heap of freshly chopped herbs... dip the fritters (you-tiao) in the hot soup...lip-smackingly good! 👍🏻

reviews.author: Joanna_CF
reviews.title: One of the best pho in town
reviews.content: This is one of the best pho I have eaten in Vietnam hanoi! The broth is good and different from the ones I have tried here. Generous portions of beef and vegetable is given. It may be hard to find as it’s not as fancy as those normal pho chains but definitely worth to try

reviews.author: Philip L
reviews.title: one of the best pho in Hanoi!
reviews.content: Fresh, tasty, and fast! This is an old family operation, founded on two things: traditional pho bo and efficient turn over!

reviews.author: 49Journeyman
reviews.title: Best Pho in Hanoi!!!!!
reviews.content: Fantastic Pho ... will be back soon to this little gem. Without a doubt the bast you can get. Loved it!

reviews.author: Chris C
reviews.title: Be brave..!
reviews.content: Looks a bit scary from outside but the staff are helpful once you’re in. Order, pay then sit. The Pho arrives red hot within 3 mins. The beef is braised and tastes amazing. The broth is full of greens and flavour. £2 a bowl. Went back for more. My favourite Pho is Hanoi.

reviews.author: David P
reviews.title: Eat where the locals eat.
reviews.content:
Typical single menu food place, but great value and the Pho tastes great!
A must do if you're in Hanoi.
Don't go here expecting 5 star waiter service, its as far away from that as you can get, but pay your money and get a great big bowl of your favourite Vietnamese broth.
Lip smacking good!

reviews.author: Allan E
reviews.title: great pho
reviews.content: It is al bit out of the way..very basic..but very tasty and a great experience. Very inexpensive...$6.00 for 2 of us

reviews.author: Alex R
reviews.title: 3 stars because maybe I’m just not a pho fan
reviews.content:
But the beef tasted like it had spent the last 6 months chewing plastic by the side of the highway. There wasn’t much else in the pho and it was lacking in flavour. 

The restaurant was cool in a street foody kind of way. 

But take this with a pinch of salt because I’m not a soup fan either.

reviews.author: CT Tai
reviews.title: pho sure is good
reviews.content: had a couple of pho bo the week i was in hanoi. this pho bo is definitely the most tasty. i was the first customer in the morning. the warm broth in the cold morning was one of the better things in life !!!! then i went to cafe giang for egg cafe. very good !!!

reviews.author: eannineja
reviews.title: Phó sure
reviews.content: Not the best not the worst.  I didn’t care for the fried pastry too greasy.  But the beef phó was fine but a bit gamey....was it beef?  I kept getting ripe whiffs at first was afraid it was the soup but the breeze shifted and I realized it was just the street garbage.  Everything was beyond grimy.  I dont think the bottles of sauces have ever been wiped down.  But I wanted to give it a go because Anthony Bourdain had given it good reviews.  I wouldn’t return with so many other options.

reviews.author: Mayumi I
reviews.title: The greatest pho bo
reviews.content:
The best pho no in my life. Always crowded with both local people and tourists. Only menu is pho no. You can add raw egg or fried bread if you want. Pay first, take a sheet, then, a staff will bring your bowl to your place. 60,000VND/bowl.

美味しいですよ。混んでいると思いますが回転は早いです。わたしが訪れた時は60,000ドンでした。地元の人はテーブルの上の調味料をかなり足して食べてましたが、そのままでも十分でした。

reviews.author: Elena Florez
reviews.title: Best Pho in Hanoi!
reviews.content: My partner and I really wanted to try Pho in Vietnam and this little ‘hole in the wall’ shop was the perfect place!! The pho was phenomenal and probably our favourite meal in Hanoi! We ended up going twice in the four days we were in Hanoi. I would definitely recommend giving this place a try.

reviews.author: Matteo Albania
reviews.title: Best pho in town
reviews.content:
Best Pho in town! The place is simple and minimal, you pay the Pho 60k and the fried sticks 10k and then you sit waiting to be served. The turnover of tables is fast so if you see it full, wait a couple of minutes.

It is a really great experience to eat in a local and typical Vietnamese place, not really a resto, more a street food place. Truly amazing! Must try if in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Eliza M
reviews.title: BEST Pho!!!
reviews.content: Well ... I had the best Pho of my life at Pho Thin. All they serve is the Beef Pho, and it’s a hole in the wall spot that was filled with locals. The broth is robust, hearty and flavorful. The price is posted at the front, the staff is nice and the service is quick. It’s on the list for a second visit during our short trip to Hanoi.
