reviews.content: It provides an interesting history of the country and the POWs that were imprisoned there during the Vietnam war.  There is plenary to read in English without the need for the audio tour.  I am not a huge fan of museums and $13 USD for an hour tour seems high.

reviews.author: Linda B
reviews.title: Heart breaking.
reviews.content: Part of history that is a must see but hard to see. No trip to Hanoi would be complete without a trip to the prison.

reviews.author: jack M
reviews.title: EVILS OF COLONIALISM
reviews.content: Given the moniker of "Hanoi Hilton" by the relatively few American prisoners kept here when captured by the North Vietnamese during the Vietnamese war (mostly notably later Senator McCain), this prison is actually a brutal place used to house, torture and kill thousands of Vietnamese political prisoners and freedom fighters by the French colonial army.  It is a shame that Western visitors focus so much on the dozens or so US prisoners there and not on the immense tragedy of the Vietnamese people.  Walk around and pray in your heart.

reviews.author: Johnfrisbee
reviews.title: Sombre but essential visit
reviews.content: We'd strolled around central Hanoi on our last day in Vietnam, taking in the Old Quarter, lake, Red Bridge, etc, and finally the historic prison.A brutal place in brutal times, not much is left to the imagination in this well-preserved remnant of the once much larger set of buildings.We had no guide, but enjoyed reading every notice and info board, taking around an hour for our visit, which does end on a happier note, promoting peace and reconciliation.My advice would be to take your time at this notorious piece of Asian history. Most areas are on the level, but there occasional steps too.

reviews.author: Michelle C
reviews.title: Well set up, good information
reviews.content: We visited this museum on a walking tour with a university student, so were treated to additional information by our guide. The price point was fantastic (less than $2 CAD per person), and there was signage throughout the museum. Only a small part of the prison is preserved for the museum, but told a chilling tale.Great exhibition looking forward to peace at the end. The museum is worth a visit to learn about the prisoners (Vietnamese by the French, Americans by the Vietnamese), terrible conditions and history.

reviews.author: Hardbodyrealtor
reviews.title: Very Raw
reviews.content: This tour is very graphic, raw and chilling. You get a sense of the struggle and rise the Vietnamese went through. It feels like you can still feel the spirits of the people in the cells.. sheds a new light on Vietnamese culture and is definitely worth a visit. Its about 2 hrs.

reviews.author: Miondon
reviews.title: A well maintained prison
reviews.content: This was recommended to us by another couple who we met on a tour. The prison has been really well maintained and they have preserved the sentiment and feelings. It was so sad to see the treatment of the political prisoners in the prison but it is a good trip to make. The memorial was very touching especially the exhibits from around the world.

reviews.author: Amar K
reviews.title: Inspiring struggle against colonialism
reviews.content: Our second time to visit this prison museum.  I enjoyed it even better this time and found the determination of the Vietnamese people as they struggled for freedom under French colonialism very inspiring.  The long rooms with their shackles, the heavy iron doors, the solitary confinement cells, the instruments of torture and finally the guillotine brought into sharp focus the cruelty of imperialism and conquest, and the resilience of the human spirit. The “Hanoi Hilton” part of the exhibit is equally interesting, with videos and exhibits from the American war on Vietnam.  A section on the anti-Vietnam war activities in the US and other countries was a heart-warm reminder of how the last generation stood up against war. The audio guide is very informative. I would suggest at least 2-3 hours for the museum.

reviews.author: Scot
reviews.title: Worth Seeing
reviews.content: Known as the Hanoi Hilton from the "American" war, as the locals call it.  I was unaware that before the American pilots were held there, it was a French prison for Viet Namese, and  not a very nice place.  As others have said, it is a good place to go to be reminded of man's cruelty to man.  It has a fascinating history and lots of interesting information, definitely worth a visit

reviews.author: MarkfromtheIsland
reviews.title: Interesting and depressing at the same time
reviews.content: A sad reminder of the cruelty humans are comfortable inflicting on one another.  Worth a visit if only to remind ourselves never to allow these kinds of horrors to happen again.  This isn't a particularly large museum but they've left enough of the original nightmarishness intact to drive the point home.

reviews.author: CherelleJ
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: I had no expectations. We paid 30,000vnd each and another 50,000vnd each for audio tour. Very informative and raw. The way they created realistic conditions with sculptures made it seem very eerie. The tour took about 1.5 - 2 hours.

reviews.author: Sharad Khurana
reviews.title: A lot of history behind the bars
reviews.content: Like any other prison in a colony, this one also has many stories of human rights violations and atrocities  of the rulers over the common people. Depressing but important to see and appreciate the efforts of those who fought against the colonial rule to over turn it and attain freedom for their nation.

reviews.author: vacation and foodie
reviews.title: Bit of a rip off
reviews.content: Charged 40,000 to enter asked if I’d like to buy a guide at 20,000 Went in to collect audio guide the leaflet was the guide I bought another 50,000 for audio Plus 100,000 security deposit Phew I was now in!!!!Interesting account of how poorly they were treated by the french when occupied Not much about the Hanoi Hilton prison where high ranking officers were kept So if your wanting to learn more about this don’t waste your money

reviews.author: quavec
reviews.title: Informative and well-preserved
reviews.content: Did not have any expectation when we visited the place, but turns out to be one of the places in Hanoi city that left an impression. Well-organised museum with good information about the history and exhibits. Worth a visit if you like history and museums.

reviews.author: thelionspet
reviews.title: Insightful
reviews.content: Really enjoyed this visit to the Hanoi Hilton. It’s small but captures a lot about times past and the terrible conditions. Would recommend.

reviews.author: DRW44
reviews.title: NOT GOREY
reviews.content: We were worried that the old prison would only be featuring the story of US prisoners of war but no, it tells the story of the prison and its prisoners from a long time ago under both Vietnamese and French control. Audio guides available. Basic WC.

reviews.author: adit3005
reviews.title: Well kept memorial
reviews.content: Consistent with views of the other reviewers on this site, being informative and well preserved.  Also retains the eeriness of the prison

reviews.author: tjys
reviews.title: A decent Vietnamese historical perspective
reviews.content: First the good. It’s easy to find. We were told it was free but it was only 10K VD. The museum is logically laid out and is easy to follow. Displays have English entries. Audio is offered for 50K VD. Interested perspective on how the French and US plays in Vietnamese history. Down side. It’s a lot of propaganda but once you realize what the underlying themes are it’s easy to get by it all. It is worth the visit. Just realize that the victors get to write their history.

reviews.author: yv
reviews.title: Educational place!
reviews.content: The place is very educational and I’ve learned a lot about the history of the revolution in Vietnam. It is also a very inspiring place.

reviews.author: Ruth B
reviews.title: Prison visit
reviews.content: The prison was easy to wonder through, displays were in Vietnamese and English and it was not crowded. I found some of it hard to take due to the topic but interesting none the less.

reviews.author: kanddhanson
reviews.title: A prison you have to visit to learn about history
reviews.content: We decided to head to the prison to learn about what happened during the wars. The prison was well preserved and had lots of information about the history. Eye opening (and some bits maybe not suitable for children) but worth seeing to understand history (I kept our 4 year old away from some of the areas). It’s very well kept and lots to do although it’s small - I think we were there for a max of 1 hour.

reviews.author: yvonne405
reviews.title: Interesting & eye opening
reviews.content: The prison is interesting & tells the history from  perspective that people in the western world don't normally get. Well worth visiting.

reviews.author: Candice T
reviews.title: Interesting exhibits
reviews.content: This place will take about 1-1.5 hour to visit. I suggest getting an audio guide (50K VND plus another 50K VND as a deposit) to get more detailed information about the place. They actually have a lot of signages and explanations in English already, so you can just read it at your own pace, especially if you just want to go through some areas faster than the others. Overall, good place to learn about their history.

reviews.author: Ev_kka
reviews.title: A bit depressing
reviews.content: It is good to see these things, but be prepared, that it is a bit depressing to see the conditions in which the prisoners have to live. It took ua sbout 45 minutes to see the expositions and it was not crowded - only few other visitors were there.

reviews.author: Jay
reviews.title: Fascinating for a different reason
reviews.content: There are two themes I saw here: how badly the French treated the Vietnamese during their occupation, and how well the Vietnamese treated US POW during their capture. It's definitely worth a visit if you are educated in the west and you want a different perspective on parts if history you have learned. Definitely won't see these things in any Western text books.

reviews.author: baghdadlian
reviews.title: Experience-Sad what prisoners went through
reviews.content: Went to visit the Hoa Lo Prison or Maison Central it is a nice interesting museum and it shows what the prisoners went through.  Very sad to see the awful treatment that they had to endure.  War is awful Never again should anyone experience this.

reviews.author: Jackthegardener
reviews.title: Boring
reviews.content: Not that exciting really. Audio guide was poor. Could have been good if items had been left in original place, and the main prison kept.

reviews.author: Brad R
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton, but not really.
reviews.content: Only part of the prison has been preserved. Rest has given way to urban renewal. They show some of the conditions that existed but speak mostly of its time as a prison the French used against the Vietnamese. There is a small section that talks about the Vietnam war but it is kind of glossed over and there are propaganda photos of American pilots playing basketball, chess, and appearing to be having a comfortable captivity. Still a place that needs to be seen.

reviews.author: Simone B
reviews.title: Informative prison visit
reviews.content: Very interesting visit . Great to understand the history of Hanoi Hilton . This was my second visit as I came with friends this time

reviews.author: Martin D
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: Very interesting place lots of history well worth a visit, allow at least 2-3 hours to take it all in

reviews.author: ELRamsden1994
reviews.title: Interesting visit
reviews.content: Really interesting visit, for such a good price. Definitely make sure you get the audio guide (if you don't speak Vietnamese) otherwise you'll have no idea what's going on!

reviews.author: Manogaran S
reviews.title: Han La Bay Tour
reviews.content: We travelled on the V Spirit Premier to Lan Har Bay. We enjoyed the bright caves, the food on board the cruise. The cabin was clean and v comfortable. The staff like Manh were friendly and we had excellent food - lunch, breakfast and wonderful dinner. There was a musician on board who entertained us with traditional Vietnamese music.

reviews.author: Candice
reviews.title: Place worth a visit
reviews.content: Well worth to spend an hour or more at this place to learn more about how the life of the Vietnamese prisoner during the war period. The Audio Guide can be obtained at counter at 50k dong and 50k refundable  deposit, the guide is useful to learn more background of the displayed item.

reviews.author: Izzy P
reviews.title: Decent museum
reviews.content: This prison is a good visit if you are in the area. The audio guide was good and very informative if at times repetitive. The museum itself is well presented and has good artefacts. They have presented the cells well within the prison so that you get a real feel for how they were back then. It is hard to navigate around the audio tour as some bits end and there are no signs to the next stop. Inexpensive for entry and the audio tour.

reviews.author: John W
reviews.title: Well worth a visit.
reviews.content: Only a small part of the original prison remains as a museum. The displays do not hold back on the brutality inflicted on Vietnamese political prisoners by the French colonial regime. From the punishment cells where prisoners were forced to sleep on a sloping concrete floor with their heads lower than their shackled feet, to the guillotine which claimed many victims, it's all there.A further exhibit paints a rosy picture of life for captured airmen shot down in the American war in this, the Hanoi Hilton.A temporary exhibition at the time of my visit honoured peace activists from all over the world who protested against the war.This is not a comfortable place to visit, but it is rewarding.

reviews.author: Muhammad A
reviews.title: Good experience
reviews.content: This place is good to visit because you can get a new experience here.the entry ticket also really cheap.

reviews.author: Nicki L
reviews.title: Known locally as Hanoi hilton
reviews.content: This was included on one of our walking tour trips. Very informative and gives a real insight into what went on here.

reviews.author: familyb5
reviews.title: Quite good
reviews.content: Interesting and distressing at times to see the rooms/cells and learn about prisoners life here in the Hanoi Hilton. Display told us how good life was here for the American soldiers - am fairly sure they would  not  have felt that way all of the time. Worth seeing.

reviews.author: JrnyJunkie
reviews.title: No visit to Hanoi would be complete without a visit.
reviews.content: So many awful things went on here and of course the information posted is from the Vietnamese side which denies some of what we know to be true.  John McCain's flight suit that he was captured in is on display.  He returned to Vietnam twice after the war from what I read so no American should feel odd about coming to Vietnam and contrary to this prison and the awfulness of all war; the Vietnamese people are very endearing and friendly toward Americans...the war was a generation ago.

reviews.author: Yhk44w
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: I would say you get some insight into how the prisoners lived day to day. I personally don’t know if the political information provided is unbiased. Overall, I enjoyed walking the streets of Hanoi. Stopping in at the prison wasn’t a highlight. It nonetheless is not a regret.

reviews.author: GenoMichiganYooper
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison - Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: A little hard to get past the history of this place, in order to give an honest review.This was a part of history that redefined the previous glory of war.When we visited Vietnam, most of the local people told us they just wanted to work on what they were doing.  Vietnam has been invaded so many times, by so many countries/kingdoms, the people just want to be able to make a living, and provide for their family.Vietnam is still a communist country, but only approx 20 percent of the people are part of the communist party.  You have to apply to get in, and if anyone in your family past committed any previous affront to the party, you will not get in.This prison museum depicts the prisoner conditions, including photos of previous prisoners, how well they were treated, and how they lived while in prison.The photos included shots of John McCain, and his history in the prison.  How he refused to be released from prison, until all prisoners were released.There is a souvenir shop, restrooms/WC onsite, and the souvenir shop takes credit cards.The museum is a political statement on how well the prisoners were treated, and knowing that the internet in Vietnam is still controlled by the government, to this day, it is a sad state of affairs. Our intent was not to make this review a political statement.  We lost the war, but left them with generations of physical deformation from using Agent Orange....who really won, and who really lost.This is an inexpensive look into the war, and the reality that if a government/nation controls the flow of information, they control the perception of reality for the population.We heartily suggest visiting this museum.Mahalo

reviews.author: Spaghetti and Meatballs
reviews.title: Worth a look
reviews.content: Very interesting reading about all the prisoners and learning history of Vietnam. Very cheap to get in.

reviews.author: Michael
reviews.title: Interesting & Detailed
reviews.content: This is a really interesting place to visit as it highlights the brutality of war and has plenty of information and artefacts. We didn't use the audio service and we still had a good experience and learnt a lot. The prison is also quite open in that you can walk into the cells and torture rooms etc. which makes the experience more moving. It is also close to Hoan Kiem lake (around a 15 minute walk) and the tickets are very cheap. They also do discounts for students and elderly people. You could spend 1-3 hours here depending on your interest and attention to detail. The only negative is that some of the displays did seem a bit biased; implying American POWs had a great time in Vietnam and went home with nice souvenirs... we weren't entirely sure on the authenticity of that.Overall, it was really interesting and eye-opening, I would definitely recommend!

reviews.author: Ati
reviews.title: Nice place with loads of history behind
reviews.content: Strongly recommend if you are visiting Hanoi. It will take around 30-45mins to finish and quite fascinating to go through little tiny cells where prisoners were kept.

reviews.author: Serena
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton - A moving visit
reviews.content: Worth seeing. Only a small part of this prison remains but it’s enough for you to try to imagine what it must have been like. You really get an idea of how it was and the hardships that were endured. Give yourself time to read the many moving stories.

reviews.author: Sue M
reviews.title: The Hanoi Hilton for those interested in history
reviews.content: For the American prisoners during the Vietnam War it must have been like a bit of a five star hotel. A bit of R and R and an escape from the horrors of war. Well, that is the impression I got from the photo exhibits. They were smiling, had warm clothes, pyjamas, tooth brushes and slippers supplied to them. However the true horrors of this jail was at the hands of the French Colonialists to the Vietnamese political prisoners during the early part of the Twentieth Century. I don’t think they called it the Hanoi Hilton. I wonder where they hid the Guillotine during the Vietnam War???For those interested in the Vietnam War and the history of French Indo-China then this Prison is a must-see. Well exhibited and there is an audio tour if you don’t have a guide. Spend at least an hour or two here.

reviews.author: EddieTdot
reviews.title: Worth visiting to see the Vietnam perspective
reviews.content: This prison was originally built by the French to imprison Vietnamese revolutionists, some of which later became founders of the Vietnam communist party. It was also a prison for USAF POWs, who referred this prison as Hanoi Hilton. The Vietnamese government depicts the Hanoi Hilton as a great place for American POWs, where they were treated with respect. Of course the Americans will tell you a different story. The late John McCain was here when he was a POW.

reviews.author: Husain
reviews.title: Awfulness
reviews.content: Visiting it keeps you calm & shocked. How Vietnamese revolutionary were suffering in prison, struggling until they got freedom.

reviews.author: WileyCoyote2
reviews.title: Cold ,depressing and a true history
reviews.content: This is the instant pick-me -up Go to prison + then back into the sunlight3 minutes walk back to Lake ,sunshine and freedom All things you appreciate more after seeing the conditions and lives of the prisoners

reviews.author: Michael L
reviews.title: Good Morning Vietnam
reviews.content: Where Senator John McCain was allegedly incarcerated for 5 years. Originally built by the French when Vietnam was owned by them to imprison any militants. Then used to take care of shot down US pilots and was coined Hanoi Hilton. Gruesome place but interesting to see. Worth a visit for the £1 entrance fee(30,000 VD)

reviews.author: Jonh LA
reviews.title: a place in the center
reviews.content: It is a fairly old prison, where most guards and is quite large and certainly. It was fixed a long time ago and looked old.

reviews.author: MrsLunchy
reviews.title: A Sombre Experience
reviews.content: Hubby and I have always gone to prisons where ever we go and this one in Hanoi is a sad reflection of war.  The building has been preserved and the sad memories still haunt those who see it.

reviews.author: Raghunandan S
reviews.title: Interesting and touching
reviews.content: The old prison is almost gone but the recreation about the atrocities perpetrated in the prison does evoke strong emotions. Do spend 2-3 hours here and reflect on the spirit of those that were at war against mighty powers. Must do in Hanoi especially if you are interested in history.

reviews.author: Yvette B
reviews.title: mixed feelings about this place
reviews.content: It really had 2 lives.  One as a prison and torture center run by the French for Vietnamese people who protested. Once as a cushy jail where American fighter pilots captured in the war had everything but freedom. Recordings of how Vietnamese people "saved"him from the lake.  Christmas dinner letters and momentos from home basket ball games...you get it.  Except i seem to remember that John McCains time there was all but cushy. Having seen John McCains interviews about this time I know he was beaten, tortured and kept in solitary Ha Lo is largely self serving propaganda.   The tour seems honest pre war but not so much post war. Keep in mind while touring.  Do you need the audio meh I got it but could have just read and looked had I known the stories would be largely BS.

reviews.author: Biffee63
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: We utilised the hop on and off bus service which stops here. It is a very interesting place to visit... very sobering to take in the history of the prison. Westerners really don't understand what human rights we have in comparison to places like this.. food for thought

reviews.author: Steve Q
reviews.title: The victors write the history
reviews.content: Touring any prison is a bit horrific. The rosy picture of how the enemy American prisoners were treated here is an interesting take. I'm sure the American Senator John McCain has a very different take of his 5.5 years here. Worth going to.

reviews.author: Mason T
reviews.title: Very informative, interesting, and unique
reviews.content: A fascinating place to learn party of the history that took place in Vietnam, very interesting with some great displays, not for the faint hearted

reviews.author: Tristan S
reviews.title: Waste of Time...
reviews.content: I am beyond surprised that this museum has such high ratings. This only shows the clear lack of knowledge visitors have about the events that took place within the walls of this prison. This museum is a perfect example of spreading historical misinformation and political propaganda. The hellish torment and conditions the American POWs were subjected to can only be compared to the atrocities of the Holocaust. They referred to notable prisoners like John McCain as “special guests“ as if they were celebrities who should be appreciative for their time spent in the prison. It shows photographs of soldiers getting “regular” medical checkups and smiling prisoners of war enjoying a game of basketball and celebrating/decorating for Christmas.I think this direct quote sums up the viewpoint perfectly: “No more flights on B-52s and carpet bombings, only a serene time for these American pilots to think about what happened and the beauty of peaceful life and warm humanity in Hoa Lo Prison.”As an American, I do not condone the USA’s involvement in the Vietnam War and certainly not some of the actions that took place during this time. However, anyone with a basic understanding of the events will know that this is not the type of treatment that took place. Although it’s only a few dollars, I highly recommend saving the money so that this is not further supported. It is especially upsetting if you are a veteran or have a family member who served.This “museum” should be absolutely ashamed.

reviews.author: ochassot
reviews.title: A must visit while in Hano
reviews.content: A must visit while in Hanoi, the Hoa Lo Prison served as a French colonialist prison where Vietnamese political prisoners where kept in infra-human conditions and were tortured. The Vietnamese turned this place into a American War Prisoner facility a few decades later. The photo exhibit with testimonies is especially moving. This is one of these places you have to visit in order to remember and never forget the terrible things that the human being is capable of.

reviews.author: Caroline S
reviews.title: Worth visiting
reviews.content: Came away feeling that it was an important part of our tour around Hanoi, but the exhibition is small.  Much of the prison building itself has been sold off to property developers, so only a small section is left.  That being said, it is a sobering place, and an important part of the city's history.  Rose coloured specs version of treatment of the US prisoners at the end of the tour.

reviews.author: Steven322
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Visited the prison while in Hanoi, it’s really worth it, very Informative and interesting, the guided listening tour is also worth getting so you can hear stories and experiences from people that were involved. My only criticism is that it’s hard to follow the timeline of what happened. But I’d definitely recommend this to do when in Hanoi.

reviews.author: donnagough17
reviews.title: A must do
reviews.content: This is a must do to experience the history of Vietnam take some tissues it can be quite heartbreaking listening to the stories of what the people have experienced you really need to go and take some time to reflect on the amazing resilience of the people of Vietnam

reviews.author: RibValRover
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton. Very informative museum
reviews.content: We visited the museum in November 2019. The museum was very informative and gave a great insight into the conditions and the initial use of the Prison by the French during the colonial times. The museum then has a small section detailing the American pilot POW’s who stayed at the prison. I would recommend visiting Hoa Lo Prison.

reviews.author: Richard A
reviews.title: Nice Place to visit if you like History
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison Historical Relic is located at no. 1 Hoa Lo street.  It was built in 1896 by the French when they still the colonial rule of Vietnam, to hold thousands of Vietnamese patriotic and revolutionary fighters.  Even though now only 1/5 of the original area of the prison are still there, here we can learn how the prison was built, the rooms and how the prisoners were treated. It’s an interesting place if you like history.

reviews.author: Rob Á
reviews.title: Historic prison, worth a visit if you're in Hanoi.
reviews.content: A lot of history in this place. Apparently John McCain was in here for a while. Entry is cheap, worth a visit for an hour or two. Central location so you can visit en route to seeing other places like 'train street', the Ho Chi Minh mausoleum or the French Quarter.

reviews.author: 216spring
reviews.title: A reminder
reviews.content: Not a very pleasant visit, but from an historical point-of-view a must see exhibit displaying the cruelty of people/nations from all over the world. Torture being the central theme of this prison, one must pray that torture, especially state-sponsored torture, must disappear from the face of this world. The visit also feature the struggle of the Vietnamese people against the American aggression following the French one.

reviews.author: Margaret L
reviews.title: Quick visit
reviews.content: Don’t need much time to do this. We skipped around on the audio guide and needed only 45 min to see it. Worth it—reminder man’s inhumanity to man

reviews.author: clintellis99
reviews.title: Very Interesting Museum
reviews.content: This prison did not feel as though it had been modified a whole lot before they let tourists explore it so you actually get a sense of what it was like to be there. You could easily spend about 1-2 hours here. There is a lot of history and worth exploring.

reviews.author: Jason L.
reviews.title: Interesting Info
reviews.content: We toured without audio and found it to be worth the ticket cost but probably wouldn’t return for another round. Plan for at least 1 1/2 hours.

reviews.author: Abigail D
reviews.title: Our visit when in Hanoi
reviews.content: We went here in the afternoon after checked in hotel. This place is place  to explore with so many exhibits about Vietnam war.

reviews.author: chiangmaicharlies
reviews.title: A part of Hanoi's history
reviews.content: A very good museum that's been well modified. Less than $2 to get in, and well worth it. If we'd have had more time, I would have gone for the recommended headphones and commentary - but we didn't.Well laid out, with plenty of informative signs and text.Good new wall sculptures in the Hoa Lo Prison courtyard, plus a photo exhibition.Recommended.

reviews.author: Brian C
reviews.title: Very interesting but biased propaganda
reviews.content: I found the prison really interesting. Not as good as the War Remnants Museum in HCMC but lots of things worth seeing. Major concentration on the Vietnamese struggle against the French. I am curious about the Vietnamese treatment of US prisoners as well. John McCain was one of their most celebrated inmates. Whereas the French treatment of prisoners is portrayed as barbaric (which it undoubtedly was), the view of the treatment of US soldiers is seen to have been kind and sympathetic. Except that we now have Google so we know that they tortured their prisoners as well. I have no particular axe to grind but the strong propaganda element to some of the exhibits is off putting. Don’t let that stop you. This gives a great feel for what the prison was like and how prisoners managed some amazing escapes. If you speak French and English, note how the English descriptions are much stronger than their French equivalents. (See photo)Entry is only 30k dong per person and is well worth seeing.

reviews.author: Anna
reviews.title: excellent place to visit and learn
reviews.content: it said that there used to be much larger complex but due to city development, there is  just small part of it left. worth to visit!  close to the Indian restaurant namaste

reviews.author: Leisa Mc
reviews.title: It was okay
reviews.content: It was okay. It was interesting to see the history , sad about the torture. entry is reasonable but then they try and sell you the audio part , approx 100,000 dong which makes the tour not overly economical. It doesnt engross you for hours.  The gift shop is reasonably priced, I thought I got ripped off with my wooden box with chopsticks but overall it was okay. The drink vending machine was well priced. It took us 30mins to see it.

reviews.author: sportcar
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton a must see
reviews.content: Interesting to see another piece of history.  Not crowded at all.  Well documented facts and pictures representing different times in history that this prison was active.

reviews.author: MikeLimTravel
reviews.title: Important to know the history of Vietnam
reviews.content: The Evil French. Then the Evil Americans. This country has shown their resilience and forgiving attitude despite all they have faced. As I walked through each room in Hoa Lo Prison, I became upset. How would I feel if people came to my home, telling me what to do? On top of that face unimaginable treatment and torture in this prison. Killing women and children. But I think it’s important to see all of this. But be prepared to be nickel and dime at the entrance. First the tickets which goes without saying. Then they’ll offer a little booklet for 20k dong, which is a waste, don’t buy it like I did. Then when you enter, they will sell an audio tour with headphones for 50k. Maybe it will be helpful, maybe not. For me, I got it for my wife and I asked her to just tell me the important stuff. Much of the information is right at each display. I’m not a big fan of museums etc but I was glad I came to Hoa Lo Prison. I can watch all the YouTube videos I want but actually being here, help me understand what the Vietnamese have gone through.

reviews.author: Star1310
reviews.title: Touching
reviews.content: It was very touching to visit the prison where so much pain was endured by the different prisoners of war. Also amazing that so many countries banded together to help to ease the pain and rebuild Vietnam.A must see place

reviews.author: Ange
reviews.title: Nostalgic, heartfelt, Humbling.
reviews.content: I’m a avid lover of Historic places. The translation service with the headphones was extremely helpful. (Comes in english or french) Establishment can deeply consider Mandarin and Korean as I witness plenty of tourists from China and Korea. Otherwise, it will be a waste for them to just be able to walk around and look images without proper introduction and guidance of the history.

reviews.author: Jane
reviews.title: Really interesting and well worth a visit
reviews.content: Very much enjoyed this museum - do get the audio guide and allow a couple of hours to do it properly.

reviews.author: Malcolm K
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: Better than a regular museum, you can really feel the oppressive atmosphere of the prison. Highly recommended.

reviews.author: 199cate
reviews.title: Very emotive but worth a visit
reviews.content: I would definitely recommend a visit to this museum, you must get the audio tour though as you will miss so much if you don’t. It’s a powerful experience as you walk through the cells where prisoners were kept and you hear their stories. It is air conditioned (to an extent) but I’d recommend going in the morning or late afternoon as it does get very hot (depending on the time of year obviously).

reviews.author: Sally harris
reviews.title: Moving
reviews.content: This is an eye opener! To see the conditions people were kept in after the French occupation and the war was shocking. Must see but very moving. Peace garden lovely. Recommend a night escaping to something happy after! It has to be seen to be understood

reviews.author: PatnPete
reviews.title: Interesting place
reviews.content: There's not much left of the 'Hanoi Hilton' now , as only the gatehouse remains. It's worth a visit though. Interesting to find out how cruel the French were when they occupied Vietnam as normally just associate this prison with American prisoners during the Vietnam/American war.

reviews.author: ARTK81PL
reviews.title: Hoa lo Prison
reviews.content: Worth to see how the western Europe democratic country(FRANCE this time) build in the democracy system. By violence.

reviews.author: Rohit D
reviews.title: Intense
reviews.content: Very deep rooted if you want to understand how the French and Americans tried to colonise Vietnam through military power.Get the audio tour it’s really cheap (50k).Note- not for the feint hearted

reviews.author: Ed P
reviews.title: Interesting!
reviews.content: Well worth a visit, the exhibitions show the history and appalling conditions that prisoners were kept in. Shows displays on the political and war prisoners and those who escaped (sometimes several times). Would recommend about an hours visit!

reviews.author: Mus
reviews.title: Thought Provoking
reviews.content: If you love history and want to understand the Vietnamese and their past Hoa Prison is a must. It gives an insight into the role two world powers have played in the history of the country. They both tried to colonise and control the Vietnamese  through military might. Hoa prison is proof of that. It is small, but fascinating, as it captures the horrors of suppression with documentation, models and pictures. It highlights the awful living conditions of those who were detained there.  It is not for the faint hearted! The American POW’s who were detained here called it the Hanoi Hilton and this last part regarding the American POWs we found the most interesting. I recommend everyone to see it. Good value of VND 30,000 ( US$1.30 or £1.20 approx) for admission and took us about 90 minutes to see.

reviews.author: Maria B
reviews.title: Propaganda
reviews.content: Were excited to visit after visiting Tuol Sleng in Phnom Penh. But this was disappointing. Entrance 40k and then extra 50k for audio guide. The extra for audio guide not advertised at ticket cabin or at audio guide borrowing-place. There is a very little left of original house and building and so the atmosphere of the place can’t be felt. The information provided is full of communist propaganda about the strength of communist fighters tortured by French. They indicate that the American POW that were held here had a great time celebrating Christmas and playing basketball. Suppose that’s how McCain injured his shoulders...

reviews.author: Meghan
reviews.title: Amazing museum
reviews.content: Great museum, the conditions and torture the prisoners dealt with was shocking. If you have the time, don’t skip it

reviews.author: lemmo26
reviews.title: The human can be so atrocious
reviews.content: The remaining part of the former prison has been turned into a museum, that will show you how bad prisoners have been treated during the decades of the 20th. century. I took an audio guide for more detailed informations (2€) Tuol Sleng genocide museum in Phnom Pehn is definitely more explicit, nevertheless I wouldn’t recommend to take small children along.

reviews.author: Andrew C
reviews.title: Interesting experience
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit to what the locals dub 'Hanoi Hilton'. Its an eye opener on what humans can do to each other when war is used as an excuse. There is a bit of history to learn especially from the Vietnamese point of view.

reviews.author: Nick
reviews.title: Different Perspective
reviews.content: The self guided tour is set up well and easy to follow. The tour is very informative and focuses on the relationship between the Vietnamese and the French. A large section of the prison no longer exists but with the many photos and full scale model gives you a good idea of the size. It’s worth a visit.

reviews.author: Annie Hoang
reviews.title: Best place to visit and exflore Vietnamese history
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is the best place to visit and explore Vietnamese history, there are many foreign visitors here, Vietnamese visitors is few. It is actualy not boring like they said, come to Hoa Lo you have a unique experience and know about Vietnam war & history value, to see crime of the French colonialists.

reviews.author: Novice trekker
reviews.title: A small sliver of the orginal architecture
reviews.content: There was not much to see in the prison. Most of the original structure has been demolished, replaced by the tower right behind. Guessing because it's an infamous reminder of the Communist military's past. Only worth a visit if you are bored.

reviews.author: Greenclifflady
reviews.title: Well Worth a Visit
reviews.content: So glad we visited- the history of this place is important and the story well told here. Great exhibits very well portrayed. We loved the Peace memorial especially. Do go!

reviews.author: tubbies74
reviews.title: ' gruesome, yet educational'
reviews.content: This very old colonial prison, shows the unfortunate gruesome side of french colonism..A truly educational experience of times gone by.Barbaric, yet reflective to visit..No amount of words will justify or help you make up your mind to visit here..But having now done so twice, we still left feeling both very moved and again educated..As you walk from.room to room, around a wall, or appear outside in fresh air, try to imagine NOT being able or allowed to, because you were shackled and incapable of going anywhere..Worth your time too visit this prison..Let's hope this type of hell hole, is never to be used again anywhere in this world..

reviews.author: _clesste11
reviews.title: Horrible Place, but Learning Experience
reviews.content: I heard so much about the Hanoi Hilton from old documentaries that had to check it out. It was an experience to be remembered in the horrible way human beings can treat other human beings. More educational and depressing than inspiring, but there’s still a deep respect for history and what others had to go through.

reviews.author: isabella_deruiter
reviews.title: Vietnamese fight for independance
reviews.content: Amazing museum situated in a former prison, dedicated to the Vietnamese fight for independance from the French colonial regime. The building is the remainder of the original prison built by the French. The exhibits walk you through the history of the building and the Vietnamese independance movement including life conditions in this prison. Definitely take the audioguide, it's worth spending the extra 50.000 Dong. The last part of the exhibit is dedicated to the American pilots which were kept here after they had been shot down in the Vietnam War, John McCain being one of them. Of course there is some propaganda here and there but in essence it's a very informative and well set up place.

reviews.author: AnggaBS
reviews.title: You must visit!
reviews.content: Recommendation: 1,5hr - 2hrThis place was surprisingly amazed me! Not only that the museum has some of the old artifact of the prison, but it also succeed to capture the emotion of the event. It's a combination of the perfect storyline and great showcase of artifacts in each room.I love the memorial place too at the end of the journey, it has beautiful stories of the reconcilation in VN and how other countries help the people in the name of love and peace.

reviews.author: julietheoracle
reviews.title: Grim but fascinating
reviews.content: This place is well worth a visit.  The self guided audio tour is very detailed and provides lots of information.  There are some really interesting exhibits and the reconstruction of fate of prisoners is very well done. The guide book was excellent, too.There is also a good gift shop.We spent around 90 minutes here and would have liked to stay longer.  Recommended for anyone interested in history.

reviews.author: Yo Giacomo
reviews.title: Scary
reviews.content: Really glad I never ended up there. The cells were so scary I would have requested the guillotine ASAP.

reviews.author: chloe m
reviews.title: Very historically interesting and informative
reviews.content: I found I learned a lot on my visit to the museum. It is well laid out with plenty of information. I recommend getting a head set to maximise the experience. In my opinion it definitely a must do in Hanoi to begin understanding the history.

reviews.author: swazzi
reviews.title: Very informative
reviews.content: I normally don’t go to these sad places but it was very well documented and lots of information. The statues in the cells and audio was very life like.

reviews.author: S123
reviews.title: Fascinating
reviews.content: Fascinating place to visit. We used the guide book rather than the audio guide which gave extra information. It cost 30,000 Dog which was fantastic value as we were their for over an hour.

reviews.author: Tran
reviews.title: It’s sad but the world needs to know
reviews.content: Very good display. It is more about the French time than what the American POWs experienced in the prison during the Vietnam War. But it’s fair enough because the prison was built by the French. The temporary exhibition yard is necessary but it would be more vivid with exhibits rather than just photos. The room with guillotine was the most scary but the world needs to know what the French did to the Vietnamese people during their colonialism. Very educating stop!

reviews.author: sundogg99
reviews.title: A sad but compelling stop
reviews.content: Hoa Lo (known in the 1960s as the Hanoi Hilton) was built by the French to house political prisoners, so its history begins long before it was used for American prisoners of war. Although most of the prison complex has been demolished, the museum retains enough of the original building to provide a grim look at its somber history.

reviews.author: GuiWong
reviews.title: Somber
reviews.content: Rich in history and important to acknowledge this horrible time in history. Interesting exhibits and just the right amount of detail and time for 1-2 hours. We arrived early and more people arrived as we were leaving. Reasonably priced souvenirs too.

reviews.author: Jud1thmason
reviews.title: Fascinating and terrifying
reviews.content: To go round and see where prisoners were kept and how they were treated makes you appreciate your freedom.  This is not for the squeamish.

reviews.author: L7384VCdeborahh
reviews.title: Sad reminder
reviews.content: An essential visit to be reminded of the horrors of this war.  Emotional to see a picture of one of the protests in which I participated.

reviews.author: N4373RTjimg
reviews.title: A visit to the prison
reviews.content: A great place to visit and learn about the prison and the history behind it all.I would recommend having the audio headphones for the full experienceAllow at least an hour to 1.5 hours

reviews.author: Rony R
reviews.title: Prison overview
reviews.content: The place shows the conditions and places in which american prisons were held during the war time. The small original building that remained gives a realistic feeling fo the though conditions in the prison

reviews.author: Melissa W
reviews.title: Great glimpse into the history of the city/country
reviews.content: Really enjoyed this visit. We opted not to get a tour guide, but I think this would be worth it if we went again.You do not need the booklet they offer you at the ticket office. It has the same information as what is on the walls in the prison.

reviews.author: Lee D
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: We visited the Prison as part of a walking tour and would recommend. You probably don't need to allow more than an hour. It was atmospheric and well layed out. Fairly limited information.

reviews.author: bertiespiv
reviews.title: Troubling account of western imperislism
reviews.content: Worth a visit. Provides an historic picture of Vietnams history, if slightly glorifying Vietnams path to communism.Surprisingly more focus on the French colonial  period rather than the war against the USA.

reviews.author: Enock
reviews.title: Amazing !
reviews.content: It’s must visit place if you are in Hanoi ! I liked it a lot and learned a lot too . You can buy post cards and books in the store. I had a different of his chi min and this place helped to understand more about his legacy.

reviews.author: Dave T
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: A good place to visit most of the prison has been torn down but there is enough left to appreciate how harsh conditions would’ve been here. It costs 50,000 dong with a booklet or 30,000 dong without a booklet to get in. You can walk around yourself or get audio headphones once inside for 50,000 dong which gives you a guided tour so pretty cheap really. A lot of the information is in regards to the French colonial period. Not a lot on the Vietnam War period but definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: christine n
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: This is a tough visit, though there is very little of the prison left, what’s there is sufficient. Built by the French to house 400 political dissidents, it ultimately housed 4000 men women and children in horrific conditions.  Many died by guillotine one of which is still there and there are dioramas of the prisoner, and photographs of the heads. Then you move to the American POW exhibit and its hard not to feel the Vietnamese learned all they needed to know from the French and repeated it.  Worth a trip but it is tough.

reviews.author: Rafe Wood
reviews.title: Worth a Visit!
reviews.content: Overall a real interesting insight into the history of Vietnam, the War and the struggles of the people. Tackles the conflict from a different perspective than the other War Museums I had been too. One of the highlights was to see the reconciliation efforts and progress made in international relations over the last few decades. Put a real global perspective on harmony and repair. Overall a fantastic history lesson and eye opening experience

reviews.author: Pushpal P
reviews.title: Struggle of Freedom!
reviews.content: Visit this place to experience the determination of vietnamese people to gain freedom. You can relate to any other struggle for independence. Though the complex is now small but you can checkout the cells and the way the prisoners lead their life. At times it can be quite saddening

reviews.author: Anniesg L
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: This was an interesting place in the heart of the city. Get a feel of the history in this well preserved part of the prison. A good way to spend half a day to look through the exhibits.

reviews.author: Eilidh MacKinnon
reviews.title: An Absolute Must
reviews.content: If you're visiting Hanoi, I think Hoa Lo should be part of your trip. We got the audio guide which is full of fascinating info (almost too much, but you can of course skip parts which are less interesting to you). The descriptions of the imprisonment and torture of Vietnamese patriots under the French helped further my understanding of the country's colonial history. In terms of American POWs, I am not certain that the information provided about how the soldiers were treated is accurate. Nevertheless, it is interesting to note how this information is presented by the Vietnamese authorities. My advice would be to give yourself more time for Hoa Lo than you think you need, as we ended up spending a good few hours taking it all in.

reviews.author: Matt
reviews.title: Informative
reviews.content: Good history lesson on the prison and it's role in history of Vietnam to more recent history during the Vietnam war. Entry was 30k per person

reviews.author: Raymondale
reviews.title: History
reviews.content: It is the prison built in French colonial period,people locked up here due to their anti -french standpoint,they were political prisoners.during vietnam war,prisoners changed to American Army.visitor can learn some history here,and see some instrument of torture,of course prison cells that day.you can buy a small guide book at the ticket counter if you want to know more about the prison.inside there are some souvenirs shops,but not much related to the prison.

reviews.author: Dave P
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: So much history to be learnt here. Great experience and pretty brutal. Its a must see in Hanoi......

reviews.author: bobbief747
reviews.title: Very Educational
reviews.content: I was very young during the Vietnam War and only know of the protesting that was going on in the US. I had no idea what the Vietnamese had gone thru both with the French invasion and the US involvement. This memorial is very eye opening and educational. You can easily spend a couple of hours here.

reviews.author: Tiktok
reviews.title: Lots of terrible history
reviews.content: This may be known in the US as the Hanoi Hilton, but it began as a French prison, and saw many horrible years of inhuman torture and deprivation by the colonists against the Vietnamese. That went on for more than 100 years, and explains why that occupation carved more deeply into this nation’s memory than the American War, as horrible as the latter was.

reviews.author: Alan C
reviews.title: An education on inhumanity.
reviews.content: This will both fascinate and challenge your senses. The prison is steeped in History and reflects how Hanoi and Vietnam have suffered under 3 major occupations. I was lucky enough to visit with a Vietnamese friend who was a tour guide and learned a lot more than what is displayed on the walls. The inhumanity that has taken place inside its walls is harrowing but it is a symbol of strength and resilience to the Vietnamese people and a symbol of their courage. It is rightly held in great respect by all Vietnamese people. (look for the almond tree). Guide book and audio tour available.

reviews.author: Linda C
reviews.title: Humbling Experience
reviews.content: Worth a visit.  Incredible to see how these people lived and what they did to survive.  Good description of life in the prison as you walk through.

reviews.author: Marilyn S
reviews.title: Audio Guide
reviews.content: Make sure you rent the audio guide for this tour.  The prison has been very well maintained and the tour is very well presented with the audio guide.  I am not sure if you would have the same experience without it.  You have to keep in mind that the perception is from the Vietnamese point of view so as an American my knowledge and perception is quite different.

reviews.author: Richdubey
reviews.title: Would recommended
reviews.content: The prison is an interesting historical site which gives you a good understanding of the history of Vietnam. We didn't have an audio but the information boards were helpful. It's very informative and well worth the visit.

reviews.author: Susannah P
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: Thoroughly interesting visit, concentrating on its time under French occupation.Well documented throughout.  A must see attraction.

reviews.author: Brad M
reviews.title: Interesting and eye opener!!
reviews.content: A look into Vietnamese history from the darkest moments of history from war time to the French colonial times. While showing the amazing triumphs humans will go to escape from torture or food deprivation. Reccomend a couple of hours to truly understand this place. The place is only a quarter of the original size, educational from young to the old.

reviews.author: Elspeth Hunt
reviews.title: Propaganda plus history
reviews.content: Yes, interesting story about colonial oppression, but how about add in the bit about communist oppression post colonial period

reviews.author: RobandJoPerth
reviews.title: must see
reviews.content: Although housing Amercan POWs in the Vietnam war as the famous Hanoi Hilton, this museum mainly deals with the period of French occupation.   Absolutely fascinating while being thoughtful.  A sad testiment to our ability to inflict pain on others.

reviews.author: Nicole C.
reviews.title: Interesting!
reviews.content: Interesting trip albeit a bit eerie in certain areas. If you'd like more detailed information, get the audio set 50,000VND. Entrance fee is 30,000VND.

reviews.author: Deb
reviews.title: Great m
reviews.content: What a great place to learn the history of the country. Did it in an hour. They had headset translators, and tour guides. We chose to go without both and still understood everything.

reviews.author: whereismare
reviews.title: Important for Americans to visit
reviews.content: This was a somber but important visit. We knew someone who had been captured and held prisoner here so we came to see and pay respect for the sacrifice so many men had made on behalf of their country even if it was a war we may or may not have supported. You learn more about the history of the prison before the American war and when it became nicknamed “Hanoi Hilton”.

reviews.author: Austin D
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: Well worth a visit, shows the history from the French right the way through to the Vietnam War. Would recommend

reviews.author: Jose Angelo S
reviews.title: 30 minutes turned into 3 hours
reviews.content: Had a day ticket for the Hop On Hop Off in Hanoi and decided to check out this stop. What was supposed to be a quick visit in and out turned i to a 4 hour educational and even emotional experience learning about the prison's history. Highly recommended

reviews.author: Alejandra
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: Excellent and they offer audio guides which is the best way to learn about the place. We really enjoyed the tour, we spent 2 hours and it wasn’t enough time.

reviews.author: SamW
reviews.title: Brilliant best in hanil
reviews.content: This was by far the best museum we visit in Hanoi, don’t hesitate go and see it. The audio guide is a must gives you so much more info

reviews.author: Simon E-J
reviews.title: A sombre experience.
reviews.content: A very interesting but somewhat sad place when you learn the hardships endured by the inmates it was made for. The staff at the front entry were very helpful. You should go.

reviews.author: Samuel Piette
reviews.title: HOA LO PRISION
reviews.content: A close insight into the ages-old history of this places. A must visit place in Hanoi if you're running low of time to spent here

reviews.author: Jack
reviews.title: Fascinating history and very moving
reviews.content: An insight into the attrocities committed by the French. There is a 'feel' to the place that is hard to describe unless you have experienced it yourself - which I recommend you do.

reviews.author: michael050560
reviews.title: Good experience - good information
reviews.content: It is a special place- depressing - but a place you need to visit. Well organized exhibition. Please spend the last 50t dong for the audioguide. It is worth it

reviews.author: Ariane L
reviews.title: The Prison
reviews.content: The Prison of Hoa Lo is a must visit if you have very little time in Hanoi. It gives more insights into the history of Vietnam, of its fight for independence when Vietnam was part of colonial French Indochina. The French built that prison to jail the Vietnamese prisoners and later in 1954 it became a prison who served the Vietnamese government to jail American prisoners during the Vietnam war. There are archival films, letters, documents, sculptures and more contemporary 3D movies which add a vivid sense to the place and to its tough history.

reviews.author: Sam P
reviews.title: Number 1 place to visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: If you have time for just one place of historical significance to visit, this is the place. Not big, but full of history.

reviews.author: Jsymonds95
reviews.title: Interesting visit
reviews.content: Spent just over an hour here, it was eye opening and a good overview of the history. The conditions the prisoners were kept in was awful, but they handle the matter in an empathetic way. Worth visiting

reviews.author: vickizig
reviews.title: Great for those who like history
reviews.content: Really enjoyed our visit here. If you have 2 days in Hanoi and you’re interested in more than shopping and temples, I’d call this a must.  And I would consider the audioguide a must if you do go. It’s very helpful for understanding the history of the Hanoi Hilton, since signage is limited. Some of the audio segments are long, but you can just skip to the next. Audio is 50k dong, or little over $2. You have to leave a deposit for same amount but get that back at the end. Fairly quick walk to the prison from the old quarter area.

reviews.author: travisde
reviews.title: Haunting reminder of colonialism
reviews.content: The museum shows with brutal detail the punishment handed out to Vietnamese people during French colonial rule.It brushes over the treatment of POW during the American war, but as always, the victors write the record books.Spend the extra couple of dollars to get audio headset,although some of the detail can be quite stomach churning.

reviews.author: Di Thurston
reviews.title: Enlightening
reviews.content: A must-see.  A sobering insight into the French Colonists' thought processes, if nothing else. Uncomfortable, but very interesting

reviews.author: DeltaDawnD2
reviews.title: A thoughtful vist to a place of great historical significance
reviews.content: A good deal of the tour is devoted to the use of the prison by the French to punish/torture the native Vietnamese population during their reign.  Only at the end is there mention of the American prisoners of war during the American-Vietnam war.

reviews.author: Cristy
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: Definitely a place to see. Best to pay the few dong extra to get the audio tour, to get the full history and understand what you are seeing. Worth a visit!

reviews.author: The-Mong-Melbourne-Australia
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton - interesting enough
reviews.content: This place is not the greatest tourist attraction in the world, but then again that’s interesting enough to spend an hour or so in. This is mainly focused around how the French use the prison to keep local Vietnamese in 100 years ago. Minimal focus on post 1960’s prisoners etc, i.e. where Westerners would know the prison as the Hanoi Hilton. There was only a small portion of the original prison retained, but it certainly gives you the feel for what it was. Only about one dollar to get in, and you can guide yourself around very easily. If you have a free hour, it is definitely worth doing, but if you’re trying to maximise your time and see the sights, this is something that you could miss without too much regret.

reviews.author: Leearna from Sydney
reviews.title: Great insight into Vietnam’s history
reviews.content: We spent a couple of hours here. The kids got a bit bored after an hour but hubby and I really enjoyed I t. The kids did learn a lot about Vietnam’s history, despite their eagerness to leave before we were ready. Under 15’s are free. Must get the audio guide to get the most out of it.

reviews.author: Russellx4
reviews.title: Very interesting opportunity to learn more about Vietnamese history, past and more recent.
reviews.content: Interesting and informative tour. A great way to learn more about Vietnamese history particularly pre the Vietnamese war with the US with an in depth look at French colonialisation and its impact on the Vietnamese people and its early revolutionary leaders. Tour also covers more recent history and the imprisonment of US airmen including Senator John McCain.Top tip - get the audio tour, it is well worth the additional costs and add significantly to the experience.

reviews.author: Susan M
reviews.title: A necessary visit
reviews.content: A necessary visit to contemplate and pay respects to all the prisoners who have been incarcerated here. Fortunately there is a joyful, hopeful courtyard at the end of the visit after all the darkness and reflection of bad times.

reviews.author: Turkey007
reviews.title: Very thought provoking
reviews.content: Definitely worth visiting and does give an interesting historical perspective and it is presented very well. The French, US, China, UK and the last South Vietnamese governments do not come out of this story very well. Quelle surprise.

reviews.author: Bouy TorQue
reviews.title: Fantastic history
reviews.content: Well worth the time and money.I’m interested in the life which prisoners went through back in those hard hot days.It really opens your mind up to what people really went through.Admission is 50,000d and audio headset which is much needed is 50,000d with another 50,000d deposit which you will get back and this is per person.Allow at least 90mins to 3hrs to complete.

reviews.author: KSM939
reviews.title: Tour
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is a must see while you are visiting Hanoi.  Very educational.    This was a dark time in American history.

reviews.author: Malcolm C
reviews.title: Important history.
reviews.content: The Hanoi "Hilton" is a disturbing insight into the awful history of this country so often devastated by external forces. The inhumanity of the treatment of prisoners here is graphically explored and reminds us that Asia has suffered terribly in the hands of European invaders. The US use of napalm and other appalling and indiscriminate assaults is very hard to learn about.

reviews.author: Yvonne W
reviews.title: An important piece of Vietnamese history
reviews.content: Visiting a prison is never easy but it is so important to keep the history of a city and a country.  Hao Lo prison does that. It takes you back to the French colonial days and the fight for independence. The prison exhibits are well preserved and vividly tell the story of its past. I particularly liked the almond tree in the prison yard which has a history of its own, playing a part in providing shade to prisoners in hot summer days and almond fruit to help heal them.

reviews.author: John F
reviews.title: John fitzpatrick
reviews.content: Well worth the tour through the place also know as hanoi.hilton.the history of the place gives you goose bumps

reviews.author: Anupam_Chakrabarti
reviews.title: Very good
reviews.content: Gives an insight to the plight of common Vietnam people during the French occupation. Very concise and informative. Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Becki W
reviews.title: heartbreaking
reviews.content: very thought provoking and heartbreaking.....a real insight in to some of the history of vietnam and what the country has been put through!!

reviews.author: BabsSC
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Visit
reviews.content: I wanted to visit this site for its historical significance to the history of Hanoi. It’s hard to learn about the atrocities that were inflicted on the people of Hanoi, I just didn’t have that knowledge....additionally as Americans, having grown up during the Vietnam war, we knew the term”Hanoi Hilton”, which was also part of our reasoning for a visit. We didn’t do the audio tour as didn’t feel like we missed out. Yes, it was depressing but isn’t that what happens in wartimes?

reviews.author: Debs362014
reviews.title: The Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: A very moving experience visiting the prison. You can hire headphones and hear the commentary. The Vietnamese have endured much opression throughout their history. Conditions in this prison must have been horrendous.For me it was interesting to learn about some of the courageous women who were involved in the movement and the contribution they made.There are records of a lot of rich history supported by photographs and relics. The contribution from many countries and their involvement in bringing the war to an end is very interesting. Accounts from those who were interred in the prison make it a very personal experience.

reviews.author: Panhawk
reviews.title: Very Thought Provoking
reviews.content: Very moving experience. It’s disgraceful to think what humans have done to each other through history. The ‘models’ on display add to the reality of the horrors that occurred there. Definite place to go while in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Moimak
reviews.title: Wonderful Communist propaganda
reviews.content: The prison is a must-see in Hanoi.The commentary re the American inmates who were locked up there by itself is reason enough to go.Yes the French were the bad guys... but luckily the good guys - aka the VietCong- won! Thank you for this revelation, dear comrades.

reviews.author: Stephen Trawinski
reviews.title: Just visiting wouldn't want to stay
reviews.content: Definitely a place to put on your list of things to see, very humbling and sad to see what people were put through. Information overload.  Staff are very friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: Prince_Brand999
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: Very emotional place that you have to visit to see and feel the history of Vietnamese people. Warmly reccommended

reviews.author: Ji R
reviews.title: Sobering
reviews.content: The conditions endured by the prisoners kept here.  I cannot imagine.  I walked through listening to the audio guide and a little pained hearing how the people were treated.

reviews.author: Will P
reviews.title: Very interesting
reviews.content: Me and my wife had a spare day in Hanoi where we didn’t have any excursions planned so we decided to go to the prison and then to the women’s museum which wasn’t far away from here. It wasn’t expensive to get in and we both found it really interesting to see how these prisoners were kept. We both had an audio guide which you have to pay to use, but I don’t think you’d enjoy it much if you didn’t use this. We were there about 2 hours in total so if you have the time, id recommend for you to go there.

reviews.author: Martin Coleman
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: So interesting, Dont miss this if you are visiting Hanoi. It is full of interesting information about the vietnam war

reviews.author: Rach F
reviews.title: Engaging - easy to explore!
reviews.content: If you go - grab the audio tour - made such a difference to really engage with the place. We took our 3 young kids with us and ended up staying for 2 hours..  The audio has history plus stories from prisoners - it really made for an interesting visit.

reviews.author: Teresiatraveller
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: Certainly worth the visit very informative and thought-provoking on the inhumane conditions of the Vietnamese politcal prisoners. However, the American POW section presents their time in the prison as somekind of a happy summer camp, which I certainly don't believe. I am not American so nothing personal, but it seems clear you don't get the whole truth on the treatment of the American POW. Because of this only 3 stars.

reviews.author: Aj123
reviews.title: Prison propaganda
reviews.content: Very interesting tour and worth going to see. Found it very interesting how it was portrayed- Vietnamese were in leg chains and treated like dirt but you move over to the American captors rooms and it was all volleyball and blackjack (and apparently frequent doctor calls, half the pictures were of US being medically treated)- a real Hanoi Hilton! I guess propaganda works in both worlds...

reviews.author: rfstat
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: Small and sparse. Not much to see. Having a guide to explain the amount they have is a big plus. The story behind the prison over time is critical.

reviews.author: mattodowd
reviews.title: Extremely interesting
reviews.content: This is a great place to go to understand some of the history of Vietnam during their war and the kind of punishments prisoners of war (both American and locals) were given. There is a small entry fee. Would recommend 1 hour to see the museum.

reviews.author: T-P-trips
reviews.title: Sobering & Thought Provoking
reviews.content: A must see while in Hanoi. We knew little of the struggles of the Vietnamese people trying to take back their country from the French. The minimal 30k dong entry fee is worth it. We got the audio tour which cost 50k dong each (plus deposit) and we feel we got so much more out of the experience by paying the extra. The exhibits are haunting, thought provoking and emotionally charged. Allow 2 hours with the audio tour. Would highly recommend to families with teens.

reviews.author: Ash Mehta
reviews.title: One of the tour guide tours.
reviews.content: This is very sad place to learn history of Vietnam.Take time learning and understanding events of history.Not suitable for young kids.Place is very informative of past.

reviews.author: Julian F
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Enjoyed my visit to the Hanoi Hilton. Inexpensive entry and audio tour. Most of the exhibits centered on the poor treatment of Vietnamese nationalists by the French imperialists- which was fine. However, the treatment of American prisoners during the Vietnam War was glossed over and exhibits made out that they enjoyed a “summer camp” atmosphere. Interesting place- a shame the whole site was not preserved.

reviews.author: 4tuataras
reviews.title: Worth a visit!
reviews.content: We came here with our family (2 adults and 2x 15 year olds) to kill a bit of time, and were pleasantly surprised. They didn’t charge us for the girls, and it is quite reasonably priced.When you enter, you enter into the middle of the prison- so make sure you go to both ends. We watched the videos of the history- gave us an idea of what it must have been liked (and interesting to hear who long it had been there- and the different types of ‘prisoners’ who had been incarcerated (Vietnamese, American soldiers etc).The actual relics and photos were interesting to see- and the exhibition of the ‘American/Vietnamese war’ thought provoking. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: LeeCSydney
reviews.title: Very informative
reviews.content: A great place to learn about the history of the Vietnamese  people. Highly recommend getting audio guide. Very hot but worth the effort. Imagining what it was like for inmates living in those harsh conditions.

reviews.author: Victor M
reviews.title: Important Part of Vietnamese History
reviews.content: Interesting and important part of French Colonial Vietnamese history.We got very bad vibes here - reflecting past events in this place with Madam Guillotine still in situ.

reviews.author: bushroda
reviews.title: Fascinating look at history with a different perspective.
reviews.content: Fascinating look at history with a different perspective.I enjoyed (if that is the right word) a couple of hours here and came a way with a new understanding of colonial times and also a new view on more recent history.You do have to keep in mind that you are only getting the "official" version of events.

reviews.author: Bodzamick
reviews.title: Loved the History
reviews.content: Well worth the visit. Well organised and helpful staff. An amazing history from the French colonial days to "Hanoi Hilton".I found ut fascinating.

reviews.author: Livethedream2019
reviews.title: Well worth the visit!
reviews.content: With an audio guide, you really get some good insights into the history of this prison.  Very sad but very important part of Vietnam history.

reviews.author: Anderskov02
reviews.title: The Old prison in Hanoi
reviews.content: truly worth a visit, a powerful experience that shows the atrocities of the prison under the French colonial power.  The exhibition is beautifully illustrated with figures, letters and tools from time in prison.  it is possible to rent audio hearing guide, we did not do this, so do not know if this is recommended or not

reviews.author: ExplorerGabor
reviews.title: Little piece of history
reviews.content: The prison is interesting to visit and there are plenty of interpretive signs and videos in English.  It’s very focused on the French era when the Vietnamese revolutionaries were imprisoned and tortured.  Only a small section on the US war prisoners.

reviews.author: Andrew P
reviews.title: Interesting place but sad
reviews.content: Really worth a visit.It costs pennies to get in but if you don't have a tear in your eye when you leave you have a heart of stone.The history it covers is really interesting from the French colonisation through to present day.Obviously a more local slant to what you usually hear but it would be a real shame to miss this place.

reviews.author: Manuhel M
reviews.title: Culture & heritage
reviews.content: A place “must visit” because it’s esencial HaNoi and vietnamese culture and history. Be aware this is a place that can touch your emotions if you are sensitive enough

reviews.author: BigFoodBigTipsBigFun
reviews.title: More of a communist party propaganda vehicle than a historical attraction.
reviews.content: Fairly interesting tour which details the imprisonment of the Vietnamese by colonial French forces as well as the later imprisonment of American pilots during the Vietnam war. I wouldn't place much credence on its factual accuracy. The prison is described as "Hell of hell" when run by the French, but suddenly turns into a happy summer camp for Americans when imprisoned by the Vietnamese (photos of smiling Americans and alleged doctors). The propaganda is rife throughout, which I found quite amusing. Other than some interesting photos there isn't a great deal to view here. It's a time filler, not a "must-see".

reviews.author: Ian W
reviews.title: Good history lesson
reviews.content: No wonder it was called the Hanoi Hilton by the captured American pilots, they got it pretty good compared to the suffering the Vietnamese endured from the French. A real eye opener for history buffs. It is air conditioned and comfortable and you can hire audio tour headphones for 120,000 dong and 100,000 being refunded upon return of the headphones.

reviews.author: Chris J
reviews.title: History with a healthy dose of propaganda
reviews.content: If you're to believe everything at the Hoa Lo Prison, you would believe that the Vietnamese were always persecuted, but they were good to their captives.  (I think John McCain recalled otherwise).   I know that the winners always get to write history, but I don't really believe that POWs were only "temporarily detained"

reviews.author: Adam Pham
reviews.title: The hell of the hell
reviews.content: Thank for having this in Hanoi to help us (Hanoians) understand more about what happened in the pass, we really learn from this

reviews.author: Josh
reviews.title: Necessary and Inspiring
reviews.content: I was so moved by this place. My heart was broken after seeing the inhumanities done, and the museum did a good job of telling it as it is. While depressing, I was also impressed by the unwavering strength and determination of the Vietnamese—something that they undoubtedly carry to this day.Overall, I recommend this museum to acknowledge a dark chapter in Vietnam’s history and honor those suffered and resisted.

reviews.author: Heather D
reviews.title: Too little time..
reviews.content: Was visiting as part of day tour so was rushed through. Plan to spend an hour or two here, learning about the history of the Hanoi 'Hilton and the inhumane treatment of Vietnamese prisoners, the American pilots shot down over Hanoi and the exhibition of the desire for peace around the world. Well worth the visit.

reviews.author: murrbren
reviews.title: interesting
reviews.content: Very interesting place to visit. Audio is excellent.Bit of propoganda to deal with but stillvery  good and gives you more of a picture,horrific as it sometimes was, of the history of Hanoi and Vietnam when it was part of Indo China and the role of the prison in the Vietnam war.

reviews.author: terriw1212
