reviews.content: When visiting the Hao Lo Prison, be ready to be taken back into a gloomy past, yet so fascinating…especially for the history buff or if you have seen the movie “Hanoi Hilton” which is Hollywood movie based on life in this prison. This is also the famous prison where the Late Senator John McMcain (U.S.) was held as a P.O.W. There will be some artifacts from his time there. The prison shows how daily life was in the prison run by the French. Half of the prison is intact and gives you a surreal feeling of being inside. There is so much to tell abut this place that I do not know where to begin. We do have a video we posted on our Youtube Channel: Tenaj and Tino. Please feel free to check it out for more in-depth review. A Must Go…While In Hanoi

reviews.author: thamnguyen994
reviews.title: Good choice to visit in Hanoi
reviews.content: Our family went there in last Sunday, the prison normally not very crowded. Staffs are friendly and enthusiastic. You can see the introduction video about the war in Vietnam. Every picture has explanation which make you understand everything without the guide.

reviews.author: George S
reviews.title: Very biased view of history
reviews.content: If you want an accurate count of history, don’t follow this tour. Very inaccurate accounts were stated based on what people have said to the public verse what was stated in the prison itself.

reviews.author: Dionges1
reviews.title: Emphasis Mostly on the Mistreatment of Vietnamese During French Colonial Times
reviews.content: Visited with a tour group. There is only about 15% of the original prison left. Land no longer part of the prison used for commercial businesses including the Somerset Grand Hanoi Hotel. Museum and displays more anti-French and the French Colonial period, that were very trying times. Very little regarding the imprisonment and treatment of US service personnel. There are a few pictures that implied good treatment, which was not true. Consider saving the price of admission by reading up on the history of the prison online, hopefully a balanced history, and walking around what remains of the original building which is a little more than the front façade. What I found most interesting were the historical photos and diagrams.

reviews.author: Tiffany
reviews.title: Extremely interesting!
reviews.content: My boyfriend and I went to Hoa Lo Prison after our tour guide suggested that it may be something we would find interesting.We went alone without a tour guide and found the history of the prison so fascinating. We learnt so many historical facts that we did not previously know. This prison has a very rich history and the museum has been so well preserved. It is absolutely worth the visit!

reviews.author: jim b
reviews.title: An absolute must
reviews.content: I grew up with the war and has heard about the Hanoi Hilton but I learned so much more. As a colonial prison the treatment of prisoners was horrendous and testament to the cruelty of a imperialist western cultures. The history is presented very well and the past can be felt

reviews.author: WhiskeyKent
reviews.title: Hanoi Prison
reviews.content: Brought sorrow to the suffering endured. Enlightened to the full history covering from build to as recent as 1972/73

reviews.author: Topbloke68
reviews.title: VERY INTERESTING
reviews.content: Got the hop on hop off bus to this attraction.   Not much of the original prison left but nevertheless it provides a very interesting insight when the french ruled  and also as the American prison.   There may be some propaganda of how well they treated the American soldiers in the stories told, but leave that for you to decide?  Some graphic images  within the exhibition, but well worth the visit to the Hanoi Hilton.

reviews.author: HendryD
reviews.title: The most interesting museum in Hanoi.
reviews.content: For someone that love history,this museum is really recommended. You can find the history from the French colonization and to the Vietnam war. It is a small museum but it held so much history in it. The museum have some aircon so you will be find on summer time. 30.000 for adult or 100.000 for a group below 20 pax.

reviews.author: Robert P
reviews.title: Very moving but interesting tour
reviews.content: Excellent exhibition and museum. Well worth getting the audio guide and spending the hour and a half or so it takes to get round.They don’t pull any punches about the history of the “Hanoi Hilton”. Excellent value for money.

reviews.author: Cherry P
reviews.title: Interesting visit
reviews.content: An okay way to spend an hour if you’re in the area. We didn’t buy an audio guide which may have been a mistake on our end as there wasn’t much information provided. Still very interesting and I would recommend it if you are in the area. It can be hot in some areas so go in the morning or afternoon, either side of the hot lunchtime sun.

reviews.author: Patrick D
reviews.title: Hoa Lo Prison
reviews.content: The prison Hỏa Lò also called Central House was used by the French, and later by North Vietnam during the Vietnam War. Used from 1899 to 1997. It was originally a prison decided by French colonization in Indochina, to imprison political prisoners and members of the Vietnamese independence movement. Ho Chi Minh himself spent a few years thereDuring the Vietnam War. it was a second period of activity when American pilots whose aircraft were shot down in the north during the Vietnam War were prisoners here. It's  code name was T141, the American pilots held here called it  the Hanoi Hilton or Heartbreak HotelThe name Hoa Lo, translates as "fiery furnace" or "hell hole" but also means "stove". The name comes from the street name "Phố Hỏa Lò", many shops sold wood stoves and coal stoves along this street in the pre-colonial era.The museum consists of three 2-storey buildings. They contain common cells for men and women, isolated cells for convicts, dungeons and exhibition hallsA building is devoted to the French occupation, the construction of the site. and the conditions of detention of Vietnamese prisoners during the colonial era. The women's building, where the prisoners were piled up in three "big" cells, two for single women, a third for those accompanied by children. Several rooms with windows filled with instruments of torture to succinct cartels, which always carry the same comment: "used by French colonists for torture Vietnamese political prisoners in Hanoi Detective DepartmentA room with a guillotine exposed next to it, and the death row, a series of small cells where models represent those sentenced to death in anticipation of their fate.Another building relates the living conditions endured by American pilots captured during the Vietnam War. The most famous of them is John McCain (former vice president of the United States)All is based on the contrast between the fate imposed by the United States to Vietnamese, and the excellent treatment offered by Vietnam to its American prisoners. In one room, a text recalls that the government did everything to offer the best living conditions to its prisoners despite the economic difficulties of the time. Unfilm, entitled "Uninvited Guests", is also about describing the daily life of the pilots in Hoa Lo, and their release, supported by a body of photographs: the pilots in the process of celebrate Christmas, sports, hospital care, prayers in church ...On the floor above, rooms tribute to prisoners made by the French between 1899 and 1954. The first two rooms house stelae covered with their names.Outside, there are sculptures, large reliefs in communist style, a memorial where vestiges of successful escape like a manhole or pipe.The buildings and collections are very rich, and illustrate, tell and understand the history of Vietnam from the late 19th to the end of the 20th century.But too much propaganda to change its perception of events, people, products, to convert, mobilize or rally supporters. Propaganda takes the form of information campaigns that are always biased and distorted, on a large scale, sometimes insidious.When we read the stories of French and American prisoners. we perceive that information is used in the service of biasedA place to visit, keeping his critical mind awake.20,000 VND per person (about one dollar), visiting time: one hour to an hour and a half with temporary exhibitions. At the entrance, free lockers allow you to put your bag in order to walk your hands in your pockets.

reviews.author: AnnaM
reviews.title: A place to visit
reviews.content: Worth a trip to remember past and don’t repeat in a future. Recommend for All, was a good history lesson we weren’t aware of.

reviews.author: Luxury Traveller
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Very little is left from the actual prison but it is still worth a visit to imagine what does people went through.

reviews.author: Tony L
reviews.title: Hanoi Hilton
reviews.content: A trip to Hanoi would not be complete without checking out the “Hanoi Hilton”!! Very good displays on the way it operates and information on some of the prisoners held there. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: Birch J
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: Small part of the old prison can be walked through, shows some cells, and memorial. Good information (in English) given on critical events. The place can get crowded with a lot of people moving between rooms, try to avoid following a large group.

reviews.author: kkwalia
reviews.title: Vietnam War prison Museum
reviews.content: Vietnam war Prison previously known as Hanoi  Hilton is a showcase of Vietnam War prisoners hardship. One get stunned after seeing  mannequins of prisoners on display

reviews.author: thornmark
reviews.title: Hanoi June 2019
reviews.content: Very impressed, good museum, from colonial times and through to the Vietnam War and up until it closed,. Get the audio guide very informative, artifacts and pictures show how life was for prisoners here and how extremely poorly they were treated.

reviews.author: Andy
reviews.title: Interesting and enjoyable
reviews.content: Was an interesting visit. Thought it would be more about the US Vietnam conflict but actually a lot of info about the French occupation. In true communist fashion the propaganda that's written makes it sound like being in a prisoner there was a tea party and a pleasure for American pow's, which I seriously doubt. In fact I'm guessing it was closer to hell than a tea party. But it was an interesting visit and if one had time to spare, go and have a look.

reviews.author: Valerie R
reviews.title: Eye opener
reviews.content: Well worth a visit to see how the people of Vietnam have suffered over the years. The building is very well preserved and easy walk round. Audio tours available.

reviews.author: FrenchinLisbon
reviews.title: A must see
reviews.content: The prison is definitely a must see while in Hanoi. You will get to learn a lot about Vietnam's recent history. A place full of memories.

reviews.author: Mark H
reviews.title: Definitely worth an hour of two of your time
reviews.content: I had some time to get my body clock acclimated to Vietnam time and it was short walk from my hotel.The infamous Hỏa Lò Prison made me reflect on the horrible things humans can do to each other.The prison was built by the French colonists for political prisoners. Among Americans it gained infamy and the nickname "Hanoi Hilton" when the North Vietnamese held U.S. prisoners of war there during the Vietnam War, including the late Sen. John McCain. Most of the exhibits tell a story of the Vietnamese communists overcoming their French rulers despite torture and executions. The brutal treatment of U.S. POWs is glossed over, but don't let that stop you from visiting.Seeing a guillotine set inside just steps from the death row cells was haunting and I left that room quickly.Highly recommend.

reviews.author: Rajasingam B
reviews.title: Horrors of Colonization
reviews.content: Known as Maison Centrale, it primarily showcases the cruelties of the French on the Vietnamese Revolutionaries. It is advised first to see the video on the plight of the Vietnamese people. It begets the mind how humans were treated by other humans. Also known as Hilton Hanoi by the GI’s during the Vietnam War. It housed the late John McCain.

reviews.author: Shauna H
reviews.title: Fantastic tour
reviews.content: This was a great tour in Hanoi. It was so easy to follow with or without an audio guide and it was kept interesting throughout the whole tour. Certain parts are eary which we enjoyed and we loved to learn all about the history of the prison. Its one of the most interesting places I have ever been.

reviews.author: Mire K
reviews.title: An insightful experience
reviews.content: Spent a few hours here. It was an interesting place to see the history of this prison. Very informative with lots of information.

reviews.author: CCk
reviews.content: This was a very excellent museum. Lots of information, lots of displays. Very worth the time and visit.

reviews.author: AussieAmandaPanda
reviews.title: Sobering, but very interesting...
reviews.content: Affectionately known by American soldiers held here during the Vietnam War, Hanoi Hilton is definitely worth a visit in my opinion

reviews.author: TheDaddyP1967
reviews.title: Walk through the past
reviews.content: Lots of things to read about the past and about how the French treated the Vietnamese also a lot about the Americans and some good write ups about the the revolutionary Vietnamese cons. Very enjoyable and well worth the very small fee to get in. Also you can go into the cells and see what it was like. Great visit

reviews.author: CollRr
reviews.title: Some of the horrors of the wars
reviews.content: The Hoa Lo prison is best known as the H Ali Hilton, where The late Senator John McCain was held and tortured, after he landed his plane on a lake in Hanoi, but is now held I. High regard, because he dropped his bombs outside the city and not on it. The Hanoi Hilton gives an insight into the conditions of imprisonment, including cells and lifelike statues of prisoners, manacles, the cage and a guillotine. It also gives the history of some of the famous activists and prisoners who were held here.

reviews.author: Tongtonky
reviews.title: Interesting history
reviews.content: A good stop in Hanoi- well worth the ticket price. An interesting history of Vietnam. Recommends highly.

reviews.author: JaceyRight
reviews.title: Definitely worth a visit (even with the Propaganda)
reviews.content: Hoa Lo prison was originally built by the French to hold Vietnamese Nationalists. The part of the museum that tells this story is quite good. The dedication and fortitude these men and women showed is nothing short of amazing. Hoa Lo prison is also where the Americans an POWs were kept during the Vietnam War. This is acknowledged in on small room in which they feature photos of the American soldiers playing checkers and celebrating Christmas. The placard refers to the POWs as “special guests” and goes on to say the Americans loved it so much the named it the Hanoi Hilton. This narrative was almost laughable. Still it’s amazing piece of history, to think of everything that happened within those walls.

reviews.author: Simon
reviews.title: Happy to enter, but glad to be able to get out.
reviews.content: Hoa Lo Prison is a must see attraction in Hanoi. The rich history of the prison is accessible through displays and a small but informative publication available for a small cost.Built by the French, "Maison Central" as it was originally called, reveals the might and control that the occupiers foisted on the Vietnamese. It also confirms that populations learn behaviors, from the invaders, that are not life-affirming, but are as cruel and inhuman. That said, the institution with its painful displays and artifacts puts this history into some perspective and context.You should explore this museum with care and acquaint yourself with the layout. On my first go-round I missed a few rooms, and also discovered a small second floor display. There are some interesting out-side areas to sit and get your breath, and think about that old line "if these walls had ears".My wife and I spent a good number of hours wandering through the complex system of rooms and corridors, sharing observations with as many OMG's as you may have in a brilliant church or museum, but for different reasons.Vietnam War Museums and post American War destroyed buildings refer to the objects on display as "evidence of war", a curious term. Hoa Lo Prison is evidence of mans cruelty to man, and this visit will give the viewer a time to reflect, not only on that theme, but to remind us of the tragedies of invasion, colonization and imperialism. Injustice never becomes old, and it should never be forgotten.

reviews.author: Vincent
reviews.title: history
reviews.content: a nice establishment showing the history of hanoi. I bought the ticket at the entrance but didn't purchase the map. overall i spend 30 mins in this place and gain a lot of knowledge.

reviews.author: Greg J
reviews.title: Tour
reviews.content: Great service and Good sightseeing placeVery well documented and lot of history Tour guide explained it very well

locationDesc: Every weekend, a section of Hanoi’s old town is closed to road traffic, and the streets come to life with stalls peddling clothes, footwear, sunglasses, souvenirs, and more. So put on your haggling hat, and come hungry, as delicious local delights and snacks are on offer. Cap off your evening at one of the adjacent bars, preferably one with a balcony overlooking the hustle and bustle below. Or wander the streets surrounding the market and make your way over to the always lively nightlife area of Ta Hien Street or Bia Hoi corner. – Tripadvisor

reviews.author: kisha m
reviews.title: Best of Night Market Experience
reviews.content: We were lucky enough to visit during the  festival and it was beautiful to see all the lighted boats and lanterns on the water. Worth a visit but be prepared for crowds. Still we hardly ever waited to order or eat at the restaurants or street vendors.

reviews.author: Jean-Emmanuel R
reviews.title: Somewhat mixed review
reviews.content: Very large night market that gave us a mixed impression. There is a good atmosphere there and it is pleasant to look at the different stalls.On the other hand, the choice for dining is very limited compared to the night markets we visited during our vacation in Malaysia in 2025. Here, you should expect a lot of clothes, jewelry, and souvenirs for tourists. The stalls sell roughly the same items (inexpensive, it is true) and in the end, there is nothing very authentic.Furthermore, the space to move around is very limited and unfortunately, scooters continue to drive in the street. I dare not imagine the chaos in high season.

reviews.author: Chrissie H
reviews.title: Fun shopping experience-bring cash!
reviews.content: Lots of great clothes, shoes and souvenirs and super fun atmosphere. Don’t forget to bargain and take cash :)

reviews.author: Travel Girl GR
reviews.title: You must be a weekend in Hanoi
reviews.content: The night market is held on the weekend only on the main street.You'll find everything, clothes, shoes, bags, souvenirs, food...

reviews.author: Rimjhim R
reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.content: Amazing vibes and goves the feel of vibrant Hanoi

reviews.author: thila2015
reviews.title: Safe, careful and comfortable.
reviews.content: Can get lots of stuff and souvenirs with reasonable price.

reviews.author: Jatin V
reviews.title: Hanoi taxi fraud
reviews.content: I have been to so many countries in europe and asia ...but in  hanoi i was told that there are so many pickpocketers and fraud.. i had terrible fraud experience in night matket grab taxi scam.. i took taxi from night market to my hotel ..that was showing grab lebel on the taxi...so i trusted...but when the driver dropped us ..He insisted to pay me without going out of the car and turned on blue light...and when i payed exact amount, he denied that it is not and asked me to show me my purse so he can help...and in the fraction of seconds he took big notes and put on the floor...and i caught him and he told me that accidentally fell ...and i saved my money..but that was the first experience in my life of this kind of fraud..

reviews.author: Jacqueline
reviews.title: If you enjoy markets, you'll love this.
reviews.content: We walked through the market but as markets and crowds aren't really our thing, it wasn't really for us.

reviews.author: Ray Yantch
reviews.title: Better night markets in Vietnam
reviews.content: The market was the same as all the other night markets there wasn't as much food and with all the motorbikes cutting through we made it difficult to walk I would not recommend this one in Hanoi. The one in Da Lat was a lot better

reviews.author: Mohit B
reviews.title: Lots of people and a lot more vendors
reviews.content: Crowded but lots of stuff to buy! Don’t forget to bargain but be respectful. Most of them sell similar stuff but prices might vary

reviews.author: Jacky D
reviews.title: Bustling Market
reviews.content: Wonderful experience of the local market here. Amazing food n music to experience. Had fun interacting with the locals and knowing about their products.

reviews.author: ATH Theatre
reviews.title: Spacious but a Bit Rough Around the Edges
reviews.content: I visited Dong Xuan Market in Hanoi with my friends. The market has an old design, but it feels spacious and familiar. Inside, it looks quite nice, though the surrounding area is a bit dirty. This place mainly sells wholesale goods, so it’s hard to buy just one or two items. It’s a pity that the vendors weren’t very friendly. Still, it’s worth a visit to experience the atmosphere.

reviews.author: loonylou78
reviews.title: Night market.
reviews.content: Very large,busy but repetitive market.Great to wander along at the weekend.If you're lucky you can grab a bargain!Street food readily available too!

reviews.author: Shalini Lalwani
reviews.title: Great deals if you have the patience to crack it!
reviews.content: Huge walking market to be discovered on foot. Loads of food and things to be haggled on… colourful and vibrant street shops with great bargains.

reviews.author: Simon S
reviews.title: Hoi An Night Market
reviews.content: Really enjoyed a stroll through the night market in Hoi An. A good selection of merchandise. As you'll find throughout the world at night markets, some vendors were really pushy, others were good. Be prepared to say no thank you more than once at some stalls.

reviews.author: Matvl
reviews.title: Bustling market
reviews.content: The Night Market is great to explore. Sure mostly cheaper items, knock offs etc but this isn’t a market geared up for tourists. It was very busy. Plenty of food options too - both market stalls and small eating places that operate out of market times too. It’s definitely worth exploring if you’re in Hanoi over market opening days. Nice to combine with a walk around the lake too.

reviews.author: Sharnee K
reviews.title: Atmosphere and food
reviews.content: The atmosphere was amazing and highly recommend for a look and great food choices but if you’re going for shopping it’s all the same things on repeat store  after store.

reviews.author: Thanh Xuan
reviews.title: Nơi mua sắm trải nghiệm tuyệt vời
reviews.content: Shopping at the night market was an unforgettable experience!The moment I stepped in, I was greeted by the colorful lights, the buzz of chatter, and the irresistible aroma of street food. Every corner was alive – with rows of stalls selling everything from handcrafted souvenirs to trendy fashion and quirky accessories. I found unique items I wouldn’t see anywhere else, and the best part? Bargaining with the friendly vendors made it all the more fun!There’s a kind of charm here you can’t find in big malls – it’s raw, real, and full of life. The energy, the people, the variety… if you’re in Hanoi (or Vietnam), don’t miss out on a night market walk – it’s more than just shopping, it’s a cultural adventure!

reviews.author: Willem B
reviews.title: Busy, busy market.
reviews.content: All markets in Vietnam seem alike, all items sold seem alike, but the experience is why I go the various markets. you see all kind of people trying to get the best deal, and that is what this market is all about. Very lively vibrant market, worth a try.

reviews.author: Remi A
reviews.title: Okay experience
reviews.content: Nice but a little underwhelming when compared to other night markets. It does like variety in the goods being sold and some of the foods were not tasty. However, I will still recommend as it is a change in pace and something to do.

reviews.author: corinne_prevost
reviews.title: HORROR
reviews.content: A night market where mopeds pass everywhere, nothing is controlled, an endless broom of mopeds that honk non-stop to pass. Prices are no more interesting than elsewhere

reviews.author: Kenlly Bowne
reviews.title: Overpriced and Too Crowded
reviews.content: The Hanoi Night Market is lively but overly crowded. Prices are quite high, especially for tourists, so be prepared to bargain. The atmosphere is fun, but the experience is not the best if you dislike large crowds. Worth a visit, but not a must-see.

reviews.author: akio9jp
reviews.title: Negotiating prices is imperative
reviews.content: The night market is held only on weekends (Friday, Saturday and Sunday) with traffic restrictions of approximately 700 meters from the rotary intersection on the north side of Hoan Kiem Lake to Dong Xuan Market.The area is packed with local citizens and tourists, selling a variety of goods such as clothing, accessories, household goods and souvenirs. However, there are many without price tags, and you basically have to negotiate a price to lose money, so you need wisdom and guts to get a good deal.

reviews.author: netnut2008
reviews.title: A nice change in the evening.
reviews.content: The Night Market is a nice change from the shops open during the day. Here you will find a lot and sometimes at significantly cheaper prices than during the day. However, the many fake brands have annoyed us a bit.

reviews.author: Keelyimps
reviews.title: Worth a visit, lots of nice things to buy.
reviews.content: Huge street market selling all sorts of stuff. Well worth going to and walking along looking at the different stalls. Grab yourself a bargain. 😄👏

reviews.author: Louise
reviews.title: Worthwhile But Tourist Traps Lie Within
reviews.content: The first 50 or so meters of the market is great! However, the rest is the same - pretty much all sellers are selling the same products but it’s still worthwhile! You can get some great bargains, don’t pay more than 100k for a branded T shirt and 150k for a branded windbreaker - definitely lots of tourists traps here with sellers overcharging, just know your prices and you can get some great trinkets for back home.

reviews.author: BenZ
reviews.title: 100% Go Visit
reviews.content: If you want to visit a really good market visit this one in Hà Nội. There is so much to see and lots of bargains, it’s amazing to see how good the copies are they are literally 10/10. Amazes me how they do it, the market has a good buzz and always haggle. They will always give you a high price but most of the time you can get them down to 50%

reviews.author: Sandrine F
reviews.title: A must do in Hanoi
reviews.content: Nice to see, great atmosphere, loads of good bargains. Perfect to buy souvenirs, do not hesitate to negotiate the price.

reviews.author: Rita N
reviews.title: Hanói night market, not to miss
reviews.content: Hanoi night market happens every friday, saturday and sunday. Hang Dao street is where you have to be. Busiest hour is between 19.00 and 20.30. I whas in Hanoi for 3 days and i found there all the best deals: under wear, sun glasses, sport wear (north face, Nike...), scarfs, souvenirs. No food strolls in this night market but in the streets around it. It is sure a "don't miss it" .

reviews.author: Sunil D
reviews.title: Great shopping experience in night market
reviews.content: great place to get some nice bargains for souvenirs and other stuff . the quality of clothes is good and this is one of the cheapest places in vietnam to shop ... YES... HCM is more expensive than this market

reviews.author: Ros C
reviews.title: spectacular
reviews.content: exceptional a night visit must not miss The inhabitants are really welcoming Here you can eat and buy lots of fresh fruit

reviews.author: Alessandro
reviews.title: Great for Evening Shopping
reviews.content: Characteristic Point of Sale where objects, clothes and food are sold. Famous brands Made in Vietnam are frequent for which the authenticity is doubtful. It remains open until about 11.30 pm Definitely worth a visit

reviews.author: Rachelle C
reviews.title: Fun pedestrian zone, weekends in the evening
reviews.content: We kind of stumbled onto the night market in Old Town in Hanoi but were glad we did.  The lights were so much fun and the streets reserved for pedestrians  (finally no mopeds!) were filled with young families.  It was amazingly hot and humid in August, even at night, but we still had a great time.

reviews.author: RIchard035
reviews.title: Weekend night market
reviews.content: The night market in Hanoi takes place at the weekend and extends from Ho Hoan Kiem lake at one end along Hang Dao and Hang Duong streets. It a large market that seems to go on for ever. It is very well lit and seems very safe. We were there in the summer when the area around the lake is closed to traffic in the evening at weekends and the were many families with young children walking around. The market sells food, clothing, souvenirs, etc. Prices are cheap, particularly if you bargain. However, I found there seemed to be more items with fixed pricing than in other markets I have visited in Asia.

reviews.author: Julie M
reviews.title: Hanoi.
reviews.content: Due to the effects of the typhoon, the Yash Market has not been opened for 2 times. Follow schedule.

reviews.author: Coyote-Travelerz
reviews.title: Pleasant
reviews.content: Compared to other night markets in Southeast Asia and Vietnam, this isn’t the best. Don’t let that discourage you from taking time out to enjoy the market. Each one is different and offers its own unique opportunities. We found wondering the streets and soaking up the atmosphere to be a very pleasant experience. It wasn’t too crowded (we didn’t feel like sardines) and we saw some interesting things on our stroll. It’s also a good opportunity to visit some of the historical places in the old section (like the gate or temples). As noted in other reviews, there are a lot of vendors selling knockoff products (which makes it a tacky experience) and not nearly as many street food vendors as you might see in other night markets.

reviews.author: these boots are made for walkin'
reviews.title: Tragic
reviews.content: Redundant (and oddly overpriced) fake garbage imported from China. The grossly underwhelming experience is tragically worsened by cranky retailers. I recommend a trip to Bangkok for anyone  interested in a good day/night market.

reviews.author: D McNeish
reviews.title: Steer clear market
reviews.content: A market full of plastic junk  . Worst market I have ever been to . I Couldn’t leave quick enough. Not a pleasant experience.

reviews.author: Skeets54
reviews.title: Average market for fake clothes
reviews.content: If you’ve never been to a night market before in any other part of Southeast Asia, you might think that this is really great however if you have been to other markets like those in Bangkok, Thailand or other parts of Thailand this market was quite poor in comparison. Firstly the street is not closed to motorbikes and they are still driving up and down incessantly whilst you were trying to shop which is really annoying. They should stop the street For All traffic including bikes. Secondly the stores are mainly clothing and fake goods which is fine if you want some counterfeit crocs handbags wallet belts and sportswear stuff but it wasn’t like other markets that had cute dresses or other types of interesting items. There were very little handcraft as well but the usual tat that you can find everywhere .Thirdly we found the market was significantly lacking in food options compared to other markets we’ve been to in Southeast Asia. There were a lot of reviews about the food so we came without eating hoping to to try a few things but we really couldn’t see anything apart from a few stools selling octopus tentacles and other things on a stick.  We were so disappointed by this market we thought that we went to early so then we went away and had some beers and came back again later in the night thinking that maybe more things would be open then however it was still exactly the same so all of the other reviews that we read about this market Were quite confusing. There were also very little places to sit and enjoy a drink or beer and watch the world go by all of the shops on the sidelines are clothing shops there’s only really one coffee shop but we saw that had a small balcony all in all probably one of the poorest, experiences.

reviews.author: AJ2000
reviews.title: Fun night out with family of teenagers
reviews.content: So much fun with the family! Great for picking up some bargain clothing or cute souveniers. Gets very busy but is easy to navigate. Recommend finishing with a relaxing walk around the lake soaking up the atmosphere and enjoying some fun performances along the way. Also great after the intensity of the market.Teenage kids cut their teeth bargaining and picked up some decent bargains at the market (I think the stall owners were being kind!). We stopped at an ice cream stall on the lake during our walk which finished the night perfectly. Very squashy at the market and not recommended for prams, wheelchairs etc however plenty of space around the lake which would be wheelchair / pram friendly.

reviews.author: The Travelling Chef
reviews.title: A Must in Hanoi
reviews.content: Prepare for a pleasurable assault on the senses.If you love great food, street side grills of questionable tasty meats on a skewer, a bustling chaotic atmosphere, market stalls of counterfeit designer brands, garments, fruit and veg, fresh juice, toys, electronics just too many to list, live performances of traditional and modern music and pantomime, endless streets of packed bars and restaurants all inviting you in ,photo opportunities and a warm scenic walk around the lake.I highly recommend the night market to all travellers to experience.

reviews.author: Amy
reviews.title: Pocket Thieves
reviews.content: One of the better night market in Vietnam. Lots of vendors and activities. We got 15 toddler clothes set. 1 set (shirt & pant) for under $1 USA or 25k dong. Such a good bargain, I wish I got dresses too for my daughter, but we didn’t have room in our suitcase.Beware of pocket thieves! A guy tried to steal my phone in my bag not realizing I was holding on to my phone strap the whole time lol he was shocked and apologized for trying to steal my phone -_-

reviews.author: Varsha S
reviews.title: So much fun and fantastic prices!
reviews.content: During my final Sunday evening in Vietnam, I found myself wandering through the charming streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter and stumbled upon the Night Market. To my delight, I discovered that it offered everything I had purchased earlier, but at even better prices. In hindsight, I wish I had saved my shopping for this vibrant market experience. It's certainly a worthwhile addition to any itinerary, making it worth considering planning your trip around a Sunday evening in Hanoi.

reviews.author: arpitam
reviews.title: Second to Danang night market
reviews.content: This is actually a busy thoroughfare throughout the day which turns into a night market after 7 in the evening. The flea market is good for tourists though preference would be to shop from the Dong Xuan wholesale market. The latter closes by 6pm. So if one has the evening only for shopping the night market is the good option.One may also club the Hoan Kiem lake - Nhoc Son Temple visit and finish off with night market.

reviews.author: Thanh N
reviews.title: Night Market in Hanoi
reviews.content: Great city to walk at night. They close off the streets Fri-Sun for pedestrians.  Much more chill than HCM but awesome all the same.

reviews.author: Arundev
reviews.title: It was an amazing experience in the night market
reviews.content: A must-visit place on your Vietnam trip. In fact, this is a weekend night market, open on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m. Try to reach there around 6 p.m. and experience the arrangements for the night market. How they are changing a normal street into a night market where a lot of antique shops, street foods, dress shops, etc. are available. Vietnamese are very kind and always put a smile on their faces, which makes us more comfortable and gives us a feeling to spend more time there. Like everywhere, you need to bargain at some points. Sometimes, we may feel it is worth buying something at their cost. We stay there till the market closes. We had street food, bought many items, and talked to many local people. You need to add weekends to your trip to experience the night market. We put the night market on our last day for final shopping before going back home. This is a must-visit place to complete your Vietnam-Hanoi holiday.

reviews.author: Dan80_2013
reviews.title: A large night market, good but nothing more
reviews.content: This remains to be done when you pass through Hanoi even if it is essentially the same items that the neighborhood stores display on stalls (clothes, shoes, etc.) and a lot of trinkets... Too bad there are no very little street food.People and a lot of “xe om” (two-wheel motors) who take the same single path of walkers. Less pleasant (night market not as good as other night markets in Vietnam...) but to do quickly once to see Hanoi.

reviews.author: Vijay
reviews.title: nice long night 🌙 market
reviews.content: very nice market comparing other countries, had great time enjoyed bargaining ,u can buy souvenir, cloth ,and more made in vietnam items

reviews.author: Taryn W
reviews.title: It was okay
reviews.content: honestly not a lot to say about the night market, go expecting to spend money even if you don't need anything or want anything. These lovely people know how to suck you in for a 'bargain'

reviews.author: Jenny Nguyen
reviews.title: Night Market
reviews.content: There are not too many options for shopping but the atmosphere is important when you go to the night market in Hanoi. Remember to bargain and be careful of pickpockets

reviews.author: Sarah
reviews.title: Awful night market
reviews.content: This night market is only held on weekends, but there was nothing I wanted there. It was winter, so there were a lot of shoes, socks, and winter clothes, which didn't interest me. More than anything, I was scared of the motorbikes rushing towards me, so I couldn't calmly look at it. I wish they would regulate motorbikes as well as cars. There were some interesting street food stalls nearby, which I found more interesting.

reviews.author: mayccm2018
reviews.title: Night market
reviews.content: Convenient location.   Lots of the stalls and numerous merchandises that you could purchase.   Prices were not very cheap.   Bargaining was necessary.  However, it was a great experience to visit Hanoi's night market.

reviews.author: Paperlapeipul
reviews.title: Mass gathering
reviews.content: Lots of people, lots of crowds and ten thousand things that nobody needs. You can hardly put one foot in front of the other.

reviews.author: Michael T
reviews.title: Lively Night Market
reviews.content: We were walking back to our hotel which was in the Hanoi Old Quarter after dinner at Bun Cha Ta restaurant.Along the way we passed by a busy pedestrianised area which was the night market. I could not remember the name of the street. It was a Friday evening. The streets were closed to traffic. Vendors set up stalls selling clothings, souvenirs, food, paintings etc. It was a lively place.The most prominent and most brightly lit building was the Ham Ca Map (which means teeth of the shark). That appeared to be the most photogenic and sought after spot for that instagrammable shot.The weather was cool that evening. We had so much fun just being outdoor and wandering around (when you don’t have to worry about motorbikes circling round you).

reviews.author: AJ2000
reviews.title: Average market, enjoyable lake walk away from the stalls.
reviews.content: This was pretty convenient for shopping but only if you already want to buy things. Our teenagers were happy expanding their wardrobe at good prices. Agree with others it is repetitive and a few stalls close by the lake are probably enough before it's all the same.Best value is in keeping it short and finishing off with a beautiful walk around the lake where the vendors are gone and is filled with activities and shows instead, all free and family friendly. A completely different and relaxed vibe! We had also been warned about pick pockets and shady vendors in the market area. I got ripped off like others! Someone recommended have lots of small change and only give exact money and this is fantastic advice. Heaps of chancers around.Is extremely crowded at the market, mayhem in the streets where the traffic is blocked, but really joyful around the lake.

reviews.author: Al37_11
reviews.title: A walk to take whether you have something to buy or not.
reviews.content: The street is occupied in its center by stalls and passers-by wander on each side. The approximately 2 km long market is held every weekend on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays from 7 p.m.There you can find clothes, shoes, souvenirs, handicrafts and everyday items, most often at relatively affordable prices. On some stands it is possible to haggle, but not on all!It is also possible to eat there.There are crowds especially as the two side passages are not very wide.

reviews.author: JnVSydney
reviews.title: Fave outing.....
reviews.content: This clearly, was our fave outing in old town Hanoi, 9for shopping) as the streets are closed and you can browse in relative piece away from, the hustle and bustle of the traffic, avoiding the infernal beeping, and craziness.The market itself is quite fun, everything you could possibly want concentrated in one area, a lot of the stalls are actually an extension of the shops that line the closed street which, is quite long, (extending from Dong kinh Nghia Thuc square to the Dong Xuan market),  we did most of our shopping here, to be frank at these prices, to question the authenticity is a bit naive.

reviews.author: Abhishek
reviews.title: Better options, higher prices.
reviews.content: The night market is a celebration of everything that Hanoi has to offer. It takes place on Saturday and Sunday from 8 pm to 11 pm. However, prices on Sunday are better than that on Sunday. However, the prices you get on normal days in shop are better and in fact, the night market prices were quoted on the higher side. You must bargain a lot and not hope for anything authentic.

reviews.author: duuuudi
reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.content: A very nice place to shop and buy clothes and gifts. We will find what you like at a good price after bargaining. Of course, it stays open until late at night. You will not be able to complete it in one night.

reviews.author: Mark D
reviews.title: Not like Night Market in other Asian Cities
reviews.content: I thought there would be more food stalls at the weekend night market, but there was not. Just the same old stuff you can find everywhere around old town. Not really worth the hassle.

reviews.author: davelori
reviews.title: Seen it once no need to go back
reviews.content: First of all watch out for people who pick pocket. A lot of counterfeit things. Super busy, super hot. Just my opinion

reviews.author: dpghatak
reviews.title: Night market for all
reviews.content: A whole Street is shut down on Saturday & Sunday from 8 PM onwards. The street is opposite to Lake and Domino's. Series of stalls selling pin to elephant. Prices are not very low. Makes a late start and hence you should be prepared for a late night experience. I found it warming up at 9 PM and hence didnt hang around late night. All in all can pick up the experience but don't expect to make a killing

reviews.author: Chessie O
reviews.title: Visit store 33!
reviews.content: Visit store 33 if you go! Super friendly guy, great deals and lovely jewellery. Found my new favourite necklace that I’ll treasure forever. Thank you! Chessie and Joe

reviews.author: Aman Mehra
reviews.title: Shop your heart out and bargain!
reviews.content: We shopped our hearts out here. It's pretty big. Loads of shops with interesting stuff. Must visit to shop if you want shoes, clothes, bags, toys etc.

reviews.author: Sera-sgd
reviews.title: Na
reviews.content: Night market was so so. Selling the same stuff as the stores. Beware the donut lady seller pushing a trolley. She willRipped you off seeing you are a tourist

reviews.author: Scott W
reviews.title: Hanoi Night Markets
reviews.content: If you're after a deal on clothes or souvenirs, then this is the place to go with lots of stalls and plenty of bargains on offer.

reviews.author: David D
reviews.title: Cheap market stalls not much different from what is in the shops
reviews.content: The night market is large but really no different from the many markets we have visited in Europe. Shops are open either side of the market and if anything we bought more from these shops than the stalls. It was raining when we went and once or twice the stall holders had to clear the collected water from the roof of the stall, we got wetter from that than the rain. The other issue is that the motorcyclists are allowed up both sides of the stalls , just have to keep your wits about you. Had to go but not the highlight of our Hanoi stay

reviews.author: Jobearoundtheglobe
reviews.title: Some bargains to be had! All in all great fun.
reviews.content: Not the 4000 stalls that you read online. Lots of things for sale but local shops around it will be cheaper. No consistency in the prices and you can often negotiate well in excess of 50% off (despite the 10-15% the guides say you will get) as long as you are polite to them.

reviews.author: Ali07London
reviews.title: If you like a market it’s worth a stroll
reviews.content: Lots of stalls. Some pretty things but lots of the same. Goes on forever!  Bought a pretty pair of earrings but the small shops are just as competitive.

reviews.author: Rini M
reviews.title: Overrated
reviews.content: It is overrated. You can find same products for cheaper price in shops. For foreigners they ask too much price .

reviews.author: Silas E
reviews.title: After dinner walk
reviews.content: Went for a stroll around the market. Got something small to eat. Typical market. Good vibes tho :) Can recommend it for an after-dinner walk.

reviews.author: KTP310
reviews.title: Good atmosphere and prices
reviews.content: We enjoyed strolling through the night market which had a relaxed atmosphere, with no pressure to buy. We bought lots - the prices seemed even more reasonable than local shops. But do be aware, at one point we felt we were being followed, possibly by pickpockets.

reviews.author: Jonathan C.
reviews.title: hanoi night market
reviews.content: Beautiful night market in the old quarter. Walkable, plenty of stalls, food stands, restaurants, and shops.

reviews.author: Janelle
reviews.title: Ms. Anh Stall 39
reviews.content: Ms. Anh at stall 39 was such a fun lady and had a great shop. She was not pressuring at all and it was so fun bargaining with her. She gave us some great deals on numerous items. We got an adorable incense holder with the best incense over ever burnt. Loved her such a blast. My boyfriend and I still talk about Ms. Anh and how much she made us laugh. Highly recommend!!

reviews.author: eileent3821
reviews.title: WEEKEND NIGHT MARKET IN HANOI
reviews.content: A very popular place among the local community, it is even more interesting to see it as a tourist. A wide variety of food - from meats and seafood, to food especially local snacks. You can get through it quickly if you do not have much interest in any of the products but you can also spend a reasonable time if the products are what you are after. Definitely worth a visit.

reviews.author: TravelinMan411
reviews.title: Fun night market!
reviews.content: A great night out! Many people, live music, plenty of shopping, they close off the streets so it’s nice to be able to walk around without looking for Motos!

reviews.author: Ali921
reviews.title: Market stalls for tourists mainly
reviews.content: It's a market. Most clearly aimed at tourists. Depends what you want and how you want to pay. Lots of cheap stuff - clothes, shoes, bags etc. Not for me. Once you seen one market you've seen them all

reviews.author: smewar
reviews.title: Must visit for weekend in hanoi
reviews.content: Lively market with food , live music, First copy of branded shoes, clothes, watches. Quiet a long, some shops have fixed price and some does bargain

reviews.author: Compudex
reviews.title: First Copy Biggest market
reviews.content: If you love value for money, its great place. If you're Brand Freak then you wont enjoy much. They have all Chinese made clothing and cutlery at cheap rate, (you must bargain a bit) I would call it all first copy market from Clothing, shoes, Watch, Belt and Toys !!we even bought new bag from here, after shopping :)

reviews.author: G2Kpauly
reviews.title: Lovely night market
reviews.content: This is a really cool market to walk around especially on weekends it's so busy with locals and tourists. Look for the hotpot food stall on the corner it is amazing food. Also the meet on stick bbq stalls are nice. There is plenty of shopping to be done too and it goes along way this market.

reviews.author: Felice Santiago
reviews.title: Walk and see around
reviews.content: Went to see and stroll around.. if you buy something try to haggle first (if you want) just like any market. Clothes, bags, shoes , souvenirs, coffee, food, can be found here. I remember it was a hot night too but all good :) I enjoyed sight seeing.

reviews.author: Travelove58
reviews.title: Big & colorful night market, with wide varieties of products.....
reviews.content: This weekly night market only opens from Fri-Sundays. Its a huge, huge market stretching to a few streets. We spent about 3 hours here . Quality of sports shoes & apparels here are good. Don't forget to bargain, as prices are always highly inflated. This is expected . Otherwise you end up paying ridiculous prices.We bought different sports shoes that were quoted 450K-500K but in the end , got it for 300K- 350K.

reviews.author: Samantha H
reviews.title: Don’t miss Mr Thanh! Stall 34
reviews.content: What a fabulous experience this was.  So glad we came! Mr Thanh at stall 34 is a legend!  Great fun and so helpful.  Good prices and great choice.  Kind man with a lovely family.

reviews.author: 오 오
reviews.title: store recomendation
reviews.content: No.39 MsAnh wat really good and cheap!The owners were so nice and lovely!They are asking me to write it but it's good tohavecommuication like this.

reviews.author: Max H
reviews.title: Stall 34 is a great time
reviews.content: Stall 34 is well worth a visit. Lovely man running it who was very funny and I enjoyed chatting to him about the football. Really loved it!

reviews.author: Rory Huynh
reviews.title: Great Stall, Great Staff, Great time
reviews.content: Stall #34 was excellent! I visited the night market of Ha Noi and it was amazing! I was greeted by a lovely man who was helpful, funny and a down to earth guy. The stall #34 was so lovely and had many products for great value! I would definitely recommend visiting the place as the service was excellent as well as the stall.

reviews.author: David
reviews.title: So many people!
reviews.content: The Hanoi night Market is extremely busy! So many people! Other reviewers have suggested that it is s Fri, Sat and Sun night affair only - so worth coming on one of these days.A District of the old town is coroned off to all but foot traffic, which makes the area around the night Market a chaos of pedestrians, cars and motorcycles all coming to - or trying to bypass - the market.Recommend you go to the what is now the Old Town Restaurant and Pub and watching from the balcony aa another reviewer helpfully suggests.

reviews.author: feltroneu
reviews.title: Crowded
reviews.content: The night market is very huge which have occupied few of the streets. The more impressive was the big crowd along the streets. Must be careful of your belongings and small kids. Some of the stalls selling very unique souvenirs but majority offered clothing. There were variety of choices maybe other night markets wouldn't offered. Be prepared to negotiate the price as the initial price they offered could be very expensive but it depended on your luck. It was one of the highlights of our Hanoi trip ended with a sweet memory.

reviews.author: Hana C
reviews.title: HUGE
reviews.content: Massive market, felt like it went on forever! So many cool things to look at - food, trinkets etc. Was super cool even in the rain.

reviews.author: Ann K
reviews.title: Nice stroll if you like busy markets
reviews.content: It's an nice stroll and you can see many different items for sale. Prices and items are geared towards tourists, so compare and bargain hard it you are interested in buying. Be aware of cheap quality and fake brands and keep your money and valuables in a safe place when steering through the crowds. If you are interested in street food, there's plenty of snacks to try! As the market is outside it is weather dependent and can get cold and wet, especially in winter.

reviews.author: Barry W
reviews.title: Generous Giving It 2 Stars
reviews.content: We have been to many night markets in the Asia Pacific region and this one definitely ranks as the worst. Mainly clothes, footwear, tacky jewellery, sunglasses, mobile phone covers etc. It is not a patch on Hoi An night market. I very rarely give low star ratings but this fully deserves it. Stay away.

reviews.author: K&M rates plates
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Came here after a recommendation from our hotel receptionist. The night market is really cool and very authentic. It’s really busy but it’s good fun walking up and down haggling with the market traders. It’s definitely worth a visit

reviews.author: LoBommer
reviews.country: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
reviews.title: Does what it says on the tin!
reviews.content: It's a market and it's dark! It must be a night Market!! Average but then I think all markets are average! Mostly clothes and some food stalls where they have a two tier price scale! It is incumbent upon one to visit these local markets even if it is just to say I went there!

reviews.author: TinaQ
reviews.title: Lively and noisy
reviews.content: This was my first experience as far as night markets go and I'm comparing it to other places I've visited since then throughout our travels around Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia. It's quite noisy, loads of stalls, loads of people, some street food and generic souvenirs. The best way to enjoy it is to find the Peachy Craft Bar, sit on its balcony and look at the hustle and bustle down below.

reviews.author: sg_anu
reviews.title: Massively crowded
reviews.content: Chaotic crowd with chaotic traffic thrown into it. Go only if you are comfortable moving in large crowds. Items sold are quite cheap but not of high quality. About 70 to 80% of the items sold are clothes out of which a large majority are brand rip offs. A lot of accessories and shoes are sold as well (again, lots of fake branded items). I have no interest in buying brand rip offs. With a lot of difficulty, found a pair of sports shoes for my daughter that didn't have Nike or Adidas written on it and they were actually quite good. A few places were selling curios and the prices looked quite good. But, honestly, it was a challenge deciding to buy anything in the huge crowd when you're constantly being swept off! I live in Asia and I've rarely seen that level of crowding.It's still a unique experience.

reviews.author: epruuu
reviews.title: Everything you may want for shopping
reviews.content: This market is a colourful place in which you can find many different souvenirs, cosmetics, textiles, fruits, street foods. It is available Friday and Saturday evenings, I am not sure for Sunday.

reviews.author: JPollock311
reviews.title: Crazy busy & crowded, but fun
reviews.content: The old quarter and night market on the weekend is a must, they close the streets to cars and motorbikes and the streets fill up with families and vendors - it is amazing. We have been twice summer and winter, both were fantastic

reviews.author: Jay “flower” child
reviews.title: Just okayyyy
reviews.content: This is an okay night market. I’m comparing it to other major markets like Thong Sala in Ko Pha-ngan, Bangkoks night market and Hong Kong’s night market. This one is simply, okay.... there is not much food selection at all. Also, a lot of what is being sold isn’t unique to Vietnam and necessarily souvenirs but things like air pods and iPhone chargers. This just didn’t seem authentic when you compare it to other ones. I’m all about the food stalls and these ones were disappointing at best. If I’m not getting food I want unique handmade souvenirs and I didn’t get that either

reviews.author: Kyra D
reviews.title: Eat All of the Street Food!
reviews.content: We loved the night market! We honestly didn’t know it was happening so we were lucky that we arrived on a Sunday (since it’s only open Fri-Sun). We were staying in the old quarter so we stumbled upon the market being set up when we were out and about. It’s pretty crowded but there are tons of great craft vendors and food vendors. We ate a ton of food and everything was so delicious. Specifically all of the dumplings. And it was easy to pop into the many bars along the market if we wanted to sit and grab a beer. Most of the places had outdoor balcony seating so we were able to look down on the market while taking a break. Definitely worth a visit if you’re there when it’s open!

reviews.author: Anine
reviews.title: Beautiful but crowded
reviews.content: The many multi colored lanterns that fill the streets are breathtaking and the reflection on the river even more so. The food at the night market are interesting and very tasty. There are some down sides to this night market though, it is packed with tourists and most of the stalls sell exactly the same merchandise and food. So while you are bumped and pushed through the street you are also looking at the same thing all the time. The big crowd kind of takes away from the beauty of this part of Hoi An.

reviews.author: Candice
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: If you're visiting Hanoi during the weekend, take a stroll along the night market street. Great walk with nice mixture of stuff. From shirt, souvenir, shoe, to hand make ice cream, street orchestra... A nice place to hang out after dinner. Stall starting to set up from 6+ to 7+ pm, by 8pm most of the stall is ready for the night.

reviews.author: Ati
reviews.title: Chaotic, Crazy and Beautiful.
reviews.content: Perfect for an after dinner walk and buy loads of products for a quite reasonable prices. If you visit Hanoi this a must!!!Extra if you love a bargain.

reviews.author: Raymondale
reviews.title: Price quite reasonable
reviews.content: Last year Nov/Dec when i had my North Vietnam tour,i visited Hanoi night market twice,it is close to where i stayed.If compare to other night market in vietnam,hanoi night market is worth to visit,the price is reasonable,many stalls are fixed price,unlike Hoi an or other night market,you have to bargain,sometimes very hard.i bought some small things here,like mirror,mini umbrella,quilling arts,quilling painting...be noted that it only opened during weekends,and some roads will be closed,so better go there by walking.

reviews.author: Srirambalaji S
reviews.title: Street Market by the Night
reviews.content: Located at the one of the sides of Hoan Kiem Lake, this market comes to life by evening till midnight. Its like the street market in any country selling a large range of cheaper items. Do not get fooled by the branded logos as they are all fake products branded and displayed. There are lot of hawkers, so have the patience and negotiation skills to bargain for a better rate.As the place is crowded be careful with your belongings. Unless you are sure you want to buy and have decided on a rate in your mind do not show interest and you will be lured to buy in the products just at the hint of your interest on something.

reviews.author: Harding N
reviews.title: tired
reviews.content: Do not expect something extremely authentic here. The things that you get in the stores close by - sneakers, Vietnamese souvenirs, fake jewelry, dresses - are somewhat better priced within this night market by approximately 10 20 % discount. You are able to negotiate/haggle more than the stores. It is just open Friday through Sunday later in the day. Stalls will begin opening around six pm but better to come after seven pm.

reviews.author: Abdur Rahman
reviews.title: Impressive... Mind blowing
reviews.content: I really enjoyed... Price are cheaper but you must bargain with the shop keepers. Souvenir items, street foods, cheap cosmetics, clothings everything you will found.

reviews.author: Rose F
reviews.title: Night market mayhem
reviews.content: Spent Sunday night at the Night Market but didn’t stay long because I am not a big fan of shopping and I don’t need more ‘stuff’. #1 son bought a pair of Ray Ban sunnies for 100,000 Vietnamese Dong ~$6AUD  If you want cheap clothing watches, wallets, purses, bags, electronic gadgets, cards and souvenirs or doughnuts and frozen ice confections  then this is the place. Fun to do once as it was a lovely night and seeing families have fun around Hoan Kiev lake on a warm Sunday evening was delightful (a lot better than the market in my opinion!)

reviews.author: priya a
reviews.title: over priced
reviews.content: You will find a lot of cheap stuff in this market where most of the items are overpriced. Most of the vendors are not prepared to lower the price much. I suggest paying half of what they ask you.We didn't find any good deals here although it was fun looking around.

reviews.author: Jack S
reviews.title: best night market in SE Asia
reviews.content: The best night market in South East Asia with a huge range of items including (but not limited to) knockoff branded clothing, shoes and accessories, souvenirs, electronics and food. Certainly worth the visit. Note it is opened on Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings but may close due to poor weather.

reviews.author: Ald
reviews.title: Night Market
reviews.content: Lots of stalls selling the same stuff but the hustle and bustle of the place with all the lights, music and people made it an interesting experience.

reviews.author: Jessy
reviews.title: Below average night Market!
reviews.content: Mostly selling fake or imitation items. There is no clothes representing the locals or even street foods. We didn't find much things to buy.

reviews.author: Ginnyleeinwonderland
reviews.title: Night life at weekend
reviews.content: If you are a fan of buying cheap ( and fake) stuff, this is absolutely place for you. You can find there many cheap things including clothes, accessories for phones, cosmetics or food. You can enjoy night life at weekend of Hanoian but beware of the pick pockets. You should always keep your bag in front of you or just hold it. You can also find many traditional food of Vietnam there. Just enjoy life and use calculator to reduce price

reviews.author: Cindy Marie Azur
reviews.title: Only opens every Fridays
reviews.content: We’re very lucky to experience this night market. As usually it only open every Friday night and just happened that we’ve stayed till Saturday. Plenty of shops around selling good quality of imitated products and street food. A must visit place when you’re around the area Friday night. You can bargain to some but not all vendors.

reviews.author: QuaverT
reviews.title: Worst night in Asia
reviews.content: Hanoi market is an awful experience and it’s completely ruined the charm of Vietnam for me. I’ve had a superb time over the last few months in this country but this was by far the worst and stressful nights of my life. There’s only about 5 stalls which sell anything unique. Everything else is the same rip off bags/watches/plastic toys and the vendors are rude/ignorant. It’s incredibly busy so you spend hours doing a small shuffle rather than walking. It’s an absolute waste of time and has ruined my experience of Hanoi

reviews.author: Shahana
reviews.title: Cute market
reviews.content: Very touristic place but very cute. Once it’s night time all the streets light up with a lot of lanterns everywhere. Some places charge you when you want to take photos in front of their shops, but it’s like one dollar. You can also have a boat tour on the river, with little lights in the boat.Overall a good experience

reviews.author: DerriQ
reviews.title: Great night
reviews.content: We loved this market.  Its hard to miss if your staying in the old quarter so if you just head towards the lake you will find it on a Frid, Sat or Sunday night.  We went last Sunday night and really enjoyed it more than I thought we would after reading some of the reviews.  We got some good bargains and gifts for people back home.  Its a huge market and seems to go on forever and ever.  We kept walking and eventually found ourselves in beer street which was another amazing experience.  The stall holders all seemed nice and prices were better than I expected.  I didn't have to haggle anywhere near as much as other places like Bali and Thailand to reach an agreed price. Very packed but that's all part of the fun! If you have young children I don't like your chances of pushing a pram through the crown though!

reviews.author: LinLing03
reviews.title: Great prices for mass-produced items
reviews.content: Don’t expect anything extremely authentic here. The items that you find in the shops nearby - sneakers, fake jewelry, Vietnamese souvenirs, dresses - are better priced in this night market by about 10-20% discount. You can negotiate / haggle more than the shops. It’s only open Friday through Sunday in the evening. Stalls will start opening around 6pm but best to come after 7pm. Most will open rain or shine as we experienced it while it was raining fairly heavy.

reviews.author: Nia Sarrie
reviews.title: Interesting place to visit
reviews.content: you can't resist the ambiance..it feels like you will buy everything there..lol..take me back there :)

reviews.author: Libby C
reviews.title: Seriously disappointing
reviews.content: If you’ve been anywhere else in Southeast Asia, you’ve seen amazing markets.  Often they are filled with cheap but localish handicrafts, clothes and gifts specific to the region. If that’s what you are hoping for here, you’ll be disappointed.  It was all cheap t-shirts, ugly knock-off bags, electronics, plastic jewelry.  There was some food, but even that was mostly just fruit juice stands.  The only original thing I saw was some interesting greeting cards with 3D cut out structures.   Everything else was wildly uninteresting.

reviews.author: Aneta B
reviews.title: Evening well spend.
reviews.content: It’s in the centre of Hanoi so you will definitely end up here no matter if you want to or not and I would say it was worth it. Yes, it’s packed with people and pretty noisy but the atmosphere is great. You can choose from different Vietnamese street food and also buy very cheap clothing - mainly dupes of expensive brands such as Adidas, Channel and other.

reviews.author: K5165XX
reviews.title: Very enjoyable
reviews.content: Amazing atmosphere as long as you don't have this every night. Good food and interesting shopping close to some of the high lights of Hanoi. Much better during the night but also interesting area during the day just lots of traffic...

reviews.author: Sarah
reviews.title: Noisy but cheap and good food
reviews.content: Small street with many people walking around buy food, souvenirs, clothes, shoes.... everything is cheap but i am worry about quality. But still nice

reviews.author: rearcardoor
reviews.title: Night market with 3 kids
reviews.content: I know this has had mixed reviews but we had a fun evening at the night market.  It’s not on par with some of the other South East Asian night markets but definitely worth a visit.  We browsed the stalls, ate some street food, had a drink at one of the outdoor bars on little plastic seats, and got some good bargains.  There is a lot of repetition in the stalls with so many selling trainers, electronics, clothes etc but towards the lake end, there are more stalls selling souvenirs etc.  There are lots of shops open alongside the market too and it gets quite busy as the evening progresses.  We got some incredible bargains and did not find the stall holders rude at all, it’s just all part of the game.  One example was a pair of trainers quoted at 1,350,000 dong and we got the price down to 500,000.  We got similar discounts for other items and had a lot of fun.

reviews.author: Paul's
reviews.title: tired
reviews.content: the night market is a really busy place and also a long i mean really really long market , hot and crowded took me 30m to find my way out

reviews.author: mistahfong
reviews.title: Beware of this seller
reviews.content: Don't buy food from this stall (near the crossroad at Hanoi Old Quarter nightmarket) , she cheated my money

reviews.author: psandhu1
reviews.title: Pleasant night market
reviews.content: Went here on Sunday evening at 7pm with my 8 month old baby in the sling. It is busy and the vendors are pleasant. My brother bought a Bluetooth speaker for £8. They sold mainly clothes, jewellery and footwear. Enjoyable.

reviews.author: Role
reviews.title: Market was nice if you haven’t been to one before
reviews.content: The markets are all ways cool great bargains some things are unique somethings repeat over and over. I would say if you e never been too a night market and it’s the weekend and you want something to do.  I would recommend you do the night market and walk around some. It’s safe and cool atmosphere. Hanoi is a little more laid back then southern Vietnam.

reviews.author: Andrew V
reviews.title: Busy
reviews.content: This is very busy with locals and tourists not a great deal of bargain to be had we did get a couple of good deals but on average most of the stuff is cheap knockoff that are not at a cheap price but if you’re in Hanoi it’s worth the look

reviews.author: Sherry Bischoff
reviews.title: Hanoi weekend night market
reviews.content: Interesting stroll through the stalls. Was hoping for more locally hand-made items. Lots of clothing and food. Even though the streets were closed there were still a number of mopeds driving through the crowd.

reviews.author: Jun David
reviews.title: Great Bargain
reviews.content: The Night Market runs from Don Xuang Market to near Hoa Kiem Lake.Lots of knocked off items from bags, shoes and shirts. Lots of street foods. Lots of souvenirs. Most of the stalls are selling the same items though. All items are cheap but you need to bargain.Great experience.

reviews.author: JustRose_CH
reviews.title: Not worth it
reviews.content: We arrived on a Monday and I spent the week looking forward to shopping at the night market. Other than a few stalls at the very beginning of the market, the end closest to the lake, the market was full of old clothes, underwear and generally things of that nature. The beginning had souvenirs for very reasonable prices, sometimes low enough not to bargain over. However I did not find anything at the night market I didn’t see elsewhere in Hanoi so if you are not there on a weekend don’t worry you are not missing anything. Note that the night market is only set up Friday to Sunday.

reviews.author: Francis Martino
reviews.title: Worth a Visit in crowded place.
reviews.content: The Hanoi market at night is beautiful during the week end,Definitely worth checking out. Food and Goods all you can buy. Make sure to bargain, but start with at least 20-30% of the price they say you, stay strong when bargaining. If you don't get the price you move to stand the next one will give you your desired price.  It takes a bit getting used to to the big crowd,the kind you see in the market of the old quarter, and also hair bands, jewelry, watches, some toys and shoes,IT appliances and so on.Be careful of your belongings during walking and sightseeing in very crowded place.

reviews.author: McCullough.Family
reviews.title: Good night out
reviews.content: Some of these reviews are very harsh. Do not get me wrong a lot of what is sold is the same but we never felt pressured into buying anything and no harm in looking for a couple of hours and most people will buy something

reviews.author: Simona
reviews.title: Prepare to be scammed
reviews.content: Markets in asia are kind of sightseeing, however I'd recommend avoiding this one or be very careful. The vendors are rude, not willing to bargain and you feel bad if you ask for another size. This market ruined my night as one vendor has stolen 90k dong from me. I've bargained a price to 80k dong and have her a 100k bill. She returned me 10k dong and I've tried to explain that she should give me another 10k back. Then she started yelling at me and grabed my bag with the good inside. She have scratched my arm and was insanely rude. I didn't understand what have happened when she continued to yell at me and many people gathered around. I've tried to either get my money back or get my good but she left me with only 10k dong in my hand. Basically, the scam is that she blamed me that I've given her only 10k dong and that I owe her money. She started pointing at my friend's pockets and tried to reach out to them. A crowd of vietnamese sellers gathered around and we were screamed at in vietnamese. I don't care about the 100k dong. Just the overall concept of this scam is ridiculous and we've got a bit scared when we were surrounded by vietnamese crowd screaming at us. Recommend giving exact amount to the vendors to avoid this and be very careful in the market as it seems that they would do anything for a couple of dollars, even get violent.

reviews.author: Anas A
reviews.title: Weekend market
reviews.content: Hanoi's Night Market happens every weekend and it is very popular for both locals and tourists. Full of street shops which sell a variety of products. The quality of most products is cheap and copied from other brands. The problem with the market is that it is overcrowded.

reviews.author: Sebastián M
reviews.title: Overcrowded
reviews.content: Too many people at this place. Vendors offer the same products along the street. Not worth spending time here. But for the first time it is nice experience, to see how the night market in Hanoi looks like.

reviews.author: Elsa C. L.
reviews.title: Fun and quite reasonably priced in Asia
reviews.content: Bargaining is necessary.  Naturally, vendors would like more profit.Highly unique wide assortment of Origami design cards for specific occasions or general are priced ranging from 20,000 to 35,000 Dong (US$1 = 22,500 to 23,000 Dong) depending on the size.Beautifully decorated fabric gift pouches approximately 5” X 6” are priced at 24,000 Dong.  When you buy five, you get one free.White cotton shirts with Vietnam attraction printed cost 40,000 Dong each.A native Vietnamese design colorful magnet is priced at 10,000 Dong.  My Vietnamese souvenir plate for my wall collection cost 100,000 Dong.Pork barbeque sells at 20,000.  As snack, three sticks would be satisfying for a person weighing 119 lbs as the pieces are not lean.No vehicle is supposed to go through the night market.  However, there were motorcycles.

reviews.author: hansibrahim
reviews.title: Wash your eye
reviews.content: Held every Friday, Saturday and Sunday, Hanoi Weekend Night Market is a busy, bustling gathering of roadside stalls and local food vendors that brings huge crowds of locals and tourists. It runs through the Old Quarter district from 19:00 onwards, starting from Hang Dao Street and running north to the edge of Dong Xuan Market.

reviews.author: tes108
reviews.title: Tacky junk
reviews.content: Our local friends told us that all the merchandise came from China. It did. Nothing remotely interesting and the place is devoid of charm.

reviews.author: Tabitha G
reviews.title: Crowded but enjoyable
reviews.content: Very crowded and a little overwhelming. Prices for the same item vary greatly, so be patient if you want something. If you’ve seen it once you’ll likely see it again. Get your best bargaining on, because you’ll need to cut the price by at least 70% to start. I found being patient and friendly works really well especially with young people. Lots of shoes, clothing and souvenirs. Also accessories (sunglasses, jewellery, make up and perfume.) Also electronic accessories. Remember- this stuff is all fake and the quality of the clothing in particular is very average. You’re just paying for the name brand. Overall a fun night out, recommended if you enjoy the market scene and crowds.

reviews.author: Bulbul
reviews.title: Vibrant weekend in the city
reviews.content: If you haven’t booked the tickets for Vietnam yet, book it for the dates that include the weekend. The night market is held on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday starting from 19:00. The street is a lively gathering of the roadside stalls. These stalls sell almost everything right from pop up cards to shoes. The prices are reasonable too. However, negotiations seemed relatively unattainable here as compared to Don Xuan and the old quarter market. A good bet is to buy souvenirs from here. You get a great variety.

reviews.author: cinbkk
reviews.title: Shopping and food
reviews.content: A good place to while away the time in the evening from Fri-Sun. Lots of food, snacks, clothes, shoes, accessories and souvenirs. Some streets are too crowded for a proper walk, but it's a huge area and there's always somewhere to go. One end of the market ends at the Hoan Kiem lake, a good place to catch some fresh air.

reviews.author: Atlas1669
reviews.title: Fun but not much else
reviews.content: A bit of fun walking past similar stalls. It was really crowded and quite fun even though there was little to tempt us to buy. Worth going to see just for the experience.

reviews.author: TonyMac64
reviews.title: Interesting but lots of the same stuff
reviews.content: We enjoyed our trip and the prices were comparative with other markets in Asia. My main criticism would be that all the clothing stalls had the same clothes, as did the jewellery and souvenir stalls etc. Worth it if markets are your thing but don’t expect anything out of the ordinary.

reviews.author: Gordo4037
reviews.title: Not much variety
