reviews.content: It's the Wandering Yank here.  Mrs. Yank and I stumbled on the Hanoi night market near our hotel when we saw the closed-off street.  On our current Asia trip we had visited night markets of varying quality in Thailand and Hong Kong, so we were pumped to see this one.It was crowded, with only a smattering of tourists, so it's obviously keyed to the local market.  That means cheap clothes, shoes, cell phone holders, more cheap clothes, etc.....  There was a small proportion of tourist-oriented goods.  There was very little food.Go for the local flavor, but if you're looking for souvenirs, etc., you'll have an easier time going straight to the tourist-oriented shops in the Old Quarter.2 thumbs up.

reviews.author: ashleylllll
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: This market wasn't particularly distinctive; it sold the same elephant-print shorts, tank tops and souvenirs that you can find in any other night market in Southeast Asia. The prices for the touristy clothes (i.e. elephant-print cloth pants) were also more expensive than I've seen elsewhere, and many vendors were not open to bargaining as prices were posted. It was fine to walk through, but I definitely wouldn't go out of my way to check it out.

reviews.author: Elibaba
reviews.title: Naff knick nacks
reviews.content: The night market is ok if you are after cheap knick knacks. We only went to snack our way through the evening while watching the crowd.

reviews.author: Mitch W
reviews.title: Little bit meh
reviews.content: Read reviews on here saying it wasn't that great but decided to go anyway.I'm here to tell you.... it isn't that great.Unless you want elephant pants for 70k there isn't much here you can't buy during the day.It takes ages to walk along, we did the whole length and back and didn't buy anything.Needless to say its pretty busy also

reviews.author: Echow707
reviews.title: Junk
reviews.content: Junk and more junk what can I say. It gets tiring looking at all the same stuff every other stall. It is a bit easier here to browse around tho as compared to old quarter shops during the day because the streets are free from motorbikes.

reviews.author: Ivyanddavid
reviews.title: Not bad at all
reviews.content: I'm surprised at some of the bad reviews here.  I've been to the night markets in Taiwan and Thailand.  This one is comparable to the others, maybe less variety of shops but equally good vibe.  Most vendors actually have prices clearly marked, much better than local shops in old quarter who will overcharge tourists.  Bought a bunch of shirts for 50k vnd each.   Good quality, didn't shrink after a cycle of wash and dry.  Kids really enjoyed the freshly squeezed sugar cane juice.

reviews.author: riggsy76
reviews.title: Not good
reviews.content: Don't come here thinking your going to find any quality things, it's all massed produced junk basically. Same goes for the majority of shops around here. Food at a shop nearby was also was the worst I had in Vietnam.

reviews.author: Asa0500
reviews.title: Better things to do in Hanoi
reviews.content: The Hanoi night market has all things Made In China, at very cheap prices.The atmosphere with the street food and thousands of people is good, the actual markets are a waste of time and cause traffic chaos.My advice would be to not waste you're time here.  Visit one of the many excellent restaurants and enjoy you're evening, finish it with a coffee from Gaing Cafe.Steer clear.

reviews.author: Kirst
reviews.title: Average!
reviews.content: After travelling through Asia we have been to a lot of markets. Pretty lights here at night and a long market strip. We didn't enjoy our trip to this markets. Lots of stalls selling the same rubbish! Very very busy full of tourists and locals. At the weekend they close it off to traffic which is a good touch.

reviews.author: Andrew M
reviews.title: Not for us
reviews.content: We have been to many markets but this one is unusually crowded never have we been to such a crowded market you could not move &  mainly Chinese cheap rubbish  no quality or unusual items just stall after stall of the same and full of locals who just seem to walk up and down to be seen and have a night outWorst market we have been to in all our travels

reviews.author: kyote2b
reviews.title: CRAZY PLACE
reviews.content: On fri sat and sun this place is crazy.  wall to wall people.  Thank god they close it off to traffic.  probably thousands of places to eat great street food.  I thought the night market in Marrakech was busy, but the Hanoi night market makes that look like a nursing home.  I felt over stimulated for sure.  It wears on you after a period of time and you just have to get away from it.  But overall, I would have been sad if I had passed it up.

reviews.author: Josh S
reviews.title: Be the first into the store
reviews.content: Traveller tip. Be the first into the store and they will do any deal to make a sale. It's very good luck to sell to hue first customer. Use that!!

reviews.author: Matty B
reviews.title: Good for a look
reviews.content: The night market is really long and has plenty of stalls but they are all the same. Everything you can get here you can get for the same price or cheaper during the day at the street shops, without fighting through crowds and almost loosing eyes from all the umbrellas flying around. It does however look really nice with plenty of lights and a great atmosphere

reviews.author: DeadlyddPerth
reviews.title: Worth a look
reviews.content: The night markets appear to run on weekend nights. They close off the street with barricades about 6.30pm. The sellers provide food, clothing, souvenirs, consumer durables etc. Each seller has a stall number - remember that. We bought some DVD's and they did not work. It is about 1 km long and if you wal through come down the other side otherwise you can exit and get lost in back streets. For some strange reason the crowd on one side goes one way and on the other the other.

reviews.author: Trypp Adams
reviews.title: Fun diversion at night
reviews.content: I'm not sure the night markets provide anything different than the day markets but they do provide a diversion from what seems like the other option of drinking. The night market in the old quarter was lively with some interesting food vendors and many clothes and knick knack vendors. It seemed to cater to more locals than tourists, but definitely worth the experience!

reviews.author: EarlyRetirementAbroad
reviews.title: Pleasantly surprised
reviews.content: We saw so many Asian markets, but this one is bad at all. If you plan to buy a particular item, scroll the stalls – the price can be increased up to 3-4 times for the same item.   Lots of local food, fruits, and ice cream – don’t afraid to taste.

reviews.author: Kirsten
reviews.title: Same same
reviews.content: If you haven't been to a night market before in Vietnam then definitely make the effort to go. However the merchandise does start to repeat after a few stalls.

reviews.author: Julie C
reviews.title: Crazy Crowded Place!
reviews.content: This is a great place to shop for everything under the sun!  From phone accessories, keychain fobs, souvenirs, lingerie, shoes, clothes, sunglasses, food, you name it!  Also fun to practice your haggling skills!  It stretches for blocks, so you're bound to find something to take home with you!

reviews.author: Alison J
reviews.title: No real bargains
reviews.content: Full of cheap tat and poor copies so ok for a walk to see the locals but not to bag a bargain really. Good Street food though

reviews.author: ozvpm_andy
reviews.title: Worth a quick look - but better things to do in old quarter
reviews.content: What can I say - its a market, and quite a big one at that. But it is mainly all the regular stuff you find in markets anywhere in the world. Have a quick look, but then venture off some of the side streets for some more authentic Hanoi culture

reviews.author: Sean B
reviews.title: Not what I imagined
reviews.content: I was rather surprised with the selection. The majority was just knock off brands and each stand had very similar items. I've been to other night markets and I'd say this was my least favorite. Even though the roads closed off motor bikes still come through here. If you need a last minute cheap gift then go, but I personally wouldn't go out of my way to go here.

reviews.author: NatashaD8
reviews.title: Bargins to be had but be aware
reviews.content: Really great experience and you can get some great bargins. It can be really overwhelming so be clear about what you want before you get there and what you are willing to pay. Be aware of pickpocketers keep valuables close.

reviews.author: SagarVS
reviews.title: Cheap goods
reviews.content: This market comes up on Fridays, Saturdays and sundays. The roads are closed for traffic and you must walk. Most of the shops sell the same goods and there will certainly be something of interest to you. Watch your personal belongings when you are here. Numerous bars and restaurants can be found in this area. You must bargain (remember that).

reviews.author: a t
reviews.title: You dont get haggled like saigon!
reviews.content: It can be crowded but you can talk prices down pretty easily, so worth a visit. They say it's 3km long, but it didn't seem that long to me.

reviews.author: whistlestop
reviews.title: Go For The Atmosphere
reviews.content: We walked through the market on Saturday night, nothing unusual to buy, most of it looked like it was made in China.  The atmosphere however took us back again last night, loved the various music played on the street, it varied from local to four old gentlemen playing Latin American music, great.  We are staying on the edge of the Old Quarter and for us the best time to walk around is in the evening.  Find a free seat outside grab a beer and soak up the atmosphere.

reviews.author: oliver_2424
reviews.title: Excellent for shopping
reviews.content: Visited the night market after dinner on Friday evening, the atmosphere was great and wasnt as hectic as we thought it would be. There was a great selection of goods at good prices (often cheaper than the usual stores) and roads were blocked from scooters - some still went thru but we were there close to closing time so we thought they were just picking up/dropping off. Would recommend a visit if you're in the area and interested in a wander.

reviews.author: Nikhil Khaitan
reviews.title: Too crowded
reviews.content: This place can be heaven for bargain hunters and shopping freaks. Otherwise the place is too crowded and you cant be sure of the quality of the products being sold.

reviews.author: TauntonBob
reviews.title: Same old, same old
reviews.content: This takes place a few nights each week.  It is quite large, taking up several streets, but is not much different to night markets all over Asia.

reviews.author: njaneardude
reviews.title: Worth a visit, that's it
reviews.content: Wouldn't be so bad if it wasn't for all the scooter going through the pedestrian only blocked off street. Same stuff you see out in the Old Quarter for sale.

reviews.author: Ozzies_From_Sydney
reviews.title: Enjoyed shopping here
reviews.content: I enjoyed visiting this night market for the shopping and the general atmosphere. I bought some lovely scarves and a pashmina, all from the same lady, at excellent prices. I also bought a couple of watches. I really enjoy visiting markets when I travel overseas and I could have spent much more time here, but my husband is not really a shopper and it was a very cold night so we returned to our hotel. I also enjoyed the walk here and back (from the Metropole) - apart from, of course, crossing the very busy and motorbike filled roads. It was a bit scary at times but it was well lit and the lake looked beautiful.

reviews.author: JasonDoz
reviews.title: Good fun
reviews.content: If you're visiting Hanoi you really need to experience the night markets. People trying to sell you stuff at every turn after dark

reviews.author: travelnomadNZ
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Pleasant surprise to check out the night market stores. Content in the night market stores are very similar. You should shop around first before buying. Some of the stalls have a lot of junk but amongst it if you look closely you will find some bargainsTip : shop around, be prepared to barter , look after your belongings, watch out for thieves

reviews.author: Jenn N
reviews.title: useful market place
reviews.content: This market opens from Friday- Sunday 7pm-11pm. The stuff they sell here is a bit repetitive, you could find many random things here from fake branded t-shirts, to vintage dresses. I brought a Baymax power bank here, which was a great find!. If you buy power banks or anything electrical such as speakers, the shop keeper allows you to try out the product before buying it, which is great. It's a great place to dig for something different, and you must bargain here and it gets pretty cheap. Watch out for your bags cause pick pocket happens here too. I think its great to spend one night here.

reviews.author: Mallukka
reviews.title: Worth to visit
reviews.content: Lot of things to see and buy, both junk and handicraft. Nice atmosphere. It was quite cold when we visited so it was not too crowded.

reviews.author: amoachaim
reviews.title: Great night walk!
reviews.content: Awesome food (we just had dessert, but it's great), super cheap (for foreigners), interesting goods. Certainly an experience!

reviews.author: Anne C
reviews.title: A lot of choices to find good stuffs !
reviews.content: Went strolling around with my hubby. Found a lot of interesting things to buy. Lots of tourist as well. People are haggling on the prices with the sellers. A lot of good finds and were able to bring home in our home country.

reviews.author: Hanan B
reviews.title: Pleasant place to visit
reviews.content: I like markets and bazaars.  So I was pleased to discover Hanoi's night market.  It is located in the Old Quarter, and is set up in the center of several blocks on weekend evenings/nights.The market predominantly features wearing apparel, but is so extensive in length (several blocks long) that there are also a not so small number of booths selling other items, like children's' toys.  The place is (or at least was on the night I visited) very crowded, mostly with locals.  Clearly this market is not set up for tourists.  In fact, it doesn't have what we would call tourist goods (define them as you choose) for sale.

reviews.author: pcrants
reviews.country: National Capital Territory of Delhi, India
reviews.title: Fun
reviews.content: Make shift stores all along the street covering a sizeable chuck of the quarters.Do walk around .one realizes that the rates are at a throwaway price and many goods and clothes available far cheaper and further bargain able than the ones available in few stores .We spotted same stuff and regretted buying them from stores though they weren't expensive either .Just that one feels ;maybe if we had stopped ourselves ..we could have shopped at further reduced rates .So advice is shop here first and then visit stores for better stuff.It is on fri.sat.sun.

reviews.author: Thewanderingpassport
reviews.title: Interesting things to see
reviews.content: I loved walking through all the people and the stalls just looking at what was on sale and the people selling them, photo opps every where and they dont mind you taking their photos, they are lovely friendly people, i would recommned to have a quick walk through at least to see what its all about

reviews.author: Dishaa S
reviews.title: weekly night market
reviews.content: the weekly night market is a must do if you happen to be in hanoi from fri-sun. it is an amazing way to experience the vietnamese life and do some super souvenir shopping at cheap prices.

reviews.author: soykathy
reviews.title: Not a surprise as a SEA night market
reviews.content: It's quite disappointed to visit this night market, may be I am from Hong Kong where has the famous night market. This one only has lots of stalls which sold the intimated goods but not at a good rate. Typically night market in Thai, Siem Reap and Taiwan I have been visited shall have stalls selling clothes and food, but this one I can't see any authentic local food are tasty to try.

reviews.author: Robzaza
reviews.title: Fun if you are into street markets
reviews.content: We found that most stalls were replicas of what the other stores in the old quarter were already selling. Not all the prices were good unless you are looking for the Vietnam printed t-shirts which you could get quite a good deal, although you can get the same deal if you haggle in the old quarter. The large numbers of people and the time you had to wait before getting assistance detracted from the experience and we returned to the street stores instead.

reviews.author: Onyib
reviews.title: Haggle and eat
reviews.content: Try all the street food you'd dare to eat. The Bap Xao (corn with butter and onions and dried shrimp) was yummy. So was the banh mi, and the freshly baked buns filled with chocolate from Roti Mexico.The embroidered bags I bought from the market are pretty sturdy even if some of them have small imperfections. It's a good place to practice your haggling skills. Although do be very alert, we've been warned that tourists often got their valuables snatched from them at the market.

reviews.author: Sandra S
reviews.title: Jam Packed
reviews.content: This market is crazy busy,lots of the same thing started repeating after a while, didn't find the stall holders overly willing to barter which was very disappointing and at the end of the day it was a lot of cheap knock off copies of trinkets and costume jewelry, watch your wallet/ purse as perfect place for pick pockets.

reviews.author: Becky L
reviews.title: Same old same old
reviews.content: This was my second evening in Vietnam and I had high hopes for the night market. Although police mark off the road so no cars can drive through the street it doesn't stop scooter after scooter squeezing through the people and stalls. The constant beeping and having to look over your shoulder makes the general experience quite hectic and annoying! As for the actual market stalls it was mostly cheap tat, mobile phone chargers, cheap clothes and unconvincing fakes. I was expecting some genuinely authentic Vietnamese things I could buy as a souvenir. Overall I think other markets in SE Asia have a lot more to offer!

reviews.author: Dan
reviews.title: Poor for a SE Asia Night market
reviews.content: Very repetitive, mostly tacky clothes and no decent souvenirs. Not very authentic. I actually had a woman yell at me for trying barter, and then signal me to get lost. All in all not very good, and you can't relax and look at the stalls as scooters are constantly whizzing past and beeping. Also prepare to be have people cough and sneeze in your face.

reviews.author: Kate_singer
reviews.title: Pretty disappointing for a SE Asia Market
reviews.content: If you've never been to a South East Asia market or night market, I'd recommend you go just for the experience. That said, this one is pretty average (or below average) as far as markets go. The experience isn't quite up to par, it's exceedingly crowded, you have to be really careful about pickpockets, and the vendors aren't all that engaged (which is half the fun usually.) You can find some cheap souvenirs, and it's a good place to pick up a lot of the 3D intricate cut paper cards for a bargain. You can pay in dong or USD. The place is 1km long, we took about 45 minutes to make a loop mostly due to the crowds.

reviews.author: izohdy
reviews.title: Great walk and loads of stores
reviews.content: If you want to buy souvineers and small items from Hanoi then this is the goto placePrepare for a long walk and crowded streets with many boths and storesNo robbers or pockets lifting

reviews.author: Goonerfoodie
reviews.title: Rows and rows of Stalls
reviews.content: This Night Market is present during the weekends and you find lots of stalls selling clothes in the majority. They are cheap but will be of low quality more often than not. And remember to always bargain. Since the products will be repetitive, you can inquire prices with different shops before bargaining with the guy who has quoted the least. Be careful of your possessions as it will be easy to pick your pocket due to the crowd. Dont carry passports and valuables. Try the street food near the street corners and at the far end there was a street theater performance of some kind going on at 10. So try to catch that if you are there.

reviews.author: CSWtravelling
reviews.title: Visit only for experience - not recommended for shopping
reviews.content: If you like to spend your spare time observing local markets, clicking pictures, and don't mind the endless walking, do visit for an interesting experience. The goods are mostly low end clothes, plastics etc that are not work lugging back home. But there are some interesting fruit vendors.......and also dogy looking make shift street food stalls :)Do skip if you are tired by all the walking in Hanoi Old Quarters or are looking for some good bargains....goods on offer are just not worth it.

reviews.author: Chand C
reviews.title: Same as any touristy city in SEA
reviews.content: It's good to do this if you had to waste some time. You will have a lot of vendors pushing their goods down your throats, so be prepared.

reviews.author: Lori Z
reviews.title: Huge but horribly repetitive
reviews.content: This market is really really long. However, you will see the same things over and over. Almost no trinkets, mainly clothes and cell phone covers. If you have nothing to do at night, I guess it's an okay way to spend your time but after one block of shops I couldn't see any more cell phone covers. There are also lots of local people at this place.

reviews.author: nofmal
reviews.title: You get at a much out as you put in.
reviews.content: If you are really keen, and maybe have never seen an Asian night market before, this could be an absolutely incredible experience with the food, shopping, and weird things going on. In my view, It really is up to you how much you how much you enjoy night markets, when my girlfriend and I visited, neither of us wanted to buy anything, and we were feeling quite tired, so naturally we just wondered about quite bored. The reviews here should not sway you either way, it is up for you to decide whether you would enjoy yourself or not.

reviews.author: Alana D
reviews.title: Good atmosphere
reviews.content: I went to the night market and found that it had a good atmosphere and that I could pick up a few last minute cheap gifts to take home. I was warned about pickpockets by the staff at my hotel but did not have any problems, nor did I see anyone else that had this problem. A lot of the same things and a long stretch of stalls. I stopped halfway for a breather and a cold drink as that night it was extremely humid. Good value.

reviews.author: brown-and-cony
reviews.title: Your standard busy-Asian-city night markets
reviews.content: This was sooooooooo long! And pretty repetitive. We expected to see more trinkets and random money-wasting things like you see in the Mongkok Markets in Hong Kong, but there were just lots and lots of stalls with clothes. There weren’t many food stalls either, but we did stop about halfway for a cup of sugar cane juice which was delicious!I don’t know what was happening, but when we were there it seemed like the stalls were all collapsing – there were ropes everywhere, it was pretty dangerous! As the store people tried to retie their ropes without noticing people around them. There are also motorbikes going along the market stalls – not sure if they’re meant to be there or not, but just watch out for those.Our hotel staff told us to be careful of our belongings because pickpocketing at the markets is pretty common as it’s busy. But we didn’t see any pickpocketing happen during our trip there.

reviews.author: Reneebalzan
reviews.title: Cheap souvenirs
reviews.content: We visited this market and were shocked at how big it was! You will not only find tourists but an abundance of locals ready to push you out of the way, cough and sneeze in your face (which makes me wonder whether they wear masques for this reason) and lots of merchandise which is not the best quality.  I would recommend it if you need to get small bits and pieces at cheap prices for souvenirs.  Prices were low and in most places a fixed price, street food was ok but be prepared to be stuck in the middle of big crowds and be pushed and shoved a bit.

reviews.author: mrsorso
reviews.title: When Hanoi comes alive
reviews.content: It's place to buy a lot of rubbish things or very nice souvenirs. Definitely a place to see and don't miss the chance to negogiate about the price, otherwise they might be feel offended.

reviews.author: Mr Mark O
reviews.title: Best Pho ever!
reviews.content: The night markets have the usual; shoes, clothes, headphones, etc but the highlight was the food. You have to walk a fair way down but when you get there it is worth it. They sell hotpot as their speciality but I loved the pho (beef noodle soup). We went to the second place on the street and the guys were really friendly. For 4 bowls of Pho and a drink each it cost us $270000 dong (less than $20 Australian dollars). I would highly suggest you try it. The markets are opened Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights.

reviews.author: Tanya H
reviews.title: Interesting, bustling night market.
reviews.content: Am glad we made it to the night markets. You can get a lot of bargains if you're prepared to barter- there are a huge range of goods. It is very crowded but still has a great atmosphere.

reviews.author: Jayasri V
reviews.title: Shopping in night market
reviews.content: We gone to night market on sat and sun night shopping with small kids. If u have bargain skill u can use it. Some shops they won't reduce the price. We can buy n8 pants , bags, purses with in $5 .some Vietnamese dolls ,magnet also I jus purchased. But I felt night market is costly comparing to other shops...before entering night market u can try some local,fruits with salty and spicy. In night market openly some pickpockets people are roaming and doing stealing from ur handbag.so be careful...have a happy shopping ....

reviews.author: LaToner
reviews.title: Interesting bustling night market
reviews.content: It's a very long stretch of night market in middle of inter-connecting streets flanked on both sides by shops. They sell street food, clothing, shoes, crafts etc....The streets are closed to traffic. It's interesting experience. We were warned of pick-pockets.

reviews.author: Terry D
reviews.title: Something to do
reviews.content: Its something to do with the family. Its just a long street like everyother maket and just walk aroundThey block the entry points so cars cant get through

reviews.author: Huette7
reviews.title: Lots of people
reviews.content: Very crowded, but a night market has to be crowded, doesn't it? :-) Even more interesting the traffic around that place. A place with great atmosphere.

reviews.author: Hautetraveller
reviews.title: Fabulous Night market
reviews.content: The night market is at the old quarters. Excellent picks and the roads are closed from traffic so that u can walk without a care in the world and shop to your hearts content. Clothes, shoes, jewelry, eatables, handicrafts etc etc..

reviews.author: Noisrucxe
reviews.title: 【 Tet Trung Thu 】
reviews.content: This night market is located near Hoan Kiem Lake.( only on weekend )It may be very crowded before Mid-Autumn Festival "Tet Trung Thu".Because so many Vietnamese-family go to this market for children.I love this Mid-Autumn Festival's atmosphere.I recommend this attraction.

reviews.author: Shasha S
reviews.title: Get ready to bargain all your might!
reviews.content: If you enjoy to shop, this is the place for you.But to get souvenirs with reasonable price you might have to bargain almost 75% off of the given price. Get ready to pretend not buying to the merchants too when the price could not get lower, they will actually come running to you at the end. Not kidding.

reviews.author: Nick I
reviews.title: Ok
reviews.content: Went with family. It was ok with quite similar stands. Lots of people with many locals. I've been to better night markets but worth a visit if you want to experience Hanoi at night.

reviews.author: ekeat79
reviews.title: A very huge night market
reviews.content: This night market only operates on weekends, and the entire length of this market stretches across several streets, therefore there's a lot of walking to be done if you are planning to cover the entire market. Just like any typical night market, the stalls here sell a wide range of items, incl. foods, drinks, souvenirs, toys, clothes, accessories, etc. Negotiate with the traders to get the best deal for your purchases.

reviews.author: mushroom001
reviews.title: Very long
reviews.content: The night market is very long, stretching along many streets, which guarantee you many things are being sold. From street food to souvenirs and clothes, even purikura (sticker photos) which I did! It closes at 11pm and the local says that it's only open on weekend nights. I went there for 2 nights to search for things to bring back home..

reviews.author: Benjamin H
reviews.title: Average night market
reviews.content: Interesting people but other than that just an average night market. More enjoyable for the street life than the actual shopping.

reviews.author: Gavatron07
reviews.title: Enjoyable slice of Hanoi nightlife
reviews.content: We enjoyed a walk through the night market on our way back to our hotel from dinner. We appreciated the vibe and as most of the people there appeared to be Vietnamese we were able to walk leisurely along without being pestered to buy something we didn't need.The people watching was the fun part and it was good to be part of a scene that was largely local.  I don't think it merits a visit for itself but if you're around about it's worth a visit.

reviews.author: EleanorCallaghan
reviews.title: Wonderful!
reviews.content: A great place to visit right in the centre of Hanoi! The street is bustling with people and full of life. Typical Asian night market with its smells and food. Great for a cultural adventure and to experience the street food

reviews.author: Kerry G
reviews.title: Busy, fun, bargains
reviews.content: We loved the night market. Good for headphones. Jewellery. Etc a nice place to browse and experience the Vietnamese way of life

reviews.author: MaakaLisa1
reviews.title: Must do
reviews.content: Crazy experience, loved it but after a few days was over the hassle and bustle and wanted peace from all the beeping of motorbikes lol

reviews.author: _-rachella-_1
reviews.title: Not worth the effort
reviews.content: I bought a nice dress for £3 but this market was exhausting and filled with a lot of tat. The designer bags are poor quality replicas with really obvious mistakes. One word: abidas.

reviews.author: Sylvain J
reviews.title: Not really worth your time
reviews.content: Mostly low quality merch. Fun to see for one time but really not that special. Lots of repetition of the same products for which there is mostly no use. Some t-shirts are fum to buy but two or three times washing and it falls apart. But what do you want for 2 euros. If you go, take good care of yor personal items as the place has as many pick pockets as they have night stands! Never bring too much money and hide your mobile well enough.

reviews.author: Puppy
reviews.title: Busy market
reviews.content: If your in Hanoi at the weekend visit the Old Town Weekend Night Market for shopping remember there are pick pockets especially at the blind orchestra show but it’s worth a look. If your in Hanoi in autumn it is time for“Com” (grilled green rice) it appeared in many streets in Hanoi. “Com” is made from green sticky rice that is harvested in the blossom period, roasted many times, crashed and sieved. When eating com, you must eat slowly and chew very deliberately in order to appreciate all the scents, tastes, and plasticity of the young rice. Com is used in many specialties of Vietnam, including com xao (browned com), banh com (com cakes), che com (sweetened com soups), etc.

reviews.author: Dodgerlong
reviews.title: Vibrant Asian Market
reviews.content: Run of the mill Asian night market, you can buy just about anything for a price. Some really yummy street food. If you have visited one night market then you know the drill, keep an eye on you valuables, and have a bargain.

reviews.author: timbles13
reviews.title: Ok if you're in town at the weekend, not worth a special visit
reviews.content: Stall upon stall of cheap imitations & poor copies! There are a few bargains to be had but nothing that can't be found elsewhere in town for the same price.Decent atmosphere though! Not too crowded! Probably more interesting at beginning or end to see still holders setting up or packing away their mountains of goods. 7:30 - 11 pm or thereabouts.A few bits of street food here & there

reviews.author: Kim R
reviews.title: Noisy and Vibrant
reviews.content: We found the night market an exciting and noisy place to visit. Just about anything you might want to buy is available (for a price - how good are you at bargaining?) and it feels like half the population of Hanoi is crammed into the streets.

reviews.author: BINHTRAN1029
reviews.title: GREAT NIGHT LIFE & STREET FOODS
reviews.content: Hanoi night market is opened on every Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays from 18h00 - 23h00. That the best place for you to discover very cheap, delicious street foods & free to enjoy traditional Vietnamese music like ca tru, cheo, xam, quan ho. You also can buy cheap clothes and souvenirs here but be smart to bargain.Don't wear luxury accessories, be aware of the pickpockets!

reviews.author: Chris101111
reviews.title: Crazy night.
reviews.content: Great night market in the Old Quarter, its hectic, busy, crowded buy also really enjoyable. Take it for what it is, a Asian market and just experience it.

reviews.author: michael f
reviews.title: Great Fun and Bargains.
reviews.content: The night market starts to get going around 7:30 pm with quite a few motorcycles trying to use the area as a shortcut so be mindful. After the officials show up with loudspeakers and gain control of the entry points into the night market then the selling really gets hopping. Lots of stuff for a tourist and local alike so be ready to push your way through the crowds and have fun. The best is getting a table near by and watching people while the evening continues to cool. Have fun!

reviews.author: Glenn M
reviews.title: Must see
reviews.content: This is a must see place hustle and bustle everywhere. If you can not find it here it probably can not be found.

reviews.author: Omaandopa17
reviews.title: Night Markets in Hanoi is a MUST
reviews.content: We have been to the night markets on a few occasions and love them.  They are on Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights and start around 6 pm and finish around 10pm.  The place is alive with people selling everything you can imagine. Lots of people bargaining and some just looking.  There is also a street that runs off from the main market street that sells food (street food).  If you are adventurous try some of the street food as its so yummy. Word of warning watch your wallets make sure they can't be pick pocketed (this happens all over the world so don't be put off).  Its a great atmosphere and worth the visit.  Prices can be overpriced for foreigners so bargain a little but don't over do it as it usually works out to be only a dollar or two that you are haggling over.  Remember a good sense of humour and a smile will get you a long way with the people of Hanoi, who seem a little stand offish at first.

reviews.author: Addy002
reviews.title: Rude rude rude!
reviews.content: Hanoi might look beautiful and scenic but the people here are absolutely rude, atrocious and major thugs. We were conned by the fruit sellers, the tuk tuk gyys and the money exchangers etc.. People in this city are super money minded and are extremely arrogant; they start yelling and screaming at tourists and after experiencing the same 3-4 times we finally got the hang of their behaviour. Having been to so many other countries , this was by far the most arrogant country. We were in Ho Chi min city and it was way more friendly and hospitable. All I can say is be alert in the city or be ready to be tricked and fooled!

reviews.author: TOAO1
reviews.title: Nice Night Market
reviews.content: We visited the night market friday night and was surprised how non crowded it was. We have been on market like this where you have to line up just to see things they sell, so this was a relief. But I guess it depends on day and time. The sellers don't seem to force people in to their sales wagon either. The market is huge so make sure you have time to explorer it, but many of the shops sells the same stuff, so you may want to compare the prices.And as many other reviewers says: Take care of your belongings. People are watching you.Anyway, if you take your precautions you will have a nice time here.

reviews.author: TonkleChicken
reviews.title: Buzzing with locals and tourists
reviews.content: As it was still 36 degrees at 8PM, I wasn't sure if this was worth the effort. Thankfully I went anyway. This is a very large linear market covering about 1km, with lots of interesting food, shoes, bits and clothing stalls. But be prepared to bargain hard as you may settle on a price of about 20% of the starting price.

reviews.author: janicejhk
reviews.title: Must Search for Locally Made
reviews.content: Fun if you've not done it but if you are used to these types of markets, the redundancy of cheap Chinese made bulk gifts is disappointing.  Take the time to look and there are local handicrafts to be had so don't be completely discouraged.

reviews.author: jason d
reviews.title: Great night markets and well worth the visit
reviews.content: Really good night markets with a really broad range of stuff. One of the better markets while we were in Hanoi. So large as well, so make sure you have the time to spend and walk around it.Watch out for dodgy ppl who are probably watching your movements so they can pickpocket you or similar. I noticed the same dodgy characters  near us in several market locations and went up to them and freaked them away. Later on I saw the same two stalking another couple who had NO idea until I quietly informed them. Don't let this put you off tho, I found this place safer than New York City

reviews.author: Braeden H
reviews.title: Never ending, be careful.
reviews.content: These markets are Massive! You'd have to rush through them to cover them over one night, keeping in mind a lot of the stalls sell the same products. Definitely worth the visit. I wouldn't take any valuables with you though, pickpockets are prominent, so just start aware.

reviews.author: Tareq S
reviews.title: Awesome experience in the night market
reviews.content: The night market was one of the few memories I have in Hanoi, Vietnam that I traveled in June 2015. The market is quite big and it exceeded my expectation. The main problem is there is very few ATM machine around that market.

reviews.author: drrosszx10
reviews.title: Large market, good last effort shopping
reviews.content: Like the shirts around here say, same, same, but different, the Hanoi street market is full of almost everything you could be looking for, and we used it to blow some local currency we had left over on our final night in Hanoi, even though the locals here really were not interest in bartering, at all, at every stall we went to, the deals compared to home were still great, so we spent up. Huge street market open friday to Sunday night from 6pm-ish.

reviews.author: Andreainalberta
reviews.title: If it's on your way somewhere, worth a visit
reviews.content: Visited on our way home from dinner one night and managed o haggle our way into a new pair of faybans (fake raybans) for 100VND including case. Pretty much all the stalls sell the same stuff: sunglasses, phone cases, electronics, etc. so not many local items or variety but if any of those items suit your fancy it's worth a visit.

reviews.author: Graham M
reviews.title: Spend some time here
reviews.content: The night markets in Hanoi are held every Friday, Saturday and Sunday evening and are ready to slope about through from seven p.m. each of the evenings. They are an eclectic mix of all things that you could possibly imagine at a market in Vietnam and they are over the top with stalls and variety. There is just so much of everything and the stall holders love to haggle with you. They are generally quite good natured about it all and seem to have very thick skins. I cannot vouch for the quality as I have purchased very little in the end, although it seems to be okay. There is a fabulous food area at the western end and I can vouch for this - the food is amazing with so much variety from which to choose. Allow yourself a couple of hours at least and enjoy the experience - I have been three times so far and will be going back again tonight on this my last night in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Ros E
reviews.title: Great way to spend the evening!
reviews.content: In the late afternoon, we loved shopping our way along the streets of Central Hanoi. By dark, we enjoyed watching the night markets being set up and streets being blocked to traffic. After enjoying the pretty town lights around the lake on a walk, we shopped our way thru the streets to this night market, where we continued shopping for everything you could think of.  Great place to stock up on essentials & clothing, as well as special items.  We loved the corner food stalls, and 'grazed' our way along the streets, tasting the many flavours of yummy Vietnamese foods as we shopped.  Highly recommended to do !  We'd love to go do it all again...

reviews.author: Jeffkhs
reviews.title: Nothing that we have not seen before
reviews.content: We were expecting the night market in the old quarter (only open on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays) to be somewhat different from other night markets in Thailand or even Malaysia but we were slightly disappointed as it seems that there is not much difference in what is sold in these night markets.Generally this particular night market sells mainly clothes. Other things included souvenirs, phone casings, a little bit of food here and there.  The weather in Hanoi at this time of the year did not help either.If you are a regular visitor to night markets, this one is nothing spectacular. However if you have nothing better to do and have some time to kill, then it may be worth a stroll.

reviews.author: Karen M
reviews.title: The Never ending Market
reviews.content: It is huge,we didn't get to the other end as you have stalls back to back so we did a few blocks of one side and turned and did the other side on way back,A typical market where many of them sell same wares but still if you barter you can grab a bargain or 10 as I did.An experience you won't forget,thoroughly enjoyed getting amongst the locals. A word of advice as it is very hot and very crowded I took a packet of facial wipes which came in very handy,we would often stop have a drink freshen up with a facial wipe and start shopping again.

reviews.author: KaLoMc
reviews.title: Barter, barter, barter!
reviews.content: The Night Market is a very full on experience - the market itself goes for blocks and blocks but there is plenty on offer - food, souvenirs, clothing and one-off relics you won't find anywhere else!

reviews.author: Amanda W
reviews.title: Eh...
reviews.content: Night market was typical SE Asian style with a lot of people and activity. We had fun bargaining (which I guess is the important part even if we probably got ripped off). There is a great night life area near Backpackers Hostel which is right off the Night Market street. Most fun of the night.

reviews.author: G C
reviews.title: High energy setting and nice street performances enjoyed by locals & visitors both :)
reviews.content: After dodging the hectic and chaotic Ha No traffic, a visit to the Old Quarter's Night Market can be a delightful change -- vehicles in this area are prohibited, and the well-lit streets have only a few scooters (that somehow manage to sneak inside the perimeter).  If you're not interested in purchasing something (mostly apparel is offered in the many stalls in the center of two streets), you can still take part in the energy and the carnival-like atmosphere... I especially enjoyed the classical Vietnamese "opera style" performances and live music, at the center of the Market; this included folks dressed in traditional regalia, and a fire dancer as well.  Small presents, and even VNDs are distributed to the children in the audience (very nice touch!).  The pubs and bars are filled with young tourists (so if you seeking nightlife with fellow travelers, this is the place to come to during the weekends... the Hanoi Backpacker Hostel was really jumping).  If you're not into the "drinking scene", you can stop at a cafe for a meal, coffee, dessert, etc. and also just stroll with the crowds, and enjoy the activities & cheerful buzz of the Night Market :)NOTE:  If you're staying at a place that's a bit distant from the Night Market, you can have your taxi driver drop you off at one of the main entrances.

reviews.author: SSDelhi
reviews.title: Visit the market only for the sake of it...
reviews.content: Comprising of unending stalls majorly of cheap and sub-standard goods, this market was way below my expectations. Being a foreigner was definitely a set back with the shop keepers demanding exorbitant price for goods that fell below quality standards. I purchased souvenirs and other gift items at much reasonable price from the streets in Old quarter on regular working days. I was actually scared of visiting the place after my hotel and my colleagues from Vietnam warned against the frequent pick-pocketing in the night market. Kept clinging to the little cash I carried after all I had heard about it. Over-crowded and not at all children friendly.

reviews.author: DebbieBridge
reviews.title: Nice stroll, but didn't but
reviews.content: I love night markets, so if you like to just wander and take in the atmosphere, then by all means do that here.I did not find that what was on sale was well made or would be likely to fit.  I never got to the haggle stage, so can't comment on price.It's huge, but can't say there was much of interest for a tourist, but, maybe it's more for the locals?

reviews.author: Duffmondo
reviews.title: Sizes and clothing - TAKE CAUTION!!
reviews.content: If your a bit bigger than the average local be carful that the ticket telling you it's your size fool you. If it has a sticker on top of the original ticket. You get home only to find it's too small. This only happened with a single pair of shorts in my experiance. They were only $10 but it still tarnished the good vibe of the market as a whole. Got plenty of honest people to. Just peel back those stickers before you buy and see what they have to say. IF you get ripped you can alway give it to a friend (small friend) as a present.Otherwise it was great found heaps of cool gadgets, nicks and nacks, plenty of snacks and much much more!

reviews.author: John K
reviews.title: Woolworths it's not
reviews.content: We walked the length of the market and back. It is supposed to be pedestrian friendly, however the occasional scooter barrels along. There is a variety of tat for sale and food stalls at the far end. The most interesting thing was a small temple beside the market where they were having a service and being able to listen to the chanting in the courtyard beside the temple. Would I rush back, no. If you found the review helpful please let me know.

reviews.author: Raintree_Thailand
reviews.title: Something for everyone!
reviews.content: It takes a pretty hardened shopper to walk the full length of the night market and not to find something to buy.  Lots of crafts, clothes, shoes,  bags, folk art, food, drinks.... the list goes on and on!!  Have to bargain hard for discounts, but always an opportunity to find something you need or want.

reviews.author: pieata
reviews.title: Another market, but in Hanoi!
reviews.content: Open.  Fri to Sunday , after 6pm.To me, just another  night market,  CHEAP.  GOODS, but to me, is it really  cheap?In Asia, cheap to me is Normally, SMILES on purchase, TEARS after  use!!!Buyer beware!NO REFUNDS (you can try).  I walked  1/2  way up, then. Turned back(no purchases)About 30 mins, others may be more interested !

reviews.author: yensta
reviews.title: Unfortunately, full of cheap tat
reviews.content: I went to the night market and left after 10 minutes. It was full of poor quality, unattractive merchandise, and was very very crowded.Considering how much Hanoi has to offer in the way of shopping, I was really surprised to find the market so disappointing.

reviews.author: RohitMonserrate
reviews.title: Almost got pick pocketed
reviews.content: The night market was nice to browse just for the experience. Almost got pickpocketed at the end the food was nice though.

reviews.author: Oller46
reviews.title: Big but not that good
reviews.content: The market is big but there are just a few food places and the goods are not nice showed to the people. Also there are not really nice things to buy. Just 50 booths with handy covers and other stuff. There are no nice clothes or nice accessories as we know it from other markets in Asia. There are a lot of people around (also a lot of locals) which is nice. But the most of the sellers are unfriendly and do not really understand what you want ...

reviews.author: Brooke R
reviews.title: Busy atmosphere
reviews.content: I went on a Saturday night, the night markets were packed. Tried some of the street food which was good but didn't buy anything from the stalls

reviews.author: shilpa swami
reviews.title: It's big!!!
reviews.content: The night market is really big.. We did not but anything, we went there just for the experience n I must say it was good.. There are lot of food stalls all around so if u can eat non veg go ahead n discover. We did not eat much cos we are vegetarians.. U should visit the night market to get a feel of Vietnam, the people and their lifestyle. But everyone advised us to be safe with our valuables, we were lucky enough to not experience anything bad, but I guess it's good to be cautious..

reviews.author: RTT
reviews.title: Not bad
reviews.content: We actually went on a Thursday night to find plenty of stalls and shoppers around, so not sure it is actually 'weekends only'. It was nice to walk around for a while, although a lot of the stalls seemed to sell very similar items. Worth a look and I'd probably go again, I wonder if there's more on offer on the weekends although there was multiple streets worth as it was. Expect high pedestrian/scooter traffic.

reviews.author: William L
reviews.title: Best shopping in Hanoi!
reviews.content: If you are in Hanoi try & make it to the weekend night markets in the centre of the old quarter (Friday-Sunday nights). These markets offer the best items from Hanoi's shops at bargain prices. I also felt that perusing these markets was less intimidating that walking into a shop & getting bombarded by the owner. Definitely aimed at tourists but attracts large crowds of locals & has a great vibe!

reviews.author: LakeComoExpert
reviews.title: Huge, amazing, a must!
reviews.content: Only open at the weekends - Friday, Saturday and Sunday, this huge market stretches for miles you can buy clothing ( handy if you are there in the winter when hanoi is cold  - thick jackets for £7.50), food, jewellery, shoes, electronics etc.Be careful with the electronics though, we bought a selfie stick and it broke after 2 days. We didn't buy a cheap looking one either!Get there around 7pm  as  between 8-9 it gets so busy y can hardly move. Do it ina logical manner to get the best out of it, start at the top, do the right side, then go as far as you can stand and walk back up the other way.Hang onto your bags and don't have an easy access ruck-sack on your back. It's a busy place, so easy to get pick-pocketed. Just be aware, it's by no means scary. And is great fun.

reviews.author: Mdayyana
reviews.title: bargains, bargains
reviews.content: Really value for money and spoiled for choice. Good place to get all those authentic handmade pouches or bags as souvenirs.

reviews.author: FormerCaliBoy
reviews.title: Ok to see once, but not impressive
reviews.content: We headed over to the night market to see if we could find any good deals and maybe find something for dinner.  Once we got to the main street it was packed with people bumping into you and it did not make for a pleasant evening.  The vendor booths, I felt, did not really offer any great deals of interest to me.    There were a couple of areas that severed food, but we decided to just go to another area of town for dinner.  We did need to use the bathrooms at the night market and there were pay toilets (tourist price) and they were pretty dirty and disgusting.  We walked back through the market to get back to our start point and were more than happy to move on.  I had no desire to return again during our stay.

reviews.author: nObOdY007
reviews.title: It Has All What You're Looking For
reviews.content: Such A Wonderful Place To Shopping At Night. It However So Busy All Time. Everything is Cheap With Good Quality. You Can Find Many Many Stuffs During The Way. Such A Long Way To Walk And Could HardLY Find The End Or Way Back. Overall, It's Good.

reviews.author: Zee S.Puad
reviews.title: Long way
reviews.content: A very very big night market.. You can't even find the end.. Located in old quarter near Dong Xuan market.. The goods is awesome.. They sell lots of things.. Went there at 11pm and it is still open.. Nice!

reviews.author: Vestfoldgirl
reviews.title: Mostly crap
reviews.content: This place sells low quality items and badly made copies of designer clothes and bags. We didnt really find anything that we wanted to spend money on, we were debating on buying a selfiestick, but decided against it in the end :-) This is a big market covering several streets, but is not the kind of market that I enjoy visiting, I would rather go somewhere they sell some genuine handicrafts and not the sort of crap and bad quality you find here. Basically I waste of time.

reviews.author: jaci55555
reviews.title: Good deals among the pushing
reviews.content: You will be pushed and shoved. Clothes are Vietnamese sized except for t shirts. Lots of other pretty things though. Definitely worth a walk through the throng! Not much bargaining, a few vendors will try rip you off, first check prices at a few places. Got some great deals!

reviews.author: Tyson M
reviews.title: Rudest people in Vietnam
reviews.content: Having travelled Bali, Cambodia and the south of Vietnam before arriving at Hanoi and seeing plenty of markets along the way this place was a real disappointment for us. The markets are basically filled with the same old crap. There is no way I would wear any of this stuff back home. The stuff is far to pricey compared to the other markets in Asia I have been to… The vendors are not willing to budge at all… Not even a few thousand dollars… They don't acknowledge you… When locals are buying things they hide the money so you don't see how much they are paying.Even though this is street is 'closed off to scooters' they seem to stream through the markets beeping there horns with an angry face when you fail to move.AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE.

reviews.author: HoneycombDreamers
reviews.title: Leave Your Motorcycle at Home
reviews.content: For us the night market was a little disappointing, as the products sold were no different from the Old Quarter during the day. The bonus was the freedom to walk down the streets without watching for traffic and no tooting horns could be heard, only the hum of chatting friends.Though the odd annoying motorcycle did try to squeeze past the crowds of people to just keep us on edge. The bright lights and the locals did give off a happy vibe. We were also warned by our guide that pick pockets were active in the area too. The night market is only open Friday, Saturday and Sunday, so we thought we'd take a peek, as we had a free Saturday night.

reviews.author: CanberraDiner
reviews.title: Fun night market
reviews.content: Ok so the wares at the night market are your typical flea market offering. But the atmosphere is very fun. Prices seem to start a little higher than what you'll be asked during the day in the Hanoi Old Quarter but sellers are happy to bargain.The main selling point for this night market is that they close off the streets to traffic. Which is a plus if you're tired of dodging hundreds of motorbikes, cars, scooters and push bikes while you shop.

reviews.author: joltt
reviews.title: Big night market with many stalls
reviews.content: This is quite a big night market with about 3 - 4 blocks of streets lined with many stalls selling all types of items.  The night market operates on every Friday, Saturday and Sunday.  Stalls start setting up at 7pm and the road is closed to traffic for the night market to be set up.  However, do watch out for motorbikes as many riders on motorbikes still try to scoot on the road even though it is closed to traffic.  Some stalls are clear in their pricing and state pricing clearly, others, probably need to bargain.  This round, I realised that I was unable to buy any items at 50% of what was quoted.  So do have some idea of how much things cost before bargaining to know what is a fair price to pay.Should visit.

reviews.author: Celebr8_8
reviews.title: Not very good... But not too bad
reviews.content: The night market, which runs on Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights from 7pm to 11pm, was one of the bright sparks for my family during our stay in Hanoi. The stuff sold there are not as junky as some described them to be. A little touristy... but IMHO it's way better than Dong Xuan Market which is too cramped and messy for me. Have fun...

reviews.author: NinaTom
reviews.title: Not the worst, not the best.
reviews.content: There is a lot of repetition along the long line of stalls in the Hanoi Night Market, but there are also some nice buys to be found amongst the clutter. The atmosphere in the whole was good and it was pleasant enough to stroll around. The whole area around the night market is scattered with small bars and food stalls to take a break. There are always going to be people trying to nick stuff but no more here than any other big city across the world, just be sensible with your belongings; we ensured we put all valuables in inside zip pockets and didn't take any bags out with us.

reviews.author: Harry R
reviews.title: 'Great atmosphere, but the cheap fakes lack any quality'
reviews.content: Recently visited the markets on Sunday night and was great to see the typical hustle and bargaining taking place in the vast amounts of stalls. However, recently coming from Ho Chi Minh and Hoi An the quality of product is much poorer and even though the price maybe a little lower, these markets have made fakes that are very tacky and with the exception of some products are not worth the low prices.These markets are definitely worth having a walk around for the vibe of a Vietnamese night market and the risk of pickpockets is unlikely providing you are wary of your possessions, with police also frequent in the area. However, unless you are happy with cheap and cheerful stuff you probably won't buy much, with other cities and the day time shops through Ha Noi selling much better quality items for reasonably similar prices.

reviews.author: Tegan R
reviews.title: A typical night market
reviews.content: We took a walk through the market while recently in Hanoi. It is your typical market found in Asia full of atmosphere and, of course, an infinite number of stalls selling souvenirs, copy clothes, and numerous other wares. My advice is if you're going to go to the market then go hungry so you can check out the food! We had unfortunately eaten before we stopped by but managed to fit in some bbq pork and it was delicious!

reviews.author: Oliver S
reviews.title: A night market like any other, but...
reviews.content: still worthwhile to stroll through it and just to observe other people haggling and bargaining for the same-same fake watches, clothes or other useless nick-nack. Or just sit down in one of the street food stalls, enjouy a cold Tiger or a feww bites and enjoy the scenery. I don't quite understand some of the negative ratings mentioning the pick pockets and thieves. On this market there aren't any more or less thieves then on any other market in the world, be it in Paris, Cartagena, Mumbai or wherever. I personally have no sympathy for those blue eyed touristst that lost their property although they knew better. Next time better keep your belongings (wallets, I-Phones etc) in the hotel.

reviews.author: Ten P
reviews.title: Affordable and Negotiable
reviews.content: The place is generally clean. The night market is not one compact place though. It is a long stretch of stalls along a few streets in Hanoi. Poor in geography, I only remember treading a short  street, crossing to the other side, walking straight a narrow street, turning left, turning right, crossing again, and taking a cab back to the hotel. But I got to buy nice bags at really affordable prices, with good quality, and warm, smiling, gentle people of Hanoi, Vietnam. Do not get fooled, though, I was able to chat with an old woman who I learned to be a revolutionary during the Vietnam war.  She was in her early 20s when she fought during the Vietnam-American war. No one would guess she was a guerilla - she is a woman of courage and righteousness hiding behind her soft eyes, gentle smile, and meek bearing. I feasted on beautifully colored tops, bonnets, shirts and masks, but bought only what I needed -uh oh, you have to have strong discipline to control impulsive buying in Hanoi because there's just a lot to want.  Prices are already affordable - but a good negotiation can bring it a few cent lower. Happy shopping :)

reviews.author: SaltyDogz
reviews.title: Worth a look and check out the street food
reviews.content: All that is said in the other reviews re the lack of traffic etc. But the stalls are nearly all cheap average quality clothing, bags, sunglasses, fake watches etc aimed at the local buyers and Vietnamese tourists.The saving grace are the lack of traffic and the many and interesting street food stalls and the plentiful cheap beer. Street side vendors with tiny stools for you to sit on (not good for the elderly or frail) will fill you up with yummy food cooked in front of you and endless cheap beer. What's not to like about that.

reviews.author: Ira S
reviews.title: Crowded, Noisy and the place to be on a Weekend Night in Hanoi
reviews.content: The night market is open on weekend nights.  We went on a Saturday night.  The vendors have  stalls set up in the street, traffic is prohibited and a cadre of police make sure the motor bike riders keep off the streets and the vendors adhere to the rules.The streets are packed with tourists and locals.  The vendors sell mostly stuff that no one seemed to want to buy, t-shirts, tourist items, purses, and so on.  There are also food vendors.  We bought  some food from a street vendor, I have no idea what it was, but it was tasty and inexpensive.To me, it was all about the atmosphere and not the items being sold.  It is a great place to people watch and worth the visit.

reviews.author: Lity M
reviews.title: Good place and Bargain
reviews.content: Good to see many things you can bargain and get a good deal. Really cheap and reasonably good stuff for the money you pay.

reviews.author: Itinerant Ozzie
reviews.title: Bustling Night Market - Limited Variety
reviews.content: The Hanoi night market takes place on Hang Dao street in the old quarter after 7pm a few nights a week (definitely Friday and Sat night). The street is blocked off to vehicular traffic during the market operation which makes a huge difference as most of the shopping streets are swamped with traffic most of the time.The market is quite large extending for at least 3 blocks and it is certainly attracts a lot of interest with large crowds.The thing that lets this market down is the relatively narrow range of goods being offered. Having said that it is quite an experience and any visitor to Hanoi should visit at least once.

reviews.author: Jack P
reviews.title: Better than expected
reviews.content: I read a lot of bad reviews on here, but I'm not quite sure what everyone was expecting. It's your typical asian market - and it's unlikely you will find a huge amount to buy, but soaking in the atmosphere is a really nice experience.In the end we ended up buying a pretty reasonable selection of things - from decorative post cards to new phone cases.Don't expect the best thing in the world, but be realistic and you'll enjoy it. As for pickpockets - we didn't see any but with any situation like this - just be wary and you will have no problems at all.

reviews.author: morgandeller
reviews.title: A fun night out
reviews.content: We went to the night market twice while in Hanoi. Lots of stalls, bustling atmosphere, street food, a decent shopping opportunity and definitely lots of fun. Dodging the motorbikes can be a little annoying as can the masses of people, I'd suggest going a bit earlier in the evening, around 7:30, if you want to avoid the crazy crowds!

reviews.author: Mahendra A
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: The market is full of stalls selling cheap quality clothes, bags, accessories, belts and souvenier items at the same price as the other regular shops in Old Quarter. There is nothing special that you would miss if you do not visit this place. Also, I was warned by the hotel staff that due to the heavy crowd in the market, there is a good chance you might get pickpocketed.

reviews.author: Prudence W
reviews.title: Busy Market not the best for shopping
reviews.content: Hanoi seems to be full of authentic knock offs and cheap clothes. The people of Hanoi seem to like this. As a tourist it's great to see local people doing what they do (great outfits from promenading couples dressed uo for the night!)But as a westerner the clothes were nowhere near my size (UK 12) as the female frame here is soooo petite. Good for people watching and wandering, but not great for shopping either for travel clothes, souvenirs or gifts.

reviews.author: Tim S
reviews.title: Bustling market but lacking in variety.
reviews.content: I live in Hanoi now so I'm used to the crowds, in fact I love being in a crowd. That's what visiting a real market is all about and this one is certainly bustling at it's peak times.What lets this place down is the lack of variety in the stalls.

reviews.author: Jeanette W
reviews.title: More for the experience!
reviews.content: It's definitely worth coming out for The Night Market on Friday, Saturday night to check out the items on sale.Take in the experience and you never know, you might see a few things that would make perfect souvenirs for your friends and family back home. P.S.Make sure you are aware of your belongings at all times.

reviews.author: Juliana788
reviews.title: BEAWARE!! WALLET THEIVES
reviews.content: whilst having an okay time looking through the many stalls and waking through the pushy crowds I was alerted that my bag had been slashed and my wallet stolen! i went to the police but they did not care! the crowds are so pushy, that if you go make sure you take no valuables and a bag in which you can hold! my friend also had her wallet stolen the night before! would never go back. you can buy anything at the market during the day at the many shops on the streets of Hanoi

reviews.author: Lasse R
reviews.title: Your average market
reviews.content: Rather crowded and nothing especially interesting. Picked up a little stuff for the kids. It's only open in weekends and closes at 22:30.

reviews.author: DanielaKLI
reviews.title: Not very different from what you see during the day
reviews.content: The night market offers the same products that you can buy in the Old Quarter during the day. No big surprise. It's good if you have an idea of the 'normal' prices, to negotiate effectively (ex: if you know that a kid's souvenir t-shirt costs around 100.000 VND maximum, when you are approached and offered a t-shirt for 200.000, you know how to react). The market can quickly become unpleasant and overcrowded. Go there at the beginning of the night.

reviews.author: ivan l
reviews.title: long stretch of shops with repeated products
reviews.content: most of the shops sells similar items and are repeated throughout the night market. not many street food choices at this night market compared to that in HCMC or Taiwan. 5 of the vendors we encountered were not open to price negotiations. not even 10% off. it leaves us wondering if the price quoted in the first place is inflated or not? most guides and even our hotel says we should bargain from 50% off and pay no more than 70%. once in a while you can find something for a real bargain. there are men's belt going for 20K, 30K, 50K VND. some children and adult clothes going cheap too. only good enough for a once in a lifetime visit to experience.

reviews.author: HairdresserAbroad
reviews.title: longest night market I've ever seen
reviews.content: This night market is amazing so many vendors lots of people it's buzzing I made a couple of good buys, there's clothes sun glasses, souvenirs, there's something for everyone

reviews.author: Brad R
reviews.title: Mostly junk
reviews.content: The atmosphere is lively but most of the stalls are selling the same junk you've seen in most of the tourist shops throughout Hanoi. It's a good place for a wander after dinner but I was repeatedly warned about pickpockets, however I saw no evidence of this - then again I am extremely cautious. Don't feel like you've missed something if you don't get around to visiting, unless you're in the market for some cheap shirts shoes or other 'bargains'

reviews.author: James S
reviews.title: Like cartoon background scenery
reviews.content: WARNING!  Keep you wallet/money out of your pockets, keep nothing in your pockets full stop - unless you want it stolen.  I caught a lady trying subtly to undo the buttons on my trouser leg pockets attempting to get at my wallet.  I managed to prevent it being stolen.  From then on my wallet stayed in my shoulder bag which remained fastened and held over shoulder but towards the front of my body in my sight, NOT on my back and out of sight.  It can be a pain when buying something, having to keep going into the bad for money but worth it in the long run so you don't lose all your cash/bank cards etc. That said, despite the warning it's still worth a short visit and it's not a bad market for picking up some cheap t-shirts or other clothing.  Also, there's some knock off rucksacks to be had (North Face) which aren't bad and came in handy for me as I was seeking out a new one anyway - got a new one for about VND200K (about £6GBP).  There's the usual sunglasses, hair accessories, shoes, t-shirts, stand-up greeting cards, but it is a bit repetitive especially as it's quite long it doesn't change much from end to end, and some of the stall holders aren't up for much negotiation over the prices.  By all means have a look, but don't expect to find anything different, including any changes in price, the further you head down.  If you see something, get it, leave.

reviews.author: kalimah
reviews.title: Hanoi Night Market
reviews.content: I was able to buy embroidered bags. It was cheaper there than the regular shops in the Old Quarter. There were combs made of carabao and buffalo horn that looked very nice. No haggling. Fixed price. There were some handicrafts too. Lots of clothes.

reviews.author: SSQuah
reviews.title: Cheap but nothing really special
reviews.content: This is just like a night market in many of Asian cities and towns. Some roads would be closed up to traffic, allowing traders to set up their stalls. The items sold weren't that much different from what I would find in my hometown: cheap clothing, shoes, handbags, sweets, fresh and dried fruits, decorations, toys, stationery, sundry goods and roadside food, except that some of the branded goods may turn out questionable. The night market stretched for about one kilometre or so, but we gave up after walking along the Hàng Ngang Street. All the goods looked more or less the same, and if you see one, chances are that you would have seen them all.

reviews.author: Sue C
reviews.title: Beware pickpockets!!!!
reviews.content: We happened to stumble across this market after a walk after a meal one night. After venturing a small way into the market and seeing that it was generally a pretty crappy market with very average things on offer, and with very grumpy smallholders, we decided to leave. I was aware of some pushing a shoving around the entrance of the market and within seconds realised that my phone had been stolen from my bag. The 'pregnant' woman who had brushed past me and stolen the phone had disappeared as quickly as she had appeared. When I put in a police report the next morning there was a Singaporean couple in front of me at the police station reporting the same crime at the same place. Unfortunately  we had not been warned that pickpockets were rife here but I do tend to keep my things close and at the front of me. These guys are well versed at their 'craft' so do be very very careful at this location.

reviews.author: JohnF47
reviews.title: Great place to buy 3D cards
reviews.content: There is a lot of market here!  And it gets jam-packed.Having read the reports/advice, I went early evening before it became too crowded.  I loved the atmosphere, the buzz.  I carried no bag, no camera, no phone - better safe than sorry - and I did feel safe, even when it became more congested and people were jostling me at every turn.  This is NOT a place for back-packs!Had been looking to buy some 3D origami cards, and this was where I found the best selection (small and larger size), and the starting prices were lower than I had seen in regular stores.  Had fun bargaining (successfully) with a very friendly vendor.As expected, there is quite a range of product quality and price on offer, however bargains are to be had.Really glad I experienced this vibrant market.

reviews.author: Carrie N
reviews.title: Waste of time
reviews.content: I was here at the beginning of April. I went to a few markets across Asia, and this one was by far the worst. My hotel warned me of pickpockets. I saw a couple sketchy individuals, and as I watched them make their through the crowd, eyeballing the purses some ladies were carrying, I am certain they were not there to shop. It’s a big market yes, but every booth has the exact same very cheaply made garbage, and vendors were not willing to negotiate at all.

reviews.author: KiwiDriver
reviews.title: Cooler time to shop, pickpockets are rife
reviews.content: The market goes through the Old Quarter, it goes for 8 blocks.  Nothing different to buy here.  But nice to shop when it's cooler at night, you can get clothing, sunglasses, DVDs, handbags, etc here.I was 2 seconds away from losing my wallet though.  It was in the main part of my backpack, not the front zip.  The lady must have watched me buying something and putting my wallet away.  Then just steps down the market, I felt a slight nudge or bump, I turned around and saw a lady move her hand a little.  I quickly took my backpack off and the main zip, which was fully closed was half open!  I went to follow her but she was gone, very quick and into the crowd.Plse do be careful in Hanoi, from reading, it seems that pick pockets are aplenty up here.  Either have your backpack on the front of your body or put some money near your body and go out without a wallet.

reviews.author: Ida D
reviews.title: Interesting Night Market!
reviews.content: Hubby and I were lucky to have arrived on Saturday as we only found out about the market on the day itself. It had the feel of both the 'Pasar Malam' in Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia except you can bargain here. We ended up buying our souvenirs here and everything was pretty cheap. You can find souvenirs, toys, clotjes and shoes.Although on the downside, in my opinion, there are a lot of repetitive goods sold in the whole stretch of the market.I don't mind going there again to shop in I choose to visit Hanoi again. :)

reviews.author: Kerry C
reviews.title: Similar to daytime shopping but streets are 'closed'.
reviews.content: We enjoyed the night market. It sells clothes, souvenirs, jewellery and general stuff.  They close the streets for the market but not everyone follows that, there is still the occasional motorbike that  comes through. My son liked the cheap helicopter toy that a lady was demonstrating - it lit up in the night and cost a whole 50c.  It was also cooler and had a nice atmosphere with the lights.  Worth a stroll.

reviews.author: travelafeme
reviews.title: Great bargains
reviews.content: We were lucky that we were there for the weekend night market.  I bought clothes, souvenirs, scarf.  There were lots of cheap items.  They close a stretch of the street of Hang Dao, but still you can encounter few motorcycles entering the street.  There were grumpy salesladies, we just walk away from them.  There were nicer ones and made our shopping a pleasure.

reviews.author: MrGoh
reviews.title: Lovely evening outing on weekends
reviews.content: The night market operates every weekend only. It is an enjoyable way to spend the evening after dinner. We visit the night market every night when we were in Hanoi. The place is ordering (one way in, one way out) and there are many stuff to see and buy. Some of the stalls change over the days.

reviews.author: ShawnLiv
reviews.title: Dong Xuan Night Market
reviews.content: Hanoi night market, also known as Dong Xuan night market, held on weekend evenings in the Old Quarter of Ha Noi. Basically, I went because the night market is very close to my stayed hotel. Overall, I think it is worth a visit to experience the local lifestyle. You can see locals and tourists mingle along the streets. People were everywhere and the locals like to push their way through the crowd.As a whole, many stalls were selling the same things and isn’t much unique stuffs being sold here. Therefore, walk back half way. However, I still managed to buy some souvenirs, clothes, hand make Christmas card and etc. On the other hand, many reviews and my tour guide do remind me regarding the pickpocketing issues. Therefore, I keep all my valuables at the hotel.

reviews.author: Shawn_Storm
reviews.title: Detailed review of the Hanoi Night Market.
reviews.content: After reading the other reviews on here I decided to contribute an in depth review that addresses all aspects of the night market and hopefully clears up a few things.
