reviews.title: Beware of this seller
reviews.content: Don't buy food from this stall (near the crossroad at Hanoi Old Quarter nightmarket) , she cheated my money

reviews.author: psandhu1
reviews.title: Pleasant night market
reviews.content: Went here on Sunday evening at 7pm with my 8 month old baby in the sling. It is busy and the vendors are pleasant. My brother bought a Bluetooth speaker for £8. They sold mainly clothes, jewellery and footwear. Enjoyable.

reviews.author: Role
reviews.title: Market was nice if you haven’t been to one before
reviews.content: The markets are all ways cool great bargains some things are unique somethings repeat over and over. I would say if you e never been too a night market and it’s the weekend and you want something to do.  I would recommend you do the night market and walk around some. It’s safe and cool atmosphere. Hanoi is a little more laid back then southern Vietnam.

reviews.author: Andrew V
reviews.title: Busy
reviews.content: This is very busy with locals and tourists not a great deal of bargain to be had we did get a couple of good deals but on average most of the stuff is cheap knockoff that are not at a cheap price but if you’re in Hanoi it’s worth the look

reviews.author: Sherry Bischoff
reviews.title: Hanoi weekend night market
reviews.content: Interesting stroll through the stalls. Was hoping for more locally hand-made items. Lots of clothing and food. Even though the streets were closed there were still a number of mopeds driving through the crowd.

reviews.author: Jun David
reviews.title: Great Bargain
reviews.content: The Night Market runs from Don Xuang Market to near Hoa Kiem Lake.Lots of knocked off items from bags, shoes and shirts. Lots of street foods. Lots of souvenirs. Most of the stalls are selling the same items though. All items are cheap but you need to bargain.Great experience.

reviews.author: JustRose_CH
reviews.title: Not worth it
reviews.content: We arrived on a Monday and I spent the week looking forward to shopping at the night market. Other than a few stalls at the very beginning of the market, the end closest to the lake, the market was full of old clothes, underwear and generally things of that nature. The beginning had souvenirs for very reasonable prices, sometimes low enough not to bargain over. However I did not find anything at the night market I didn’t see elsewhere in Hanoi so if you are not there on a weekend don’t worry you are not missing anything. Note that the night market is only set up Friday to Sunday.

reviews.author: Francis Martino
reviews.title: Worth a Visit in crowded place.
reviews.content: The Hanoi market at night is beautiful during the week end,Definitely worth checking out. Food and Goods all you can buy. Make sure to bargain, but start with at least 20-30% of the price they say you, stay strong when bargaining. If you don't get the price you move to stand the next one will give you your desired price.  It takes a bit getting used to to the big crowd,the kind you see in the market of the old quarter, and also hair bands, jewelry, watches, some toys and shoes,IT appliances and so on.Be careful of your belongings during walking and sightseeing in very crowded place.

reviews.author: McCullough.Family
reviews.title: Good night out
reviews.content: Some of these reviews are very harsh. Do not get me wrong a lot of what is sold is the same but we never felt pressured into buying anything and no harm in looking for a couple of hours and most people will buy something

reviews.author: Simona
reviews.title: Prepare to be scammed
reviews.content: Markets in asia are kind of sightseeing, however I'd recommend avoiding this one or be very careful. The vendors are rude, not willing to bargain and you feel bad if you ask for another size. This market ruined my night as one vendor has stolen 90k dong from me. I've bargained a price to 80k dong and have her a 100k bill. She returned me 10k dong and I've tried to explain that she should give me another 10k back. Then she started yelling at me and grabed my bag with the good inside. She have scratched my arm and was insanely rude. I didn't understand what have happened when she continued to yell at me and many people gathered around. I've tried to either get my money back or get my good but she left me with only 10k dong in my hand. Basically, the scam is that she blamed me that I've given her only 10k dong and that I owe her money. She started pointing at my friend's pockets and tried to reach out to them. A crowd of vietnamese sellers gathered around and we were screamed at in vietnamese. I don't care about the 100k dong. Just the overall concept of this scam is ridiculous and we've got a bit scared when we were surrounded by vietnamese crowd screaming at us. Recommend giving exact amount to the vendors to avoid this and be very careful in the market as it seems that they would do anything for a couple of dollars, even get violent.

reviews.author: Anas A
reviews.title: Weekend market
reviews.content: Hanoi's Night Market happens every weekend and it is very popular for both locals and tourists. Full of street shops which sell a variety of products. The quality of most products is cheap and copied from other brands. The problem with the market is that it is overcrowded.

reviews.author: Sebastián M
reviews.title: Overcrowded
reviews.content: Too many people at this place. Vendors offer the same products along the street. Not worth spending time here. But for the first time it is nice experience, to see how the night market in Hanoi looks like.

reviews.author: Elsa C. L.
reviews.title: Fun and quite reasonably priced in Asia
reviews.content: Bargaining is necessary.  Naturally, vendors would like more profit.Highly unique wide assortment of Origami design cards for specific occasions or general are priced ranging from 20,000 to 35,000 Dong (US$1 = 22,500 to 23,000 Dong) depending on the size.Beautifully decorated fabric gift pouches approximately 5” X 6” are priced at 24,000 Dong.  When you buy five, you get one free.White cotton shirts with Vietnam attraction printed cost 40,000 Dong each.A native Vietnamese design colorful magnet is priced at 10,000 Dong.  My Vietnamese souvenir plate for my wall collection cost 100,000 Dong.Pork barbeque sells at 20,000.  As snack, three sticks would be satisfying for a person weighing 119 lbs as the pieces are not lean.No vehicle is supposed to go through the night market.  However, there were motorcycles.

reviews.author: hansibrahim
reviews.title: Wash your eye
reviews.content: Held every Friday, Saturday and Sunday, Hanoi Weekend Night Market is a busy, bustling gathering of roadside stalls and local food vendors that brings huge crowds of locals and tourists. It runs through the Old Quarter district from 19:00 onwards, starting from Hang Dao Street and running north to the edge of Dong Xuan Market.

reviews.author: tes108
reviews.title: Tacky junk
reviews.content: Our local friends told us that all the merchandise came from China. It did. Nothing remotely interesting and the place is devoid of charm.

reviews.author: Tabitha G
reviews.title: Crowded but enjoyable
reviews.content: Very crowded and a little overwhelming. Prices for the same item vary greatly, so be patient if you want something. If you’ve seen it once you’ll likely see it again. Get your best bargaining on, because you’ll need to cut the price by at least 70% to start. I found being patient and friendly works really well especially with young people. Lots of shoes, clothing and souvenirs. Also accessories (sunglasses, jewellery, make up and perfume.) Also electronic accessories. Remember- this stuff is all fake and the quality of the clothing in particular is very average. You’re just paying for the name brand. Overall a fun night out, recommended if you enjoy the market scene and crowds.

reviews.author: Bulbul
reviews.title: Vibrant weekend in the city
reviews.content: If you haven’t booked the tickets for Vietnam yet, book it for the dates that include the weekend. The night market is held on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday starting from 19:00. The street is a lively gathering of the roadside stalls. These stalls sell almost everything right from pop up cards to shoes. The prices are reasonable too. However, negotiations seemed relatively unattainable here as compared to Don Xuan and the old quarter market. A good bet is to buy souvenirs from here. You get a great variety.

reviews.author: cinbkk
reviews.title: Shopping and food
reviews.content: A good place to while away the time in the evening from Fri-Sun. Lots of food, snacks, clothes, shoes, accessories and souvenirs. Some streets are too crowded for a proper walk, but it's a huge area and there's always somewhere to go. One end of the market ends at the Hoan Kiem lake, a good place to catch some fresh air.

reviews.author: Atlas1669
reviews.title: Fun but not much else
reviews.content: A bit of fun walking past similar stalls. It was really crowded and quite fun even though there was little to tempt us to buy. Worth going to see just for the experience.

reviews.author: TonyMac64
reviews.title: Interesting but lots of the same stuff
reviews.content: We enjoyed our trip and the prices were comparative with other markets in Asia. My main criticism would be that all the clothing stalls had the same clothes, as did the jewellery and souvenir stalls etc. Worth it if markets are your thing but don’t expect anything out of the ordinary.

reviews.author: Gordo4037
reviews.title: Not much variety
reviews.content: This was a busy market but not in the realms of Bangkok or Saigon. Very busy with many people and a lovely atmosphere abounded. There was a lot of street vendors selling snacks which on the main were fried foods but good to get a sample of a wide range of food for only 20000 dong. The stalls were a little disappointing as they carried virtually the same clothes, souvenirs and trinkets. By the time you got to the end you pretty much knew what the return trip on the other side of the road was going to be like, The stall vendors have pretty high prices do it is important to haggle with them and enjoy the experience- after all they can only say no and you will find the same item at the next stall or two anyways. Whatever price I was given I countered with 25% of that and usually we met at 30 - 40% of the asking price. All in all a good way to spend a few hours out and about with the locals and other visiting tourists.

reviews.author: bunko007
reviews.title: Lots of people
reviews.content: It's good that we were accompanied by our Vietnamese supplier to this attraction.  The free guided tour made it easier for us to navigate the streets, where to find what we were looking for, and do translation for us with the vendors. The cool January weather made it comfortable for us to walk for at least 3 hours.  The crowded and lively atmosphere fascinated me, not with the stuff being sold.  Although I was able to buy some good quality neck ties, I couldn't find the trigger to purchase more as the options were really not interesting to me. Stalls selling similar products are bunched together so it's best to check around first before making the final purchase.

reviews.author: Albywon
reviews.title: Busy night markets
reviews.content: All sorts of different goods and foods available - some are good deals and some are not. Before you go do your research and work out what price you could pay elsewhere and make sure you negotiate accordingly!

reviews.author: Zfy Ed
reviews.title: Huge Night Market with lots to see and eat!
reviews.content: Unlike it's counterpart the famous Ben Thanh Market in Ho Chi Minh City, this night market only operates from Friday to Sunday nights with the former everyday. But in terms of size and magnitude, this is a much bigger and long, stretching over 4 streets in perpendicular direction, that could add up to about 1~1.5 km.In the day time, the place was congested with motorbikes and cars but at night when the market started, it was flooded with lots of people, especially tourists. And so it's no doubt a touristy market.As one walks along, you will notice that most stalls were selling similar items, such as fashion clothings and bags, shoes, electronic and mobile items, toys etc, of course also street food. After a while, it's just like "repetition" everywhere with the same things on sale and the only different is that of the "prices", some selling higher and some lower prices. (But who knows they maybe from the same bosses as that was what some people told us). You may get tired of it.But it's a good place to indulge into the local culture and lifestyle of the people. We ended up buying some clothings and bags and our shopping spree ended slightly an hour and a half, which we spent quite some time in pushing our way through the crowd! :)As mentioned earlier, the place was very crowed with people walking in all directions, not to mention the oncoming motorbikes, despite the fact that the area has closed for all vehicles. And as a reviewer who posted earlier, when there are many people, there is an opportunity of crime like pick pocketing. However, to be fair, such crime does happen to any other city in the world and not only in Vietnam and so cannot condemn the city for it. Even in Paris, London, Brussels, Prague and Budapest, just to name a few, such act of crime is very common and evident.Well, it is personal responsibility to ensure that your personal belongings are well taken care of. In my so many visits to Vietnam in the last 4 years (more than 6 times), I had never experienced such thing or even scamming or cheating cases, which many travel reviewers have warned about when in Vietnam.Also, always be careful, keep a low profile (not wearing expensive things or carrying bag or even clothings) and avoid putting all the cash/cards in one place, and preparing small notes that will be easier to use, you should be safe!

reviews.author: Steve R
reviews.title: Beware !!
reviews.content: We went to the markets at about 8.30pm on a Friday night. Although the markets are Ok in terms of the shops and stalls, the issue here is crime. We were warned by our hotel to be careful of pick-pockets but I guess because we'd had only positive experiences in our 2 weeks in Vietnam so far and complacency, we thought they may be a little over cautious. Well, we were wrong. It happened so fast. The markets are very congested with people making it easy for pick-pockets, who are obviously very good at what they do.So some tips: 1... NEVER carry your wallet in your back pocket. Always use a secure carry bag around your body or neck, carried in front of you and zipped up closed.2... Only carry CASH, enough that you think you will need for the night. Keep your credit cards and other cash at your hotel - safe.3.. NEVER carry your PASSPORT unless absolutely neccessary. Keep it safe at your hotel4... PHONES are also a big target. When we were at the local police station reporting the crime, there was a steady stream of people coming in, reporting their phone had been pick-pocketed and in some cases, snatched from their hands by a thief on a motorbike.

reviews.author: fizzy1991
reviews.title: Same thing everywhere you look but it's an experience
reviews.content: It is all the same tacky stuff, especially those awful banana shirts made out of cheap rayon fabric that sticks to you in the heat.  I guess if you have never been to a night market you should go but keep your money in your wallet and spend it on quality items in the light of day.

reviews.author: BC
reviews.title: Good Market
reviews.content: Lots of stalls here, all selling many different things, from bags to banana emblazoned shirts, to food. An eclectic mix, which was great to look around.

reviews.author: Seri L
reviews.title: Lot of eateries and fun shopping.
reviews.content: We stayed in Ha noi on friday and saturday so were able to visit the market for two night in a row. What a fun and interesting place to be. Wish they have it every night!! We will be back again in September and will certainly arrange to spend a week end there.

reviews.author: ozvpm_andy
reviews.title: Huge but a little bland
reviews.content: The night markets seems to stretch on for miles - but sadly, they are just stall after stall of the same old cheap bits and pieces. However, its still a nice atmosphere and something easy and cheap to do after dark in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Barb C
reviews.title: Worth a visit to get a taste of local culture
reviews.content: As others have said, it’s not a great place to shop compared to other markets throughout the world. We enjoyed a Friday night out on the town just to see the Vietnamese enjoying themselves at local pubs and restaurants.

reviews.author: roam review
reviews.title: Go hungry and curious
reviews.content: The market was just bustling and literally up our street! The smells are amazing ( some are not) and the variety of food, clothes, bags, trainers and sunglasses will  keep you absorbed for hours. Some stalls are more open to haggling then others but I managed to sniff out a good few bargains, as soon as I got hot from all the rummaging we tried some of the liquid nitrogen sweets, they were odd but refreshing, definatly a new experience.

reviews.author: Aimee H
reviews.title: Crazy and worth a visit
reviews.content: The night market is a must in Hanoi - it is vast and at times we felt we didn't know where it was going to end! It's a bustling market with lots to buy, and lots of haggling to be done. Great for getting presents to bring home as well. Really fun.

reviews.author: Dianne S
reviews.title: Night Market
reviews.content: The Night market in Hanoi  was right outside our Hotel very busy and colourful lots of food selling and people.   Great for shopping.

reviews.author: Jalal Iqbal
reviews.title: nice market in the old town
reviews.content: i enjoyed the night market very much. a lot of nice small colourful shops. liked the festive environment. honestly price was a bit high. it was a pleasant experience to walk and see those shops.

reviews.author: Steve G
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: If you enjoy markets this is a good experience drifting along a whole street opened up with stalls of clothing, shoes, sunglasses, watches etc. My wife and I traveled with our two adult children and both had a great time finding all sorts of objects to buy!

reviews.author: kpiddy
reviews.title: Combining markets in crazy busy streets
reviews.content: I am not a keen shopper or one to bargain and found no pleasure in the night markets in Hanoi.  The market stalls are set up beside the busy chaotic traffic and with shoppers passing by, the better times to shop would be on Friday to Sunday nights when the streets around Hoan Kiem Lake are vehicle free.  The stores sell clothing, luggage, handbags, souvenirs, toys and a whole lot more.

reviews.author: debbieferr
reviews.title: Weekend night Market
reviews.content: The night Market was OK, a mix of cheap clothes, toys, souvenirs, jewellery, fruit and street food.I liked the fact that the roads around the market and lake were closed so everyone could be in the roads safely. Children played and adults were sitting and relaxing.

reviews.author: 944michelem
reviews.title: Overwhelming
reviews.content: We went to this market and we were a little disappointed. After being at street markets in Thailand and Peru, it was too many cheap knockoffs, clothes,shoes, glasses and bags! It wasn’t what we were expecting or hoping for. No local products available. Lots of food stalls and cheap beer everywhere and watch out for the motorbikes!

reviews.author: Dawn H
reviews.title: Great for Shopaholics
reviews.content: The street has so many stalls - it goes on forever. Some close up by around 10pm.  Fantastic atmosphere.

reviews.author: Vivien
reviews.title: Crowded
reviews.content: It was quite crowded, and it was also raining when I was there, which made our trip to the night market less pleasant. There are a lot of shops and stalls by the road, but the prices are not like SUPER cheap, and I was expecting the place to have more night market food! I didn’t end up buying anything since it was not like really cheap compared to purchasing from an actual store and the items were not extremely attractive. But, I believe it’s nice to take a walk if you have nothing to do haha! I don’t think its necessarily a MUST go tourist spot, but I guess its a nice place to have a taste of the local Vietnamese culture. The streets were quite long and it is located next to the Bia Hoi Corner so you could go there and have a drink after walking the night market.

reviews.author: Phuketwergoing
reviews.title: Now this was fun. CHEAP CHEAP BIA HOI
reviews.content: Lots of stalls selling everything.  We got beer for around 50cents (AUD) a glass.Cold refreshing.....fantastic.Loved sitting on the little stools in the street watching people walk buy.Go.

reviews.author: dejara
reviews.title: Bargain Paradise
reviews.content: Hanoi's Night Market is a nice place to buy all kind of souvenirs,clothing, shoes, T Shirts, electronics, cameras,headphones, glasses,jewelry and many items at bargain prices. Be aware that some electronics are not originals. I purchased a Bose headphone for $15 US dollars. It sells for over $150 in US. I found out later that it was a copy made in Pakistan, The  market is open only on week ends, ,

reviews.author: Emilygg
reviews.title: Funny
reviews.content: Had a fun time there shopping and eating. Busy but interesting. Found something cheap for kids back home.

reviews.author: Safemach
reviews.title: Loved it but not for the shopping
reviews.content: Amazing to see so many people having so much fun. I have no interest in buying stuff except the occasional mango in a bag, but I have never seen a city have so much fun with itself. Dancing, playing, fire eaters all sorts. Families, couples and everyone just enjoying themselves, great to see.Not for one second did I worry about my pockets or safety. Not a policeman in sight. Ok the guys pimping their neighbors daughter gets a bit annoying but they don’t pester.

reviews.author: sandymSeasister
reviews.title: A fun and vibey place
reviews.content: The weekend Market in the Old Quarter of Hanoi with a stroll around the lake, dinner at one of the many restaurants or coffee and ice cream at a pavement cafe is worth the time.  It’s fun and vibey and although I didn’t think prices were much better than you can barter for in the shops at the night market, it’s the ambience, the people-watching and the overall experience.  We actually stayed away from bargain hunting and rather watched street artists performing dance and music pieces, had a portrait done and were generally thoroughly entertained by the vibe strolling around the lake.

reviews.author: Robert M
reviews.title: Counterfeit Chinese tat.
reviews.content: This famous market thrives on selling counterfeit everything. Clothing, shoes, bags and top end electronic goods. Buy with humour, not with the view that you've bought a genuine bit of kit.The market is impressive though, taking up several streets, no stress busy atmosphere.We liked it, but we've seen enough fakes in our 3 week tour of Vietnam.

reviews.author: sally l
reviews.title: Plenty to see if you like markets
reviews.content: Markets aren’t really my thing. We went through the market on our way to a restaurant. It’s very busy with lots of stalls. Everything imaginable is on sale. In my opinion a lot of it isn’t particularly good but it’s horses for courses.

reviews.author: gordonj258
reviews.title: Sprawling market
reviews.content: The night market occupies many streets that have been closed to traffic. I found lots of things there that were cheap but also found that the stallholders were not prepared to really haggle as the base price is already exceptionally low.There are plenty of clothes, food and all the usual "souvenir" trinkets that you would expect. Very busy and an interesting way to spend a couple of hours.

reviews.author: Hardvision
reviews.title: Great bargains!
reviews.content: If you can accept that even if it says Abercombie & Fitch or Nike or Adidas, it is not the original and can bargain like crazy, this is the place. First of all the prices in local currency are crazy. Drop the last 3 zeros and divide by 23. That gives you the USD price. STart at about 20% of that price. In most of the places you can bargain and get the stuff for about 30% of the originally quoted price. Don't expect too much of quality. Quality does not come that cheap. The experience is worth it though. In the entire complex we saw only one shop which refused to lower the price and it was the most unusual of the shops over there.

reviews.author: Heng How N
reviews.title: Special market
reviews.content: The market starts at 7pm and block traffic from using it. The place is converted to be place for many activities. It covers a big area from Hoan Kiem Lake towards the railway track.

reviews.author: Mark M
reviews.title: Haggle
reviews.content: At the weekend this street is closed off to traffic and stalls selling all kinds of merchandise are set up.We spent a good hour wandering the length of the market.Haggling is an absolute must. Offer 50% of the asking price to start the negotiations!

reviews.author: Rachael H
reviews.title: Busy, busy, busy
reviews.content: Really nice markets with lost of variety. There are both fake items and original items such as paintings. you are able to barter with the sellers to get more reasonable prices, really interesting place to visit

reviews.author: Traveller
reviews.title: Night market
reviews.content: The night market in Hanoi is only on the weekend, Friday - Sunday, 7pm-11pm.It’s one long strip of stalls in the middle of the road selling various things. One of the best things to experience in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Edge Mirafuentes
reviews.title: Amazing food & Shopping
reviews.content: Open only on weekends from 7-10pm. This place is full of AMAZING food, entertainment & fun cheap haggle shopping!

reviews.author: carloscharmy
reviews.title: Just another SEA market
reviews.content: Coming from BKK I found nothing appealing in this market. Walked around it for 10 minutes and left. If  it is your 1st time in SEA give it a go.

reviews.author: Becky & James
reviews.title: Typical Asian Night Market
reviews.content: I personally love the hustle and bustle of these markets - with the added fun of true Vietnamese bartering. Start bidding at 50% less than they ask for, and you can normally complete with a discount of about 30-40% off their price. Enjoy the bars and the old city gate whole you're in the vicinity.

reviews.author: b0rn2sh0p
reviews.title: Place for a bargain.
reviews.content: If you need cheap inflight carrier urgently, night market is the place for you. BigC market is twice more expensive than night market when it comes to carriers.

reviews.author: iliketomoveandsee
reviews.title: Rubbish Market
reviews.content: I've been to many markets while travelling around Asia, and this was one of the worse. Crowded, scooters/motorbikes still riding down at speed even though the road is closed. The produce also isn't that great on the market - I wouldn't waste your time, to be honest.

reviews.author: Bazza_752
reviews.title: Oversized china mall
reviews.content: Night market was essentially an oversized china mall... nice to see different environment - Lots of fake goods and knock-offs. I am not a fan of fake goods if you cannot afford the real item don’t buy a fake.

reviews.author: jongyungchoi99
reviews.title: nice
reviews.content: its long and having many gifts you can buy for your trip. and they are so cheap.you should see price which they write on paper and pay

reviews.author: fluffymonkey
reviews.title: Sunday family vibe
reviews.content: We visited the market on the Sunday evening, it was extremely busy so hold onto your kids if you have them! What really caught our eye though was the shear number of local families out with children enjoying a Sunday stroll and play around the top end of Hoam Kiem Lake. It was such an intoxicating atmosphere with kids playing the national sport (da cau), it involved kicking a weighted shuttlecock with feathers! and toddlers taking remote control cars for a spin (or rather the parents were controlling them!). Fascinating experience to see how Vietnamese go about their daily lives.

reviews.author: Rui Jian Ng
reviews.title: Avoid Saturdays and go to shops with prices
reviews.content: Saturdays are very packed. If possible, head there on other days like Fri or Sun. Hectic place where you can get cheap clothes, shoes etc. Remember to bargain if possible but I reckon these days the vendors have placed their “best price” and hard to bargain down further. Word of advice: go for stalls with prices shown so you’ll at least have a benchmark and how to bargain. F&B: apart from the deep fried skewers, the sugarcane drink with lime is nice.

reviews.author: webb s
reviews.title: Fun & crazy!
reviews.content: We were here on Sunday night. It was very crowded but exactly how I want it. There were many things to buy and many food joints to have some midnight snack. You might want a Vietnamese to accompany you or know enough language to get a raw deal. Still, everything is dirt cheap without a bargain. And the food is incredible as well.

reviews.author: Siok H
reviews.title: Just feel the vibe
reviews.content: I went there to just feel the vibe but really got no patience to walk around with two young kids under my arm.  Goods are not interesting.

reviews.author: scubacol11
reviews.title: Shopping fun hustle and bustle
reviews.content: The market is open 19.00 to 23.00 Friday to Sunday nights,they close off several streets in the old town directly north of the lake so easy to find.The stalls are set up down the middle of the road in a back to back lay out so it is best to walk up one side then back down the other then you can look at the market stall and also the shop there too.My tip would be to walk all the way up and down first and get an idea of whats on sale and how many similar stalls and shops are selling the goods you may be interested in before you start shopping and haggling,a lot of the stalls are just extensions of the shops they are outside off and if they don"t have the exact item you want they will go to the shop and try to find it.Many of the stall are selling the usual fake designer goods but as long as you expect this you know they can"t be genuine by the low prices they are willing to sell them at,that said if you haggle you can get some bargains in clothes,shoes,artwork,ceramics,hiking wear and many souvenirs.There are many food stalls spread throughout the market so you can always get a snack if you are hungry but on some of the streets that adjoin the main avenue they are set out with many food and beer shops and there is a great atmosphere with plenty of choice of where to eat and drink and plenty of music to listen to.I found some prices far cheaper on the market than in the shops during the day as there was so much competition the vendors were willing to be haggled down more,Great fun if you enjoy the thrill of the haggling chase as I do,I see it as a participation sport and great fun and the stall and shop owners are not aggressive at all.Many people warn you to be careful with your wallets,but that"s the same anywhere in a market like this.

reviews.author: joanne h
reviews.title: your best option for a market
reviews.content: all the markets are now aimed a tourists, but this was the best out of all of them. If you are travelling in vietman Hanoi is much much cheaper than HO Chi Minh. They are not as aggressive at haggling as other Asian countries, its more like a reduction in price than a full blown haggle. We went at 8pm, still too early stalls just setting up.

reviews.author: MMvet
reviews.title: Night markets
reviews.content: The usual hassle and bustle of markets.  Keep you wits about you and your valuables.  What was on offer can be purchased at any other market. We were fully prepared to barter but the sellers weren’t that interested in bartering, the would only knock a few dollars off the price or not at all, regardless of how much you may buy.

reviews.author: Kalie L
reviews.title: Bit of bartering fun
reviews.content: Be prepared for banana shirts and matching shorts. All a bit of fun, we had a few beers on bir corner then went for a look. Quite good quality clothing, the usual bits and bobs like all markets. People were lovely. Watch your bag and keep it to the front of you, even the locals remind you....

reviews.author: antnChris
reviews.title: market okay but visit the lake as place is pumping
reviews.content: we visited night market Sunday night.they close off streets from 6.the markets nothing flash but we wandered down to lake where we saw amazing lights,  musicians , entertainment the kids out on the remote controlled cop cars tanks and diggers.great atmosphere and a wonderful walk.

reviews.author: Bhat P T
reviews.title: a nice experience
reviews.content: I was alone and could wander all the places  just out of curiosity. Since I don't eat meat or any non-veg items, I did not get a chance to enjoy street food. But I had nice cut fruits and sugarcane juice with a lot of ice. I could not resist the temptation, though worried about the quality and effect on my stomach.There are plenty of shops mostly selling cheap Chinese items. But I found a  few shops where they have put " Made in Vietnam" board and some stuff especially cloth for kids were good. Over all nice place to kill time. Loud music from Bars all over, people sitting on red plastic stools  and enjoying their drink and food. Not recommended for family. Couple is ok.

reviews.author: Alice M
reviews.title: Very hectic
reviews.content: The atmosphere of this place was very hectic. There were tons of shops and stalls selling fake brand clothing and shoes, as well as jewelry and some cheap, touristy clothes, like fruit shirts and elephant pants. Most of the places were pretty much the same, and just about everything was cheap and tacky. I didn't buy much because the clothing wasn't good quality and I was concerned about the origins of those clothes, I imagine their production involves a lot of underpaid, badly treated, overworked workers, potentially even slavery.

reviews.author: wanderlust_rambler
reviews.title: Just like any other night market in SEA
reviews.content: Market street is quite long but in the end hey all sell similar stuff. It gets very hot and humid fast and you walk along in the crowd. Full of tourists but not many items that interested us.Found that the shops nearby sold better quality goods. Don’t forget to haggle.

reviews.author: Isabella B
reviews.title: Horror behind the facade of cheap goods
reviews.content: My partner and I went to the market and warn families not to come here.Behind the facade of glimmering lights and cheap goods is a horrific image. We witnessed a disfigured woman (not born with those disfigurements) crawling on her hands ( of which had been taken off so were just stumps) and knees attached like a dog on a leash to a pram full of heavy items, pushing a weighed down bucket with her head. A toddler was tied to her side. This woman crawled the whole length of the market on her bare skin. meanwhile we noticed shady looking men watching her on motorbikes, we assume to ensure nobody interfered. This is one of the most horrific sights I have seen in my life. Be warned this is not a sight for children and I’m horrified at what we saw. Absolutely terrible I cannot imagine the horrible life of this women, her fate is one which I don’t believe uncommon. Please be careful

reviews.author: Anne C
reviews.title: Go for the food, not the goods.
reviews.content: It was very crowded and the goods for sale are made in china, not vietnam. this place is not for tourists if you want to buy souvenirs. But the FOOD is excellent. street food everywhere. i would go here for  the food, not the goods.

reviews.author: Michelle Juul
reviews.title: Something you have to try
reviews.content: Nice to experience; a bit hectic and very busy. However, you don't spend alot of money, because you get "full" very fast.

reviews.author: Derek L
reviews.title: Nightly market visit
reviews.content: They block the roads off to cars, there are only a few scooters allowed through as well. Overall there was a lot of souvenirs to buy from here. It started to rain a little so bring an umbrella because there is little coverage. Everything from rings, shoes, food, clothes and knickknacks.

reviews.author: Matt_SE1
reviews.title: Not very interesting
reviews.content: If you need cheap trainers or knock-off Adidas t-shirts, you'll have a thousand to choose from. Otherwise it's plastic knick-knacks and phone covers. No street food you can't find in abundance everywhere else in the city. Don't make a special journey for this.

reviews.author: alimac987
reviews.title: It’s all there, at reasonable prices.
reviews.content: We were able to buy everything we wanted in the space of an hour: branded shoes, banana shirts, silk scarves (but not the Ha-noi t-shirt I found the next day).

reviews.author: Iryna
reviews.title: A long long street
reviews.content: Takes place Friday and Saturday nights. Lots of locals and tourists. Everything is for sale and everything is to be bargained for. People seem to walk up the right side of the street and return on the other side.

reviews.author: Monika A
reviews.title: Not worth your time
reviews.content: This night market is very basic, full with cheap cheap clothes, bags and accessories which you can find even better looking in the shops in the Old Quarter every day. It’s quite crowded and very hot. I love the night markets in Thailand but this one is noting similar

reviews.author: Mathewsense
reviews.title: So crowded
reviews.content: We visited here to know more about Vietnamese culture. However, it was so busy. There are various goods which was sold here: clothes, souvenirs, shoes...

reviews.author: Sarze-J
reviews.title: Buzzing markets
reviews.content: We spent around 6 hrs browsing the markets, the streets are closed off to the traffic. Very busy, huge variety including the usual clothes, shoes, wallets, sunglasses, art and street food everywhere. At the lake end there is music, dancing, hover boards and remote control cars/trucks for the kids. Fun atmosphere!

reviews.author: Annette A
reviews.title: Great night out browsing & buying
reviews.content: Enjoyed wandering through the night markets taking in the lights, ambience & the many colourful lanterns of this area. Safe, crowded,  but lots of fun to be looking and seeing how the goods are displayed & how the people try to sell their wares. Many similar stalls & shops,  but characters who try to sell them all different. A few hours well spent. Highly recommended as a few hours entertainment & shopping.

reviews.author: Mario230569
reviews.title: cheap price
reviews.content: very colorfull street night market. Anything can be found here from made in china stuffs to handcraft items. Highly reccomended if are in Hanoy

reviews.author: Rachel P
reviews.title: Worth going for the experience
reviews.content: There are many similar stalls but there is still quite a range of goods and bargains can be had by haggling with the stall holders.  We bought a handbag, T-shirt and speakers and food from some of the many food stalls.  It was very busy but we did not feel worried at all.  It is worth going for the experience if not the bargains.

reviews.author: Mike D
reviews.title: The worst of all the night markets that I have been to!
reviews.content: I have been to night markets in Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Singapore, and Taiwan and this is the first night market that I have disliked. It was mostly filled with row after row of the same old junk, it's a big night market but if you go down one small section you will see everything that the whole market has to offer.There may be a couple of useful items here but it's nothing that you can't find at any time at any of the small shops throughout the Old Quarter.To top it all off the aisles are very narrow and even if you do find something that you want to take a look at a motorbike will come up behind you honking it's horn to make you get out of the way!Why they let motorbikes run through here during the night market is beyond me, all in all the worst experience that I have had at the literally dozens of night markets that I have been to throughout Southeast Asia.Do yourself a favor and skip this one and do something that will be more enjoyable.

reviews.author: Chloe_Nguyen83
reviews.title: crowed night market
reviews.content: Although it's easy to notice that it's very crowed but it also represent Hanoi's culture. which is perfect for those who want to explore Vietnam'culture. I got there in a cool day with my boyfriend and my guide. It's taken place on walking street and consist of hundred small traders with diversity of goods such as clothes, souvenirs, handicrafts and foods. Moreover, Vietnam's traditional foods is very good with reasonable price. However, don't afraid to bargain price or asking questions to seller about price of each item. Thanks to Sunfer (my cute guide), i saved money for my journey.

reviews.author: Sumit C
reviews.title: Night market in Hanoi
reviews.content: Another Night market as it is everywhere in asia and asian regions all across. But this one is better  with wider choices and lots of bargaining. Surprisingly  the clothes( t shirts and shorts)  for daily wear are little better than some of the available in Vietnam. Plus  you never know when can you get a good bargain.  Huge crowded places  with almost half a kilometer and starts from the lake side to the other end.   Other shops also nearby for all needs.   not to mention if your feet hurt,  lots of foot massages nearby area. overall nice experience,  if you in Hanoi,  its makes sense to be there once.

reviews.author: Jamshid A
reviews.title: Nothing interesting
reviews.content: Just simple night market, nothing interesting. Some products are produced in Vietnam. There is some choice of souvenirs. Nearby many interesting places.

reviews.author: Benny O
reviews.title: Normal night market
reviews.content: It was raining when we got there, most of the stalls are selling pretty similar items. Not many stalls are selling food. Recommend to go there after dinner.

reviews.author: Lee_family_219053
reviews.title: Best street shopping to be at for all your needs
reviews.content: We were in Hanoi for 3 nights and every night walked the night market, come rain or dry. The streets will be closed to traffic yet the occasional motorbikes will compete for space with shoppers. Very interesting as each night we will find new shops and new things on sale. Prices are more fixed and bargaining seem to be a thing of the past as most shops will not budge from their asking prices nor chase you back for the sale after you walk away. Yes, their price may seem low but as we were told to bargain we felt we did not get a good sale. One can find cheap clothing, shoes, food, dessert and accessories. Items made in Vietnam are cheaper than those from China, like ladies cloth. Otherwise not to be missed. Start from Hoan Kiem Lake and it winds all the way to Dong Xuan market. We were unlucky as Night 2 heavy downpour washed out the night market as they closed shortly after opening and Night 3 they endured the rain so as not to miss the Sunday night business after the previous night's early close.

reviews.author: KNewms
reviews.title: Better than some other night markets in Vietnam
reviews.content: Markets in general have been a bit of a let down in Vietnam for me (having visited other markets in Asia). Don't expect variety or good quality! But we really enjoyed walking around the lake and watching what was going on there - dancing, kids playing games etc.

reviews.author: fiyerol
reviews.title: The street with the market stalls is ok but it's walking around the lake at night that's fun.
reviews.content: We went on a Sunday night. Main streets are closed and markets are set up. A lot of people come but it doesn't feel uncomfortably crowded. Street performers/artists, street food, people playing games, children riding tiny cars, a lot of dogs on and off lead (even a cat)! The main street with the market stalls are same-ish after a while with stalls selling the same stuff. I wouldn't go for the shopping but all the none shopping stuff that's interesting. Northern part of the lake has roads close, and also around the lake is where it's best to people watch and be immersed in a great cultural experience. Only open on weekends.

reviews.author: Peter V
reviews.title: Looking for a bargain....look here!
reviews.content: If you're looking to spend some money and do a bunch of shopping I would suggest doing it at this market as opposed to the one in Ho Chi Minh city.  I found the prices here to be much much better than at the other market.There's so much on offer.  A lot is similar to what you'll see around Vietnam but great for the atmosphere and to just wander around.  There are quite a few stalls (went for a few blocks along the same street) so there's plenty for you to look at.  Of course, being that there are so many stalls gives you some bargaining power if you're into that.Once you've had your fill of shopping and stalls it's nice to be able to head back towards the lake and into the street life of buskers, kids playing and drinking places.Just a few things: 1. Make sure your money and other goods and secured away in a zippered pocket or locked backpack as there are a lot of people walking along the market stalls and they have some very talented pickpockets among them .  2. Don't accept free puff balls/doughnut balls as they are not free.  As soon as you have one they'll hassle you for money (saw this happen to a fellow traveler).  3.  By all means be ridden around by one of the Cyclo's but you shouldn't pay more than 100,000 to 150,000.Now........enjoy!

reviews.author: tjm956
reviews.title: Be careful of women selling doughnut balls!!
reviews.content: Went to the night market with my partner after dinner. Was definitely worth a look and even brought a couple of items for a good price! Have to say night was ruined when i got forced into buying a doughnut puff off these women in a group of 4-5 after they said i could "try" one. They hasseled the hell out of me! And when i went to give them 20,000 for some puff balls, one grabed a 500,000 note out of my wallet and quickly put in her wallet while the others were distracting me and my partner. When i accused her she pulled out a 20,000 note and told me i was stupid! All of them then began to push me to make me go away. Be careful!

reviews.author: Hazel D
reviews.title: Brings out the shopaholic in you
reviews.content: Variety of things from clothes to shoes to bags to jewellery, souvenirs and food on sale. Not as great as it is hyped. Hardly found any branded/ seconds stuff. Make sure you and your group have enough energy to walk the entire stretch as it could be very tiring after a whole day of activities. With our 6 year old we had to keep looking for some chair every now then for her to sit and relax.

reviews.author: JLM3080
reviews.title: worth a look
reviews.content: worth a look, not as seedy as many in Asia, some good stalls with reasonable gear, but be careful if you buy, you need to make sure you know what you are buying. Also take care for pick pockets, worth an hour to browse but don't take it too seriously

reviews.author: Jeff L
reviews.title: Market worth a look
reviews.content: This is a market that starts after dark and then comes alive. Some of the stalls barter but a lot don’t so I would suggest you take your time and walk away if you don’t think you are getting value. It is a lot of fun with lots of stalls and a good amount of street food. If you want to make a night of it go after 8.00pm as that’s when the things spark up.

reviews.author: livk7
reviews.title: I wouldn’t recommend coming here
reviews.content: They don’t really barter at all and if they do it’s only a very small amount not like in Hoi an and Ho Chi Minh, lots of the vendors seem in a really bad mood even when asking to see something. I have never actually had a bad experience at a market and I’ve been to them all over the world, Hong Kong, Singapore , Vanuatu, etc.  It’s lots of the same stuff over and over again and I know it’s a market but if you’ve been there you’d get what I mean. It’s actually expensive compared to other markets and with virtually no haggling.

reviews.author: Kishor P
reviews.title: A bit of Fun but Really for the Locals
reviews.content: This is probably similar to a number of other markets that you find in far flung places such as these but each seems to have something of its own personality so it is worth a visit even if it is a quick one. Night markets are usually atmospheric and this one is no exception. It is a good experience to walk through and soak it all up. There are plenty of stalls selling all manner of things from fruit & veg to jewelery and clothes. Things are generally cheap but in all probability not the real deal if you want to buy branded goods. There is not much margin if you think you can haggle yourself a bargain as the goods are low priced in the first place. An hour or so was enough for me to think that I was glad I had visited.

reviews.author: RalphdaSilva
reviews.title: Amazing Atmosphere!
reviews.content: Starts every Friday evening after the roads are blocked and traffic is diverted for this weekly affair...Hundreds of shopping stalls back to back for miles on end...most of the stalls have repeat items on sale. From fake Rolexes to Tissots to Omegas all under $20 to other branded (probably rip-off) merchandise to selfie sticks...if you're into street shopping and haggling, this is for you!The overall environment is lively, energetic and fun!

reviews.author: landth
reviews.title: The merchandise isn't the highlight
reviews.content: The stalls sell various fare aimed at both locals and tourists, nothing startling but at good prices.Ignore the BS about offering 25% and working up to 50%, that may be how they used to do it, but the prices are so low that you'll be lucky to get 10% off much, and tbh you'd be being a cheapie, the prices are very fair.The highlight though is the entertainment in the open areas at the Southern end of the markets.

reviews.author: BellasWings
reviews.title: Super fuf
reviews.content: If youve been to Thai Night markets then this might be just your Thing. Though slightly less quirky and "fun" than ist Thai sisters but still absolutely worth going to if you lost or left any essentials. Otherwise just Hang out on top of a cafe and enjoy the commotion on the street below whilst sipping a delish egg coffee.Ist a Long road up and down and you can easily spend a couple of hours in and around the market. We siply People watched and made sure we get some great pics to Show our friends and Family at home!

reviews.author: Ido C
reviews.title: 4 points for the atmosphere
reviews.content: Night market Friday-Sunday, the area is closed and finally there are no motorbikes and cars that rushing the street.Few live music points, happy feelings around, the market is very busy, i didn't had actually something to buy (especially shows to my "big" size 45-46).Be there at least for 1 night, it's a must.

reviews.author: B1E9A8R2
reviews.title: Hanoi night market
reviews.content: If you’re looking for larger sizes (western large or above) then you’re out of luck, but there’s few places in the market willing to barter on prices (you’re better off in Hoi-An or Saigon markets). Despite the negatives the night market is a must, the sights, sounds & smells are all part of the Hanoi experience!

reviews.author: Litigious L
reviews.title: Fun!
reviews.content: The market gets going around 7pm or a little later so don’t get there before then, ur favourite thing about the market was the food. We stopped a few nights for street meat which was excellent and very cheap!

reviews.author: aimacarmela
reviews.title: An assault of the senses
reviews.content: Prepared to have your senses engaged. We came on a weekend during summer season. There were a deluge of people, locals and tourists alike. Be prepared to haggle. Also most shops sell similar items, so be prepared to go around to look for something different or unique

reviews.author: Katherine R
reviews.title: Fun walk
reviews.content: Yes this market is full of the same things you see at most markets but it’s fun. It’s lively and loud and full of street food and it’s a great way to while away a couple of hours on a nice warm evening. The market gets going around 7pm or a little later so don’t get there before then. The streets are blocked off to cars but you will get some scooters travelling through which can be annoying. The local shop owners have their shops open too so you have a multitude of choice - haggle and enjoy.

reviews.author: Yas
reviews.title: Drop by!
reviews.content: Night market is held from Friday till Sunday night. It has a lovely atmosphere and you can consider to stop by if you are in the area. I bought some souvenirs at a very good rate.

reviews.author: ekta1
reviews.title: shopaholic
reviews.content: The market has so much to offer.you will find everything here and that to great quality. just u have to bargain up to the t nd remember take enough of dong 'Vietnam local currency'.They don't accept cards though some shops accept dollars. Must visit if u want things at a very cheap prices.

reviews.author: ahs4y
reviews.title: More knock-off stuff
reviews.content: While there are some quaint things to see and buy, a lot of it seems like knock-off. Could be factory excess stuff of the major brands, but the regular shops and cafes and restaurants are more worthy of a visit than the night market.

reviews.author: 2footprint
reviews.title: Crowded and vibrant night market
reviews.content: Night market started after 7pm and can be very crowded with tourists and locals. Only few stalls selling niche product such as hand made pouches and bags. The rest are selling the same things such as shirts, jackets, sports shoes and handbags. 99.99% branded goods sold there are fakes. The market is a must visit night market in Hanoi.

reviews.author: CK S
reviews.title: Busy weekend market!
reviews.content: The Hanoi Night Market runs Fri - Sat - Sun beginning at 7:00 pm and it is massive. It is blocks and blocks long filled with all kinds of vendors! You can buy everything from watches to electronics to clothes from one of the hundreds of booths lining the street. Our favourite thing about the market was the food. We stopped a few nights for street meat which was excellent and very cheap! They also have a number of sit down food stalls near the end of the market as well as folk performances running.

reviews.author: Ivča I
reviews.title: Friday huge market
reviews.content: I was shocked, how a huge area was closed for the market. We had a good time there, lots of tasteful street food and enjoying the atmosphere - local people were happy to be together if they were not selling their staff.

reviews.author: Amartya C
reviews.title: Vibrant environment ... Do bargaining before shopping ...
reviews.content: I will not say, it is the shopper's paradise, but the concept of closing all cars/public vehicle on the road and open the whole place for night market is just awesome. The environment is so vibrant, people are dancing with music on the road and lot of people are showing their different talent on the road.     It is situated near the Hoàn Kiếm Lake. Yes, you need to know bargaining, before you want to buy anything. Shops are roadside, nothing very high-fly sort of shop. Safety wise, police are around every corner of the place to get them down.

reviews.author: XPLORING
reviews.title: Rough
reviews.content: Not too impressed by this market . A lot of clothing vendors . Vendors are rude and goods are overpriced and poor quality. Street food galore. Over crowded with people pushing . Pick pockets galore so hold on to your belongings and take only what’s needed.

reviews.author: Melissa A
reviews.title: Lots of vendors
reviews.content: This was a good market with lots of vendors. I‎t was more focused towards fake designers rather than homemade products. I‎t was a good time though, and they shot off surrounding streets by the water which lends for a nice view at the end.

reviews.author: purplekitty2016
reviews.title: Shopping Galore
reviews.content: If you enjoy shopping then the night market is a place to be in Hanoi on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday night between 7-11 pm. Easily spot able opposite the street in front of the fountain opposite the Aldo showroom. First of all be very, very, very careful with ur belongings. I got totally saved. On my very first night we headed for the night market n when I returned I saw a huge sharp cut on my bag.  It could immediately be seen that it was cut with a very sharp knife. Luckily inside this bag was my backpack purse which they could not get through though they did try coz there was a small cut in that too similar to the one in the outer one but they faced a hurdle as the place where they cut in the inside purse had one more pocket which they could not penetrate!!! And imagine all this happened without even an inkling at my end & even when I was being cautious😰 So plz don't underestimate them. Yes there is tons to shop at the night market from clothes to shoes to bags to craft items etc etc but make sure you bargain like crazy.  Start initially just by enquiring the price n bargaining n once u get a knack of it then bargain n buy. The market is quite long so be prepared for a long walk.

reviews.author: PKKL
reviews.title: Too crowded and too much traffic. Will say so-so
reviews.content: Ok for those keen on night market adventure but really it's scary with the bikes zooming all over the night market . Do take of your belonging . We left after a few minutes of walking as we felt there was nothing interesting there that we could not find  in their more  organized day markets

reviews.author: varun c
reviews.title: More than just a market
reviews.content: Remember its open only on Weekends (Fri-Sun) from 7 PM. An amazing time where the entire street turns into a market with everything you could possible think of buying. The Circle from where the market starts turns into a place with lots of things to do. Entry of Vehicles is restricted to late in the night with People just sitting on the roads, dancing. You should definitely go here and enjoy!

reviews.author: Omaandopa17
reviews.title: Great place to have a wonder.
reviews.content: I have lived in Hanoi of and on for 5 years and although I don’t visit every week I still enjoy it when I do. Lots of the same stuff being sold and can be a little over priced but really worth doing at least once. Beware- watch you hand bag and keep your wallet in your front pocket, just to be safe. Like all markets there are some people who make a living out of pick pocketing. Friday and Saturday nights are the best time to as the lake close by is closed to traffic. There is also plenty of street food and other delicious goodies to tantalise you palate.

reviews.author: Fair_is_Square
reviews.title: Cheap goods, good street food and amazing sugar cane juice!
reviews.content: We had a great time at these markets - a bit cheaper than those in Saigon. The merchandise was a little repetitive  (but that expected) but some great finds. Streets foods everywhere and AMAZING sugarcane for about 10,000VND - must try! One of the best we had all around Vietnam (& other parts of SEA). Beware of the flies in wet season though...

reviews.author: Renella H
reviews.title: very interesting
reviews.content: the night market is held every Friday, Saturday and Sunday.  There are hundreds of vendors there, each with their sale items.  You can find almost anything you need at a bargain price if you are willing to haggle

reviews.author: Iris L.Y
reviews.title: Not a must-see
reviews.content: This weekend night market lacks variety. It has the same stuff over and over again---fake branded clothes, fake branded shoes, phone accessories, and a lot of cheap stuff from China. It is a far cry from the night markets of Bangkok.

reviews.author: Karen
reviews.title: Not so big, boring wares
reviews.content: Was expecting more local crafts and unique souvenirs, but all the stores peddle the same repeated items. Was done in less than an hour. Rather disappointing compared to other night markets in Asia

reviews.author: FrancisCKSeah
reviews.title: Crazy busy weekend
reviews.content: People and more people. Identical to most night market in Asia. You can get almost everything in the market. A lot of fake stuff, cheap food and drinks.

reviews.author: Coryy20
reviews.title: Can't go wrong here
reviews.content: Lots of stalls and open only on weekends. You can get very reasonable souvenirs here and electronics .. Lots of memory banks and headset at bargain pices. Lots of tourist can be seen here shopping at night and lots of haggling taking place. I was very impressed by the items I bought and the prices I got them at when compared to other places where they sell for more money. Go n enjoy

reviews.author: NatCee19
reviews.title: Busy night market
reviews.content: This night market has all the typical tourists souvenirs, fake designer:shoes (Nike, adidas), clothing, bags, sunglasses etc. it’s a pretty big market and is very busy. The market stretches down several blocks. There’s also a lot of food you can buy. The streets are blocked off as a pedestrian area only during this market but some scooters still make it through. Also our hotel warned us of pick picketers here I but we didn’t see any.

reviews.author: calpar22
reviews.title: A very large night market
reviews.content: An enormous range of goods ranging from clothes to electrical and make up. You can pretty much buy anything. Don't be afraid to haggle as a lot of stalls sell the same thing so they want your business.There are extremely cheap deals to be had, t shirts are worth a look I picked up 3 for £3 roughly but you could probably get better, girlfriend picked up urban decay naked 2 make up for £3 worth £40 in U.K.

reviews.author: moshiyana
reviews.title: Depends on your preference
reviews.content: Basically, tourist night markets are the same - same souvenir shirts and items, street food and vibe. The market is open on Friday up to Sunday only. But if you must, a visit cannot harm you.

reviews.author: Kamil B
reviews.title: Go there and negotiate everything you want to buy!
reviews.content: Worth-going, definitely. We stary at the lake and finish at the end of this long street.You can buy something to eat, some sweets, ice-cream, but also fake "adidas" t-shirts or electronics like "JBL"😂Negotiate hardly! You can pay even a hard of a price, trully! Do it always when price isn't written.It starts 19 p.m. and is till midnight or even longer. Go there and buy something whst you don't need at all, it is still ok👌😀

reviews.author: Nunngo
reviews.title: Your enjoyment is dependent on expectation
reviews.content: We loved these markets.  The only expectation we had was that we would have a good time looking around and enjoying the people and culture and the market night life.  We were not after any specific bargains so no disappointments there, but nonetheless enjoyed the options for buying locally made goods and souvenirs.The night market stretch is about 2 kilometres in distance and goes from Hang Dao street to Dong Xuan market.  It aims to promote Vietnamese culture for international tourists and also encourages the younger generations of Vietnamese to remain connected with Vietnamese tradition.   The markets are only open from around 6pm to midnight Friday, Saturday and Sunday.  There are 100's of stalls with traders selling traditional local food, clothing, fashion items, jewellery, household goods, souvenirs and handicrafts. Items are pretty cheap but bargaining is still acceptable and part of the Vietnamese market culture.  The markets are an opportunity to enjoy traditional Vietnamese folk music and local artists display their artistic talent also.  The food available at the market is worth trying also.

reviews.author: MH
reviews.title: Don't bother
reviews.content: Poor quality of the same stuff. The stall holders aren't interested in engaging. Don't waste your time.

reviews.author: Adeline C
reviews.title: Food and people watching
reviews.content: If you've been to street markets, this is similar. It joins with the weekend night market. We ate here two nights in a row. Food is reasonable and tasty. We ordered the fried noodles with beef 50,000 VND and pho beef 25,000 VND. Eager to please and very local atmosphere. (Warning) If you can't accept chicken bones & tissue waste strewn on the floor, then this is not the place for you

reviews.author: Ronny T
reviews.title: It's a place you can go but not necessarily
reviews.content: If you are in Hanoi there is not as much to do in night-time so you go on weekend to the night market because everyone go.You can find there a lot of things you don't need but also the little things you need and you don't know where else to find.It was impressing how fast all the stands were built up and away. One tip don't go there for diner (barbecue ), go around a corner (opposite the great market hall) and you will find the same food in a small Street for nearly nothing compared to the places directly in front of the hall.

reviews.author: Chris D
reviews.title: Shopping and people watching
reviews.content: This multi-block street market offers a bit of everything you must get want to take home from Hanoi. Cold beers and shopping, street food and night life are just a few options you have at the night market. Some stalls can be a bit repetitive, but good deals can be found, bargain hard.

reviews.author: paul r
reviews.title: Fun on a bun
reviews.content: In the cooler night air you can stroll up and down the market for what seems like miles. Forget the fact that many if not most of the stalls are selling the same thing and just enjoy the experience. Along the way stop to buy some street food and then pull up a doll size chair to sit and relax.

reviews.author: John L
reviews.title: Night Market Streets
reviews.content: The night market is opened only on the weekends and it gets EXTREMELY crowded. The vendors sell various merchandise (e.g. shirts, shoes, souvenirs, bracelets, etc). The majority of the stands sell similar items and thus the price range is all similar. We went during mid-July, thus there were sudden random rains that poured for hours, so it would be a wise decision to pack an umbrella or poncho. There is also street food available in the intersections, mainly skewers, snacks, and drinks. We thought it was a pretty decent experience and make sure to keep your bags close due to the possibility of pickpocketing!

reviews.author: GBflysagain
reviews.title: Give it a miss
reviews.content: We normally love night markets. We when twice, both times awful. Unfriendly stall holders who have no idea how to engage there customers. These were the only times in a decade that my daughter has come back from a shopping trip without buying anything. One stall holder even took the items out of my daughters hand and put them back on his table, these were the items until then that she had decided she wanted to buy!! She also wanted to buy shoes, but before they would take about price they wanted to know what size and what color and then what size l was l told the girl l didn't want to buy shoes my daughter did. She then turned her back on us. Much the same happened to another teen. Why did stall owners keep pushing me to buy (fat, once 50 and jaded) and ignore my teenage daughter who wants to buy. Crazy! The normal shops around old town are much better. I was getting annoyed at this stage and remember the girl that sold me a bag saying she thought the last 20000vnd l drove her down was very little for me. If we were having more fun we would have bought much more and l would have been happy to just do a little token bartering.

reviews.author: minimize940314
reviews.title: Busy busy
reviews.content: Night market is packed with so many people all over Hanoi. Local people selling stuff, local people buying stuff, tourists buying and bargaining. It is somewhat chaotic but the market shows a feature of the city itself. Very interesting place. If you want cheap t shirt or something like that you can buy one here. Quality is not guaranteed, but all of them are cheap.

reviews.author: 83nikk
reviews.title: Very busy market
reviews.content: This is a weekend night market, it was very busy and crowded, lots of stalls selling pretty much the same price, some stalls have set prices and are not willing to haggle at all so make sure you shop around - also check out the prices in the shops not in the market but in the streets around.

reviews.author: Andrew G
reviews.title: Busy buzzing
reviews.content: Good market lots of variety nice mix of peopleLoads of foods, stalls, clothes and shoesSoooo hot - lots of people and loads of buzzDefinitely go if you are there for the weekend we really enjoyed it

reviews.author: Greg C
reviews.title: no difference in prices to on the street extremely busy
reviews.content: No cheaper prices here than on the streets, less friendly too. Very busy actually too busy, and not fun at all with all the pushing and shoving. Didn't buy a thing went out next day and got better bargains off the streets.

reviews.author: Sam M
reviews.title: Stall 32 at the night market is number 1!
reviews.content: Great night at the market, great people, especially at stall 32, made the night he a good chat and was very friendly! Didn't push to buy and was very very good on the prices! Sam and Alex - two happy customersThank you!

reviews.author: Jessica C
reviews.title: Busy night markets for some light shopping
reviews.content: Having gone to the Ben Thanh night markets in Saigon, we found there was much more variety of clothes and knick knacks at these ones. As always, make sure you haggle and get a good bargain :)

reviews.author: Joseph Y
reviews.title: Night shopping
reviews.content: The night market only happens on the weekend. Nothing special, except you can walk around without having to worry too much about traffic. Plenty to see but buying things is really your preference. However, there was a Chinese acting show at a corner which is quite interesting to watch.

reviews.author: PierreMalmaison
reviews.title: Nothing special
reviews.content: Lots of these in Asia. This is very crowded and is a little daunting for the first-time visitor to Ha Noi. Watch for pick-pockets.

reviews.author: Reiid
reviews.title: A lot cheaper and friendlier compared to Ben thanh
reviews.content: Quality knock offs at a fraction of the price in which people ask for in Ben thanh. Haggling is easy and friendly , The pop up market shops offer a wide variety of knock offs and souvenirs . The stores that sell the jackets and shoes (in the actual concrete buildings ) situated just off the night market are run by the same cartel as Ben thanh so expect almost no haggling , but the people are friendlier than in Ben thanh still . A must go to for quality knock offs , but ensure you bring low denomination of currency if using the US dollar . ( side of caution it is rarer now but if your a woman , put your hand bag with a strap on the opposite shoulder as people on backs of scooters have been known to grab them )

reviews.author: Shahin S
reviews.title: Same shops but central position
reviews.content: The stands was selling same types of items but i still think IT was fun walking around there. Be cautions about the prices because you can many times haggle down to 1/5 of the sellers first offer.

reviews.author: Amber D
reviews.title: Shop number 11/10
reviews.content: All do the center of Hoi An is very busy it's also very beautiful. A lot of the shops have the same products made in factories. On the outside of the old town it's more quiet en you find really nice shops. Like number 11/10. Here you find a view handmade products like beautiful handmade pillowcases for a good price. (And easy to bring home!) made by a friend of the shop owner. She also sells nice handmade toys for babies and kids which she makes herself. The shop is real close to the nice restaurant " what else." Which is great for vegetarian food! Walk a little further to the outside and you will find the shop. It's all close to the Japanese bridge. Look at the photos for location! Don't park your bike inside town because it will be taken away and you have to pay. Enjoy the romantic setting of Hoi An!

reviews.author: Pampaz
reviews.title: Bargains!!!
reviews.content: I thought Ho Chi Minh was cheap but the Hanoi night markets were definitely cheaper. Operating Friday-Sunday from about 6pm. It can get pretty busy but worth all the hustle and bustle. If you get a chance over the weekend I'd check it out.

reviews.author: Biologywelch
reviews.title: An absolute MUST if you're in Hanoi!
reviews.content: The night market is just brilliant in Hanoi. Loads of street food, ornaments, nik-naks. As other have said - unfortunately there is a whole lot of junk. Selfie sticks, electronics etc. You have to explore and pick out the gems! We went in January aswell and the Tet festival market was on as well, which was beautiful! Tons of red and gold decorations and the traditional coins you see everywhere. We found some beautiful brass ornaments that we brought home with us. And there was ample street food when we went! It's well worth a visit if your exploring Hanoi in the evening - it finishes just before Hoan Kiem lake, so you can then wander around there!

reviews.author: Joseph3210
reviews.title: Enjoyed it!! No harassing
reviews.content: It's basically a couple streets blocked off with stands. I went on a Sunday night. North of the lake (across the street from the night market entrance), there were some performers around 8 pm - I'm talking about professional juggling, magic show, etc. it was very nice. The market itself is interesting. Prices are low for souvenirs, since it caters to the locals. The people don't hassle you. It's wonderful!! My wife hates markets, and she normally shops in known stores or online since prices are set already. This is the first time traveling in Asia that she enjoyed it and did not mind walking at a market.  In Bali if you make a mistake a turn your head, forget it - they're all over you and won't leave you alone.  I like this one because you have breathing room to look and move on if the items are not of interest. I tend to buy from the older folks. Enjoyed it. Highly recommend!!!

reviews.author: jack92dance
reviews.title: Market Time
reviews.content: This markets huge with lots of people with many stalls. Well worth the visit. Doesn't sell food as such but everything else

reviews.author: thd007
reviews.title: good night market to visit gets extremely crowded
reviews.content: good night market to visit gets extremely crowded, come here for souvenirs, shirts, shoes, jewellery electronics. crowded but has atmosphere. few cafe along the sides too.

reviews.author: Jennifer T
reviews.title: Not a night market at all
reviews.content: Its not a night market at all. Its just the same market as in the day time. Same product, fake items, etc.

reviews.author: 547sarinn
reviews.title: Great food! Cheap shopping! The streets come alive
reviews.content: Great place to shop. If you are traveling with kids, toys are a great bargain here. The street food is amazing and the whole concept of sitting outside restaurants with low seating chairs and small tables with a pint of beer and some great snacks is simply amazing! Great for souvenir shopping too

reviews.author: TravelEatXplore
reviews.title: Average market
reviews.content: This market only opens at night. It is really busy with locals selling all kind of products to other locals and foreigners. You can negotiated on the price. Too the locals working hard and at night time selling their products to make a living. Makes me humble.

reviews.author: Cesare B
reviews.title: A night market open only during the weekend
reviews.content: nothing interestingYou can take a rideBanal and repetitive merchandiseIt is not comparable to the Bangkok markets

reviews.author: Nigel
reviews.title: A mile of markets
reviews.content: These markets go for miles.  A lot of repetitive stalls but plenty of variety. Reasonable prices. Good for getting out amongst the locals.

reviews.author: Eugene C
reviews.title: Mountains of people
reviews.content: Not too different to what's on offer already in the area except that there's more people and great for people watching as someone already pointed out. An experience to have sure, but once is enough

reviews.author: metherat
reviews.title: Great for people watching
reviews.content: Most shops here sell the same items, many cheap fake branded T shirts and shoes. Come here to experience the Vietnamese night culture and you'll be fascinated by the size of the crowds on weekends.

reviews.author: HappySnappyGirls
reviews.title: Intense, repetitive and a little bit trashy!
reviews.content: This is definitely not one of the best markets in Asia or Vietnam for that matter. The stalls all sell basically the same stuff, it's cheap 'n' cheerful and sometimes a bit cheap 'n' nasty. If u r looking for a cheap t-shirt, fake sunnies or slave labour embroidered bags.......then this is for you! It's very crowded, probably intensified by the large number of locals out enjoying the public holiday. But it's a generally happy atmosphere, and there are loads of families out enjoying themselves. Much better, was the walk around the lake to get to the market. The crowds were happy, and people were watching little kids race on bikes down the street, skipping rope and playing tug-o-war. The walk was by far the best bit!

reviews.author: Jakub K
reviews.title: Buy Chinese stuff on Vietnamese night market...
reviews.content: The market is full of poor quality items (not all of them, but most of them for sure). There is a food section but it's pretty small comparing to the size of Chinese stuff area. You can skip this attraction.

reviews.author: Tara T
reviews.title: Basic night market
reviews.content: There were lots of stalls but the merchandise was pretty much the same.  The quality wasn't great.  People watching was top notch!  So many people, negotiating, walking around eating food, lively atmosphere.

reviews.author: Vossitch
reviews.title: Usual items but nice for a stroll
reviews.content: It's really nice when they shut down any of these streets from traffic, so it was enjoyable to stroll the night markets. It has all the usual stuff, both touristy and clothes.

reviews.author: Soloista
reviews.title: Many stores sell the same stuff
reviews.content: the streer closed from 7pm onward on Friday to Sunday for a walking street. its kinda nice to have a break from those motorcycle!!stores here sell pretty much the same stuff.there are couple of food and dessert stalls. we tried a few stuff, but didnt like all of them.we think food here is for snacks not a real meal.

reviews.author: Jo-Ann E
reviews.title: Cheaper than old quarter shops during the day!
