reviews.content: Selective publishing of facts and heavy use of adjectives give this museum a slightly one-sided feel. However, there is a great display of war remnants as well as an excellent reproduction of the battle of Dien Bien Phu.

reviews.author: Steve G
reviews.title: Very interesting Museum
reviews.content: This was a real treat for all as all of us are deeply interested in military history. The main focus for us was the military history of the war against the French and the American war against the USA.The exhibits and photographs were first rate capturing the periods of history extremely well. If you interested in these time periods I highly recommend a visit.

reviews.author: Jscpg
reviews.title: Comprehensive
reviews.content: An informative museum of artefacts, documents, weapons and photographs relating to the Vietnamese people's various struggles over the centuries. Unlike, say, the War Remnants Museum in Saigon, this museum is not graphically confronting and does not dwell on any one conflict. Unusually, one room is dedicated to the women who lost many family members to war, honoured as Heroic Mothers.

reviews.author: Wolfie2010
reviews.title: Another well worth seeing place
reviews.content: Went here and found it really informative.there is replica of the final battle with the French,told in various languages including English,and demonstrating how the Vietnamese won’t the battle for freedom,along with another section dedicated to the war against America and the south.well worth seeing.

reviews.author: dogleap
reviews.title: Good exhibits
reviews.content: Easy to visit on your own. There are many internal exhibits telling the story of Vietnam in an easily followed way, but do make allowances for the biased views. For me the external exhibits were the best with a variety from all sides. The tower is included with a good view of the planes from the top

reviews.author: lisazed14
reviews.title: Museum
reviews.content: Wow!!! Great museum. I was astounded to find out that the Vietnamese have fought their way out of occupation for centuries. Not just the Yanks & the French, but the Japanese, the Chinese, the Thais and the Mongols  etc. The Vietnamese should rightly be proud of their achievements after so long and so much terrorisation. I feel proud for them too! Just note that the museum closes between 11.30 and 1pm

reviews.author: Cheryl S
reviews.title: Great Military Museum
reviews.content: We chose to tour on our own which was ok.It is very easy to get around and the exhibits are really well done. There is so much history here and it was so much history.

reviews.author: Peter
reviews.title: My Favorite Site in Hanoi
reviews.content: I've been to the military museum in Saigon and this one is even more interesting - and decidedly slanted toward the glory of communism.  Quite interesting from the US perspective.The large collection of captured US military hardware in the yard outside is very interesting to see.  Along with an example of a Soviet built SAM used to shoot down US aircraft.  Most of the placards have English included.  The displays indoors go back to Vietnam's beginning ~ 5000 years ago.  But the majority of the museum displays concern the French and US wars.Note that price is high:  250,000 dong or $10.  Get here when they open at 8am to avoid the tour bus crowds!Highly recommended.

reviews.author: Rabbs27
reviews.title: a lot of history
reviews.content: it was interesting to see the side from vietnam. its split in different rooms and you have to walk around. a few trucks and helicopters and jets. just avoid the toilets very horrible. you can pay in usd as well.

reviews.author: petersecord
reviews.title: Interesting, and highly informative
reviews.content: This museum provides a basic outline of the struggle of the Vietnamese people against foreign invaders over nearly 2000 years: Chinese, French, Japanese, American. It has good exhibits, covering each of the major periods of struggle, and (for a military museum) is quite evenhanded in the narratives. This was my third visit over a 20+ year period. The message is powerful, in that the Vietnamese are naturally independent and will fight with whatever tools are available to remain so. If you go to Hanoi, spend the two hours for a proper visit.

reviews.author: Brad J
reviews.title: A MUST SEE
reviews.content: We visited in December 2018 and it was extremely hot.  Dress light and bring lots of water.  The muses was eye opening and a must see if the Vietnam War from the perspective of the Vietnamese.  War is horrible and both sides do horrible things. Our kids (as did we) came away with a new understanding of the war as well as all war.

reviews.author: hadyhussien
reviews.title: Learn more about the Vietnam’s war
reviews.content: We went in the after noon and I took us almost 1 hr to go through the museum, a lot of information to learn and amazing displays. Just take care that it’s closed on Friday and Monday. And they have a break daily between 11:30Am and 1:00Pm

reviews.author: Hanhiemo
reviews.title: Interesting museum
reviews.content: I had read somewhere that the museum is small, so I was surprised how big it was. There are many buildings and halls to visit and the inside yards with the planes and tanks is attractive. A good place to visit with kids. Inside the building you can read about Vietnam history and Vietnamese characters. The flag tower is nice! The entrance price was 30.000 or 40.000 VND. Then there is a camera fee separately, if you want to take pictures.

reviews.author: Sean Friend
reviews.title: Museum visit
reviews.content: Very disappointed. We came on a Friday morning only to be told that the inside part of the  museum is closed on Mondays and Fridays. Only the outside section was available at half price (vnd 20,000).

reviews.author: Craig Moore
reviews.title: A must attraction.
reviews.content: For me I loved it and so did my partner..the flag tower is on the same site which is a bonus as your ticking off 2 things for the price of 1.There's a great outdoor display with planes..and heavy artillery but most of all a huey helicopter with hanging machine gun and belt still inside...not only were these helicopter massively used in the Vietnam war for not only taking life's but saving and rescuing so many.A great visit for all young and old.

reviews.author: Greg C
reviews.title: The Norths view of the War
reviews.content: Definitely a one sided view of the war.  Displays are rundown, but it's worth it to view the equipment.  The numbers aren't consistent from display to display.  Worth a visit.

reviews.author: Wendy G
reviews.title: War and Peace
reviews.content: A must see. Not expensive and very interesting. Great exhibition which explains the history with many artefacts on show. Outside an array of planes, missiles and wreckage and you can literally walk underneath the aircraft. Worth a visit and can easily walk from the old town.

reviews.author: gordonj258
reviews.title: You should visit.
reviews.content: A museum that deals with Vietnams past up until the recent times of the American invasion. Clearly, the Vietnamese are immensely proud, and so they should be, of their victory over their American aggressors. A lot is written in English. It is a fascinating place and will elevate your appreciation of these people who have struggled with oppression for so long.

reviews.author: Grant B
reviews.title: Interesting perspective on modern history
reviews.content: Interesting visit to this museum.  Lots in gripping displays - what amazes me is the attitude Vietnamese people have - I salute them.  Moving on and building the society they have today is testament to their indomitable spirit - there is no way that they US were ever going to win this - as many of the troops involved in this pointless war will attest.

reviews.author: lclcusoon
reviews.title: Film History, and Military equipments
reviews.content: We walk there one morning from the Old Quarter...We saw tanks and aircrafts and guns etc. that has to do with the war. Also film history of how the Vietnamese people/army took back the place/fort from the french in a long battle...you can ask them to show it in english or other languages. Addition on other wars and history documents.It was a really cool place to explore, check the hours of opening...some day open  from 8:00-11:30  am and sometimes 1:30-4:30pmAdmission in $10,000VnD

reviews.author: Tonic26
reviews.title: Vietnam Military History Museum
reviews.content: Double check with your hotel to ensure this is open before you go and they will literally kick you out at 11.30 for their lunch break.  Very interesting to see the countries military history dating from the 12th century.  The American historical section was closed for refurbishment during our stay.  There were lots of exhibits of planes, choppers and tanks and other leftover military equipment as well.

reviews.author: PercyBlakeney63
reviews.title: A very worthwhile visit
reviews.content: This museum is well worth a visit if you are in Hanoi. It contains plenty of artefacts and covers Vietnam’s military history from the 12th century. What becomes very clear is that this country has been subject to various invasions from Genghis Khan to the French and the Americans. As a military history fan, I really enjoyed it and it gave me a very fresh perspective outside of the Vietnam War.

reviews.author: Jake H
reviews.title: Great place for war memorabilia
reviews.content: Highly recommend. Lots of information about Vietnams history of war. Main attraction are the full size military vehicles used in the wars. Fighters jets, helicopters tanks and artillery equipment. About 40k dong entry fee

reviews.author: donmountford
reviews.title: Mostly outdoors exhibits of the "American War" aircraft and NVA artillery
reviews.content: An interesting indoor display of many military items, photos and Ho Chi Minh memorabilia of course. Becomes a bit of more of the same after a while. Still for anyone involved in the war as Australia was, anything new is new information or better explained. The piled up remains of a downed B52 bomber is impressive just on size alone and up close and personal with a US Huey again was a buzz. Recommended.

reviews.author: John M
reviews.title: Worth Visiting...
reviews.content: This museum is not on all touring company itineraries, but it is worth making a visit. They do close the buildings for lunch, but you're still able to visit the outside areas at that time and come back in after lunch. We got there just before lunch closing time, so we went just around the corner to a very small noodle shop and soup and beers - all of US$7. Most interesting were the many pictures of their recent wars primarily against the French and US. I was a US serviceman and I expected a "winners" slant on how the war story was told - I wasn't disappointed. Nevertheless, it's easy to walk away very cynical, but if you understand the bigger picture of history, this museum is still worth visiting. Numerous military hardware, mostly US, in the outside exhibits. You can easily take 2-3 hours walking through the exhibits.

reviews.author: Ashwathram
reviews.title: Show case of Vietnam`s War History
reviews.content: Vietnam War history military Museum is must visit in list you can help us lots of destroyed war aircrafts and the tanks ,guns are the battles and the display of the various equipments that was used in Vietnam War was left over by the Enemies does Museum full just take you to the historical the Walton history of the Vietnam its evolution. I visited this Museum at noon so that you can have a glimpse of the display weapons and there is a video dislpay gallery  in which there is a video presentation which take you to the historical war that happened in Vietnam. That is also a Cafeteria besides the Museum where you can refresh you can have some drinks and you can have some food with your family and friends inside the Museum there are a lot of war of artifacts and  dresses ,clothing ,guns and the weapons that was used by the Vietnamese people during the War torn era in Vietnam.

reviews.author: Naina-Damani
reviews.title: MASSIVE TANK
reviews.content: A lot of past history, during the Vietnamese war, surrounded by huge war tanks. Ideal for photos and memory of the war.

reviews.author: Lesley C
reviews.title: History in the Making
reviews.content: Enjoyed visiting the Vietnam Military Museum to learn more about the horrific war and to see some of the wreckage which was dragged out of the sea.  A little slanted review at times as some of the numbers did not stack up.  Well worth seeing.

reviews.author: Jasmine
reviews.title: Good value
reviews.content: Having been raised and brainwashed, it is great to buy a unique viewpoint. It might appear the propaganda has been laid on a little heavy but this's most likely a more relevant representation of what happened to an entire public in the own land of theirs, than the anguished Vets material we have been given from Hollywood. Anyway - an area to contemplate numerous of recent history.

reviews.author: J-Chizzle
reviews.title: Half Off Because It was Half Closed
reviews.content: On the day we went, it was 50% off; normally the admission price is 40,000 VND but because many of the interior exhibits were closed, we got a 50% discount / refund. This was unexpected but go with it.We ended up roaming around the exterior exhibits. There were a handful of Soviet bloc fighters and tanks, but for the most part, they have more captured or abandoned American equipment. I saw a Huey helicopter, a M-48 tank, pits and pieces of a downed B-52 bomber, and a Skyraider.There were older cannons from the 19th century on display.If I do go back, I want to see the inside next time.

reviews.author: Kathy C
reviews.title: Slanted review of History
reviews.content: Great visit but a slightly slanted review on history....at times in same exhibits the numbers were totally different.  Great way to see the VietNam war from their perspective.  They are closed over the lunch hour but there is lots to see outside. Watch out for the taxi drivers outside.....some are not so reputable.

reviews.author: alf w
reviews.title: good to see
reviews.content: Like all wars there s been loads of life and this show it right down the line, But like all wars there are two sides to every storey  so like me I watch a Documentary on Net flex which tells a good storey and then go with that in the back of your mind and put it all together to make sense out of the whole lot.Worth seeing need 2 hours to read and take in all what is on display ,

reviews.author: Joseph M
reviews.title: Extra time in Hanoi before leaving.
reviews.content: In Hanoi be for heading home. This museum was very interesting and very informative. It had a lot of good information. I would recommend it. It does need some updating but over all good.

reviews.author: JSTrip_77
reviews.title: Fascinating Look at Vietnamese Military History from Ancient Times to Present
reviews.content: I noticed that some of the previous reviews noted that they'd expected to see more about the American Vietnam War and were annoyed by the focus on the fight for independence from the French - or that the museum was too "one-sided." Although I agreed that it would have been helpful to have some additional signage so as to plan the visit in a more chronological manner, I was incredibly impressed with the fact that signage was available in both Vietnamese and English throughout the interior exhibits and in Vietnamese, English and French on the outdoor exhibits (the aircraft and vehicles). To my mind the fact that this museum focuses on the entirety of Vietnam's military history provides a fantastic bit of insight into what makes this country what it is today - and perhaps helps to explain why the Vietnamese seem far less focused on the American Vietnam War than the average American. Once you get a look at the turbulent history of Vietnam, it's easier to understand why the American Vietnam War was just another war in a long list of others. And yes, the terminology in a lot of the exhibits is certainly stilted - words like "puppet government" to refer to the South Vietnamese government or the characterization of the Americans as "imperialist aggressors" might bother some. But, that's to be expected. Overall, this is a really interesting place to visit. The price is very low. The quality of the displays was surprisingly good. There are also gift shops and restaurants on site as well as the Hanoi Flag Tower which was built from 1805-1812 and from which the Vietnamese national flag has flown every day since independence from France in 1954.

reviews.author: Margaret B
reviews.title: Has some interesting exhibits
reviews.content: Being American I expected it to be heavy on the Vietnam war but it was focused on the war for independence from the French. The Vietnamese people freed themselves from the French in 1954 and they had many exhibits with photos and memorabilia from that time period. There were quite a few old airplanes and helicopters (some of which were American that were confiscated when Saigon fell in 1975) which were interesting.

reviews.author: Justin B
reviews.title: Average Museum
reviews.content: The museum has some interesting tanks, artillery pieces and aircraft, although some are not labelled very well. The indoor exhibits were only average. It would be helpful if a map was provided at entry, as the layout is a bit haphazard. Buses being allowed into the grounds near the exhibits to drop off tour groups was also pretty annoying, particularly when you have young children in tow. Still our two boys aged 7 and 4 had a good time looking at the aircraft and tanks, so a reasonable family afternoon out when visiting Hanoi. Only about AUD 6.50 for our family of four to get in, so good value. The Russian Mig-21s and Mig 19 along with a selection of American and Russian tanks were the highlights.

reviews.author: Kelsey A
reviews.title: Interesting place to visit
reviews.content: We enjoyed our time wandering through this museum! It is huge so make sure to leave yourself a couple of hours to enjoy it! Lots of interesting information although like previous reviews have stayed maybe a bit bias. Still we enjoyed our time here and spent a few hours going through all of the exhibits!

reviews.author: Bob E
reviews.title: museum visit
reviews.content: A telling reminder of the awful war that raged and the cruelty of it.Well worth a visit as it gives a different perspective.

reviews.author: Badmedicine
reviews.title: one sided
reviews.content: I'm saying "It's ok" because it is a one sided exhibit. Propaganda adjectives describing  photos of the VC soldiers as patriotic, while the Americans were tyrants, throwing VC off helicopters and shooting children in the field. The first floor was full of posters of how the world was against this conflict, including US soldier donated uniform shirt, several medals and even a chap-stick which was used during the war. The second floor contains, in part, the weapons used and an exhibit of effects of DDT and Agent Orange, and unexploded bombs had on general population and birth defects.There is no way to defend this war, and the mayhem it resulted in. There were no winners. There are no exhibits of booby traps, and the poisoned bamboo spikes used by the VC in various ways around the jungle, for that you have to visit Cu Chi tunnels. No mention of the torture they inflicted on US prisoners, etc.

reviews.author: lewielufc
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: For me this gave me a lot of information regarding Vietnam. I honestly didn’t realise Vietnam had been invaded so many times in there history. After visiting you can probably understand the Vietnamese people rebellious streak. I personally found it was a good couple of hours spent and l would recommend if in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Florence S
reviews.title: Interesting place to visit
reviews.content: I recommend going with a tour guide.  Did you know that the Vietnamese invented the crossbow.  Be open minded when visiting.  Realize that there is two sides to a war.

reviews.author: gergmu
reviews.title: Quite Interesting..but
reviews.content: I found it interesting to see the weapons, planes etc on display but think that it is more for the benefit of a local Vietnamese audience. Nothing wrong with that of course but being a foreigner I would have liked to have seen more labelling in other languages. It could do with a tidy up & modernisation. Note if you go, the museum closes at 11.30 until 1PM for lunch.

reviews.author: Traveler O
reviews.title: Dated Museum
reviews.content: Fairly sized museum with no particular clear-cut path to follow when seeing the exhibits. Terrible English translations. Place could use some serious updating and renovations. It’s a time-warp from 1975-76. It’s heavy on propaganda as well, so take it as you will. Just for being the national museum in the capitol city, you’d expect more. They could do much better than this. The Dien Bien Phu exhibit with light show is downright terrible. Hire someone to come in and modernize the display to include audio guides with an unbiased explanation of the battle. Not the best place for kids as it’s difficult to get a stroller around and some of the exhibits aren’t good for kids to see. The outdoor displays are nothing special either. If you’re seeing the masoleum and remnants of the Imperial City nearby, then you might as well stopby here too. Staff don’t seem into the museum either, except when they close for their 2 hour or so lunch each day.

reviews.author: iliketomoveandsee
reviews.title: Strange museum
reviews.content: The staff were pretty rude, and there wasn't really a layout to the museum which made any sense. The whole visit was pretty confusing.The only reason I am giving it three stars is because of the old war stuff outside.

reviews.author: green mr
reviews.title: Vietnam 's History
reviews.content: I always enjoy discovering a brand new culture and this particular museum was interesting and educational. Amazingly, one space was focused on the Vietnam (American) War although it figures significantly in Australian minds. several of the aircraft had been popular to me had also part in the earlier life of mine. Well worth a trip. Informative and educational with lots if history artifacts apparently the very poor Vietnamese are battling a very long time for independence. fascinating to find out what was left behind or perhaps taken after the war. several of the aircraft had been popular to me had also part in my previous life

reviews.author: ADCASH
reviews.title: Not as good as War Remnants Museum
reviews.content: A good overall history of conflict and fight for independence through the 20th Century. Not as graphic or as historically detailed as Saigon's War Remnants Museum.

reviews.author: Jillian
reviews.title: The military history museum
reviews.content: An amazing history of struggle and survival. These galleries and museums within the complex describe the story of the war with France and also the against the USA informed from the viewpoint of the Vietnamese. A must check out for virtually any traveller. Only two dollars entrance. Food, toilets, and even rest are available on the website.

reviews.author: mmchale2018
reviews.title: Mr Martin M McHale
reviews.content: A truly fascinating collection of visual experiences of weapons and ideals under one roof , the futility of using these instruments to impose your will on those who have no desires to take an aggressive position other than-protect freedom and stability that we all take for granted . A stark reminder of lots of pain for No gain .

reviews.author: robert w
reviews.title: A `must visit` when you are in Hanoi !
reviews.content: We visited this Museum on the last day of our Vietnam holiday. There were many (Vietnam) war machines on show outside the building and inside the building there was an absolute plethora of exhibits concerning the Vietnam War. We did not have time to look in detail at each and every exhibit on display but we were able to spend some time watching a very interesting video presentation (in Vietnamese without English subtitles !) about the Vietnam conflict. All in all, and having some days earlier visited the `War Remnants Museum` in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) as part of a guided tour, we felt that the Hanoi War Museum was a better Museum, there seemed to be many more war machines on display. Also, just outside the Museum there was a lovely large open air café which sold hot and cold drinks and very varied foodstuffs, we had lunch after the Museum visit and the lunch was excellent and very reasonably priced. :-)

reviews.author: Corinna
reviews.title: Visiting museum
reviews.content: Not well worth the trip. A museum of artefacts tossed around the school. Much of the info in Vietnamese so unobtainable for the English traveler. Would've liked learning more about the Vietnamese army history, but as a result of the organization of lack and artefacts of info I felt I came away out of the museum understanding practically nothing much more than when I entered. A missed opportunity.

reviews.author: Chester S
reviews.title: History
reviews.content: If you like history things you should not miss it. Its quite near the old town and we use grab to go there. Every monday the museum is close so double check the schedule before going. Some displays are inside the buildings.

reviews.author: R7121LWtracyc
reviews.title: Great outdoor attractions to see but disappointing displays inside
reviews.content: Following trip advisor reviews, we thought we should visit here, 40,000 dung to get in each which is very cheap for a museum but no real story unfolds and the museum is quite difficult to follow. lots of photographs but a lot of the information is not available in english or if it is its very small and hard to read. we were a little disappointed

reviews.author: RSD78
reviews.title: Cheap entry and good exhibits
reviews.content: Some really interesting displays, with very pro-Vietnam views (understandable). An impressive B-52 (that was shot down by SA-2 surface to air missile) sculpture in the middle of some former US hardware. Big flag tower in the outside area too. Entry is cheap (think it was only about 40,000 VND, so under £2, for an adult), but you are supposed to pay extra to have your camera inside (£1 extra only). Lockers available near the entrance to save you carrying your backpack round.

reviews.author: Arni S
reviews.title: Great piece of histor
reviews.content: Vietnam has experienced its fair share of war and conflict. A potted heritage is in numerous guide books. The Museum is equally an interior, space by the space bank account of what is occurring throughout the ages and additionally a remarkable collection on the machinery of wars which have occurred in much more recent times. I'd the enjoyable experience of dropping in with a number of Vietnamese ex servicemen as well as females, which generated warm conversations and greetings, many photo opportunities, directed and presented getting best advantage and also friendly chit talk amongst us.

reviews.author: Housam Elkouteini
reviews.title: Short visit to the outdoor section only
reviews.content: Has alot of destroyed enemy planes, tanks, bombs and weapons from wars with Japan, China, France and the US. We could not do the inside part as it was closed but the outside part was enough for us. It has also some nice statues around related to war. Lovely place. I loved the destroyed plane tale and the surroundings of it.

reviews.author: Soul D
reviews.title: For Me A Highlight
reviews.content: Get an insight into the recent turbulent times that have plagued this country. Plenty to see and experience if this is your "thing"

reviews.author: Stacey Chance
reviews.title: An excellent place to learn about Vietnam's history
reviews.content: For a person who had never read about Vietnam's history and grew up hearing Vietnam war until I am a teenager, this is where I learn all about it. For an entry fee of VND40,000 (USD1.70), you get to learn about Vietnam and war it fought (and won) - since the ancient time with China dynasty, Thai, Burmese, French and the Americans (the longest war in history). They fought so many wars, mostly the resistance at the boarders and invasion. If one come with an open mind, see it through the eyes of the Vietnam people, you will see how resilient and dedicated they are. The outdoor displays are mostly jets and bombers they shoot down/took control. The main hall of the museum that really interest me. The museum also dedicated a floor for mothers who contributed to the war and nation building. If you look around Vietnam today, there is hardly traces of war-torn but a thriving economy.

reviews.author: Donald J
reviews.title: Gave a complete history of Vietnams resistance
reviews.content: This place must be bigger and house a great deal more info and artifacts. Do not get me wrong, its worth a trip and they also do the very best they possibly can to express to the story of theirs but do not have the resources to get it done better.I would not have missed it and discovered it really interesting. Vietnam is invaded by the Chinese, French, Japanese as well as Americans (and partners) then the Chinese once again. They're resilient and tough and must be proud.

reviews.author: peter b
reviews.title: very interesting to see
reviews.content: a lot off proper ganda goes on they forget they invaded south vietnam and killed there own people worth the visit i injoyed it makes u think about the war cheers

reviews.author: Andrew M
reviews.title: Worth visiting, but a little tired
reviews.content: The outdoor displays were a little boring. The displays were interesting with one main hall dedicated to the defeat of the French, another defeat of the Americans. The old flag tower is worth a visit.

reviews.author: nikkisingh
reviews.title: Very Interesting visit
reviews.content: A visit here is a must as the museum has so many artefacts  and relics from the Vietnam war. It is so thought provoking as it provides a real insight into the war. There a few exhibition hall with a great deal of background information as well as tanks, helicopters and other vehicles.Really good visit which lasts about 1 hour

reviews.author: Max H
reviews.title: A little bit tired, but interesting
reviews.content: Given that the war was many years back, some of the outdoor displays were old & boring, inside display has plenty of history on Vietnam. The citadel next door also worth a visit.

reviews.author: Eleanorrigby
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Very cheap entry fee, lots of air conditioned rooms.  I’m not particularly interested in Vietnamese military history but this was good.  I particularly liked the info on America’s involvement in the Vietnam war.  We would have liked some kind of guide to show all the rooms as it was a bit chaotic making sure you saw everything.  Be aware it closes for lunch.

reviews.author: R M
reviews.title: Nice museum, especially for our 9YO son
reviews.content: It is interesting to see the Vietnamese perspective on the war.  The museum does a nice job at this.  Our son really liked the planes and tanks.  The ice cream at the shop outside at the end also helped!

reviews.author: Danielle Die
reviews.title: Must do
reviews.content: This's a must see on every tourist trip to Hanoi, and also places a really obvious point of perspective on the war. The mangled B52 sends a distinct message, but because of this and others, it's an interesting place to visit. Much less shocking compared to the counterpart of its within Ho Chi Minh City. It is not a big event, and may be performed in an hour. Watch out for the fellow outside promoting Bao in-house publication, which is worth reading.

reviews.author: Didier T
reviews.title: No interest
reviews.content: Unless you have nothing else to do, this museum is not offering any interest.  You will learn more from Internet about the war than spending 1/2 day visiting it. It is much better for you to go visit the women museum...

reviews.author: Damien
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Interesting, but nothing outside of the typical.Massive display of genuine military vehicles, planes as well as helicopters used in their many wars. Exhibits in doors with structures throughout the area of the museum. Exhibits and displays of various memorabilia and equipment in & outdoors!

reviews.author: Karl P
reviews.title: Not left wondering
reviews.content: This was very confronting but the photos dont lie, it was plain to see that a super power didnt stand a chance, i did notice there was very little mentioned about the Rusians, Australins and NVA it was the American war??

reviews.author: Eric F
reviews.title: Very informative
reviews.content: As a history and a military buff, I enjoyed going through this museum and learning a lot of things I didn't know. I'm glad the Vietnamese are no longer at war with anyone, they are wonderful people. I would highly recommend traveling to Hanoi and visiting this museum.

reviews.author: HoE
reviews.title: Very attractive
reviews.content: It was truly fascinating, but didn't actually interest me or maybe the sister of mine since The past was extremely unfortunate that these devices killed numerous Vietnamese folks and destroyed much rich historical past of the folks, like villages, temples and also pagoda's. Many individuals in the south and north of Vietnam have been brutalized and displaced from the homes of theirs due to these machines and the war. That is all I am going to say about this particular place.

reviews.author: Ouppoeps
reviews.title: If you have time
reviews.content: There is a lot to do in Hanoi, but if you have time, it's nice to walk in this relatively small space and look at tanks, aeroplanes, and various other interesting war relics. I wanted to climb to the top of the lovely tower here, but it was closed.

reviews.author: Soymylk
reviews.title: Unable to enjoy it fully due to bag rulez
reviews.content: I was really looking forward to my trip to this museum as I love learning about the military history of each country I visit.Upon entering, I was asked to store my backpack. I asked if this was optional, but was told it wasn't. This wouldn't be a huge deal, but I had neither pockets or a smaller bag that day, so was unable to carry everything I needed, including eyedrops which I need to apply regularly. This shortened my visit quite a bit.What little I was able to see didn't have much in the way of English translations. Of course, the entry is very cheap and the displays are interesting enough so this wasn't a huge issue to me, but those visiting might want to be aware of this.I'm sure that the museum has a lot to offer, but unfortunately I wasn't able to fully enjoy it at this time.

reviews.author: Lang J
reviews.title: Great place
reviews.content: Take a neighborhood tour guide when seeing. The details are able to matter a great deal, We are a family unit of five as well as contacted Hanoi Free Walking Tours that supplied us a local guide, extremely helpful and also eager and informative talk about specifics. Loved the journey and also insights provided.

reviews.author: Freddi
reviews.title: Interesting place
reviews.content: It's a tremendous site in which you are able to walk around outside looking at the planes, cannons, tanks, and cars or inside viewing the pictures. I watched the Military Museum in Ho Chi Minh City a few years back; the photos there have been a lot more graphic as well as inside your deal with regarding the Vietnam War. The Museum in Hanoi is a tamer variation for certain, spanning a broader historical past of problems. it's worth a visit.

reviews.author: James R
reviews.title: Good museum but be careful of taxis outside
reviews.content: Enjoyed the museum. Went through various conflicts that Vietnam has gone through. I would say there could have been a bit more structure to the tour as we did not know very much about very early Vietnam history but otherwise it was informative. However afterwards be careful about taxis outside of the museum as they appear to wait for tourists and we nearly got scammed out of lots of money on a taxi ride by a rigged meter.

reviews.author: Payton
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: A very emotional place, viewing the war through the eyes of theirs. Interesting, interesting, shocking and occasionally really disturbing, not for all those faint of heart. A necessity for those people who were ignorant towards the fact.

reviews.author: Debbie R
reviews.title: Mind Expanding Vietnamese History
reviews.content: This Military Museum is well worth the trip, although you may feel overwhelmed at times with the graphic details shared relating to the War being shared there, it is definitely a place that will provide you with the facts about this War and how Vietnam has healed and moved on to become stronger nation.

reviews.author: Lindas A
reviews.title: A very sad eye opening day
reviews.content: I went with limited knowledge of the Vietnam war. This museum leaves nothing to the imagination. Very graphic portrayals. We went with a variety of aged children with some finding the information very confronting. The outdoor display is very interesting as with the newspaper reports that are displayed inside.

reviews.author: schnegli
reviews.title: Interesting, but outdated
reviews.content: Unfortunately many tables and explanations are in vietnamese only. It would help, if you would be guided with some kind of visual elements through the museum.

reviews.author: Damo H
reviews.title: Very big and interesting!
reviews.content: Great value at just 40,000 dong pp. Loads to see and read. Covering centuries of war history!Really enjoy the Vietnamese take on their history. Everything is positive, great propaganda! Makes a difference from the American war films in particular!

reviews.author: Thomas M
reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.content: A great way to show the history of Vietam. Fantastic displays and well worth a look. Great coffee on site as a bonus

reviews.author: Kevinozark
reviews.title: Very well done
reviews.content: Remember all the history in Vietnam is based in their views. Very interesting to see the “other side of the story”. Multiple building filled with relics and guns.

reviews.author: The_Cheshireset133
reviews.title: Could do with more foreign language translation
reviews.content: Museum provides some historical context for the long struggle that Vietnam has had with foreign invaders.  The displays range back from the 1800 to the most recent Vietnam War as well as the modern Vietnam Armed forces.Like a lot of the historical references in official museum s the displays and narrative is probably a bit one sided.  It is therefore helpful to understand the historic context as well.A number of the more interactive displays were not working.  The museum no doubt by has a great display of military hardware and normally I would have spent more time there.  What was missing however was foreign language translations of key battles/conflicts.  These were all only in Vietnamese.

reviews.author: Mike B
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: Our family had a day in Hanoi and enjoys history.  We liked seeing all of the relics and photos from the various periods and the planes, helicopters and weaponry were all quite interesting.  It is air conditioned in the exhibits which was a welcome treat as well.  Very well done and glad we went!  Not an expensive admission either!

reviews.author: rchlwllms
reviews.title: Interesting museum with awesome displays.
reviews.content: Went into this museum not expecting much, but it was actually great to walk around and look at the exhibits. There are tanks, planes and the wreckage of a B52 which all look amazing. You are also able to climb the one flagged tower, but the stairs are steep and the ceilings are low. We could have spent more time here, but they shut for a couple of hours at lunch time, so you need to be out by 11:30am.

reviews.author: 202Mikey
reviews.title: More History
reviews.content: Had to cram this one in. Loads of exhibits and great photographs from most conflicts represented. Air con inside was playing up so had to sit down for a bit. Seriously interesting and inexpensive.

reviews.author: Austin F
reviews.title: Interesting và special
reviews.content: A museum that is great to check out. Great display of war atmosphere crafts and weapons. Everything is interpreted in English which made things easy. Allow 1.5 to two hours because of the visit. A number of gift stores are on site along with an excellent Highland coffee shop definitely outside.

reviews.author: Moodude
reviews.title: Great place about Vietnam war
reviews.content: The Vietnam Military History Museum was good from the perspective of seeing the number of conflicts have dominated the country 's the historical past. The crowning achievement of this particular museum ended up being to memorialize Vietnam's wars. Our local guide insisted we come across this "magical" museum that was average at best. Our observation is it was neither well worth the entry fee neither time spent.

reviews.author: Henk v
reviews.title: Great museum
reviews.content: Very interesting museum. It shows you the Vietnam war fro the perspective of Vietnam. Amazing to see what amount of good equipment the USA left behind during the final escape. Absolutely a must go.

reviews.author: dhmyers2018
reviews.title: Not unexpectedly biased against the American war effort. I understand.
reviews.content: Still, Americans visiting Hanoi should go to this museum.  Americans once regarded the North Vietnamese as enemies, and we need to now recognize them as part of one unified nation of warm and friendly people.

reviews.author: Roelf v
reviews.title: Part of History
reviews.content: A proud nation fought four wars and keep their dignity and willingness to forgive and open their beautiful country to the world.

reviews.author: Blue Dude
reviews.title: The museum with impressive exhibits
reviews.content: The exhibitions had been pretty like anyone with the Museum of the Revolution, though the thing which actually impressed us was all of the martial artist planes, helicopters, bomb shells within print on the other side! We took several excellent photos of these devices. It truly puts it into perspective if you think about how bombs this huge size had been indiscriminately dropped on Vietnam!

reviews.author: chven
reviews.title: Interesting with free walking tour guide
reviews.content: We learnt more about the life of people in different eras. Interesting because we had a guide who could speak in English, telling us what the artifacts meant. One thumbs down was it closes before time stated. However, our young guide convinced the person to let us finish. Great job

reviews.author: KaladinT
reviews.title: Okay but has potential to be excellent
reviews.content: Given the cultural importance of the Vietnam war for Americans, and the significant impact it had on Vietnam, I expected to learn more about the war, how it unfolded and progressed, and the impact it had on the country.It did not provide much of this, except some touching insights into the effect of bombing on the people of Hanoi.The museum does have a lot of different vehicles (tanks, planes, helicopters) and exhibitions of different weapons used throughout the countrys history.

reviews.author: Vishal Balwani
reviews.title: Audio guides would have been great here
reviews.content: The museum is very big. It takes you at least 2 hours to just go through all the rooms of the museum. the artifacts displayed here are real and preserved from the war.

reviews.author: ZoeEJoy
reviews.title: Really cool to check out
reviews.content: Includes a lot of history and is an interesting place to. Not a far walk from Hoan Kiem at all so I recommend that then stopping for a feast at Bun Bo Nam Bo on the way back :)

reviews.author: David Ho
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: The museum is a selection of structures, each dedicated to a different element of the different conflicts, a few going back thousands of years. An interesting and fascinating look at the martial historical past of Vietnam.

reviews.author: John8088
reviews.title: Worth Seeing
reviews.content: This museum has some interesting displays and artifacts. It is nothing too unusual or unexpected. Not a bad way to spend an hour or so.

reviews.author: royandevep
reviews.title: Very Interesting place to visit
reviews.content: A worthwhile visit at a reasonable price about £1 each person. Good to see planes and tanks and other exhibits that were involved in conflicts.

reviews.author: Tune Vine
reviews.title: Great insight
reviews.content: Fascinating. For some amount the inside the museum is missing exhibits other than pictures. Outside holds far more physical assets. Planes helicopters, etc. and an actual collage of aircraft wreckage. Really excellent and rather moving to consider the human misery which must have happened here

reviews.author: TYPSUKR
reviews.title: Must-Visit for Military History Buffs
reviews.content: This museum features both historical information exhibits and military equipment, mostly American aircraft captured during the Vietnam War. The information panels highlight not only the Vietnam War, but other episodes of warfare in Vietnam's history going back centuries. Most signs are captioned in English in addition to Vietnamese. Even if you're not into history, the military equipment on display outside makes it worth it.If you have a bag, you'll have to check it at the front where you buy the ticket. There is a Highlands Coffee adjacent to the museum as well.

reviews.author: 1837selvia
reviews.title: Good but was closed
reviews.content: We made our way there but unfortunately was closed, was a Friday, do take note not to visit on Fridays. We managed to snap some photos from outside while there.

reviews.author: smallhausen1
reviews.title: Not only propaganda
reviews.content: This place shows not only official look on Vietnamese wars but shows also many interesting details from the operations planning and endurance of Vietnam people.

reviews.author: Kevin T
reviews.title: Check opening times.....
reviews.content: Again we thought the place was closed but were given access to the outside at a reduced price. I have no idea what was inside the museum but all the big ticket items, tanks, planes, helis, bombs and guns were all outside and pretty impressive. It’s a 2 min walk from there to the Mausoleum so worth stopping in. Enjoy.....

reviews.author: Cathleen
reviews.title: A clear view of the war in Vietnam
reviews.content: Very exciting. Beautiful old building. It's truly good being an additional perspective of just how hard life was in the points during the war.

reviews.author: eeke2015
reviews.title: Must see!
reviews.content: Interesting museum especially for a western citizen´s point a view. The history of the Vietnam War seen from another point of view -great!

reviews.author: telcom3
reviews.title: Hanoi Military History Museum
reviews.content: Closed on Mondays, I had to return on tuesday to visit the museum. Most of these tourist sites operated by the city government are closed on Mondays.

reviews.author: KNewms
reviews.title: An okay visit
reviews.content: This museum is just okay. There is a lot of information but it is very spread out between buildings. Liked the display of war planes and vehicles. Please note it does close in the middle of the day - check the opening times before you go!

reviews.author: TrickyPerth
reviews.title: Vietnam Military History Museum
reviews.content: This museum is well worth visiting. Spread over three buildings plus outdoor areas it shows the military history of Vietnam from many centuries ago up until the present day.The exhibits are explained in English and Vietnamese.If the history of the country is of interest then this is must to visit.

reviews.author: Philippa M
reviews.title: Unorganised and uninformative
reviews.content: After learning so much from the similar museum in Ho Chi Minh, I was looking forward to visiting this museum. However I don't feel as though I've learnt anything at all. The museum is huge but disjointed and badly organised. Thr signage is minimal so I'm not sure if I visited all the exhibits. There is very little information on the artifacts and this makes for an uneducational experience. The videos are in English but the English, accent and sound quality is so bad you can't hear anything. I wouldn't recommend coming hede unless you have a guide.

reviews.author: Zac
reviews.title: Very cool sight to see
reviews.content: This place was amazing ( I say this because I’m a war buff) wondering around seeing the different weapons tanks and letter from actual soldiers that they had records of was very neat! We spent probably 2 hours wondering around looking at all the different exhibits and enjoyed every moment! The history here is very new considering but cool because it seems like Vietnam has always been at war! The aircrafts stolen from the American army still had the serial numbers on it and were in near new condition! So cool to see authentic war memorabilia and so up close and person! Plus it was very reasonable at only 40,000 vnd! Would suggest to anyone visiting Hanoi!

reviews.author: Joy William M
reviews.title: Impressive
reviews.content: You can learn more not just about the “Vietnamese War” or “American War”, but also about another conflicts.

reviews.author: Vega
reviews.title: interesting
reviews.content: We actually appreciated the visit of ours to this particular museum, you will find a lot of things to see and also the different aircraft on display are extremely interesting, its definitely well worth the visit. The thing that is much to see, lots of things to realize. The aircraft on screen look extremely old. I thing individuals at that moment have rather difficult life

reviews.author: AliceTeresaW
reviews.title: If you like History
reviews.content: If you are going to Hanoi, I think this is one of the two museums I would visit. It gives one a totally different perspective of the war. Captions could use a little work as well as some as the signage but that is minor. Tip..avoid the weekend. We went on a Saturday and had at least 20 busloads of people doing the tour.

reviews.author: bjbsurrey
reviews.title: Well worth a visit.
reviews.content: At only 40,000 vnd this was good value - there are lots of displays both inside and out.  We got there for the 1pm opening and missed the crowds from the coaches on the inside but sadly caught up with them later.  Closed Mondays and Fridays.

reviews.author: dizzywombat
reviews.title: Easy going
reviews.content: Only the outside was accessible to the public when we went, but the military vehicles on show outside were quite impressive. Tickets very cheap.

reviews.author: Dadams1991
reviews.title: Impressive selection of military vehicles and equipment on display
reviews.content: Well worth a visit and especially with the small entrance fee of 40,000 vnd. Interesting to read about the many wars in the history of Vietnam and famous military leaders from centuries ago. There is an impressive selection of military planes, tanks, anti aircraft guns from both sides of the war on the outside. Plenty of guns, bombs, historical photographs on the inside. As well as a model of the chu chi tunnels and recreation of a jungle war scene.My only complaint is that some of the information boards have no translation from Vietnamese.

reviews.author: Kevinnn_Do
reviews.title: Stunning & Interesting
reviews.content: There are stunning & interesting  stories, history about military of Vietnam. From 1000 years ago to independent day 1975.The young guy like me haven't seen these things like that, just hear through my grandparents's story but today it's in front of my eyes. Love ittttt.Btw, I'm student who can speak English and I have had a lot of tours with foreigner friends. So if u want to hang out if you're in Hanoi, pls whatsapp me: +84 1268 032 478

reviews.author: Natasha L
reviews.title: Towering success!
reviews.content: Visited on a rainy Sunday afternoon so anything indoors was closed to the public, but there was still plenty to see outdoors. It was an impressive show of military weapons and vehicles from ancient cannons to large aircraft. I enjoyed that the ancient tower was right next to it so you could look down on everything while climbing a piece of history.

reviews.author: JLM3080
reviews.title: interesting collection
reviews.content: an interesting collection, but don't read the notes, the propaganda just drips out in a very distasteful manner. There are some great things to see though, so worth stopping off

reviews.author: ulangutan
reviews.title: Smashing Little Museum
reviews.content: Spent a couple of hours here. Very cool. Loads of displays from the Chinese, French & American wars.Well worth a few hours visit.Loads to see & very informative.

reviews.author: Michael E
reviews.title: Well worth a stop
reviews.content: A small but interesting museum showcasing a well maintained collection of vehicles. It’s well worth combining with a trip to the mausoleum (although go to the mausoleum first as the queue is larger and it closes earlier). I only spent 45 minutes here so it really is quick. The collection of American and French debris is a poignant reminder of the Vietnam/American war.

reviews.author: Piggy M
reviews.title: Government Propaganda - Interesting to see what it says
reviews.content: This museum listed out and showed exhibits that Vietnam encountered since ancient time.  But of course it uses a lot of space to show they fought against American "Imperialists".  It is expected Vietnam government uses this museum as propaganda, but it is interesting to see what the other side says.  Many outdoor exhibits, like cannons, tanks, and planes.  But it is special to show an American crash plane, and old flag tower, which you don't often find in other war museum.

reviews.author: Curtis S
reviews.title: Don’t worry about their spin on history, just enjoy the displays
reviews.content: I had noticed the planes in the courtyard while driving around in our tour bus. This museum was not part of the Gate 1 tour we were on so we visited by ourselves when we had time off. I am a big military history buff, especially where airplanes are involved. There are several buildings which attempt to chronologically explains Vietnam’s attempt to break from the French and the American “Sabotage” war. How they explain the war won’t line up with what we were taught in school but that’s because the US government wasn’t completely truthful. Regardless, walk through the various buildings, seeing artifacts from pre- and post-Vietnam war. The main courtyard has several planes, tanks, and artillery. Most plaques have an English explanation. I enjoyed it and you will too if you like militaria. Recommended.

reviews.author: Nigel G
reviews.title: Museum or kindergarten?
reviews.content: The content of the museum is good, but its lighting of galleries is questionable. Management need to get a grip on the number of children it allows in at any one time. The children are rowdy, ill disciplined and the teachers have little control. Whilst I agree children should visit museums to discover their heritage - all things in moderation.Essential in two parts - the colonial invasion and the struggle against the French and the retaliation defence to US aggression - the Vietnam war.Good exhibits and nice examples of military hardware including fighter aircraft from both sides. A MIG21 with distinguished career has been designated a national treasure. Some interesting sculptures in the garden.Nice coffee shop near the entrance - a shame about the blaring music. Admission to the museum includes admission to the Flag Tower also. I hope management will do more to limit the number of school children at any one time and ensure greater discipline. I live in Singapore and if a teacher took a group of children to a museum and they behaved as badly, there would be disciplinary action against the teacher.

reviews.author: Princessetami
reviews.title: Definitely worth it!
reviews.content: An excellent collection of relics and memorabilia laid out very well. Very glad we went. Well managed and preserved. Highly recommended

reviews.author: Me_n_my_rucksack
reviews.title: Chaotic scrapyard - the Museums rhetoric and tone are history themselves..... could be SO much better
reviews.content: We visited the museum a week or so after a US Navy Carrier group docked in Da Nang, after we had a coffee in Starbucks. So the rhetoric straight out of a 1980s Commusist propoganda poster which runs through this museum appears a thing of the past it's self. Ones forst impression is not good - the car park is a seething mass of people and coaches beeping their horns at each other to get parked or get out.The external exhibits, interesting though they are, do not sit an any order, are slowly decaying and the information is limited....  its an A6 intruder aircraft for example. (No info about what it did or if that one was captured at any place or the history of that aircraft etc etc...).  I have no idea why the large transport aircraft was there - and neither has wikipedia I have just looked - just assume they had one and so they put it there.The displays inside are equally dated...  some interesting artefacts such as parts of an F111 Jet and the like. Particularly impressive is the tank which rolled into the Government compound in Saigon at the very end of the conflict. However the rhetoric is so dated and one sided. One could say "Well - its a Vietnamese museum" - and it is - but many many Vietnamese opposed the Communists and the fate of many Cathoics and particularly Bhuddists go untold - they were Vietnamese and it was their was as well. This is the military history from a very narrow prespective. The West has to a great degree confronted its failings and wrongdoings and American Museums reflect that and show the conflict in a broad context.The hardware on display is fascinating - as a History buff I loved browsing the small items and relics (Esp from the 1st Indo China War). However in an age when US warships dock in peace at Da Nang, the Vietnamese flock to KFC and McDonalds as well as study in the US in great numbers the narrow Stalinist tones of the Museum do no justice to the Indochina wars which are complex subjects and not mere party propoganda. Worth a visit but could be far better organised, far more factual (as opposed to propoganda based) and the outside exhibits better explained,

reviews.author: Voxopus
reviews.title: Relics of hardware of warfare
reviews.content: Vietnam has had its fair share of conflict and war. A potted history is in many guide books. The Museum is both an indoor, room by room account of what's occurred throughout the ages and also an impressive collection of the machinery of wars that have occurred in more recent times. I had the pleasurable experience of falling in with a group of Vietnamese ex-servicemen and women that resulted in warm greetings and conversations, numerous photo opportunities, directed and posed to get best advantage and friendly chit chat amongst us, the tone and intonation of which carried the day as neither of us could understand the language of the other. We parted as a merry band of brothers in arms.

reviews.author: sherry s
reviews.title: A must see
reviews.content: This museum is so worth seeing, it was well set out with the history of the country over hundreds of years. As an Australian born in the 60's this museum gave an insight to the view point of the Vietnamese which I was unaware of. The displays are well set out with information given in not only Vietnamese but French and English. And don't be fooled when you first walk in that the exhibit is small as there are a number of buildings with history from different periods. Also be aware that most museums are closed for lunch and reopen around 1pm, so check before heading off.

reviews.author: Widlydidly
reviews.title: Great value museum with lots to see
reviews.content: Putting aside the rather too obvious focus on Vietnamese victories and glory the museum has many good displays, planes tanks etc. The are also a number of rooms with excellent exhibits not just from the American war but also further back in time. I really enjoyed this visit.

reviews.author: qualicumgirl
reviews.title: Reality check from the other side of the story
reviews.content: The huge display of captured helicopters, planes, arms, jeeps and the most astounding remake sculpture of the crashed B52 make this a one of a kind museum. Prepare to have your mind bent if not changed.  Seeing how the Vietnamese pulled together in what they know as their war of reunification (or The American War) it would have been impossible for the Americans to claim victory. The Vietnamese just cared too much for their country and their freedom. Inside the museum are the story of several wars, sluffing off the Chinese, the Japanese, the French and the Americans. It is wonderful to have information presented in English and French, Vietnamese. It is a sobering museum, but an essential one to really understand the zeitgeist of Vietnam.

reviews.author: GrannieE
reviews.title: Thought provoking
reviews.content: So glad we visited this place.  I was a little daunted at the thought of going but it was well worth it and brought to mind all the young men who lost their lives through war

reviews.author: kimwan83
reviews.title: Plenty to see if you explore
reviews.content: This Museum is deceptively small from the entrance. However it has several places to visit and different areas related to the sad 20th century history of Vietnam. Initially I was disheartened by what I saw as glorification of the weapons, until I walked through and listened to some of the presentations. Including the '3D' lights battle map display (with a video) that needs updating. I learned a lot and got a slightly more Vietnamese perspective on this war. Some refreshing of certain displays is required, but overall -after visits to other historical monuments in S.E Asia- I was not disappointed. I spent much more time here than I expected.

reviews.author: varun_mukthi
reviews.title: Fantastic
reviews.content: It's closed on a Monday and Friday. But they have a separate ticket to view the outside exhibits at 20k dong which is what we went for. It's a great place to spend 30 minutes walking around seeing the great American and Russian war vehicles used during the Vietnam war. We had a good experience and can definitely recommend this museum.

reviews.author: Dic D
reviews.title: Interesting, with much more potential
reviews.content: Was interesting to see all of the artifacts and learn about the history prior to the American War (yes, that’s what it’s called here) and the 3D video of them ending the French invasion was very interesting.A lot of information about how the American War came to a close, just wished we got more information about the initiation of the American War, as it’s something we only hear about from the US side typically.

reviews.author: Kevin R B
reviews.title: Warning! Avoid the taxis in front of Museums
reviews.content: Warning! Avoid the taxis in front of MuseumsThe taxis in front of the museum are a scam! If you absolutely must take a taxi. Negotiate the price first.Our taxi driver used a fake meter, and charged us 55 dollars US for a short trip.They will call out to you from the gate.The museum was fun, though small.

reviews.author: steve f
reviews.title: Interesting exhibits
reviews.content: Loads of relics from the War and a tour inside. By prepared to be blown away by the planes/tanks and helicopters on display. Gives a real authentic look at the War.

reviews.author: Karl C
reviews.title: make sure its open before setting off from your hotel
reviews.content: we set off to look around the museum but on arrival we were told we could only view whats outside, we were only charged half price but still worth it,

reviews.author: Tom A
reviews.title: Well laid out and wide range of exhibits
reviews.content: A good place to get a sense of the conflicts the Vietnamese people have lived through in the recent past.

reviews.author: salestraveler69
reviews.title: Difficult to see so much war
reviews.content: Wish Vietnam had other than war as History. The restaurant there was good for a quick bite and Vietnamese Coffee.

reviews.author: Liars N F
reviews.title: Where are the Vietnamese
reviews.content: I dropped in while on a business trip to Hanoi, and our hosts arranged a drop by of this museum.  Certainly, the sculpture made by wrecked aircraft and the collection of military equipment, ours and theirs, was interesting.  I also perused with interest the portions dealing with the war with the French, but also looked at the exhibits dealing with Chinese and Mongol invasions.But this was also an extremely sleepy museum, with a dearth of Vietnamese attendees.  Contrast this with the war memorial museum in Seoul, which has lots of Koreans....maybe because that war is not over.Whereas, thankfully, Vietnam is at peace.

reviews.author: bizdean
reviews.title: Vietnam Wars
reviews.content: Obviously the museum is shaded to the Vietnam prospective.  Which is Ok since it is their museum.  It was interesting to view the times that Vietnam was at war.  With the French, the Americans, and each other.  Worth a visit.

reviews.author: mowark
reviews.title: Very interesting museum
reviews.content: Great collection of artifacts mostly from Vietnams wars against colonialism. Always appreciate seeing history from a new perspective. Worth a visit for the small entrance fee.

reviews.author: Beesy1950
reviews.title: Great place to visit allow 2-3 hours to really enjoy it.
reviews.content: Entry fee was very modest 40K which included the flag tower. There are planes and tanks on display and the flag tower to go up.Ice cream is available when you need respite from the heat and walking around, we had coconut flavour for 10K VND

reviews.author: Sue V
reviews.title: Worth an hour or two
reviews.content: Some interesting vehicles, including a US plane that was shot down. It’s a good opportunity to see the flag tower up close and climb up it’s lower levels

reviews.author: Felipe42
reviews.title: Flashback to Vietnam-US war
reviews.content: Full of milititary equipment from the Vietnam-US war, this one of the few museums of Hanoi. Though is a nice place to visit is not in the standards of an excellent museu,

reviews.author: SQLRTD
reviews.title: interesting, lots to see
reviews.content: we meant to go to the citadel and ended up here by accident.  Lots of exhibits, planes, tanks, bombs, etc, some of them dramatically displayed.

reviews.author: hokenyu
reviews.title: Has seen better days
reviews.content: This museum does not do justice to Vietnam's proud military history. Overly reliant on photos despite the wealth of military artifacts that should be available, especially from 20th century conflicts. Makes mention of triumphs over imperial China, the Mongols, French, and US, but does not put the struggles into context. Could do a far better job of putting Vietnam's admirable military history on display.

reviews.author: Dean M
reviews.title: Interesting place with a rich history
reviews.content: This place should be bigger and house a lot more information and artefacts. Dont get me wrong, its well worth a visit and they do they best they can to tell their story but dont have the funds to do it better.I wouldnt have missed it and found it really interesting. Vietnam has been invaded by the Chinese, French, Japanese and Americans (and partners) then the Chinese again. They are tough and resilient and should be proud.

reviews.author: raghdashukri
reviews.title: Place Where You Know the Great Vietnam
reviews.content: This museum introduces the visitor to Great Vietnam. You feel more of respect to this  great country, to its proud people and to their great leader at that time, The Great Respected Ho Chi Minh

reviews.author: John A
reviews.title: Very interesting to see the the military equipment on display and to see the other side of the story.
reviews.content: We had an interesting visit to the Military History Museum, there is a lot of signage in english.  I would recommend it for anyone who has an interest in the war that took place not so long ago.  There is a lot of equipment and displays too see.  During our visit it was very busy for a while with bus tours but they don't stay long so if you have time you can enjoy the visit.

reviews.author: ArdsWorld
reviews.title: War history partly in EN, mostly in Vietnamese only
reviews.content: This museum is mostly about past wars until the end of the French ruling, and is set up rather poorly. Parts are translated into English, but I would say 40-60% is in Vietnamese only. The war remnants museum in HCMC is much more better structured , caters for non-Vietnamese visitors and is about the period 1945-1975 which is easier to understand.

reviews.author: Mehul Kirit Shah
reviews.title: National Museum
reviews.content: Vietnam’s military history extends back some two millennia, and this museum covers it on four buildings with interesting pieces. Item descriptions on museum exhibits are in Vietnamese, French, and English. On display outside are the ubiquitous MiG-21 jet fighter, T-54 tank, and many bombs and articles captured on Indochina and Vietnam wars.

reviews.author: Lost_Duck
reviews.title: Worth visiting
reviews.content: As a museum it could certainly benefit from better execution.The place is rather cluttered, like a military surplus garage, where all are just left as when parked. No kind of guide line or story told.The inside is more visual then fact based, and rather one-sided presented (as one should expect, was a hard fought war after all).However.It is daunting to stand by all of thise machines, that so many of us really only read about.Gives glimpse of the scale of the war, the stacking amount of resources poured into it on both sides... just sit and let it sink in.If you give it time and study the facts presented, even if rather one-sided, you will find fuel for thoughts in area usually not presented in western history... and never any harm in hearing the other side of any history.Interesting museum that helps give a slight better understanding of Vietnam today.

reviews.author: 306NatalieJ
reviews.title: A absolute must
reviews.content: This was one of our high lights even though it was heart breaking to see what these poor people have been through. At time I cried. But you have to go see it...

reviews.author: LetsGetLost_2Gether
reviews.title: Don't go if your American or French!
reviews.content: Another Museum dedicated to political messages rather than balanced fact.There's a strong Anti feeling throughout with some of the reporting a little light on the truth to say the least.The contents are moving, as with any war, but be prepared to only hear one side.

reviews.author: euromat
reviews.title: The inside was shut!
reviews.content: Sadly when we visited, this inside part to the museum was closed, as was the flag tower. Despite this, i enjoyed what was on display outside, it gave quite a good insight into the war. The displays had english translations too

reviews.author: Mark P
reviews.title: A Must Visit Location
reviews.content: If you don't know history, you are bound to repeat it. Great museum on the American War and a testament to the people who fought off western aggression and won...but at what a price? It was interesting to see how  children  of various ages were brought here to understand the war and what happened. Every American who visits Hanoi should visit this monument.

reviews.author: adventureaustralia
reviews.title: Plenty of planes, helicopters and tanks but difficult to follow the history
reviews.content: Museum has good war artifacts but unless you are already well versed in the history of war in Vietnam it was very difficult to follow the historic timeline and detail.

reviews.author: Claire Banks
reviews.title: Moving Place
reviews.content: We went here with our guide and found it a moving place to visitA real must if visiting Hanoi if your interested in history, military or the Vietnam war.

reviews.author: dguppy
reviews.title: Get another perspective
reviews.content: The museum is thematically laid out to reflect the four major stages of the war of liberation. The post world war 2 resistance to the French, the first US involvement, the guerrilla war in the south and then the final liberation campaigns. Major signage is untranslated, but all individual exhibits have full English translations. As expected the narrative celebrates thirty years of unremitting struggle and gives a central place to the Vietnamese fighters. You find no heroic enemy figures here, just as you find no  heroic  enemy figures in US museums. Some displays simply state some uncomfortable truths but are backed up by relevant artefacts. The outside vehicle and aircraft displays are not well protected. Somewhere between the mythology generated by  both sides lies the truth but this museum provides an opportunity to see the conflict from the perspective of the other side. Treat your visit with the respect it deserves.

reviews.author: Targaryen-Traveller
reviews.title: One to do to understand modern Vietnam
reviews.content: Incredible history of survival and struggle.  These museums and galleries within the complex explain the story of the Indo-China war with France and the Cold-war ERA against the USA told from the perspective of the Vietnamese.  A must visit for any traveller.  Only $2 entrance.  Food, toilets, and rest area available on site.

reviews.author: Joanne C
reviews.title: An interesting experience but lacked overall cohesion
reviews.content: An interesting experience but lacked overall cohesion in the story/stories it told. It was fascinating none the less.

reviews.author: marco c
reviews.title: Visiting museum
reviews.content: Nice place to remember the hystoric war between usa and Vietnami suggest the 3 floor and the second floor

reviews.author: Nansudesh
reviews.title: The military history museum visit was an afterthought for us and we never regretted it!
reviews.content: The kids enjoyed seeing place. There was a special inside showing the military history and put so well for kids to understand. The garden and museum is so well maintained too!

reviews.author: Maree774
reviews.title: Interesting place to visit
reviews.content: We found this to be an interesting museum. There are lots of war vehicles to look at and lots of information to read.

reviews.author: Ralph J
reviews.title: Disorganised
reviews.content: The museum is not unnaturally written from a North Vietnamese perspective and has some interesting exhibits but it is terribly dis organised and difficult to follow the timeline around the museum, simple signage would have helped. I would recommened a visit but maybe a guide or a map before you go would be helpful

reviews.author: Rosina M
reviews.title: men would love this tour
reviews.content: It was really interesting but did not really appeal to me or my sister because The history was very sad that these machines killed so many Vietnamese people and destroyed so much rich history of the people, such as villages, temples and pagoda's. Thousands of people in the north and south of Vietnam were brutilised and displaced from their homes because of the war and these machines. That's all I will say on this place.

reviews.author: Camelgirl43
reviews.title: Sobering
reviews.content: As an American who lived through the Vietnam war, we felt it was important to see this museum.  It was the last day of our 2 week trip to Vietnam and we're glad we took the time to look at it. A lot of it is boring, as a lot of museums can be if you aren't an expert in what you're looking at, especially the historical stuff. Vietnams struggles go back a thousand years fighting off invaders, and France and the U.S. were the last, so they get the biggest rooms.  Apparently, the museum was started in 1956. I did find it sad, particularly when you see Vietnam today and how they have moved on and created a vibrant society. I found the outside part really interesting with all the pieces of military equipment, mostly things they captured from the U.S. Well worth the visit.

reviews.author: Cazzarin
reviews.title: Underwhelming
reviews.content: Not worth the visit. A museum of artefacts thrown around the place. Much of the information in Vietnamese so inaccessible for the English tourist. Would have loved to learn more about the Vietnamese military history but due to the unorganisation of artefacts and lack of information I felt I came away from the museum knowing nothing more than when I entered. A missed opportunity.

reviews.author: kyra_ha23
reviews.title: Great!
reviews.content: Loved seeing all the planes, helicopters and tanks. They have some really cool stuff here! The English translations are hilarious and really made my day for a lot of them. Definitely would have enjoyed a guide or something to read while we were walking around, a lot of the artifacts had no translation and a lot of the areas didn't have explanations for why they were in certain areas but I still enjoyed it more then some of the other museums in Hanoi.

reviews.author: nataliesX5076KR
reviews.title: Cool stuff but poorly executed
reviews.content: The artifacts are not set up in a logical order and the English descriptions are terrible. We were making the most of it but were rushed out, rather rudely, by an employee at 16:30 saying the museum is closed.

reviews.author: Nitieman
reviews.title: Fabulous and must visit
reviews.content: Quite big and has a wide collection.You can also see some remains during the US-Vietnam war.The tower in front can get you some nice views and nice clicks (selfies).The entry ticket is a bit on a higher side though

reviews.author: DCTravelers69
reviews.title: Interesting...
reviews.content: Definitely an interesting display of the citadel, planes, past battles. Vietnam has had a tumultuous past and it is shown here.

reviews.author: CaliCo2455
reviews.title: Not worth it!
reviews.content: Unless one has a real reason to go to this tourist attraction, I do not recommend it.I found it boring, uninspiring and very subjective... don't waste your time.

reviews.author: Steve33328
reviews.title: Must do if you like history. Vietnam - France & Vietnam - USA
reviews.content: Depending on your interest I would suggest anywhere from 1 hour to whatever you need.  Easy to get to by taxi for the old quarter.  I liked it a lot.

reviews.author: Twoyorkie
reviews.title: november visit
reviews.content: Gives you an insight as to the horrors that the Vienamese people had to endure..............everyone should visit and read/look/and sympathize

reviews.author: Anurag Nirmal
reviews.title: One of the places to see in Hanoi
reviews.content: We visited the museum in December. The entry ticket is 40.000 Vnd for one adult. There is lot of historical pictures, artifacts, and story available from 100 BC to modern wars. Also there are real models of aircrafts, cannons, etc from US Navy, US Airforce and Vietnam Forces. One can visit the museum if nothing else to do in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Brufsters
reviews.title: A Different Perspective
