reviews.content: Visited military history museum in November this year. Overall experienve was quite good, though the parts with Vietnam war stuff were filled with too much propaganda. Historical parts (pre 19th century) were more interesting to my taste.

reviews.author: noone28
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: This was one of the better museums we went to in Vietnam on the subject of military history. It had a bigger collection of planes and tanks, from both sides rather than just US and had a much clearer, linear narrative about the military history of Vietnam than other museums. We only had about 90mins before it closed, which was a shame because that wasn’t quite enough time to see everything, even though some areas were currently being renovated.

reviews.author: NinaTom
reviews.title: Always good to get another perspective.
reviews.content: A lot of the signs are translated into English and French, and a lot of this museum is visual anyway. For anyone who likes a bit of military hardware, there's plenty to float your boat here.I would recommend reading up on the history of Vietnam over the past 100 years before visiting as this would help put the museum into some context. It is of course coming from the Vietnamese point of view and therefore seem to can lack balance; this also adds to the intrigue for those of us brought up on a western version of history.

reviews.author: Lucy M
reviews.title: army and independence
reviews.content: I didn't understand how hard the Vietnamese were subjugated by various external forces until I came here. Between the French, Japanese, Chinese and Americans, those poor people suffered. The Vietnamese were stoic. A small taste of their suffering over the last 160 years. I really learnt something here.

reviews.author: Rod R
reviews.title: The American fascist war
reviews.content: The items on display are good, with the central points being the flag tower and a piece meal collection put together with a large photo of a peasant "hero" standing ontop a B52 after it was shot down. Lots of propaganda, but very interesting displays. We spent most of the day going right through this place. History from early dynasties through to where the world supported the war against the puppet south and the aggressive Americans, with news clipping showing how most of the world supported the liberation army (two papers showing Vietnam protests in Australia and many others from all over the world). very interesting.

reviews.author: awayoverthere
reviews.title: Better out than in
reviews.content: For me, the outdoor part of this museum is far better than the indoor section.The indoor sections have various items from previous wars / conflicts which are interesting enough to see.  The outdoor part of the museum has a US helicopter, fighter planes, tanks and the wreckage of a jet that the Vietnamese shot out of the sky during the war.

reviews.author: LME_aus01
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: Having read a few reviews of this attraction on trip advisor I didn't go with high hopes - or with the expectation of being able to understand anything for that matter!! However, I was pleasantly surprised to find that enough of the museum content had been translated to English for my husband and I to understand. Having an understanding of the history of war in Vietnam definitely helps but isn't necessary if you enjoy looking at war time artifacts.Many other reviews had said how good the view was from the flag tower but disappointingly this wasn't open on the morning we visited. Definitely a good way to spend an hour or so appreciating the war torn history of this country.

reviews.author: David R
reviews.title: Almost interesting, but disappointing
reviews.content: Unfortunately this museum has some stuff to look at, there is a lot that isn't translated into English or any other language. We didn't get the audio guide - maybe we should have, but a review stated that it was only for a couple of sections.The building for section 3 is currently being redone, so we didn't get to see that. The main thing missing for me was context and the story behind the things on display.  I leaned a LOT more via Wikipedia after we had left - as I didn't have mobile access. I think some of the signs that weren't translated into English would have described what we were seeing and why it was important, but without that it was a waste of time (but at least not very much money).Definitely a disappointment after the women's museum the day before, which was much more professional and told a clear story.

reviews.author: Yori R
reviews.title: Interesting museum
reviews.content: Pretty interesting display outside with planes, tanks, bombs, etc. The inside display is also quite good although it lacks of english explanation. Given its extensive military campaigns, military history is a big part of the country's history and well worth a visit.

reviews.author: wajihb
reviews.title: Favorite part of Hanoi, but!
reviews.content: The museum is by far my most favorite part f my visit to Hanoi, especially that i love history and enjoy the sight of tanks and fighting jets.The outer part of the museum is much better and has a good collection of heavy weapons, they even tell you how the captured these weapons from the Americans and shot down the plane. But the part inside the building was not so much, mostly documents and belongings of Vietnamese generals. part of it was under renovation.the flag tower had the best view, over looking the heavy weapons and part of the city, there are bombs and cannons from the Vietnamese war and 18th century.

reviews.author: Graeme25
reviews.title: Even my wife sort of enjoyed it!
reviews.content: I love all this stuff so a true test for others out there is how your wife views it. So with some trepidation I dragged my darling wife here and amazingly she thought it was pretty good!! There is a fair bit to see, quite a lot outside, especially big military vehicles and planes etc and quite a bit inside the buildings.It has the tank that broke through the gates of the reunification palace in Saigon and a lot of artefacts from the various wars.For us it was worthwhile. Easy to get to and not overpriced by our standards.If you want to kill a couple of hours in hanoi and have nothing better to do it is worth the effort.

reviews.author: bbycutie
reviews.title: Interesting Military and army museum
reviews.content: I visited this museum on my recent trip to Hanoi. Admission charge of 40,000 VND applies. I am not a big fan of army and military weapons and such, however my hubby was. The museum is of a good size with displays situated in different buildings. Outside stands a tall flag tower and next to it large military planes, choppers and missile launchers. It does not tell much of the war history but has a good variety of weapons display. Worth a visit at least once if you are in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Andrew N
reviews.title: Definitely worth the Visit
reviews.content: A Bit wet at this time of the year, but still worth the effort to see a part of VIETNAMESE History that my generation lived through.

reviews.author: PolepoleGirl
reviews.title: Lots of things to look at
reviews.content: Museum exhibits are spread out in a number of buildings which is sometimes hard to follow, but the highlight of this museum is definitely the tanks, planes, etc...that are on the grounds. There are many pieces on the grounds that you can look at and explore. Also, I found this museum to have the least amount of propaganda over other museums I went to in Vietnam (both in the north and south).

reviews.author: James C
reviews.title: Pleasantly surprised
reviews.content: Took my 12 year old daughter as well. Enough to keep her interested and also learning and appreciating the history of events.  Planes and tanks were a big hit. Easy to get to and a must to see.

reviews.author: Jonhnathane
reviews.title: Impressive stories of vanquishing technologically superior foes.
reviews.content: Hanoi's Military History Museum is the standout of Vietnam's numerous war museums. There's plenty it lacks in terms of narrative and English language descriptions. But it's a great place to get the winner's official take on battles against the French and the US backed South Vietnamese government. The museum is located a short walk from Ba Dinh Square and sits opposite this park with what must be one of the most well placed Lenin statues left in the world.

reviews.author: TruongAnhTuan
reviews.title: Understanding the history
reviews.content: I is quite nice to understand the history of Vietnam, a history of flighting back to invaders to keep our independent and freedom. You will understand why and how a small race like Vietnam can win over strong and big enemies like China (a lot of times), France, US, etc. We have the truth.

reviews.author: gwygal
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: We visited here in August 2014 and we're pleasantly surprised at how big it was.We enjoyed looking at the old tanks and planes and taking a walk up the flag tower. There were plenty of good picture opportunities! Within the museum there were information cards, war artifacts and a short film.We managed to spend about 90 minutes here and this was much better than the army museum in Ho Chi Minh City.

reviews.author: Doro M
reviews.title: Quite disappointing
reviews.content: The museum was poorly engaging the visitors.  The videos were only available for groups of 10 people and from what we could see it was only in vietnamese. The route was unclear and the employees had no attention, or decide, to help visitors: they were too preoccupied with their mobile phones.

reviews.author: Kevin P
reviews.title: But the audioguide!!!
reviews.content: Well laid out museum which comes alive when you spend an extra 40000 doing and buy the audiophile. Many stories and descriptions are on this in multi languages.The museum is in 2 parts and the only thing that stops me giving this a 5 is that the audioguide only covers the first part.

reviews.author: SymJon
reviews.title: Not what you expect and so disappointing
reviews.content: While marketed to tourists, nothing is translated so you walk around lost and confused trying to make sense of what all the artefacts represent. We were so disappointed and we got the sense that this place was all about taking tourist's money and not about sharing the harrowing stories of combat and respecting the Vietnamese army. Unfortunately we left disappointed and underwhelmed, we would recommend skipping this museum!

reviews.author: MrPKI
reviews.title: Good for learning the history of the Vietnam army
reviews.content: It only costs a few dollars to enter and a few dollars more to take pictures, but it is not a bad museum.  It has a lot of artifacts from the WWII era, fighting the French occupation and then the Vietnam war.  Most of the exhibits have English placards to explain what they are.  Overall, it is not a bad stop for 90 minutes to check out a lot of captured equipment and downed planes in addition to all the different weapons that were used in the war.  Some of the helmets and gear from downed US pilots was hard to see, but it gives you a different perspective from the other side of the war.

reviews.author: MikeyP7987
reviews.title: Pretty Interesting
reviews.content: Our visit to the Army Museum was a bit of a 'Brucie bonus' for me. When planning our trip to Vietnam, there was an element of compromise to be made. We only had ten days and so I couldn't dominate our time with all things Vietnam Conflict/ American War (the terminology is based on where in Vietnam you are from, as the South Vietnamese played a massive part in the conflict too). On our way from the Presidential Palace to the Temple of Literature we decided that we were in need of a refreshment (Vietnamese coffee is amazing), and just happened to find ourselves next door to the Army Museum, so why not visit it too? It would be rude not to. The museum traces the history of the Vietnamese Army from its origins to present day, and bits of it are quite cheesy, like the mock up of a jungle trail, but it is cute. They also have quite a bit of equipment left behind by the Americans like a Huey, a Chinook, a couple of tanks and APCs, but for me, the highlight was a short film that they put on regarding the Battle of Dien Bien Phu. There is also a large diorama that depicting the base at Dien Bien Phu, and as the narrator explains the battle, little LEDs light up showing where the action took place. I didn't know much about the battle prior to this, but when watching things about the siege at Khe Sanh there were many references to the similarities between the two battles, and the diorama showed that perfectly. Many other museums would benefit by following the same idea.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: A bit disappointing
reviews.content: This museum is basically a collection of military objects from the American war. There are no guided tours and the museum doesn't really seek to explain the war. If you don't know the history of the war beforehand, you still won't after.Having said that, it is interesting to be able to wander under helicopters and planes and around tanks from the war.The toilets are to be avoided if at all possible as they were pretty unpleasant when we visited.

reviews.author: BenAndTash
reviews.title: Interesting but limited English.
reviews.content: The best part about this museum is the displays of war planes and tanks in the outside area. The museum exhibits information and stories from many wars throughout history, however it is difficult to gain a comprehensive understanding of the history due to the lack of information in languages other than Vietnamese. If you decide to go here, try to pick a cool day as it is very hot and muggy inside the buildings, with no air circulating. If you want to take any photos at all during your visit, you must pay a compulsory fee at the entrance. The attraction would be made so much better if the information was displayed in languages other than Vietnamese. Interesting for a morning out.

reviews.author: Oana
reviews.title: Interesting, but not very well structured
reviews.content: Interesting museum, but do not expect a comprehensive war museum, as the details on the reality of American war or comments in English are minimal.There are some projectors and monitors to present videos, but when we requested to watch some, he were screamed at a very agressive "NO". Obviously, governmental staff not in the mood to be interrupted from tapping on their phones.

reviews.author: Deb N
reviews.title: Visit this museum
reviews.content: I have been to hanoi a number of times and this museum is high on my list of visits, as well as one I recommend to friends. Although not all information is in my language, English, it is very visual. There are exhibits both inside and outside. Photos, weaponry, stories, planes....It is not just the story of the American (Vietnam) war, but of Vietnamese struggles and victories throughout their history. There is a flag tower, very old with stairs inside that can be climbed. My particular favourite is the diorama of Dien Bien Phu. This is in English, as well as Vietnamese and Chinese. It is accompanied by the story and original film footage. It is a large museum, so when you get tired, thirsty or want a break, there is a very good coffee shop on the grounds.

reviews.author: iejan
reviews.title: Interesting museum to visit :)
reviews.content: My husband and I find that this museum is quite interesting with many war planes and tanks displayed. If you are into war and history, this place is one of the must visit. We love the plane wreckage in the museum compound. It was such an epic display.

reviews.author: ofriedm
reviews.title: Redundant but interesting
reviews.content: Poor narrative structure, but cool relics from the French Indochina War, the American War and the Vietnam War with the Khmer Rouge

reviews.author: ivan l
reviews.title: minimal english description
reviews.content: most of the display are written in vietnamese. we left with half the time not knowing what was displayed. the display date backs to early days like the 11th century. this place is also very stuffy! a few static planes were displayed in the museum. there is also a flag tower to climb if you are keen.overall nothing much of interest. if pressed for time, better to skip this.

reviews.author: Kiwi P
reviews.title: great collection
reviews.content: for a different view on the Vietnam war this was worth a look. It has an interestring collection of US army tanks and planes etc so for me a war buff i enjoyed it.

reviews.author: brandasa
reviews.title: Great outside display
reviews.content: The inside was okay - not a lot of English and no real "story."  The coolest part was out back where there was a few planes to see, as well as a large bombed down plan display.  Won't take more than an hour.

reviews.author: CosmosTravelVietnam
reviews.title: Exciting to explore
reviews.content: This museum is worthy of your time in Hanoi. We Cosmos Travel Vietnam co., ltd recommend Military History Museum to travelers from France, Australia and the USA. You can learn how Vietnamese people fight for independance all the time

reviews.author: Jay
reviews.title: A lot of good exhibits, not a lot of English...
reviews.content: The exhibits here were very well done.  There were many different types of weapons, from spears all the way to tanks and everything in between, which I enjoyed.  There was some english translations, but not as much as I would expect for this type of museum.  The outside exhibits of the bombers and tanks were great.  The most interesting exhibits weren't actually the ones about the Vietnamese-American War, but were actually about the independence war fought by the Vietnamese with France.  I thought that was especially interesting as I had not known much about the conflict before I visited.  One of the best things we did in Hanoi.

reviews.author: margatemum
reviews.title: Great walk through Vietnams conflict history
reviews.content: Vietnam has had a very torrid history of conflict and here they have catalogued it all.The highlights are the planes/tanks/bombs mainly from the American conflict which whilst interesting do leave you a little sad!But I would recommend especially if you have children as they will like the army memorabilia.

reviews.author: ChacmoolsFriend
reviews.title: Very little in English
reviews.content: I know it's a Vietnamese museum, but as a tourist attraction (especially when a large part is about the Vietnam-America conflict), I suppose I expected to have the faintest idea of what the displays were about.  A LOT of material in there, just don't know what any of it was.  If you're going there (as an American) for clarity/to see propaganda/another view of the war, I'm afraid you won't have much luck unless you speak the local language. The destroyed/captured planes and tanks in the courtyard are a reminder, though: war is hell.

reviews.author: Jak x
reviews.title: Awful Racist Staff, worst experience in Hanoi, Dont bother!
reviews.content: Just arriving to the ticket counter I knew this was going to be a typical tourist money trap when I had to pay an extra $2 for bringing a camera in with me. I was somewhat annoyed when the women at the ticket counter couldnt even stop chatting with her colleague long enough to take my money. But fair enough it could have been important. I then proceeded to walk to the entrance but a member of staff ran out shouting incomprehensible Vietnamese to me, which after some confusion and pointing made it clear that I was not allowed to bring the backpack I was wearing into the museum. There was no reason given for this and all the lockers available to store my backpack were ridiculously small, so I was told I had to leave it on the floor, out in the open, outside the museum. I then noticed other tourists there did have their backpacks on but I was told 'they Vietnamese, you foreign, you leave backpack'. Since I didn't fancy having my belongings stolen I decided to leave instead, and asked for a refund but the women who had literally just sold me then tickets said she couldn't refund them as they were fake tickets!!!. This place has single handedly ruined Hanoi for me and paints an awful picture of Vietnamese people. DO NOT GO HERE. The B52 museum down the road is much friendlier!

reviews.author: androidsdream
reviews.title: Feels like a missed opportunity though some interesting artefacts
reviews.content: This museum has the potential to be amazing but unfortunately most of the exhibitions are very dated looking and due to the lack of english information seem to jump about without any coherent narrative. Expected to be educated on the Vietnamese perspective of the numerous 20th century conflicts but came away none the wiser. The collection of tanks and planes is interesting although it would be better if you could actually see or sit in them. Most of the museum isn't really air conditioned so its hot. So overall unless you like tanks and planes probably try other attractions over this first.

reviews.author: Zenobia K
reviews.title: Recommended
reviews.content: For those who are genuinely interested in the history and wars of Vietnam, this is a definitely recommended visit. It was part of the half day city-tour and the entrance tickets are very reasonably priced. The Museum is maintained very well and has aircondition which makes the visit comfortable in the hot months. The detailed war history of Vietnam is spread across different floors and different rooms topic-wise and good detailed explanations in English make it a very interesting read. Must visit if interested.

reviews.author: Barneyannie
reviews.title: Interesting items, not well explained.
reviews.content: After the outstanding but harrowing museum in Ho Chi Min city, this was a little disappointing. More everyday items on display, and the English explanations were not very clear or well written at all. Museum seems to be targeted at locals (there were many school groups while we were there).The open air display was interesting if you like looking at military equipment.The early sections covering the very early invasions by the Mongols and others seemed very interesting, but the English explanation was so poor in translation and so short it was difficult to understand much of what was displayed.If you have the chance to visit the Museum at Ho Chi Min, skip this one as it is far inferior.

reviews.author: Darren O
reviews.title: Wow so much history in 1 place!
reviews.content: It was closed on the first day we went and we tossed up whether or not to head back the following day as we were running out of time, we are so glad we decided to return.So much to look at spread out over several buildings, overwhelmed at the sheer amount of artifacts to check out and the information to absorb, definately worth the visit.

reviews.author: robby321
reviews.title: Absolutely Stunning Planes and Tanks
reviews.content: I love the amazing actual planes, helicopters, tanks, missile launchers (with missiles), and APCs on display outside. I really liked the MiGs they have too!

reviews.author: MaestraM
reviews.title: Captured US planes
reviews.content: We spent most of our time looking at the outdoor displays of captured US planes and tanks, including one that is completely destroyed but propped up to resemble its former shape. (My husband is a pilot and enjoys seeing planes, in particular.)  Although there isn't much labeling, he was able to tell what most everything was. We also looked at many of the inside exhibits, which were quite good. For Americans of our age group, the Vietnam war was very important, and it was interesting to see the Vietnamese take on it.  For former military personnel, especially those who fought in the war, it might be disturbing to see the captured US planes and tanks.

reviews.author: Christina P
reviews.title: recommended!
reviews.content: vietnam is famous for war, everybody know it. but when i come here it is al displayed in museum, in real life, people are very friendly!

reviews.author: Peter L
reviews.title: Underwhelming
reviews.content: It was OK, but I guess we had hoped for a little more.  The inside stuff was quite good with some interesting items on show from past conflicts, but the outdoor planes and tanks were what we came for an they were, well, fairly rubbish if I am honest.  Not much description, and would be nice to have been able to see inside one or two of them-perhaps we came with too high expectations.  Off to saigon tomorrow and hopefully their museum will be better.  A point of note, the Hanoi museum is actually OK for kids-nothing too gruesome on show (unlike Saigon apparently).

reviews.author: Calvin D
reviews.title: Great for lovers of Tanks and Planes
reviews.content: decent place to visit 30000 per person and 40000 for a cameralots of tanks , planes etc to viewAlot of old war history although no where near as good as the museum in Ho chi minhWell worth a visitbe warned they close the internal exhibits  from 1130 - 1 for lunch so get there early

reviews.author: Robert R
reviews.title: Worth seeing another viewpoint.
reviews.content: As a child watching Walter Cronkite give snippets of the Vietnam conflict, I got a clear American viewpoint.  This series of buildings will give you a view from the Hanoi side of things.  As would be expected this is clearly a nationalistic presentation giving insight to that perspective.  It is a stark reminder walking out among French and American artifacts on display that any war has victors, victims, and vanquished.  To this I would add a trip to West Lake to see remnants of an American jet that crashed and though not a tourist destination, Bach Mai hospital that in years past used to have images of the destruction when it was bombed during the conflict.  A somber, sobering experience; but glad I went.

reviews.author: roslena8
reviews.title: Military Magnet
reviews.content: My family consisted of 4 males and 3 females.   The males loved it.  The weaponry, armored vehicles, fighter jets and historical events made their day.  They couldn't get enough of it all.   Not  that the females were less susceptible.   We were impressed and enthralled as well.  Just a reminder - the internal  part of the museum closes at 11.30am for lunch.   Practically, everything stops.   However, the external exhibition is still open during lunchtime.

reviews.author: Ashley80550
reviews.title: Good Museum
reviews.content: The museum is quite large with many different displays. Some displays were better than others. Being from America it was a little difficult looking at the helicopter and airplanes they kept as well as the crashed plane. I know people that fought in the war so it felt odd looking at that sort of thing and taking pictures. They also kept some planes and chinooks that we actually left at the airport. Overall, I would recommend visiting this place.

reviews.author: Kay H
reviews.title: Only bettered by the Women's Museum
reviews.content: Give yourself plenty of time to discover the Chinese and Mongol invaders, French, Khmer Rouge and American wars.  Three interesting floors - some of the photograph labelling might make American visitors feel uncomfortable, as would some of the photographs.  Outside displays of military equipment are sure to appeal to lovers of modern military history.

reviews.author: Verobecker
reviews.title: Interesting
reviews.content: This museum was very interesting for my husbund, instead it wasnot attractive for me. For people that really likes the theme. Award, it closes at 11.00 (for lunch) and opens at 13.30 hrs.

reviews.author: marijnnl
reviews.title: No basic information
reviews.content: We went to the museum to learn something about the vietnam wars, of which we know very little. There were a lot of items and photographs from several battles, but no basic info about those battles. Without this context, it was all quite meaningless for us. So I can't say we learnt anything. The outside display of planes and tanks was impressive though.

reviews.author: Emily C
reviews.title: Meh
reviews.content: It was ok... Not too expensive.The English translation at times was very poor and it doesn't really teach u about the war. It felt more like Vietnam showing off with random items. But it wasted a little time and some of it is pretty cool, like the planes and chinook they have out the back!

reviews.author: Barb893
reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.content: Such a great place very interesting,but make sure you leave yourself a lot of time,cause a lot of government building close at eleven thirty till one thirty pm in Hanoi .

reviews.author: kmclatchie
reviews.title: Fantastic museum if your with your group (never been discriminated against for being a couple)
reviews.content: Im sure you could learn alot at this museum if there were tour guides available for individuals or couples... but apparently only available for groups!  Never had such a disappointing experience at a museum.  Again probably would be alot better if you had a solid grounding in vietnamese history, which unfortunately neither of us had. Left the museum none the wiser even  though there are english panels against most artefacts there needs to be more than that in order to understand the full history.  Very uninterested staff that were extremely unhelpful to add to the disappointment.

reviews.author: AlbertaRN
reviews.title: Well worth the few dollar entry fee
reviews.content: Stumbled across this museum on our walk through Hanoi.  My husband love this museum, with all the artifacts and historical displays.  Quite a large museum complex with lots of different buildings to see.  Huge signage isn't the greatest, so we did a bit of backtracking, but not terrible overall.  Any of the video displays are not in English, so has to skip out on those.  Very cheap price to pay for what you get and even I enjoyed it.  $1.50 extra fee if you want to use your camera to take pics throughout the complex.

reviews.author: Shellie L
reviews.title: Some interesting exibits
reviews.content: We found the place quite interesting, covered mostly the war against the French and the USA. Also some info about feudal wars. The old planes, helicopters ect were worth a look. It was only a couple of dollars to enter. Well worth a look while in Hanoi.

reviews.author: Martk82
reviews.title: Amazing piece of history
reviews.content: Going to this museum was a really nice experience, the museum contains real life artifacts of previous combat tanks, military airplanes and all sorts of vehicles and other machinery. Numerous items within the museum were collected after the Viet-Nam war which gives a unique feel to the items displayed there. Additionally there are photographs displayed of Martyrs who fought the war, which i thought were very deep and meaningful photos.

reviews.author: mamoore1953
reviews.title: The museum was fairly rustic which enhanced its appeal.
reviews.content: set in a great building the museum was very cheap and gave a feeling of the hardship the vietnamese must have gone through.the large tanks, cannons and rockets were very impressive. Well worth a visit.

reviews.author: lsmkw
reviews.title: Felt it
reviews.content: As someone who remembers that awful period, I found myself feeling down, sad for the lost lives on both sides, and as a patriot, sad to find my country on the wrong side of history. The photos, exhibits and downed planes, helicopter, tanks made it real for me in a way that the history/revolution museum and Hoa Lo prison did not.

reviews.author: Fredrik N
reviews.title: Yes and there was these wars...
reviews.content: Vietnam is a country where you inevitable will come in contact with the wars and of course Ho Chi Minh. When it comes to the wars this museum in Hanoi is a good place to visit. They have lots of objects on display although the facilities in it self and some of the objects need some attention, but that is secondary. You will find aircrafts, weapons and vehicles from the US war and also some history about the colonial war before that all from the point of view of the Vietnamese.This museum had the greatest amount of objects on display, but I would recommend trying to find your way to the B52 victory museum as well. This museum is the only one I've visited that charges you an extra fee for your camera, translated to your currency it is not much, but it feels like a strange foreigner tax though. Most likely they wont check up on you if you've paid for the camera or not, I however did pay.

reviews.author: Marijke L
reviews.title: A Different View of the Vietnam Conflict
reviews.content: The museum has a number of interesting artifacts including the conflict with the French colonialists, but I found the most interesting artifacts outdoors towards the rear of the museum and included a number of planes and tanks used against or captured from the US forces during the Vietnam War.It is a good museum to look at the conflict from a different perspective.

reviews.author: denise2113
reviews.title: Worth the visit
reviews.content: After growing up in the US in the 60s-70's we felt that visiting this museum was something we should do while in Hanoi.  It was very interesting seeing things written from the "other" perspective.  The displays were excellent as well as the planes, tanks, artillary, etc.It was a very emotional visit, but one well worth taking.

reviews.author: Michael T
reviews.title: Period of history
reviews.content: I don't understand reviews saying this is not worthwhile. Especially if you grew up in the 60's and 70's in the US. Visit Han Lo prison before or after. Good displays inside and clearly documented. I didn't realise how small the planes, tanks and other armoury were till I got up close. As many Vietnamese visitors as tourists. As per a review I read, be sure to go way out back to the Chinook and other planes. You can look through the fence to the huge garden as well. I did stop along the way at a street near train line. Cheap beer and good food. Go, with google maps.

reviews.author: Bob H
reviews.title: US tax payers dollars on display
reviews.content: The collection of seized US military equipment underlines the futility of war and the horrendous money invested in killing machines.  Although the museum exhibits both Vietnamese and US relics from the 'American' war (as it is known here) you can't help but think that this place is a sorry reminder of human failings.

reviews.author: Zoeee_1234
reviews.title: A bit disappointing
reviews.content: The outside area is probably more interesting than the inside. We loved the planes etc on the outside then when we ventured inside it was a real anticlimax. It could do with a bit more effort. I'd say it's worth a visit anyway.

reviews.author: ArtyGr
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: This has the potential to be a very good museum, since the collection is impressive. However, there are many descriptions of the individual objects without any context of the bigger picture of the various wars and their backgroun, causes and consequences. This has the potential to be a very good museum, since the collection is impressive. However, there are many descriptions of the individual objects without any context of the bigger picture of the various wars and their backgroun, causes and consequences. The distribution of exhibits over several buildings and several floors enhances the sense of chronological dislocation that the visitor quickly succumbs. The two diarama's are officially only switched on for a minimum of ten people. The intense efforts of the attendants to enhance their personal beauty and to remain submerged in their iPod games adds to the general aura of fatigue and disinterest. As historians, I had this museum visit as one of the highest priorities on my list for Hanoi, but, military hardware notwithstanding, I left extremely disappointed. In this age of ICT, fabulous ways of displaying history cheaply and effectively, this museum is in desperate need of a makeover by some young people with imagination, flair and commitment.  distribution of exhibits over several buildings and several floors enhances the sense of chronological dislocation that the visitor quickly succumbs. In this age of ICT, fabulous ways of displaying history cheaply and effectively, this museum is in desperate need of a makeover by some young people with imagination, flair and commitment.

reviews.author: Photo G
reviews.title: Worth a visit
reviews.content: Interesting to see the military items on display here and also interesting to see the information and propaganda on the wars from the perspective of the Vietnamese. Entry fee is next to nothing.

reviews.author: AussieAbroad011
reviews.title: Definately worth visiting.
reviews.content: This was a little hard to find. Apparently not many taxi drivers know where it is. It was about 15 minutes in a taxi from Old Quarters area. There's 2 military museums. If you arrive at one that has war planes, trucks etc out the front then you're at the right one. The entry fee was minimal and well worth it. To our surprise out in the open with no protection from the elements were military artefacts. You can walk right up to them and touch them. There's plaques on each item detailing it's relevance and role. Make sure you go inside the museum too. It's easy to get sidetracked by the amazing things outside but if you go inside you'll see a captured Russian fighter plane in perfect condition and it's got a ladder which you can climb up and into the plane, pull the lid shut and pose for photos! No way would you be able to do that anywhere else!

reviews.author: crazy_k_2014
reviews.title: Well worth a visit
reviews.content: This is well worth a visit even for non history buffs! It takes you through the ages through the lens of the Vietnamese army! There are some splendid propaganda items from the War in the 60s and 70s which are fascinating to look at with hindsight!

reviews.author: kwasiqtown
reviews.title: Boys afternoon out
reviews.content: Good afternoons entertainment while the ladies shoppedVery impressive. Great exhibits well presented.

reviews.author: Pat H
reviews.title: A journey back in time
reviews.content: I barely missed going to be at moms during the war. This is a must-see attraction. There's lots of Soviet and Chinese made tanks and weapons as well as American made tanks and planes and destroyed B-52

reviews.author: Rick C
reviews.title: Good museum
reviews.content: I think this is worth the time. Of not for anything else, a reminder that war is horrific and the west made some poor choices getting involved in the issue. This definitely isn't the museum's intention....it's a 'patriotic' look at the success of the North against the US and the the South. The displays are generally quite impressive.

reviews.author: Exmouthviet
reviews.title: Worth a visit while in Hanoi
reviews.content: May not interest all,but I was impressed with the citadel tower,history of many centuries the country has experienced war & still come out resilient,forgiving & sharing.

reviews.author: Stolid
reviews.title: Very moving
reviews.content: This is a must visit to remember what hardships war can cause to the innocent children. Horror photos but by viewing we will remember before condoning war.It's the children that suffer the most. We had wet eyes on leaving here.

reviews.author: Michael B
reviews.title: Contrast between historic citadel tower and war relics
reviews.content: Situated in the heart of Hanoi in the grounds of the historic Hanoi Citadel Tower, this museum traces the long struggle of the Vietnamese people for independence and freedom. From the ancient battles to the more recent and better known American / Vietnam War, there is a vast assortment of weapons, tanks, aircraft and bombs. It demonstrates just how resilient and resourceful the Vietnamese people were and still are. I notice that a lot of reviewers are critical of the fact that there are few English translations and that few staff speak English. In my opinion these tourists are missing the point. Don't forget that this country was almost bombed out of existence by the USA B52's and then the Americans imposed heavy sanctions for decades after losing the war, killing many more people by starvation. It is only in recent years that Vietnam has started to recover. English tuition is not readily available and the Tourist Industry is still learning. Everything is in Vietnamese ! - How odd - This is Vietnam! Enjoy the experiences this beautiful country and these beautiful people have to offer.

reviews.author: Dave S
reviews.title: Okay if that is your sort of thing
reviews.content: The displays of pre 20th century were interesting but few translations made it difficult to follow. The 20th century stuff was better labelled but got very repetitive. If you see this, probably don't need to see Hanoi Hilton as there is quite s bit of repetition.

reviews.author: suem56
reviews.title: Disappointing museum...very little English translations but good displays of aircraft.
reviews.content: The museum was very much up there on my friends to do list.  I'm really not into museums so my review may seem negative.  The museum seemed dated and not well set out.  The staff did not speak English so when we asked a question they just stared blankly at us?The displays were nothing special...a tin mug with a description of "Tin mug used to drink water" please!The entrance fee was minimal...paid,extra to take photos which seems to be the go in Vietnam.It was raining on the day we were there but it did not dampen our spirit to browse around the aircrafts and tanks outside of the museum.  I read a recent review on trip advisor that there was another area of display out the very rear of the museum which we were unaware of.Got some good photos of the planes and chopper and tank though.Would have been helpful if they would have handed out a brochure or map of the museum to assist us.Vietnam has numerous museums....none of them impressed me but still glad I got to see them. The museum closes for a couple of hours around lunchtime so plan you visit carefully.  Enquire about the hours or you may be like us and run out of time.

reviews.author: beers-and-chillies
reviews.title: Disappointing inside but vehicles and aircraft outside are impressive
reviews.content: Outside exhibition - planes (Mig-21, Mig-17, Il-14 and others) helicopters (Iroquois, Chinook), tanks and other armored vehicles (T-34, T-54, M113, etc), AA guns, torpedo launchers claimed to be used during Gulf of Tonkin incident - is quite interesting, but the inside disappoints. It's not even that it's mostly blatant propaganda - which is a given and can be quite interesting from historical/political point of view - it just seems to be a disjointed collection of items ("rice tube" used by Mrs X to bring food to help heroic combatants, bowl used by Mr Y to refresh himself before battle by drinking his own urine) without broader context. It would be great to see - for example - a small description of tactic used when fighting with anti-tank Lunge Mines or laying spike traps or short story of fascinating Dien Bien Phu battle or... you get the idea. A lot of opportunities missed. Tickets were 40K VND.

reviews.author: thespgtraveler
reviews.title: Better from the outside - poorly maintained but worth a visit
reviews.content: Sadly the inside is poorly maintained, but outside they have a great display of Vietnam war tanks and aircraft. A Big tip (only found out this trip and not my first to Hanoi) is walk around the the very back of the main building and there are about 10 old tanks and 6 old aircraft and a Chinook Helicopter. These are different from the ones at the front. No one knows about the back as there are no visible signs and when we were there only two other people came around the back.

reviews.author: Agro_Sydney
reviews.title: A bit disappointed
reviews.content: I was looking forward to visiting this museum as I have visited excellent  Military Museums in Great Britain, Europe and Australia.  I was disappointed by the basic displays and exhibits which appeared to be poorly preserved. Faded blurred photos, very little in the way of English descriptions and Anti American propaganda.  Staff were unfriendly and unhelpful. Outside exhibits of  planes, tanks and helicopters were interesting and good for photo opportunities.  The Vietnamese don't do good Museums.

reviews.author: Jac A
reviews.title: Another disappointing Vietnamese museum
reviews.content: The planes and tanks outside are interesting, but that's about it. The majority of the "exhibits" inside the buildings are old, blurred black/white photos. If you have visited any European/US military museums, you will be disappointed.Like the majority of other war/history museums in Vietnam-most provide the bare basics.

reviews.author: PeterGlasg0w
reviews.title: Ok if you have time
reviews.content: We visited on the same day as a large contingent of new recruits in the vietnamese army. It was logistically a bit difficult to view the exibits a bit underwhealming to be honest but if you know nothing about the french and american wars or have a keen interest in wars then worth a stop if you have time. If your going to saigon or have been to the war museum there then you have seen everything here and more

reviews.author: gracelsh
reviews.title: Coolest museum ever
reviews.content: I'm a huge military history and propaganda buff and it's fascinating to see the war from this perspective. Spent hours wandering around the exhibits, the crowning glory being the massive wreckage of a downed fighter plane. There's a real sense of history in the place, like the equipment really went through a long, hard war.A must-see!

reviews.author: Byronlady
reviews.title: Chucks Travels
reviews.content: When visiting Hanoi the Vietnam Military Histroy Museum is a must.  It's fascinating to get Vietnam's views of recent wars, etc.  The museum also includes, old helicopters, planes, tanks, it gets the imagination going and invites further research when you get home.

reviews.author: ivan i
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.content: Some of the static displays outside are quite interesting - especially the collection of US plane wreckage which looks like it has been sculpted into some kind of profound and symbolic memorial. However, I not sure of the permanency of this and the other display items. Given the general condition of their displays, it clear that they should be investing some serious funds into preserving and maintaining their aircraft, vehicles and other spoils of war. Whilst its quite generally interesting, especially from a Vietnamese national perspective, including some obvious propaganda, this is not a very good museum for non-Vietnamese speakers - given the lack of available information in English.

reviews.author: ames101
reviews.title: Vietnam trip 2013
reviews.content: My husband was very interested to go here and although I could have given it a miss, it provably does allow you to get closer to the planes and other war machines than you would ordinarily get. My husband really enjoyed the visit and I'm sure if you are into this type of thing it must be one of the best places to visit. Very cheap and good value for money.

reviews.author: Bernie D
reviews.title: Everything you wanted to know about the war
reviews.content: The site of the museum is hard to miss with the tower of the Citadel rising over it. The old citaddel structure is the most outstanding item you see first - just around the corner from the old Mig on a stand. Scattered through the section adjacent to the Citadel are examples of flying machines from the Americam war. The tower of shot down aircraft is particularly impressive. Inside the buildings are other artifacts and photos that will take hours of your time as you wander around the exhibits. another great museum.

reviews.author: Chris G
reviews.title: Must See
reviews.content: it's full of interesting exhibits and gives you a good understanding of their military history. it's obviously biased against the United States but otherwise I found it worth the visit

reviews.author: David D
reviews.title: Propaganda at its finest
reviews.content: Don't be alarmed when you go in and see the U.S. bashing that goes on, remember the museum was organized right after the war and they have good reason to be angry. And they won the war.

reviews.author: Bear
reviews.title: Must Visit for Military History Fans
reviews.content: Well put together military history museum. Plenty of displays and artifacts from the U.S. Vietnam war including U.S. cars and airplanes. Well worth a visit!

reviews.author: Slapheado
reviews.title: Go to the History Museum instead
reviews.content: The History Museum on the other side of town has nearly an exact replica of this entire museum and exhibits (bar the outdoor vehicles).There isn't too much here and nearly everything is in Vietnamese so its not great for tourists.

reviews.author: Perthgal2010
reviews.title: Huge & many aircraft
reviews.content: From the gates out front it didn't look that big but once we entered the buildings it was quite a large museum and theres plenty of war time craft to see Informative, especially for those that are war buffs.

reviews.author: tkap_12
reviews.title: Very extensive look at Vietnam's military history
reviews.content: Not much of a war buff but this museum was very interesting. It doesn't look very big, but plan to spend many hours here because it is very large. Lots of planes, tanks and other stuff to look at outside. Not to mention the many buildings full of guns, battles and other items to see inside.

reviews.author: LivingAsia7
reviews.title: Recommended...
reviews.content: If you are a history buff you will love this place (I did). Not a polished museum, but no need. It was a great diversion, if you have time drop by and absorb the culture...

locationDesc: Hanoi Train Street in Hanoi's Old Quarter is a narrow, roughly 0.85 kilometer stretch of active railway where trains pass a short distance from houses and sidewalk cafés. Built by the French in 1902, the line runs near Hanoi Railway Station along parts of Phùng Hưng and Điện Biên Phủ and sees several scheduled trains each day. Visitors commonly watch trains from outdoor café seating or nearby viewing spots while residents clear the narrow space as trains approach, and the route developed into a tourist attraction that was closed to visitors in 2019 on safety grounds before reopening with restrictions in 2023.

reviews.author: Rilana G
reviews.title: Pull in feet and experience
reviews.content: What an experience, just sitting on the terrace and watching out that you pull in your knees and toes 😅. The train really passes by. Very special to see.

reviews.author: Viet m
reviews.title: Ha Noi street train tour
reviews.content: A truly memorable experience with our guests while exploring Hanoi’s famous Train Street! 🚂❤️Ngu Hanh May Tour sincerely thanks you for choosing and trusting our services. We are delighted to have been part of your journey and hope to create many more wonderful and unforgettable memories with you in the future.Thank you for traveling with us

reviews.author: Hozyr
reviews.title: Cannot miss this!!!
reviews.content: Such a cool experience and don’t think you will get this experience anywhere. The train actually is just cams away from you and you can enjoy the drink while you wait for it. Get there early if you can.

reviews.author: Mie N
reviews.title: Check train schedule if you want to see train
reviews.content: I should’ve checked train schedules before the visit. When I got there, next train was coming in 2 hours. I couldn’t wait 2 hours so  I had a glass of coconut coffee by the train     Rail and took some pictures.

reviews.author: Theyarv
reviews.title: A good way to spend a couple of hours
reviews.content: We decided one evening to have dinner at train street. Nobody knew when the train was coming that evening (guide, concierge, AI) so we guessed and arrived 2.5 hours early. I'd probably aim for 1-1.5 hrs if you can get an accurate time, and if you can go over sunset, even better - it's pretty cool to see it in the light and the dark We decided to eat in one of the restaurants that had a balcony instead of down the track for safety. The kids (8 & 11) enjoyed walking down the tracks and seeing the hustle and bustle of all the tourist bars along the side of it. Food was poor quality but it was the only place we ate nuggets for the whole trip so the kids were happy, smoothies were surprisingly great. It was a fun and relaxing way to spend the evening Just turn up, walk down the tracks and pick one of the multiple bars/restaurants. It did get really busy with 30 minutes to go. Bring cash.

reviews.author: Beatrice L
reviews.title: To do
reviews.content: It’s impressive to see, having a drink while waiting for the train is nice

reviews.author: Martin Kral
reviews.title: Train street Hanoi
reviews.content: Hanoi train street full of restaurants and tourists waiting for train photo for social media

reviews.author: Saracen Groyper
reviews.title: Very thrilling
reviews.content: Lines of shops that sells drinks along the railway track where trains pass inches away .An absolute experience when in Hanoi

reviews.author: Andrea L
reviews.title: Something to do, but with some doubts!
reviews.content: Train Street is now one of the most famous attractions in Hanoi and, although it is definitely touristy, seeing the train pass at a very short distance from the tables is an experience worth having.Access, however, is not as immediate as it might seem. Do not think you can just arrive and walk freely along the tracks: there are checkpoints and a lot of police, and the entrances are closed, especially near when the trains pass. The simplest system is to choose one of the establishments that overlook the railway and follow the staff's instructions, who will accompany you inside when it is possible to do so.We went to the Hanoi 1990s Café and had a very good experience, so we recommend it. We arrived about 40 minutes before the train passed, ordered something to drink, and waited calmly, sitting practically right next to the tracks.When the train is about to arrive, you absolutely must follow the staff's instructions: tables and chairs are moved, everyone must stand in the indicated areas, and in a few seconds, the train passes at a truly impressive distance. Avoid taking personal initiatives or moving onto the tracks to try to get the best photograph.We chose an afternoon train and, in my opinion, it can be even more pleasant than in the evening: there is still light to see the whole street well, take photographs, and observe the surrounding environment, and we found less confusion than we expected.It has certainly become a very commercial attraction, but it remains one of the most unique experiences to have in Hanoi. I recommend checking the train schedules beforehand, arriving with some advance notice, and, above all, always following the instructions of the staff and the police.Be careful because there is no safety and the risk is high!

reviews.author: Cecile N
reviews.title: A shopping street without much interest
reviews.content: See it if you can but it is not a must-do for me.Our guide dropped us off at this place after the guided tour of Hanoi and out of curiosity we went there.

reviews.author: Linda
reviews.title: Great fun
reviews.content: We went with our guide so the seat for watching the train go by was already booked.  You can eat and drink here plenty of service.  It is very much worth visiting but bear in mind you will be squashed next to someone to experience the scene.

reviews.author: Will
reviews.title: Gangsters, bribed police at Hanoi train street
reviews.content: "Hidden" admission fee applied as you have to pay to any one of the cafe along the street for standing at the safety zone to watch the train passing by. There were gangsters and the bribed polices at there to chase tourist away in case you don't pay to buy drink at any cafe along the street. It not because of safety but because of you don't pay. Don't recommended as it gonna be chaotic and disappointed for over modified train street photo online.

reviews.author: glenn d
reviews.title: Train street Hanoi
reviews.content: Train street was a short walk from where we were staying, so we walked there and went to the cafe was okay but the beers were very dear. Great experience though the way everyone has to get off-line and all vendors pick up their tables but just be careful to ask how much before you buy any drinks or food.

reviews.author: m a
reviews.title: Instagramable
reviews.content: Different and Instagramable. Varied bars, possibly the highest concentration of gringos per m2 in Hanoi! Walking vendors. Always have DONGS!

reviews.author: Вадим К
reviews.title: ✨ Compulsory to visit! Our best evening on the legendary Train Street at the Hương Lê Cafe ✨
reviews.content: ✨ Compulsory to visit! Our best evening on the legendary Train Street in the cafe Hương Lê ✨Had an unforgettable family evening (3 adults and 2 children) on the famous Train Street in Hanoi. Our journey to this place started from the Hotel L'heritage Premium: we walked for only about 10 minutes along the completely quiet, strict government street Lý Nam Đế to the marching music of the city garbage machine. And this contrast is astonishing – after absolute silence, we instantly plunged into the incredible, surging wave of emotions and capital high of Hanoi!At the entrance to the location we were immediately warmly welcomed by an active call and professionally escorted to the available tables at the Hương Lê.🟟� RESULTS OF OUR OPERATIONAL AUDIT:▪▪ Comfort and ergonomics: Sitting was incredibly comfortable, despite the fact that it is the very center of tourist activity. Directly above our tables, the fans worked at full capacity, creating a pleasant coolness on a tropical evening.▪▪ Orders and cuisine: Prices on the menu range from quite high to quite adequate for such an iconic attraction. We ordered 4 bottles of cold beer, traditional Vietnamese iced coffee (Ice Coffee), 2 milkshakes for children and chocolate ice cream. Everything came in quickly, the drinks are excellent quality and perfectly refreshing. The total bill was VND 640,000. Cash payment on the spot.▪️ Interactive and traditions: We arrived about 50 minutes before the train arrived. This is the perfect time: the people gather very quickly, and by X-hour there were no more seats available at all. Waiting for the train is a separate pleasure, we have made wishes by laying coins and bottle caps directly on the tracks!▪️ Top level security: Ten minutes before the train arrived, all the cafe staff mobilized instantly. We were asked very sternly and clearly to change seats, and all tables and chairs were moved quickly to a safe distance so that the train would not be guaranteed to hit anyone or anything. The team's coherence at this moment is admirable.🚂 CONCLUSION AND SUMMARY:Running literally thirty centimeters from your knees, a huge train is one of the brightest, most memorable and adrenaline-filled rides in all of Vietnam! It's pure magic from the night of Hanoi. Thank you very much to the Hương Lê team for the welcome, atmosphere and safety of our children. Place must visit absolutely every traveler!

reviews.author: Didi
reviews.title: Good...
reviews.content: *Note...There are two distinct sections of the famous "Train Street" in Hanoi.1. The North Train Street (Old Quarter / Phùng Hưng)-Location: Starts around the intersection of Trần Phú Street and runs for about 100 meters along Phùng Hưng Street.- Vibe: This is the most popular, vibrant, and photographed section. It is heavily lined with cafes where visitors sit right beside the tracks to watch trains pass.2. The South Train Street (Lê Duẩn / Khâm Thiên)Location: Located south of the main train station, accessible via Alley 224 on Lê Duẩn Street.Vibe: This stretch is less crowded and more authentic, offering a quieter look at local residential life, though it still features a handful of local businesses and coffee shops.&...The little resto called 28 TRAIN TRACK FOOD AND DRINK HANOI --- delicious food, great service!!!

reviews.author: Jean-Emmanuel R
reviews.title: Nice
reviews.content: One of the must-see attractions of the Vietnamese capital. Located in the heart of the old town, the street is essentially set up for tourism. The idea is to have a drink at one of the terraces while waiting for the train to pass right by the tables. Of course, the drinks are more expensive than elsewhere but the prices remain reasonable.Nice to do...For your information, there are 3 trains on weekdays in the morning (8:50 AM, 9:20 AM, and 11:50 AM), one in the afternoon (around 3:00 PM), and two in the evening.

reviews.author: Nicnack35
reviews.title: The trains do not go slow!
reviews.content: Crazy place! Finding train times was tricky so we just turned up and got lucky. Even if you don’t see a train go past… worth a walk down the tracks. We went to both sections but either north or south section good. A little more space to sit at a cafe at the south section

reviews.author: Doina C
reviews.title: Go visit—you won't regret it.
reviews.content: Although we had a similar experience in Thailand, we wanted to see the famous "Train Street" in Vietnam as well. We didn't regret it, because we had the most spectacular egg coffee there (you'll understand once you see the photos). It’s different from Thailand because, instead of shops, there are cafés here. I’m posting a few photos so you can get a better idea. Go visit—you won't regret it.

reviews.author: RandPUk
reviews.title: Bit of Hanoi fun
reviews.content: Definitely worth a visit if you have an hour or so available. Get a grab taxi to the area. Arrive 30 - 45  minutes early and have a drink . Wasn’t that busy late morning and staff at little forest cafe and cafe Hanoi 1990s pleasant enough to us. Safely advised when train approaching. Fun experience.

reviews.author: Igor Alexeev
reviews.title: Phố Đường Tàu Hà Nội: so not a sight...
reviews.content: Hanoi Train Street (Phố Đường Tàu Hà Nội) in the Old Quarter of Hanoi was not impressed. A narrow street along which the French built railroad tracks in 1902. Curiously, of course, sometimes trains run on these tracks in modern times. However, Hanoi Train Street itself did not cause much delight: dirty, huge number of tourists, vendors, pickpockets, etc. There are plenty of cafes on the street, but none of them have made you want to come in...

reviews.author: Robert Raniti
reviews.title: A MUST VISIT
reviews.content: What a unique experience. A MUST visit in Hanoi as photos do not do justice. Sit down and enjoy a great coffee and the hype. Worth doing at least once…we did it twice.

reviews.author: sandydee_7
reviews.title: A great experience
reviews.content: Visited in the afternoon when it was a bit quieter.  Was met at the top of the street by one of the vendors and as we were a group of 8 he managed to arrange tables so we could all sit together.  Tried a Vietnamese Egg Coffee which was nice.  Great atmosphere and our cafe had a first floor balcony which was great for viewing the train when it came through.  If in Hanoi do not miss.

reviews.author: raaghu007
reviews.title: Not worth
reviews.content: Not worth it.It gets very crowded, and a long waiting time, just to watch the moving train from close.Most of the cafe owners/staff are very rude.

reviews.author: Emmanuel811
reviews.title: A must-see in Hanoi
reviews.content: It’s the perfect opportunity in the heat to cool off while watching the train pass by a few meters from the cafes.

reviews.author: Tyrone H
reviews.title: Train street Hanoi.
reviews.content: The train street in Hanoi is an unforgettable experience! Seeing the train pass by up close while enjoying a coffee – exciting, authentic, and perfect for photos. An absolute must!

reviews.author: Phil B
reviews.title: exciting! not
reviews.content: if this is exciting people must live incredibly lives the cafe down there the people are liars . downright rude and ignorant

reviews.author: Tommy
reviews.title: On the tracks
reviews.content: Great to see train so close but too many tourist

reviews.author: Nisha D
reviews.title: Tourist trap
reviews.content: Shop keepers there are mere heartless animals, least bothered about tourists safety. They are way too greedy for money.  Wonder why the government isn't doing anything about them.

reviews.author: Agnès
reviews.title: Shame!!!
reviews.content: There's no point in being forced to overpay for consumption to watch a train go by...The atmosphere is abhorrent, the bar owners yell at you to sit at your table. I saw a woman chasing an elderly tourist couple by throwing a stone at them. A man insulted my husband because he had changed places. Shame

reviews.author: Marc B
reviews.title: Nice.
reviews.content: Nice tourist attraction. The train travels down the street with almost no space on either side.

reviews.author: Vit M
reviews.title: Best experience but better with a booking
reviews.content: I booked a spot and everything was super smooth. When I arrived, our seats were already reserved right in the middle of the street with an amazing view. No stress, no being forced to buy expensive drinks, and no confusion. Better to book, so many tourist-priced coffee around.

reviews.author: Sal14460
reviews.title: Great lifetime experience
reviews.content: Well talk about an experience. Wow. Now we had a group of 4, with a formal travel group so had seats set aside for us, so going with a tour can help you get the best seat in the house. BUT beware, don't leave your seat unattended it will be occupied. There was  a lady sitting in middle of track cleaning shoes too. We were there for 540pm train but told 740pm is nicer as lights around. Be there early for the atmosphere

reviews.author: aishna j
reviews.title: PATHETIC
reviews.content: Absolutely terrible experience. The restaurants beg you to come and sit at their place and then force you to order a minimum number of dishes. When you don’t order enough, they scream, shout, abuse and embarrass you in front of everyone. Create a scene. I went with my familyof 8 and we ordered 4 dishes but it still wasn’t enough for them. Train experience is good but the thrill goes away in a minute. Overhyped place with extremely rude people.

reviews.author: Tom&NikkiTravel
reviews.title: Great experience it’s a must do here
reviews.content: Such a great experience, we visited through one of the restaurants as it’s not possible to walk straight onto the tracks. With the restaurant we booked with they gave us a timetable of the trains for the whole day so we could choose a time to go. We went for 6.15pm in the evening to get a good seat as the staff kind of choose where you sit it’s best to have more options so you can ask to keep moving on to the next seats. Going at this time of the evening meant we saw 3 trains go past at different speeds and directions which is highly recommended. We ordered a couple of beers and placed the caps on the track ready for the train to flatten them such a cool souvenir but it’s really hard finding them we found 3 out of the 4 we placed.

reviews.author: Zarajane
reviews.title: Short but Memorable
reviews.content: A must see destination as a tourist, however if you want to secure a seat before the Train passes. You must come early and enjoy the place first.Nice bustling crowds and diverse place to go.

reviews.author: David L
reviews.title: Excellent experience
reviews.content: Excellent experience.  It's a "street," although it's actually the railroad track.  On the sides of the tracks it is full of bars to sit and feel the adrenaline of watching the train pass by you.  When it will happen, the chairs are drawn into the premises, as well as put bottle covers (shoes) on the rails, and then removed crushed.  Very good experience, super recommended.

reviews.author: Mae & Armando Gil
reviews.title: A Thrill Just Inches Away
reviews.content: Hanoi Train Street is such a unique and unforgettable experience. Sitting just inches away from the tracks while enjoying a cup of coffee felt both thrilling and peaceful at the same time. The narrow street, lined with cozy cafés and friendly locals, gives you a glimpse of everyday life in Hanoi. When the train passes, it’s an adrenaline rush you won’t forget. Definitely a must-visit—but make sure to follow safety guidelines!

reviews.author: roberto p
reviews.title: Picturesque
reviews.content: We were in Phung Hung street at 1700 and 2000 hour when the train passes in this narrow street surrounded by bars and palaces.Nowadays it has become a must to see this single track train that seems to take away the chairs of the various places put along the street where tourists can drink a good beer and a Ban Mi sandwich and watch the train go by playing to warn you to get as far away from the rails as possible.It is worth seeing it......

reviews.author: sandylindsay
reviews.title: If in Hanoi, try to get a trackside seat!!
reviews.content: As part of our time in Hanoi, our Tour Manager Rob organised an evening "street food" tour in Hanoi where he took us to places which we wouldn't have considered. Due to his foresight and culinary research, we enjoyed an evening of fabulous food and entertainment as well as having a  drink at a bar in "Train Street" just in time for not 1, but 2, trains to pass. This was a fascinating experience.

reviews.author: Daflee
reviews.title: Crazy, wild but fun
reviews.content: There’s nowhere in the western world you could stand centimetres from a train as it whistles by having a drink and a bite to eat. The local shop owners vi for your attention with every train that goes by.We had some yummy food at 2 separate locations, we event sat upstairs to watch the spectacle. Make sure you put your bottle top on the tracks.

reviews.author: Mr Buster Bluth
reviews.title: Go at lunchtime to avoid the Intagrammers
reviews.content: I wasn't going to go but I strolled past the place around lunchtime. A great time to go if you want to avoid all the ghastly Instagrammers trying to be cool. Plenty of great food places. If you really want to see a train cutting through a town, get on the Toy Train in Darjeeling.

reviews.author: Jazz Gumbo
reviews.title: Fantastic - a one off location & experience.
reviews.content: We visited three different spots along train street, each with its own individual feel. All with a quite individually crazy, exciting feel. You must listen to the cafe owners concerning safety, they are fully in control of where you can, cannot sit & know better than anyone what is acceptable. Its truly a one off experience that you cannot believe you've experienced afterwards. Even without the trains there, it is a lovely & picturesque place to sit & enjoy a drink of your choice. Catch it while you can as there are consistant rumours the streets are to be closed off.

reviews.author: WillRod321
reviews.title: Good experience in train street
reviews.content: Well worth the visit, found best time was 11 am to see the 11:30am train come through, this is a big train, get there and find a bar or coffee shop to sit at, remember to take your camera and stay in a safe spot as the train passes.

reviews.author: PM-65-UK
reviews.title: I don’t get it
reviews.content: Tourist discovered trains running down a narrow street and word spread making it ‘a thing’ to see. Cafes and bars opened up serving the tourists who kept on coming. Personally I don’t get the interest of sitting (bordering on dangerously) close to a train track waiting for one of the very infrequent trains to roll by pumping out diesel fumes and adding to the heat.

reviews.author: stephane v
reviews.title: Must-see hotels in Hanoi
reviews.content: Sure it's overloaded with tourists but you can't not go if you're in Hanoi. We must favor the evening passages because the whole path is illuminated. The one at 7:40 is good, it allows you to have an aperitif, you will not make others like that elsewhere in the world. You just have to find the right place and get there early. It is better to favor the outside of the track, so you see the train arrive. I recommend the bar immediately after the traffic/railway junction.

reviews.author: Ria1104
reviews.title: Nice Place with a Good Vibe
reviews.content: This is one of the most sought after tourist destination in Hanoi City. It is a good place to grab a drink/coffee and wait for the train to pass by. Honestly, I was not very excited for the place but did enjoy the vibe of the place. Small well decorated shops lined on a narrow passage surrounding a train track, we could indeed get good photos here. Then the train comes and suddenly the entire area becomes alert and the shop owners force every people into their shops to avoid accident. Do check the timings of the train before visiting.

reviews.author: Jeremy C
reviews.title: Unique Tourist Attraction
reviews.content: It is a glorified tourist experience but then again it is unique. The train time are advertised so all you have to do is pick a bar, buy a beer and then watch that train go by and it is an experience and it is worth it.

reviews.author: GROSU C
reviews.title: New way of enjoy an cofee
reviews.content: We take a cup of Vietnamese egg coffe and enjoy in time of train passing. An thrilling experience! An must to do when in Hanoi!

reviews.author: Sandra
reviews.title: Thrilling must-do
reviews.content: The Train Street experience in Hanoi was an absolute highlight of the trip! Watching the train pass by at such incredibly close range is both thrilling and unforgettable — it really does come just inches away from where you’re sitting. One moment you’re enjoying a drink at a tiny café, and the next the entire street transforms as the train rolls through, creating an atmosphere that’s exciting, unique, and surprisingly well-managed by the locals. A must-see experience that perfectly captures Hanoi’s vibrant charm.

reviews.author: David B
reviews.title: Hanoi Train Street
reviews.content: If in Hanoi do this now, there is talk of ending this and rerouting the trains, it's a fullon fantastic experience that I fully recommend.

reviews.author: bebeThionville
reviews.title: Unusual show😂
reviews.content: A stop in a narrow street where the train levels the houses but this 9 February bad luck the train didn’t pass 🙄more time was not at the right time 🙄~~~~We've settled in. and had a coffee with coconut that I recommend 😋after our break we continued our visit to Hanoi~~~we saw her passing by on ninh binh 🤪~~~~Do not forget to taste thecoffee with egg ~~~

reviews.author: MrBoggen
reviews.title: Evening activity
reviews.content: Like this street. A must in the evening when it lives up. A lot of bars trying to get you in but you just have to focus on a good place. Sure it's a tourist trap but well worth a visit

reviews.author: DRBAUKE
reviews.title: An experience day and night
reviews.content: Definitely a highlight in Hanoi, especially if you sit with a drink in one of the numerous cafes. In the dark, I found it even more impressive.

reviews.author: Richard T
reviews.title: A must see quintessential Hanoi experience
reviews.content: Probably the most quintessential Hanoi experience. Hustle, bustle, sometimes chaos, and coffee and tea drinking. There are several trains a day…..we just turned up and asked the cafe owners what time and which direction. The trains really do pass by very close indeed. Cafe owners are responsible for safety so are intent on making people comply with the simple rules….stay seated and do not move the tables.Great to sit and have a coffee or beer whilst waiting for a train. A very “happening” place, and seems to attract an eclectic mix of people…..standing on 1 leg on a rail with arms outstretched for a photograph seems popular 😀We went three times during our 4 day stay.Fairly uneven underfoot so care and good footwear require

reviews.author: Murton68
reviews.title: Unique experience
reviews.content: This was a unique experience and not one recommended by our tour guide and yet most of us paid a visit.We got there early so no problem getting a seat at a cafe and enjoying a nice iced coffee.  The nearer it gets to the train coming the busier it gets. The cafe owners move everyone back behind a line just before the train comes.  Nevertheless it is extremely close when it does come through.

reviews.author: Jopat111
reviews.title: Must be done
reviews.content: Fun, vibrant and a little crazy. The craziness of Hanoi gets even more crazy when the train rattles down train street. The street is exceptionally narrow, lined with cafes all reliably priced. Lots of colourful lights and general party atmosphere as the train approaches. Get here about 20 minutes before the train is due in case it is early.

reviews.author: 昕桐
reviews.title: It's a place well worth watching.
reviews.content: I went to see it during the day.Still highly recommended this attractionThe beginning of a particularly multi-net red cafeThere are a lot of people who solicit.Just choose your favorite store and sit down.It's better to keep an eye on the train before you go.so as not to wait too long.There's another part of the road where there's no one to take pictures of.You can walk all the way down Train Street.

reviews.author: Talant2007
reviews.title: Railway Street
reviews.content: It is essentially a narrow alley where trains pass in close proximity to cafe tables on the street. Not much of an impression, I suppose.

reviews.author: paula k
reviews.title: Train Street is a must visit place when in Hanoi
reviews.content: Loved our experience at Train Street. We ate at May Hanoi Train Street Restaurant, which was a great place to watch the train go through. We also tried the delicious Vietnamese Egg Coffee.

reviews.author: Francois T
reviews.title: Interesting and worth a visit
reviews.content: Train street with the coffee shops, bars, restaurants and little shops next to the railway is definitely something to experience and worth waiting for the train to pass. It is a very interesting experience and exhilarating when train passes. Downside is the constant requests from people trying to sell something and shop owners trying to get you to sit at their shop.

reviews.author: VASU SUMATHI
reviews.title: Hanoi Train Street - Never miss this in Hanoi
reviews.content: Hanoi Train Street at the old quarters was one of the most unique and memorable experiences of our Vietnam trip. Sitting just inches away from the tracks, enjoying simple local food pho and chicken barbecue, a perfectly made egg coffee, while chatting with the warm and welcoming café owner, felt incredibly special. The atmosphere builds slowly, and then suddenly the train passes so close that it feels unreal — dramatic, thrilling, yet completely safe and well managed. The mix of everyday life, human warmth, and sheer spectacle makes Train Street a must-experience spot in Hanoi. A moment we will never forget. ❤️❤️❤️

reviews.author: Ruben A
reviews.title: No special experience
reviews.content: I don't understand why people think this is so special. The train passes with a lot of noise and the tourists take pictures. Maybe nice for people who live in areas where you rarely see a train. Bars and restaurants along the route are slightly more expensive than usual.

reviews.author: george c
